15. Of the monetary deposits and contributions coming under the authority of the Board of Guardians, the sums remaining after meeting the needs of the poor are deposited by the Board of Guardians in the Moscow State Savings Bank [Sokhrannaya Kazna], for the accrual of interest.

16. For the administration of the affairs of the Board of Guardians, the Guardians elect from among themselves, or from the Active Members, a Chairman and three elders, one from each of the three Evangelical parishes in Moscow. A Treasurer is elected from among the Guardians for the safekeeping of monetary funds and bookkeeping, and a Secretary for the conduct of written business.

17. These persons (art. 16) constitute the Committee of the Board of Guardians, which is charged with maintaining continuous oversight of the conduct of the affairs of the entire administration.

18. The election of the persons composing the Committee is held annually, at a general meeting of the members of the Board of Guardians present, by majority vote; the same persons may hold office for several successive terms.

19. The Committee, under the direction of the Chairman, deliberates on all matters within the scope of the Board of Guardians' activity, and determines, according to the need that arises, the measures and means for achieving the purpose set by the Board of Guardians. In addition, the Committee is charged with the duty, in order to prevent any abuses, of communicating with other charitable societies to obtain information on the condition and way of life of the poor belonging to the three Evangelical Moscow parishes who receive assistance from the Board of Guardians; for its part, the Committee likewise communicates to these societies, when necessary, observations concerning poor persons requiring care and assistance.

20. The Committee holds meetings every two weeks, and more often if necessary. Its decisions are entered in the minutes and read out at the general monthly meeting of the Members of the Board of Guardians.

21. The particular duties of the Treasurer and Secretary, as Members of the Committee, are as follows: a) the Treasurer receives from the Guardians all monetary contributions, keeps the accounts, and holds the funds; every three months he reports on the state of the treasury, and at the end of the year renders a detailed account, which he submits for verification to the Members of the Board of Guardians; b) the Secretary draws up the minutes of meetings on all matters before the Committee, prepares documents, and in general manages all record-keeping, conducting it in proper order and with due diligence. A clerk is assigned to assist him.

22. Members of the Committee (§ 16) undertake the duty of assisting the Board of Guardians in its charitable work without compensation; the clerk, however, is assigned a fixed salary from the funds of the Board of Guardians.

23. A full meeting of the Board of Guardians is held once a month. The Chairman, in setting the day for this, invites all the Guardians, as well as the Chairmen of the church Councils and the pastors of the Evangelical churches.

24. At these meetings the Members give each other an account of their activities, put newly arisen questions to general discussion, adopt decisions on them, and encourage one another to the most zealous fulfillment of the good intentions of the Board of Guardians.

25. At the end of each year a detailed report is drawn up on all the activities of the Board of Guardians, both regarding the management of its affairs and regarding the use of all contributions received for the benefit of the poor. This report is printed, and copies of it are distributed to all Members, together with an alphabetical list of the persons composing the Board of Guardians, and one copy is submitted, through the provincial authorities, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

26. The rules set forth above may be amended, in accordance with circumstances, by majority vote of the Members of the Board of Guardians, with the confirmation of the government.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXII. P. 28-30.*

## No. 102. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE CONDITIONS FOR COLONISTS' DEPARTURE ABROAD, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS I (1849)

23051. — February 28. Highest-confirmed opinion of the State Council, published April 25. — On the release abroad of foreigners who had entered the estate of rural inhabitants under the designation of colonists.

The State Council, in the Department of Economy and in General Assembly, having examined the most humble report of the General Assembly of the first three Departments and the Heraldry of the Governing Senate on the question: whether, with regard to colonists who have declared a wish to return abroad, the permission of the Governing Senate should be sought — took into account that, with regard to foreigners who had entered the estate of rural inhabitants under the name of colonists, there exist special rules contained in the Code of Statutes on the Good Order of Towns and Villages (Digest of Laws, Vol. 12). By force of these rules, they are granted free departure abroad altogether, subject only to certain conditions concerning the one-time payment of taxes and debts owed by them and the disposition of lands belonging to them in ownership (Arts. 151, 462, 542 and 543); but those rules contain no provision that permission of the Governing Senate must be sought for colonists to relinquish Russian subjecthood, as is prescribed in the Laws on Estates (Art. 1406) with regard to foreigners in general, that is, those who have entered other social estates of the state; it is stated only that in the case of departure from the state (without distinction between temporary absence and departure forever), colonists are obliged to furnish themselves with passports, through communications of their authorities, from those places and persons to whom, on the basis of the Statute on Passports and Fugitives, the issuance of such passports is assigned as a duty (Art. 461). This enactment has always been understood in this sense in practical application, for, according to the certification of the Minister of State Domains, the Guardianship Committee for Foreign Settlers of the Southern Region of Russia, established as early as 1818, has always released colonists back abroad at its own discretion. In consequence of this, the State Council, in agreement with the conclusion of the General Assembly of the Governing Senate, recognizing for its part that, given the definiteness of the rules and conditions by which colonists may be discharged for return departure abroad, the seeking of special permission from the higher government for this would constitute a mere formality, without any substantial benefit to the matter, and would serve only to needlessly constrain the colonists, resolved in its opinion: 1) To confirm the Senate's report, and, in consequence thereof, to leave the aforementioned Committee with the right it has enjoyed until now, and further to supplement Art. 1406 of the Laws on Estates (Digest of Laws, Vol. 9) with the following note: "the release abroad of foreigners who have entered the estate of rural inhabitants under the designation of colonists is carried out in observance of the rules established for that purpose in the Statute on Colonies." <...>

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the question of whether, with regard to colonists who have declared a wish to return abroad, the permission of the Governing Senate should be sought, and commanded that it be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXIV. P. 121.*

## No. 103. DECREE OF NICHOLAS I ON THE SETTLEMENT OF PRUSSIAN MENNONITES IN SAMARA GOVERNORATE (1851)

25752 a. — November 19. Nominal [decree], announced to the Senate by the Minister of State Domains on July 31, 1852. — On the settlement of Prussian Mennonites in Samara Governorate.

Certain Mennonites living in West Prussia petitioned for permission to settle in Russia on the rights granted to their co-religionists, with the allotment of land to them from the treasury, or with the grant to them of the right to acquire such land by purchase. Regarding this petition, he, the Minister, had the honor of most humbly presenting it for the Highest consideration of His Imperial Majesty, proposing for his part:

1) To admit the Mennonites, in the number of one hundred families, to inspect and select lands from the free plots in Samara Governorate; and should they not find suitable lands there, then to permit them, in accordance with their own wish and on the rules established for foreign settlers in Art. 538 of the Digest of Laws, Vol. XII, to acquire such lands wherever they might wish by purchase from private owners; — and

2) To grant to those Mennonites who shall in future be permitted by the Government to settle in Russia in new colonies, on the rules set forth in the Digest of Laws, Vol. XII, in the Statutes on Colonies of Foreigners in the Empire, exemption from military service for twenty years from the time of settlement, and, upon the expiration of this term, to impose on them, by calculation, a permanent monetary levy under the name of recruit money.

To this proposal, on the 19th day of November 1851, Highest assent was given, on condition that the payment of recruit money be calculated according to the rates now, and hereafter, established by law.

Conditions on which it is proposed to admit into Samara Governorate

the settlement of up to one hundred families of Prussian Mennonites.

1. Mennonites who, on the basis of the Highest assent that has been given for the settlement of up to one hundred families of Prussian Mennonites on state lands of Samara Governorate, shall wish to resettle to Russia, are obliged to obtain from their Government a release consent [Konsens] and, upon presentation of it to the Russian Imperial Mission, on which the furnishing of passports to them will depend, to deposit with it, as security for the settlement of each family, not documents_________________________________________________________________________________ 259

less than three hundred fifty Prussian thalers, which, after deduction of forwarding expenses, will be returned to them upon arrival at the place of settlement.

2. Likewise, they shall give a written undertaking that they will constantly bear in mind the purpose of their calling to Russia — to serve as models for other agricultural estates, following in this respect the example of their Molochna brethren.

3. For the first undertaking of resettlement, a party of not fewer than twelve families must be formed, since only under this condition will it be possible to lay a solid foundation for the colony.

4. All rules existing in the Statute on Colonies, both in general for foreign settlers and in particular for Mennonites, — concerning which no reservation is made in the present conditions, — are extended also to the new resettlers.

5. To them and their descendants is granted freedom of exemption from entry into military service. In lieu of the performance of this obligation, they are subject, upon the expiration of twenty years of exemption from the time of their enrollment into the estate of foreign settlers, to a permanent levy under the name of recruit levy. This levy shall be calculated in accordance with the value of a recruit as established by the Government, which is presently fixed at three hundred silver rubles.

6. They enjoy a ten-year exemption from the payment of taxes from the time of their enrollment into the estate of foreign settlers.

7. To each settling family shall be allotted sixty-five desiatinas, if this proves possible in the localities that will be chosen for their settlement.

8. For the settlement of the Mennonites, lands of Samara Governorate in Novouzensk and Nikolaevsk districts are designated, where German colonies already exist. In making this designation, subject to confirmation by the Minister of State Domains, upon inspection of the land by the first party, or by Mennonites entrusted by it, and upon their expressing agreement to accept it, consideration is given to the possibility of the joint settlement of up to one hundred Mennonite families and the convenience of establishing several separate colonies within this area. But should difficulty be encountered in allotting land on this basis in Nikolaevsk and Novouzensk districts, or should the Mennonites, for economic reasons, decline settlement in those districts, then they shall be permitted to choose lands in other localities of Samara Governorate.

9. As quitrent payment for lands in Novouzensk and Nikolaevsk districts, they will, upon the expiration of the ten exemption years, be assessed at the rate established for Mennonites in the southern region of Russia, namely four and a half silver kopecks per desiatina; in other localities, the quitrent payment will be determined by valuation, based on the relative quality of the plot chosen.

10. Plots once designated for the settlement of up to one hundred Mennonite families shall be exempted from any other use, but allotment to the Mennonites, as they arrive, shall be made only at the rate of 65 desiatinas per family; the remaining area, pending settlement, shall be let out as a state quitrent item, with the Mennonites being granted the right to retain for themselves all free land, or such part of it as, without violating the rules of husbandry, can be set aside, upon payment of the existing quitrent with an addition of one percent for each year.

11. The right of distilling and selling beverages in the districts of their settlement, granted to Mennonites already settled in Russia, does not extend to the Mennonites resettling on the basis of these conditions; they must, in this respect, submit to the excise-farming conditions in force in Russia; — and

12. The resettlers are granted the right of duty-free import into Russia of goods to the amount of up to one hundred silver rubles in duties per family, in addition to used clothing, linen, agricultural implements, and the like, which are subject to free passage under customs regulations.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXVII (Supplement). Pp. 69-71.*

## No. 104. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON THE DEPARTURE OF COLONISTS ABROAD, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS I (1852)

26070. — March 18. Highest-confirmed statute of the Committee of Ministers. — On the discharge of colonists abroad.

A memorandum of the Minister of State Domains, of February 26, was heard, on permitting twenty-one Bulgarian colonists to travel to Mount Athos, and one female colonist to Jerusalem, for veneration of the Holy places, and on discharging colonists abroad henceforth without seeking special Highest permission for this.

The Committee resolved: to confirm this submission.

The Sovereign Emperor was Highly pleased to consent to the discharge of the said colonists, whereupon there followed a command in His Imperial Majesty's own hand: For departure to Germany, always seek My permission.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXVII. P. 158.*

## No. 105. DECISION ON THE RESETTLEMENT OF INHABITANTS OF THE VORONEZH COLONY OF RIEBENSDORF TO THE YEISK DISTRICT, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS I (1852)

26077. — March 20. Highest-confirmed statute of the Caucasus Committee. — On the resettlement of colonists from the colony of Riebensdorf, Voronezh Governorate, to lands near the town of Yeisk in Chernomoriya.

A memorandum of the Minister of State Domains, of January 31, was heard, on the resettlement of thirty colonist families from the colony of Riebensdorf, Voronezh Governorate, to lands near the town of Yeisk in Chernomoriya.

The Committee, finding for its part the establishment of a German colony near the town of Yeisk to be quite useful, resolved: to confirm the conclusion of the Minister of State Domains as set forth in his present submission.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the journal of the Committee, on the 20th day of this March, was Highly pleased to write in his own hand: "To be carried out."

Memorandum. The colonists of the colony of Riebensdorf, situated in Voronezh Governorate, owing to the shortage of land they were suffering and to a fire that occurred in their colony in June 1850, which destroyed more than half the houses, petitioned, in the number of fifty-four families, to resettle to Stavropol DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 261

Governorate, on free lands near the town of Yeisk, previously inspected by their representatives.

The Minister of State Domains, recognizing for his part also that the resettlement of a certain part of the Riebensdorf colonists would be useful, communicated regarding this petition to the Viceroy of the Caucasus, who responded that the establishment of a German colony near the town of Yeisk was quite desirable, and that he would consider it possible to permit the requested settlement on the following conditions:

1. To establish near the town of Yeisk a German colony, for the first time as an experiment, of thirty families, permitting its subsequent increase to sixty families, depending on the benefit that proves to result from those initially settled in practice.

2. To assign land to the colonists at the rate of thirty desiatinas per family, between the town of Yeisk and the stanitsa of Staroshcherbinovskaya, or at Shirokaya Balka. At the first location, given the good quality of the land, the proximity of the liman would afford the colonists great conveniences for deriving benefit from water communication; at the second location, the water and soil are better, but there is no liman nearby. The choice of one or the other point for the settlement of the colony is therefore left to the discretion of the authorities.

3. For the initial establishment of households, to give the colonists, as a loan from the funds of the Black Sea Host, up to one hundred seventy-five silver rubles for each family, with repayment of the money within ten years from the time of settlement. Together with the principal sum, the colonists must pay the statutory interest on the general rules for loans, so that this transaction, while providing the colonists with substantial assistance, does not deprive the Host of the income it would receive from converting the free sum into credit institutions. The prompt repayment of the loan shall be imposed on the whole community of colonists, with the obligation to answer for one another, without prohibiting repayment of the debt before the term, when the colonists deem this possible for themselves.

4. In addition to the said loan, to grant the colonists an exemption for eight years from the time of settlement in the payment of state taxes and dues.

5. For the resolution of matters, oversight of order, and the exact fulfillment of everything relating to the economy, police, and moral condition of the colonists, to allow them to appoint elders and elected representatives from among themselves. Thereafter to leave the colony under the immediate subordination of the Investigative Authority of the Yeisk district, where it will be settled, under the general administration and patronage of the Host Administration of the Black Sea Host. To act: the elders and elected representatives on the basis of the duties defined in the Statute on Colonies for Schulzen and Beisitzer (Vol. XII, Arts. 20, 50, and others); the Investigative Chief — on the rights of a Colony Overseer (Art. 80 and others), and the Host Administration — on the rights of the Guardianship Committee for Foreign Settlers of the Southern Region (Art. 42 and others). Criminal cases of the colonists are to be referred for decision to the Host Courts.

6. All other rights of estate of the colonists are likewise to conform to the general provisions on colonies contained in the Digest of Laws, Vol. XII, Book IV; the colonists may enjoy fishing rights on the same basis as Host inhabitants; but neither distilling nor the manufacture of any beverages granted to the excise farm existing in Chernomoriya shall be permitted to the colonists, for such permission might undermine the excise farm and diminish the revenues it brings to the Host.

7. The conditions of settlement are to be announced to the colonists, and from among those who agree to them, preference is to be given in selection to those most knowledgeable in husbandry and most reliable; after which the actual settlement of the selected persons at the designated place is to be permitted without delay, under the special supervision and care of the Ataman of the Black Sea Host, so that no difficulties or disorders occur in the process.

These conditions were presented to the petitioners, who, by a resolution drawn up on this subject, expressed their agreement to submit to them, declining only to receive the loan money for settlement from the funds of the Black Sea Host.

The Minister of State Domains, bearing in mind the agreement expressed by the colonists of the colony of Riebensdorf to submit, upon resettlement to lands near the town of Yeisk, to the conditions proposed by the Viceroy of the Caucasus, and encountering for his part obstacles to their implementation, since the colonists have no need of monetary assistance for settlement, while the exemption from tax payment is requested for them at the rate established in a similar case for state peasants, — the Minister of State Domains would consider it advisable: to permit the resettlement of thirty families of the colony of Riebensdorf to lands near the town of Yeisk in accordance with the conditions proposed by the Viceroy of the Caucasus, but without the grant to them of the assistance mentioned in point 3, unless the colonists, upon arrival at the place, themselves request it.

Of which the Minister of State Domains has the honor to submit for the consideration of the Caucasus Committee, deeming it his duty to add that, upon the confirmation of the requested measure, arrangements will be made both for designating for resettlement those families that would, so far as possible, correspond in economic respects to the expectations of the Viceroy of the Caucasus, and for excluding the said families from the jurisdiction of the Administration of State Domains.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXVII. Pp. 160—162.*

## No. 106. DECISION ON EXEMPTIONS FOR THE TRANSCAUCASIAN COLONY OF MARIENFELD, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS I (1852)

26226. — May 2. Highest-confirmed statute of the Caucasus Committee. — On granting exemptions to the Marienfeld colonists settled in the Transcaucasian region.

A memorandum of the Manager of the Ministry of Finance, of April 11, was heard, on granting exemptions to the Marienfeld colonists settled in the Transcaucasian region.

The Committee resolved: to confirm the conclusion of the Manager of the Ministry of Finance.

The Sovereign Emperor was Highly pleased to assent to this statute of the Committee on the 2nd day of this May.

Considerations and conclusions of the Manager of the Ministry of Finance. Basing himself on the certification of the Viceroy of the Caucasus that, owing to the extreme poverty of the Marienfeld colonists, it is necessary to grant them exemption in the payment of DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 263

taxes and dues, and taking into consideration that, upon the initial settlement of these colonists beyond the Caucasus, one thousand five hundred silver rubles were issued to them as a loan for establishment, to be repaid within six years without interest, the Manager of the Ministry of Finance, in agreement with the opinion of the Minister of State Domains and the proposal of the Viceroy of the Caucasus, would consider it possible to grant the said colonists a ten-year exemption in the payment of taxes and dues, reckoning it from 1849; and, as to the term by which the loan issued to them in 1845 for establishment was to be repaid, since six years have already elapsed since that time, to add a further four exemption years, and then, in accordance with note to Art. 322 of Vol. XII of the Digest of Laws on Colonies, to begin collection of the loan money from 1856, over the course of ten years, in equal annual installments.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXVII. Sect. 1. Pp. 311-312.*

## No. 107. DECREE OF NICHOLAS I ON THE NEW PLAN OF THE VOLGA COLONY OF YEKATERINENSTADT (1852)

26704. — October 27. Nominal [decree], announced to the Senate by the Minister of State Domains. — On the new plan of the colony of Yekaterinenstadt, in Samara Governorate.

At the petition of the Society of the colony of Yekaterinenstadt, Samara Governorate, for bringing the latter into a desired condition as regards good appearance and regularity, — I had the honor of laying before the Highest consideration of His Imperial Majesty a newly drawn-up plan of the colony of Yekaterinenstadt, proposing to issue it for the guidance of the local colonial authorities, on condition that, in carrying out the said proposals, which depend on financial means, no constraint be placed upon the householders, and that the terms for the relocation of private structures be determined by communal resolutions.

This proposal the Sovereign Emperor, on the 27th day of this October, was Highly pleased to command to be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXVII. Sect. 1. P. 628.*

## No. 108. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON EXEMPTIONS FOR THE SCHOOL AT THE LUTHERAN CHURCH OF ST. ANNE IN ST. PETERSBURG, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS I (1852)

26731. — November 3. Highest-confirmed opinion of the State Council, published December 10. — On granting certain privileges to the school existing at the Evangelical Lutheran Church of St. Anne in St. Petersburg.

The State Council, in the Joint Departments of Laws and of Civil and Ecclesiastical Affairs and in General Assembly, having examined the submission of the Minister of Public Education on granting certain privileges to the school existing at the Evangelical Lutheran Church of St. Anne in St. Petersburg, found that the school, which has existed for more than a hundred years at the St. Petersburg Evangelical Church of St. Anne, was taken in 1840 under the special patronage of the Government, and, as the Minister of Public Education certifies, brings real benefit. Therefore the State Council, agreeing with his, the Minister's, proposals on granting the said educational institution certain rights and privileges comparable to the school at the Evangelical Church of St. Peter, resolved in its opinion: to confirm the submission of the Minister of Public Education, and, in consequence thereof, to enact the following:

1. The school at the Church of St. Anne is under the jurisdiction of the Trustee of the St. Petersburg Educational District, who, receiving reports on the condition of this institution, is obliged to oversee everything relating to the moral purpose of upbringing and the teaching of academic subjects.

2. The textbooks used in the school must be approved by the Ministry of Public Education.

3. To the Director of the school is assigned Class VIII, to the Inspector Class IX, to Teachers of sciences and languages Class X, to teachers of drawing and calligraphy Class XIV, according to the schedule of civil-service positions by class appended to Article 355 of the Statute on Service by Government Appointment (Digest of Laws, Vol. III); teachers of other arts, however, are not considered to be in state service.

4. All these persons are confirmed in the classes assigned to them, following the example of other school officials, in the established manner: the Director after six years, and the Inspector and Teachers after four years, of service in these capacities. Seniority in class, upon completion of the said terms, is reckoned, for those already serving at the school, from the day of the confirmation of these rules, and for those newly appointed, from the day of their confirmation in office.

5. In further promotion in rank, the Director, Inspector, and Teachers of drawing and calligraphy are subject to the general rules concerning civil officials; the other teachers of the school, except teachers of the arts, are promoted three ranks above the class assigned to their position.

6. With respect to categories for rank promotion, Teachers of sciences, Russian, and ancient languages are classed in the first category of officials, that is, those holding certificates of completion of studies at higher educational institutions; Teachers of modern foreign languages are classed in the second category of officials, that is, those holding certificates of completion of studies at secondary educational institutions. It goes without saying that Teachers of modern foreign languages who have obtained certificates from higher educational institutions will be promoted in rank according to the rules for the first category of officials.

7. According to the schedule of posts and ranks for distinctions in uniform (Digest of Laws, Vol. III, Statute on Service by Government Appointment, appendix to Art. 935), the following are assigned: the Director of the school to Category VII, the Inspector to Category VIII, Teachers of sciences, Russian, and ancient languages to Category IX, Teachers of modern foreign languages, drawing, and calligraphy to Category X.

8. As to the appointment, in the established manner, of both the heads of the two divisions of the school and of the teachers, women teachers, overseers, and women overseers, the Council of the Church of St. Anne submits, under its own responsibility for the selection, to the Trustee of the St. Petersburg Educational District, DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________265

with the sole condition that those admitted to teaching shall have the certificates established for that purpose by the general school authorities.

9. Persons from the taxable estates, or those registered as merchants, are appointed as teachers only upon presentation by them of certificates of discharge from their communities, and, after communication with the proper authorities, are excluded from those estates.

10. With regard to the rights of the school's graduates in civil service, it is classed in the second category of educational institutions, on a par with Gymnasiums (Digest of Laws, Vol. III, Statute on Service by Government Appointment, Art. 81 and appendix thereto).

11. Female graduates of this school, of free status, are granted the right, upon successful completion of the full course and receipt of a certificate, to become governesses without the examination established for that purpose, as is granted to those who have completed their education at educational institutions maintained by the Government and under the Highest patronage of the Empress.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was Highly pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on granting certain privileges to the school existing at the Evangelical Lutheran Church of St. Anne in St. Petersburg, and commanded that it be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXVII. Sect. 1. Pp. 641-642.*

## No. 109. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSING COLONISTS WITH THE QUITRENT TAX, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS I (1853)

27068. — March 2. Highest-approved opinion of the State Council (<...>). — On the procedure for assessing the quitrent tax on colonists emerging from their exemption period.

The State Council, in the Department of Economy and in General Assembly, having examined the report of the Minister of State Domains on the procedure for assessing the quitrent tax on colonists emerging from their exemption period, resolved by opinion: to approve the conclusion of the Minister, for the reasons he presented, and, in consequence thereof, to set forth articles 287, 293, 294, and 295 of the Statutes on Colonies of Foreigners in the Empire (Digest of Laws, Vol. XII) as follows:

Art. 287. All Novorossiysk and Bessarabian colonists settled on state lands, not excluding those who are not engaged in agriculture, upon expiration of their exemption years, must be placed on an equal footing in the payment of taxes with the state peasants of that locality, with the sole exception of the Mennonites, as well as the Bulgarians, Rumelians, and other Trans-Danubian settlers of the Bessarabian region (arts. 286 and 288).

Art. 293. The apportionment of taxes among the colonists is of two kinds: a) general, throughout the whole governorate, and b) internal, within each colony.

Art. 294. The general apportionment of taxes for each governorate is carried out by converting them into a land-based assessment, on the basis of the regulation on the equalization of taxes by land among the state peasants.

Art. 295. The internal apportionment of taxes within the colonies is left to the community of each colony to make at its own discretion, in proportion to the means and advantages of each householder, not excluding those colonists who, being occupied in trades, let out their allotments for rent.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was pleased to give His Highest approval to the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council concerning the procedure for assessing the quitrent tax on colonists emerging from their exemption period, and commanded that it be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXVIII. Pp. 89-90.*

## No. 110. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON THE REORGANIZATION OF RUSSIAN SCHOOLS IN THE VOLGA COLONIES, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS I (1855)

29026. — February 8. Highest-approved regulation of the Committee of Ministers. — On the transformation of Russian schools in the Volga colonies.

The memorandum of the Minister of State Domains, of January 18, on the transformation of Russian schools in the Volga colonies, was heard.

The Committee resolved: to approve this report.

The Sovereign Emperor was Highest pleased to approve the Committee's resolution:

Memorandum. In the Volga colonies of foreign settlers there exist, for the teaching of the Russian language, two schools, each for twenty-five pupils, established on the basis of the regulation of the Committee of Ministers, Highest-approved on November 7, 1833 (6551), with the purpose that pupils, upon completing the course, should teach colonist children Russian in the rural colonist schools, where the Schulmeisters teach in German, with the division of time between both languages in all classes; whereby it was decreed that the selection of children for the schools be left to the communities, subject to the approval of the pastors, preferably from the more populous colonies and from among orphans, with the necessary expenses charged to all the colonies in general.

Experience has demonstrated the unsatisfactory arrangement of these two schools, arising chiefly from the fact that in them, for lack of any issued regulation or even a program of instruction, the course has hitherto been limited to the Russian language alone, whereas in the rural schools, in which those graduating from these schools are to be teachers, colonist children are also taught reading, writing, and the Law of God.

In consequence of this, and in view of reports from the local colonial administration concerning the difficulty encountered in filling teaching positions in the colonies, it has been deemed useful to transform the schools presently existing for the teaching of Russian, so that pupils graduating from these schools may occupy teaching posts in the rural schools in all subjects, thereby eliminating the need for two teachers at each rural school, and consequently the double expense thereof, and so that these teachers might also teach certain subjects in the Russian language, with a view to the more rapid dissemination of knowledge of this language among the colonists.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXX. P. 151.*

## No. 111. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A TOBACCO FACTORY IN THE VOLGA COLONY OF SOLOTHURN, APPROVED BY ALEXANDER II (1856)

30309. — March 27. Highest-approved regulation of the Committee of Ministers, communicated to the Senate by the Minister of Finance. — On permitting, by way of exception, the householders of the community of the colony of Solothurn, Nikolaevsk district, Samara governorate, to establish a tobacco factory in the said colony.

The Sovereign Emperor, pursuant to the report of the Minister of Finance to the Committee of Ministers and to the resolution thereof, on the 27th day of March of this year, was Highest pleased to command: to permit, by way of exception, the one hundred twenty-nine householders of the community of the colony of Solothurn, Nikolaevsk district, Samara governorate, to establish in the said colony, on the basis of the resolution drawn up by them, a tobacco factory, with the registration in the 3rd merchant guild of only one commissioner thereof, on condition that in the operation of the factory, the manufacture, sale, and dispatch to other towns of the tobacco products prepared therein, and the selection of excise bands, the rules set forth in the Statute on the Tobacco Excise be strictly observed.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXI. Sect. I. P. 157.*

## No. 112. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON THE PROCEDURE FOR COLONISTS' DEPARTURE ABROAD, APPROVED BY ALEXANDER II (1856)

30380. — April 10. Highest-approved regulation of the Committee of Ministers. — On the procedure for granting foreign colonists leave to travel abroad.

The memorandum of the Minister of State Domains, of March 24, on permitting the colonist Pahl to be absent for one year abroad, was heard.

The Committee resolved: to grant the said colonist leave to travel abroad, in accordance with the report.

In discussing both this and other similar cases, the Committee has repeatedly noted that colonists' leaves of absence abroad are presently excepted from the procedure established by article 461 of the Statutes on Colonies of Foreigners, Digest of Laws, Vol. XII (1842 edition). This exception was made in 1849, when, owing to the political unrest disturbing Western Europe, the Minister of State Domains, with a view to possibly reducing colonists' absences abroad, petitioned the Committee of Ministers that, until the restoration of calm and order in Europe, Highest permission be sought each time, through the established procedure, for all such absences. This report, by resolution of the Committee, was honored with the Highest approval of His Imperial Majesty the late Emperor Nicholas Pavlovich of blessed memory on May 24, 1849.

Thereafter, in 1852, Adjutant General Count Kiselev, finding that the influence of the causes which had prompted the Government to adopt this measure had more or less already been removed, considered it possible, with a view to reducing correspondence and preventing delay in granting colonists leave to travel abroad, to return to the procedure previously in force for matters of this kind. The Committee of Ministers resolved to approve this report; but on the journal concerning this matter, the Emperor Nicholas Pavlovich, now with God, deigned to write in his own hand, on March 18, 1852 (26070): "For leave to Germany, always seek My permission."

Now the Committee, having examined all the details of this matter, found that, with the change in circumstances that had called for special precautions regarding the granting of leave to colonists to travel abroad, and with the restoration of peace and calm in Europe, there is no inconvenience whatsoever in returning again to the procedure for granting foreign colonists leave to travel abroad that existed prior to 1849, and accordingly resolved to seek His Imperial Majesty's Most Gracious permission for this.

To this resolution of the Committee there followed His Imperial Majesty's command, written in his own hand: "Agreed."

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXI. Pp. 209-210.*

## No. 113. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A SHELTER FOR BOYS AT THE LUTHERAN CHURCH OF ST. PETER IN ST. PETERSBURG, APPROVED BY ALEXANDER II (1856)

30425. — April 24. Highest-approved regulation of the Committee of Ministers, communicated to the Senate by the Minister of Internal Affairs. — On the establishment, under the oversight of the Council of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of St. Peter in St. Petersburg, of a special educational institution for poor male minors.

The Sovereign Emperor, by resolution of the Committee of Ministers, on the 24th day of April of this year, was Highest pleased to command: that a special educational institution for poor male minors be established under the oversight of the Council of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of St. Peter in St. Petersburg, on the rules proposed by the Society for the Care of the Poor, provided that this institution be placed under the authority of the Ministry of National Education on the same basis as governs all schools existing at churches of foreign confessions, and that, in case the sum of one thousand two hundred rubles in silver allotted for the maintenance of the institution proves insufficient, the additional funds required for this purpose be disbursed by the Council of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of St. Peter from the sums at its disposal.

Concerning the aforesaid Highest command, the Minister of Internal Affairs submitted a report to the Governing Senate, for the necessary action, adding that the Society for the Care of the Poor had proposed the following rules:

1. Children of entirely destitute parents lacking the means for their support and upbringing, from the parish of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of St. Peter, are admitted to the educational institution for poor male minors. Boys are accepted no younger than seven years of age and remain in the institution, at its full expense, until the day of their confirmation, that is, until their fifteenth or sixteenth year.

2. In the institution, boys are taught the Law of God, reading and writing in Russian and German, and the rules of arithmetic, as well as certain trades and gardening, under the guidance of craftsmen belonging to the same parish.

3. The institution is under the oversight of the Council of the Church of St. Peter, following the example of the Orphanage under the authority of that same Council; a Trustee of the institution is elected by the Council from among its Members; and

4. For the maintenance of the institution the following is allotted:

a) For the rental of premises, from the funds of the Church of St. Peter, by resolution of the Council, with the consent of the whole parish, at ........................................ 300 rubles per year.

and b) For other expenses, from the funds of the Society, which annually receives from four to five thousand rubles at its disposal, at .......... 900 ---------

Total................................................................................... 1200 rubles per year.

The disbursement of nine hundred rubles by the Society will continue until such time as the institution accumulates its own capital, which may be formed from private donations. Those who donate not less than one thousand rubles in silver in favor of the institution acquire the right to place, free of charge, one poor boy from the parish of St. Peter in the institution.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXI. Sect. 1. Pp. 241-242.*

## No. 114. STATUTES ON THE SPIRITUAL AFFAIRS OF FOREIGN CONFESSIONS IN THE RUSSIAN EMPIRE (1857)

### BOOK ONE. ON THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE SPIRITUAL AFFAIRS OF CHRISTIANS OF THE ROMAN CATHOLIC CONFESSION.

#### SECTION ONE. ESTABLISHMENT OF THE SPIRITUAL AUTHORITIES AND ADMINISTRATIVE SEATS.

##### CHAPTER ONE.

On the composition of the dioceses.

11. In the Russian Empire there are seven dioceses of the Roman Catholic confession: the archdiocese of Mogilev, and the dioceses of Vilna, Telšiai (or Samogitia), Minsk, Lutsk-Zhitomir, Kamenets, and Tiraspol.

Note. The laws on the administration of the spiritual affairs of Christians of the Roman Catholic confession in the Kingdom of Poland are not included in this Digest.

1798 Apr. 28 (18504); 1840 Oct. 11 (13854); 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, art. I; 1848 Nov. 29 (22766); 1852 Nov. 6 (26748).

12. To the archdiocese of Mogilev belong the Roman Catholic churches: a) in the Mogilev governorate, b) all those which, according to the schedule set forth below (art. 13), are not included among the other diocesan districts of this same confession in the Empire, and c) in the Grand Duchy of Finland.

1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, art. I, para. 1; 1848 Nov. 29 (22766).

13. To the diocese of Vilna belong the Roman Catholic churches in the governorates of Vilna and Grodno (understanding the boundaries of these two, as well as of the following six, governorates as they stood in 1848); to Telšiai, in the governorates of Kovno and Courland; to Lutsk-Zhitomir, in the governorates of Kiev and Volhynia; to Minsk, in the governorate of the same name; to Kamenets, in Podolia governorate; to Tiraspol, in the governorates of Kherson, Yekaterinoslav, Taurida, Saratov, and Astrakhan, in the Bessarabian region, and in the Caucasus and Transcaucasian territory.

1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, art. I, paras. 2-7, and art. II; 1848 Nov. 29 (22766).

14. The number and names of the parishes of each diocese are determined by a specially approved schedule. Their number may be increased when required either by an increase in population or by the excessive size of existing parishes and the difficulty of communications.

1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, arts. II and XXXI.

15. For closer oversight of the parish churches and their clergy, the parishes of each diocese are combined into special districts called deaneries.

See the enactments cited under art. 36.

##### CHAPTER TWO.

On the ecclesiastical hierarchy.

16. In the archdiocese of Mogilev, the head is an Archbishop; in each of the other dioceses (art. 11), a Bishop.

1798 Apr. 28 (18504); 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, art. I.

17. By virtue of the privileges attached to the Mogilev Church of the Roman rite (de jure et dignitate Ecclesiae), the Archbishop of Mogilev is at the same time Metropolitan of all Roman Catholic churches in the Empire and the Grand Duchy of Finland. In these parts of the state he takes precedence over all clergy of his confession; the Bishops, presiding in the other dioceses, are at the same time Suffragans of the Metropolitan.

1798 Apr. 28 (18504); 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) para. 2; 1817 Oct. 24 (27106) § 141; 1848 Jul. 5 (new style), act of the Roman Pope; Nov. 29 (22766).

18. Under the Archbishop and each of the other Diocesan Heads (art. 16) there is a fixed number of Suffragan Bishops.

Note. The number of suffragan sees: in the archdiocese of Mogilev, three; in the dioceses of Vilna, three; Telšiai, three; Minsk, one; Lutsk-Zhitomir, two; Kamenets, one; Tiraspol, two.

1798 Apr. 28 (18504) para. 4; 1842 Jan. 1 (15188) staff regulations; 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, arts. III and IV; 1848 Nov. 29 (22766).

19. At each cathedral church there is a Chapter (Capitulum) composed of a fixed number of Prelates or senior members (Dignitates), Canons (Canonici), and Vicar Priests or Mansionaries (Mansionarii vel Beneficiarii).

1784 Apr. 17 (15982); 1798 Apr. 28 (18504); 1842 Jul. 17, detailed staff regulations; 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, art. VI; 1856 Jul. 16, information of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 271

20. Under the Archbishop and each of the other Diocesan Heads (art. 16) there are:

1) A Consistory, under the chairmanship of an Official, consisting of a Vice-Official, a Visitor of monasteries, and a fixed number of members from among the clergy. It has a Chancery consisting of a Secretary and other civil officials, on the basis of the staff regulations.

2) Personally attached to the Archbishop, a Chancery, and to the Bishop, a Secretary, on the basis of the staff regulations.

1839 Jul. 18 (12549); 1842 Jul. 17, detailed staff regulations; Dec. 16, Highest command; 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, arts. XVII-XIX.

21. For the examination and decision of matters common to all Roman Catholic dioceses (art. 11), specified below (art. 67), there exists in St. Petersburg a supreme spiritual body under the name of the Roman Catholic Ecclesiastical Collegium, under the chairmanship of the Archbishop-Metropolitan (art. 17), consisting of two Members and seven Assessors from the dioceses. — Attached to the Collegium are: a) a Procurator, and b) a Chancery, on the basis of the staff regulations.

1801 Nov. 13 (20053) para. 1 and staff regulations; 1839 Mar. 15 (12122) staff regulations.

22. At each parish church there is a Rector, or a Priest holding the title of Rector (Administrator), and, under him, one or more Vicars. One of these Rectors performs the duties of Dean (Blagochinny) in the district to which his church belongs (art. 15).

1842 Jul. 17, detailed staff regulations.

23. Each male monastery has its own Superior, and each female monastery its own Mother Superior, according to the rules specified below (art. 78 et seq.). All these Superiors and Mothers Superior are subject, in the same way as the rest of the Roman Catholic clergy, to the jurisdiction and oversight of the Diocesan Heads.

1784 Apr. 17 (15982); 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) para. 5; 1832 Jul. 19 (5506) para. 12; 1842 Dec. 16, Highest command.

##### CHAPTER THREE.

On the procedure for appointing and dismissing clergy

and lay officials serving under the spiritual administration.

24. The Archbishop-Metropolitan, the Diocesan Bishops, and the Suffragan Bishops are appointed by His Imperial Majesty, upon prior agreement with His Holiness the Roman Pope, and canonical confirmation according to the accepted procedure. — His Majesty's Highest will regarding their appointment is expressed by his personal decrees to the Governing Senate.

1784 Apr. 17 (15982); 1817 Oct. 24 (27106) §§ 143, 144; 1824 May 15 (29914); 1826 Sept. 21 (593); 1832 Feb. 2 (5126); 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, art. XII.

25. After these clergy (art. 24) have taken the established oath of allegiance to His Majesty the Sovereign Emperor, Autocrat of All Russia, and to the lawful Heir to His Throne, they are permitted, upon the performance over them of the church rite, to take an oath also to the Supreme Pontiff of the Roman Church, according to the form Highest-approved for this purpose.

1784 Apr. 17 (15982) form of the oath; Fundamental State Laws, App. V.

26. In the event of the death of a Diocesan Head or his resignation from his office, the Vicar temporarily taking his place by election of the Chapter (art. 59) is likewise confirmed in this office by the Supreme Authority.

See the enactments cited under art. 24.

27. Only such clergy as have studied at the Roman Catholic Ecclesiastical Academy or the former Main Seminary and have received diplomas therefrom for ecclesiastical academic degrees are appointed as Cathedral Prelates and Canons (a). Those found worthy by the Diocesan Head are confirmed in these ranks by Highest decrees, announced by the Minister of Internal Affairs (b).

(a) 1784 Apr. 17 (15982); 1833 Jul. 1 (6296) § 83; 1842 Jan. 1 (15188) staff regulations; 1856 Jul. 16, information of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. — (b) 1817 Oct. 24 (27106) § 145; 1824 May 15 (29914); 1829 Mar. 14, Highest command; 1832 Feb. 2 (5126).

28. The appointment and dismissal of members of the Diocesan Consistory rests with the Archbishop or Bishop presiding in the diocese (art. 16). All of them are appointed, with the consent of the government, from among clergy. If the Diocesan Head deems it necessary to remove any one of them, he immediately appoints his successor, likewise with the consent of the government.

Note 1. Visitors of monasteries, who sit in the Consistories in addition to the other members, are confirmed, upon nomination and presentation by the Diocesan Heads, by the Minister of Internal Affairs.

Note 2. If, owing to illness or other valid reasons, the number of members required by law is not present in the Consistory, the Diocesan Head may invite members of the Chapter (art. 27) to sit temporarily therein, reporting this each time to the Roman Catholic Ecclesiastical Collegium and to the Minister of Internal Affairs.

1798 Apr. 28 (18504) para. 5; 1804 Sept. 27 (21467); 1817 Oct. 24 (27106) § 148; 1832 Mar. 11 (5225); 1833 Jul. 1 (6296) § 83; 1842 Dec. 16, Highest command; 1843 Jan. 19 (16464); 1845 Nov. 29, order of the Ministry of Internal Affairs; 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, art. XVII.

29. The offices of members of the Consistory cease upon the death of the Bishop, or in the event of his resignation from the episcopal rank, and also upon the termination of the administration of a vacant diocese by the Vicar (art. 26). In the event of the death of the Bishop or his resignation from the episcopal rank, his successor, or the one temporarily taking his place (a Coadjutor with right of succession [cum futura successione], or the Vicar elected by the Chapter under article 59 for the temporary administration of the diocese), immediately forms a new Consistory, always, however, as stated above, with the consent of the government.

1804 Sept. 27 (21467); 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, art. XX.

30. Secretaries of the Consistories are appointed and dismissed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs, from among persons of the Roman Catholic confession, upon the recommendation of the Diocesan Heads.

1804 Sept. 27 (21467) report; 1842 Jul. 17, Highest-approved staff regulations; 1856 Apr. 7, Highest-approved regulation of the Committee on Roman Catholic Church affairs. DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 273

31. The other officials of the Consistorial Chancery are confirmed by the local Diocesan Head, upon the recommendation of its Secretary.

1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, art. XVIII.

32. Secretaries and other officials of the Consistorial Chanceries are considered to be in state service.

1804 Sept. 27 (21467); 1846 Sept. 23 (20458).

33. Secretaries attached to the Diocesan Heads for their official and private correspondence (art. 20, para. 2) are appointed directly and immediately by the Diocesan Heads themselves, who may, at their own discretion, choose them from among clergy as well.

1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman Court, art. XIX.

34. Members of the Roman Catholic Ecclesiastical Collegium are appointed, one from among the Bishops and the other from among the Prelates. They are appointed and dismissed by Highest decrees upon the recommendation of the Collegium, submitted by the Minister of Internal Affairs. Two candidates are presented for each vacancy.

1817 Oct. 24 (27106) § 142; 1832 Feb. 2 (5126); 1833 Jul. 1 (6296) § 83.

35. The Assessors of the Collegium are elected, each in his own diocese, by the Cathedral Chapter, every three years, from among the Prelates or Canons (art. 27) (a). — The Chapters ensure that persons elected to these offices combine knowledge of canon law with a thorough command of the Russian and Polish languages and of the state statutes (b).

(a) 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) para. 2; 1839 Mar. 15 (12122) staff regulations. — (b) 1815 Jul. 20 (25903).

36. Deans are appointed at the discretion of the Diocesan Head, preferably from among persons who have completed a course of studies at least at the diocesan Seminary.

1798 Apr. 28 (18504) para. 6; 1817 Oct. 24 (27106) §§ 144-146, 148; 1833 Jul. 1 (6296) § 83; 1842 Jul. 17, detailed staff regulations.

37. Parish priests, and Superiors and Mothers Superior of monasteries in the diocese, are appointed by its local Head (art. 16), wherever the right of patronage (jus patronatus) does not exist at all or has been temporarily suspended. Parish priests are appointed by the Diocesan Head, with the consent of the government, after preliminary examination and competition among candidates, in accordance with the canonical rules. — Superiors and Mothers Superior of monasteries are appointed according to special rules specified below in their place (art. 78 et seq.) (a).

Note. Attendant positions at churches are filled by hired persons (b).

XXX; 1847 Oct. 6, order of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. — (b) 1838 Jun. 24 (11358); 1850 Jan. 11 (23817) § 5, note 3.

38. For positions of parish priests in all first- and second-class parishes, preference is given to those who have completed a course of studies at the Roman Catholic Ecclesiastical Academy.

1844 Dec. 14, Highest command.

39. The rank of Infulate (the right to wear the mitre during divine service in specified cases) is granted, upon the recommendation of the Diocesan Head, only with the Highest consent (a).

Note. All matters concerning appointment, dismissal, rewards, and penalties requiring Highest approval proceed to Highest consideration through the procedure defined above, in articles 8 and 10 (b).

(a) 1798 Nov. 3 (18734) para. 10; 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) para. 6; 1842 Jul. 17, detailed staff regulations; 1857 Jul. 10, Highest command. — (b) 1810 Aug. 17 (24326); 1856 Aug. 10 (30838).

40. Persons of the Roman Catholic clergy, upon their appointment as Rectors of a church or monastery, or as members of the Collegium, Consistory, or Academy, or to sit in civil government offices as deputies of this clergy (art. 55), take the oath of allegiance to the service before the civil authorities (Fundamental Laws, App. V).

1832 May 3 (5319); 1857 Dec. 31, information of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

##### CHAPTER FOUR.

Rights and duties of the authorities and offices of ecclesiastical administration.

Section One.

On the Archbishop-Metropolitan.

41. The Archbishop of Mogilev, possessing all the outward distinctions that, according to the rites of the Roman Church, belong to so preeminent a rank and office, enjoys also those rights that may be assigned to him not only in his own but also in the other dioceses of that Church, as its sole Metropolitan in the Russian Empire and the Grand Duchy of Finland (Art. 17).

1798 Apr. 28 (18504) pt. 8; cf. the enactments cited under Art. 17.

42. With respect to the other Diocesan Ordinaries, the Archbishop-Metropolitan acts within the limits of the spiritual authority assigned to him; in cases exceeding this authority, he applies to the Roman See and receives from that See authorizations, in the order established for that purpose (Art. 47, note).

1803 Dec. 13 (21078) pt. I, § 12, pt. 5; 1817 Oct. 24 (27106); 1824 May 15 (29914); 1832 Feb. 2 (5126); 1833 Jan. 24 (5931); cf. the enactments cited in the note to Art. 47.

43. In the administration of his own archdiocese the Archbishop-Metropolitan acts according to the general provisions concerning Diocesan Bishops set forth below, while in the consideration and decision of matters and cases common to all dioceses (Art. 11), as defined in article 67, he acts in accordance with the Statute of the Roman Catholic Ecclesiastical Collegium, over which he presides.

Cf. the enactments cited under Arts. 44–56, 60–64, and 67–74.

Section Two.

On Diocesan Bishops.

44. Ecclesiastical justice and the administration of church affairs in each diocese belong exclusively to its Bishop, without however infringing the subordination established for him (a). He therefore has, within the bounds of his diocese, supreme oversight both of the secular and monastic clergy of his confession, and of the churches, monasteries, seminaries, and in general of all ecclesiastical institutions of the same confession and their properties (b).

(a) 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) pt. 1; 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman See, Art. XIII; cf. above in this Statute, Art. 3. — (b) 1772 Dec. 14 (13922) pt. 3; 1774 Feb. 6 (14122); 1780 Jan. 9 (14966); 1782 Jan. 17 (15326) pt. 11; 1783 Nov. 14 (15876); 1784 Apr. 17 (15982); 1798 Apr. 28 (18504) pts. 10 and 11; Nov. 3 (18734) pts. 3, 11, 16, 17, and 19; 1800 Dec. 11 (19684) pts. 8, 13, and 16; 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) pt. 5; 1832 Jul. 19 (5506) pt. 12; 1843 Jun. 11 (16939); 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman See, Arts. XXI–XXVIII.

45. The Diocesan Bishop administers the ecclesiastical affairs of his diocese with the assistance of his Suffragan Bishops (Art. 57), the Cathedral Chapter, the Consistory, the Deans, the parish rectors, and the local superiors of monasteries and schools (a); but, as the chief superior of all the ecclesiastical institutions of the Roman Catholic confession in his diocese, he is answerable to the higher government for the enforcement of the rules on oversight of the acts of these immediate superiors (b).

(a) See the enactments cited under Arts. 44, 57, 58, and others. — (b) See the enactments cited under Art. 44.

46. The Diocesan Ordinary is obliged, on the basis of the canonical rules, either personally or through others, to inspect the churches and other ecclesiastical institutions in his diocese, to eliminate abuses, and to correct morals.

Cf. the enactments cited under Arts. 85–87; 1844 May 5, order of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

47. When a Diocesan Bishop, in matters relating to the dogmas of the faith and to canonical rules, finds it necessary to obtain a higher ecclesiastical authorization exceeding his canonical power, he applies for it to the Roman See, and carries out its decisions, but only in accordance with the order established for relations with the Roman See.

Note. All Christians of the Roman Catholic confession, clerical and lay, among the subjects of the state, communicate with the Roman See on matters of their confession only through the Minister of Internal Affairs, who refers the matter to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. No bulls, briefs, or instructions of the Roman See may be put into effect in the Empire, the Kingdom of Poland, or the Grand Duchy of Finland without the authorization of His Imperial Majesty, requested by the Minister of Internal Affairs after prior verification that these acts contain nothing contrary to the state enactments and to the sacred rights and prerogatives of the Supreme Autocratic Power.

1798 Apr. 28 (18504) pts. 12 and 18; 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) pt. 3; 1803 Dec. 13 (21078); 1817 Oct. 24 (27106) § 12, pt. 5; 1824 May 15 (29914); 1829 Mar. 14, Imperial order; 1830 Mar. 10 (3522); 1832 Feb. 2 (5126); 1833 Jan. 24 (5931); 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman See, Art. XIII; 1857 Jun. 4, Imperial order.

48. Appointment to all ecclesiastical positions within a diocese, for the filling of which no special rules have been established in this Digest, is left to the discretion of the Diocesan Bishop, subject to the following rules (Art. 49 et seq.).

1817 Oct. 24 (27106) § 148.

49. Only Russian subjects may be appointed by Diocesan Ordinaries to ecclesiastical positions of their confession. The appointment of foreign clergy requires the higher authorization prescribed by the Laws on the Estates; once authorized, such clergy are obliged to take an oath of faithful service and due subject's obedience.

1780 Jan. 9 (14966); 1783 Nov. 14 (15876); 1784 Feb. 28 (15943); 1789 Nov. 26 (16820); 1795 Sept. 6 (17379) pt. 6 and (17380) pt. 5; 1798 Apr. 28 (18504) pt. 7; 1820 Mar. 13 (28198); 1844 Mar. 16, Imperial order.

50. To the office of Preacher at Cathedrals only such clergy are appointed as hold an academic theological degree; the same is observed, as far as possible, in appointing Instructors of Religion in all educational institutions and in all ecclesiastical positions in the capitals.

1833 Jul. 1 (6296) § 83; 1844 Dec. 14, Imperial order.

51. In distributing parishes according to church rules, the Diocesan Bishop retains none of them for himself in his own diocese and may not hold any in other dioceses. Nor may he, under any pretext, give more than one parish to a single person.

1801 Nov. 13 (20053) pt. 6.

52. He may not transfer or accept into his diocese any clergyman of another diocese without the prior consent of the local Diocesan Ordinary and without the knowledge of the government.

1842 Dec. 16, Imperial order.

53. The Diocesan Bishop may not, on his own authority, order a general solemn prayer service throughout the diocese in memory of any deceased private person, apart from the customary sermon at burial, the requiem, and commemoration according to the church rite (a).

Note. Laypersons may not be permitted to deliver speeches at these religious rites, either inside the church or outside it (b).

(a) 1826 Dec. 4 (726). — (b) 1836 Nov. 15 (9706).

54. It is among the duties of the Diocesan Ordinary, on the basis of the Censorship Statute, to conduct the prior review of all kinds of Roman Catholic religious books, and to appoint censors for manuscript sermons (a).

Note. In general, persons of the Roman Catholic clergy are strictly forbidden, in the sermons they deliver in churches, to touch upon political matters, even in general terms, or to publish writings on political affairs, especially those relating to the internal governance of the state (b).

(a) 1828 Apr. 22 (1979) § 23; 1832 Mar. 11 (5225); 1853 Feb. 18 (27017). — (b) 1798 Nov. 3 (18734) Art. 22; 1800 Dec. 11 (19684) pt. 19; 1832 Mar. 11 (5225) pt. 5.

55. The Diocesan Ordinary appoints permanent deputies from among the clergy under his authority to sit in the secular courts of law in civil matters relating to church and monastery properties, and in criminal matters, whenever clergy of the Roman Catholic confession are implicated.

Note. Permanent deputies are appointed, from one to four in each district (uezd), in proportion to the number of churches, the extent, and the local circumstances of the district. They are appointed preferably from among the secular clergy, but where such clergy are few, deputies may also be appointed from the monastic clergy, upon the instructions of the Diocesan Ordinary to the Superiors of the monasteries. — The office of deputy may also be entrusted to a clergyman who has studied only at a seminary and not at an academy. It may not be combined with other duties that would hinder its performance, except the office of Dean. — Deputies, upon their appointment, must, pursuant to Art. 40, take an oath of faithful service. — For investigations and court proceedings, deputies are always required from the nearest places. — The dismissal, and, in case of misconduct, the removal from office, of a deputy rests with the Diocesan Ordinary.

1810 Oct. 18 (24380); 1832 May 3 (5319); 1833 Jul. 1 (6296) § 83; 1846 Nov. 4 (20581); 1847 Dec. 16 (21804).

56. The remaining rights and duties of the Diocesan Ordinary, owing to their close connection with the rules concerning the ecclesiastical institutions subordinate to him, are set forth below, each in its proper place.

Section Three.

On Suffragan Bishops and Cathedral Chapters.

57. Suffragan Bishops assist the Diocesan Ordinary, upon his instructions, in discharging the duties entrusted to him with respect to the diocese.

See the enactments cited under Art. 18.

58. The Cathedral Chapter constitutes, in accordance with the canonical statutes of the Roman Church, the Council of the Diocesan Ordinary, assists him in affairs, and celebrates solemn divine service together with him.

See the enactments cited under Art. 19.

59. In the event of the death of a Diocesan Ordinary, or of his resignation from his office, if there is no Coadjutor Bishop with right of succession, the local Chapter, on the basis of the canonical rules, within the period fixed by them, elects a Vicar to administer the vacant diocese until the appointment of a successor to the deceased or otherwise departed Ordinary.

1798 Apr. 28 (18504) pt. 5; 1832 Mar. 11 (5225); 1842 Jan. 1 (15188) establishment; 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman See, Art. XX.

Section Four.

On Consistories.

I. On the subjects of the Consistories.

60. In diocesan administration, the following judicial and administrative matters are subject to the prior review of the local Consistory:

§ 1. Matters relating to the diocesan clergy: a) Disciplinary matters in general. However, of these matters, the less important ones, which do not entail removal from office or confinement for a longer or shorter period, are decided by the Diocesan Ordinary without the prior opinion of the Consistory, unless he himself deems it necessary to refer these matters as well, like the others, to the prior review of the Consistory. b) Disputed matters between clergymen concerning movable or immovable church property. c) Complaints and suits against clergymen, brought by clerical or lay persons alike, for injuries or damages, or for non-fulfillment of undisputed obligations, in cases where the plaintiff, to protect his rights, applies to the ecclesiastical rather than the secular authority. d) Cases concerning the invalidity of monastic vows, examined and decided according to special church rules.

§ 2. Matters relating to lay persons: matrimonial cases, certifications of the legitimacy or illegitimacy of a marriage, records of birth, records of baptism, death, and so forth.

Note 1. The first instance of ecclesiastical judgment in matrimonial and other spiritual matters is constituted by the local Diocesan Bishop, or Archbishop, together with his Consistory, on the basis of Article 61; the second instance, for matters decided in the first instance by Bishops, is constituted by the Archbishop, while for those matters that were decided by the Archbishop himself together with his Consistory acting as the first instance, it is constituted by the Bishop of one of the dioceses nearest to the archdiocese, previously designated for that purpose by His Holiness the Roman Pope. If the decisions of the two first instances of this ecclesiastical court differ, as likewise in the event of appeal, complaint, or protest, the examination of matrimonial cases is referred to the Roman See (a).

Note 2. Matrimonial cases are carried from the first instance to the second without any appeal. If the second instance renders a decision consistent with that of the first instance, and both parties are satisfied with it, the case is considered finally decided (b).

§ 3. Mixed matters: cases in which church penance is to be imposed for some crime or offense, after the case concerning it has been decided in the secular courts.

§ 4. Matters of an economic nature: the schedule or estimate of sums allotted for the maintenance of the clergy, the verification of expenditures and accounts relating to these sums, matters concerning the repair or construction of new churches, chapels, and so forth.

Note. In addition, the Consistory is obliged to draw up lists of the clergy and parishioners of its diocese, and to circulate circulars and other announcements that do not relate to the administrative affairs of the diocese (v).

(a) 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman See, Art. XIV; 1848 Nov. 29, special agreement with the same See. — (b) 1798 Jun. 22 (18560). — (v) 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman See, Art. XIV.

61. The above-named matters (Art. 60) are decided by the Bishop after their examination in the Consistory. The voice of the Consistory is, however, merely advisory. The Bishop is not obliged to explain the grounds of his decisions even where his opinion should not accord with the conclusion of the Consistory.

1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman See, Art. XV.

62. The remaining matters of the diocese, which are called administrative and which include matters of conscience (casus conscientiae, fori interni), as well as, as stated above (Art. 60, § I, pt. a), those disciplinary matters that entail only minor corrective penalties or pastoral admonitions, depend exclusively on the authority of the Diocesan Ordinary and are decided at his own discretion.

*Ibid., Art. XVI.*

63. In disciplinary matters, appeals to the Roman Catholic Ecclesiastical Collegium are permitted against decisions ordering removal from office and, in general, any significant penalty (Art. 60, § 1, pt. a); but those sentenced to such punishment in the diocese may not leave their place of residence without the permission of the authorities.

1798 Jun. 22 (18560); 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) pt. 4.

64. Criminal cases and civil cases, other than those indicated above, are not subject to diocesan jurisdiction: their investigation and trial are conducted according to the general rules of the secular courts, with the participation only of deputies of the clergy (a).

Note. If a clergyman is accused of violating the prohibitions specified in Articles 4 or 5, he is likewise subject to the general criminal court (b).

(a) 1798 Nov. 3 (18734) pt. 4; 1800 Dec. 11 (19684) Art. 4; 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) Arts. 1, 8; 1806 Dec. 13 (22395); 1807 May 15 (22528); 1810 Oct. 18 (24380). — (b) 1840 Jan. 27 (13116).

II. On the conduct of cases in the Consistories.

65. The order of conducting, deciding, and executing cases in the Consistories, the accounting of matters and sums, and the duties and responsibilities of those serving therein are determined by the general rules established for the civil service and by a special instruction of the Minister of Internal Affairs.

1804 Sept. 27 (21467); 1856 Apr. 7, Imperially confirmed resolution of the Committee on the Affairs of the Roman Catholic Church.

66. In cases of particular importance, such as: the delivery to the proper parties of ecclesiastical orders accompanying Imperial manifestos or decrees for publication and reading in the churches, likewise the forms for the commemoration of the Imperial family at the litanies, tables and additions to these forms, transmission is made through the rural post, by means of the District Courts (Zemsky Sud), the Stanovoi Pristavs (district police officers), and the sotskys (village constables).

1826 Nov. 24 (694); 1837 Jun. 3 (10306) §§ 4–6; Jun. 3 (10307) § 8.

Section Five.

On the Roman Catholic Ecclesiastical Collegium.

I. On the subjects of the Collegium.

67. In the Roman Catholic Ecclesiastical Collegium are concentrated, for the entire administration of the Roman Catholic clergy, the following matters:

1) Complete records of all Roman Catholic churches, monasteries, clergy, educational and other ecclesiastical institutions, and movable and immovable properties (a).

2) Supervision of the proper and successful conduct of business in the Diocesan Consistories, review of their decisions, and measures of correction upon appeals, complaints, and private grievances or protests, except in matrimonial and other spiritual matters (b).

3) Examination and submission to the higher government of all kinds of proposals of the diocesan authorities relating to the general good of the state together with that of the church (v).

4) Matters concerning the admission of those wishing to enter the monastic state (g) <...>.

5) Management of the auxiliary fund of the Roman Catholic clergy in the Empire, according to special rules on this subject (e); likewise management of a special repair fund allocated for the construction and repair of churches, and the use of only its interest for these purposes, at the Collegium's own discretion, as loans or as non-returnable grants (zh).

6) Audit of the accounts of the auxiliary and repair funds (pt. 5), and audit of the accounts of the use of all sums disbursed for the maintenance of the Roman Catholic clergy from the state treasury. Both audits are conducted in accordance with the rules established in the General Accounting Statute and in the Accounting Statute of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, under the special supervision of that Ministry (z).

(a) 1798 Nov. 3 (18734) pt. 16; 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) pt. 8; 1817 Feb. 5 (26660). — (b) 1798 Jun. 22 (18560); Nov. 3 (18734) pt. 2; 1800 Dec. 11 (19684) pt. 2; 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) pt. 4; 1829 Mar. 27 (2773); 1847 Jul. 22, treaty with the Roman See, Art. XIV. — (v) 1800 Dec. 11 (19684) pt. 23; 1817 Oct. 24 (27106) § 132; 1832 Feb. 2 (5126). — (g) 1829 Mar. 27 (2773) pt. 4; 1842 Nov. 17 (16222a). <...> — (e) See below, Arts. 129–133. — (zh) 1847 Jul. 27, Imperial order. — (z) General Accounting Statute, introduction, Art. 3; Accounting Statute of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, Arts. 79–92; 1842 Jan. 28 (15251a); 1844 Oct. 23, Imperial order.

II. On the order of conducting, deciding, and executing the affairs of the Collegium.

68. The Collegium meets in session three times a week, on the days appointed for that purpose, and in summer, from June 15 to August 15, only once a week.

1844 Apr. 29, Imperial order; 1852 Feb. 25 (26023).

69. All matters of the Collegium are conducted according to the general provisions concerning collegial institutions, and are decided in its session by a majority of votes, according to church rules. In the event of a tie, the side is preferred with which the presiding Archbishop-Metropolitan agrees (Art. 21).

1801 Nov. 13 (20053) intro. and pt. 8.

70. Matters coming before the Collegium under Article 67, pt. 2, from the Mogilev archdiocese (Art. 12), if they were decided personally by the Archbishop-Metropolitan, as Diocesan Ordinary (Art. 43), before being submitted to the Collegium, are decided in the Collegium without his presence.

1801 Nov. 13 (20053); 1803 Oct. 26 (21010).

71. Matters requiring higher authorization, or the consideration and resolution of other state authorities and offices, are submitted by the Collegium to the Minister of Internal Affairs, who gives these matters their proper course, appending to each his own conclusion. Excepted from this are judicial matters: in these the Collegium applies directly to the Governing Senate and to the Minister of Justice.

1817 Oct. 24 (27106) §§ 131, 132; 1832 Feb. 2 (5126).

72. In the event of disagreement with a decision of the Collegium, the Minister of Internal Affairs presents to it his opinion. If the Collegium finds any inconveniences in carrying out this opinion, it reports them to the Minister, and thereafter proceeds according to his resolution.

1817 Oct. 24 (27106) § 133; 1832 Feb. 2 (5126).

73. The Procurator attached to the Collegium is obliged to submit to the Minister of Internal Affairs memoranda and reports on matters decided in the administrative sphere, and is answerable to the Minister for their prompt and proper delivery and for oversight in this regard. If the Procurator observes anything to the contrary and the Collegium does not accept his proposal, he submits his protest to the Minister (a).

Note. During the period from June 15 to August 15, when the Collegium sits only once a week (Art. 68), the Procurator has the right to open packets addressed to it that arrive on non-session days and to forward them to the Chancery for preparation for report to the session of the Collegium (b).

(a) 1817 Oct. 24 (27106) § 131; 1832 Feb. 2 (5126). — (b) 1844 Apr. 29, Imperial order.

74. The Collegium communicates with the Governing Senate by reports and receives decrees from it, and with the Ministers of Internal Affairs and Justice by representations and receives proposals from them (a); it sends decrees to the Diocesan Ordinaries and Consistories and in general to the offices and persons subordinate to it, and receives from them representations and reports (b); with the provincial establishments it communicates by official communications (v).

(a) 1803 Oct. 26 (21010); 1817 Oct. 24 (27106) § 133; 1832 Feb. 2 (5126); cf. 1845 Jan. 2 (18580) Arts. 176–180. — (b) 1801 Nov. 13 (20053) pt. 1. — (v) Cf. 1845 Jan. 2 (18580) Art. 180.

Section Six.
