268. Divorced spouses may again enter into lawful marriage with one another, but must be published anew and married anew.

*Ibid., § 135.*

##### CHAPTER FIVE.

On Preachers and the Church Clergy.

Section One.

On Candidates for the Clergy.

269. A person wishing to become a candidate for the clergy of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Russia must complete, at one of the Russian Universities, the full course of theological sciences required by regulation for the clergy of this Church, and, upon leaving the University, be examined, first by the Faculty of Theology, and thereafter, on the basis of the provisions set forth in this chapter, twice by one of the Evangelical Lutheran Consistories: at the first of these examinations, the candidate is examined in order to obtain the right to preach (pro venia concionandi); at the second, in order to acquire the right to be appointed Preacher of some parish (pro ministerio).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 136.

270. A person wishing to obtain permission to preach (veniam concionandi) must, within the first year after completing his course of study at the University, apply with a written petition to the Consistory of the district in which he intends to exercise this right; if he presents himself later, he must explain what circumstances caused this delay.

*Ibid., § 137.*

271. The following certificates must be attached to the petition for admission to the examination for the right to preach: 1) of baptism; 2) of confirmation; 3) from the University, of diligent attendance at theological lectures throughout the full course of study prescribed by regulation, of moral conduct throughout the entire University course, and of having passed the examination in the Faculty of Theology; and 4) from the Professor of Russian Literature, of sufficient knowledge of the Russian language. In addition, the person requesting examination must present a brief account of the events of his life (curriculum vitae), indicating in it the whole course of his intellectual, moral, and especially religious upbringing.

Note. Persons who were formerly of taxable status must, in addition, present certificates of their exemption from it. Those who left the University more than three years before must also present a certificate of their conduct from the Provost, or Superintendent, of the district in which they resided, and, if they were private tutors or held some other position, a certificate from the proper offices or persons.

*Ibid., § 138.*

272. If the University certificate of the knowledge of the person presenting himself as a candidate is not entirely satisfactory, or if the candidate has not completed the full course of study at the University in the established order, then he must be refused the examination, and he may not be admitted to it DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 311

until he has fulfilled all the above-mentioned necessary conditions for this, and has presented sufficient certificates to that effect.

*Ibid., § 139.*

273. If the candidate admitted to the examination is found capable, he receives from the Consistory permission to preach. The certificate issued to this effect states that the candidate demonstrated at the examination knowledge that was excellent, or good, or merely sufficient (egregie, bene, satis bene).

*Ibid., § 140.*

274. A candidate who has received a certificate granting permission to preach (venia concionandi) may be admitted by any Evangelical Lutheran Pastor to preach in his church, and in this respect the certificate of each Consistory has equal force in all Consistorial districts.

*Ibid., § 141.*

275. Every candidate who has received permission to preach is obliged to present in person the certificate he has received to the Provost, or, where there is no Provost, to the Superintendent, or General Superintendent, of the district in which he resides, and to endeavor to make himself sufficiently known to him in every respect; in the event of a change of residence, he must notify him of this, and enter into the same relations with the Provost, Superintendent, or General Superintendent of the district to which he belongs by his new place of residence. He is also obliged, until his appointment as Pastor, to submit annually to the Provost, Superintendent, or General Superintendent, one dissertation, composed according to his guidance and instruction, on some theological subject in Latin, and one sermon in the language in which he intends to preach.

*Ibid., § 142.*

276. A candidate who, at the first examination before the Consistory (pro venia concionandi), does not receive a certificate that he demonstrated excellent knowledge, may not be admitted to the second examination (pro ministerio) until a year has elapsed.

*Ibid., § 143.*

277. A person presenting himself for examination to obtain the right to be appointed Preacher is obliged to present a certificate issued by the Provost, or Provosts, of the districts in which he has resided since his first examination before the Consistory; and if there are no Provosts in those districts, and the residence of the Superintendent or General Superintendent is very remote, then a certificate from one of the nearest Preachers. This certificate must be composed not in general or negative terms, but must indicate with precision the moral conduct of the candidate and his diligence in pursuits befitting his calling.

*Ibid., § 144.*

278. Upon the conclusion of the second examination before the Consistory (pro ministerio), the Consistory likewise states in the certificate it issues that the candidate demonstrated at it knowledge that was excellent, or good, or only sufficient.

*Ibid., § 145.*

279. This second examination before the Consistory (pro ministerio) gives the candidate the right to be elected and called as Preacher of some parish within the district of that Consistory. Candidates retain this right only for a fixed period: those who demonstrated excellent knowledge, for three years, and those who demonstrated good knowledge, for two years, while those whose knowledge is found to be merely sufficient, for not more than one year. He who wishes to be appointed Preacher in the district of another Consistory is examined at a full session thereof by means of a theological colloquy (colloquium); in addition, he is obliged to present the written dissertations composed for the examinations pro venia concionandi and pro ministerio. After this colloquy he is issued a certificate, likewise indicating the degree of knowledge he has demonstrated.

*Ibid., § 146.*

280. If a candidate is called as Preacher even within the district of the Consistory before which he was examined, but after the expiration of the period specified in article 279, then, in order to obtain confirmation, he must likewise be examined anew at a theological colloquy; he is not, however, obliged to present new written dissertations.

*Ibid., § 147.*

281. No candidate for the clergy may be appointed, called, elected, or confirmed to the position of Preacher or Adjunct unless, after the second examination before the Consistory (pro ministerio), he was declared worthy to occupy such a position (a). After the examination, the candidate is appointed for one year as Assistant to a Pastor chosen for this purpose by the Consistory (art. 767, note); the Consistory, if the candidate's teaching is found not to be in accord with the rules of the Evangelical Lutheran confession, has the right to extend the period of probation (b). Those candidates who, at the first examination in the Consistory (pro venia concionandi), do not receive a mark that they demonstrated excellent knowledge (egregie), are admitted to the practical year of probation not only after passing both examinations (pro venia concionandi and pro ministerio), but immediately upon the conclusion of the first examination (c).

(a) Ibid., § 148. — (b) 1843 Apr. 2, Imperial Order. — (c) 1856 Oct. 23 (31044).

282. Professors of theological sciences at the University of Dorpat and the Alexander University of Helsingfors may preach without special certificates from the Consistories pro venia concionandi; but in order to obtain the right to occupy the position of Preacher, they are likewise invited to a theological colloquy in a full session of the proper Consistory (colloquium).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 149.

283. Students of theology of the University of Dorpat and the Alexander University of Helsingfors are permitted, during the last year of their course of study at the University, for the purpose of examination and the acquisition of proper skill, to preach before some parish, provided, however, that the draft of the sermon is each time submitted beforehand for review by the parish Preacher and approved by him.

*Ibid., § 150. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 313*

284. Foreigners in Russia may obtain permission to preach and occupy the positions of Pastors only by order of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, on the basis of the rules established for this purpose, and upon presentation of a certificate of their having accepted Russian citizenship.

*Ibid., § 151; 1842 May 19 (15658).*

Section Two.

On Preachers.

I. On the vacating and filling of preaching vacancies.

285. In order to take up the position of Preacher, the person wishing to occupy it must, first, at the examinations prescribed in the first section of this chapter, be found worthy of it not only by his talents and knowledge, but also by his blameless morality and Christian sentiments; second, in accordance with the laws and customs, be elected or called to this position, and thereafter be confirmed and, in the established order, ordained and inducted into office.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 152.

286. The office of Preacher is entrusted to candidates only after they reach the age of twenty-five. Exceptions to this rule are permitted only in special cases, with the authorization of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

*Ibid., § 153.*

287. When a Preacher's vacancy opens as a result of the death of the Pastor who occupied it, the Church Elders and relatives of the deceased are obliged to notify the Provost immediately, or, where there are no Provosts, the Superintendent, or General Superintendent, who reports to the Consistory, and the Consistory to the Ministry of Internal Affairs through the General Consistory.

*Ibid., § 154.*

288. When the position of Preacher of some parish remains unfilled, the Provost sees to it that divine services and all the spiritual needs of the parishioners are conducted by a Vicar appointed by the Consistory, or by all the Preachers of the district in turn, and reports to the Consistory on his arrangements to this effect. Where parishes are not divided into separate Provostal districts, the Consistory places the duty of performing the spiritual services of the parish left without a Pastor upon the Preachers nearest to it, or appoints a temporary Preacher to it.

*Ibid., § 155.*

289. Vacated positions must ordinarily, within four months, or at least not later than within half a year, be filled by other Preachers. If those to whom the right of appointing a Pastor to the vacancy belongs do not exercise it within this period, then the Consistory, at its own discretion, gives them a new, short period, and if they still do not appoint a candidate within this time, it enters, for this occasion only, into their rights and appoints a Preacher of its own choosing.

*Ibid., § 156.*

290. The order for appointing Preachers to vacated positions remains, in each parish, the same as existed before December 28, 1832.

*Ibid., § 157.*

291. In those parishes in which the right of appointing a Preacher belongs directly to the Crown, the Pastor is appointed by His Imperial Majesty upon the recommendation of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. If the Ministry does not have in view a worthy candidate who could occupy the vacant position, it first requests from the Consistory a list of the worthiest candidates who have already passed the examination for the right to occupy Preacher's positions (pro ministerio).

*Ibid., § 158.*

292. In those parishes in which the Crown enjoys only the right to confirm the Preacher, while the election is left to the parish itself, or to part thereof, the person elected is presented to the Consistory, and by it, together with a statement of opinion on the candidate, submitted for confirmation to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

Note 1. In the Baltic governorates the Consistory reports the election to the Governor, who communicates it, with his opinion, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, for confirmation.

Note 2. When it becomes necessary to appoint a Preacher for the foreign settlers of Saratov or of the southern region of the Empire, an invitational charter summoning him is drawn up in the Consistory and forwarded to the colonial administration for announcement to the parishioners at a communal assembly. If all, or the greater part, agree to the terms of the charter, the charter is then returned by the local administration to the Consistory, for execution; but if, at the communal assembly, the parishioners do not voluntarily express their consent to the conditions proposed to them, then under no circumstances is the charter carried into effect.

*Ibid., § 159; 1821 Dec. 31 (28857).*

293. For those Preacher's positions dependent on the Crown, in filling which the Consistories, before December 28, 1832, enjoyed the right of electing Preachers, they are obliged each time to submit the candidates they have elected for confirmation by the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

Note. Consistories are obliged, in their recommendations for Preachers' positions, to give preference to those candidates who at the examination demonstrated excellent, or at least good, knowledge.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 160.

294. In those places where the parishioners themselves, or a patron, or several patrons, have the right to call and appoint a Preacher, the elected person is presented to the Consistory with a request for his induction into office; the Consistory may not refuse, if there is no lawful impediment to it. Of the appointment of these Preachers the Consistory reports each time to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and to the General Consistory, for information.

*Ibid., § 161.*

295. At every election of a Preacher, the Provost, or a member of the Consistory, or a person authorized by it, must be present, and must see to it that the election proceeds in the established order.

*Ibid., § 162. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 315*

296. That candidate is deemed elected for whom the greatest number of votes is cast; if the votes are divided equally among several candidates, then the senior of those enjoying patronal rights (der Patron unter den Compatronen), and, where there are none, the Consistory, chooses one of these candidates as Preacher at its own discretion.

*Ibid., § 163.*

297. No Preacher may be appointed against the wishes of the parishioners, when they have reasons worthy of respect for expressing this; to this end it is observed that in all those parishes which do not enjoy the right of electing their own Pastors, with the exception only of those very remote from the seat of the Consistory, the Preacher to be appointed must deliver a sermon, before his appointment, in the presence of the parish to which he has been called. If the parishioners have any lawful reasons for not wishing this Preacher to be their Pastor, they must, within the first two weeks thereafter, present them to the Consistory through the Provost, Church Wardens, or Elders, and the Consistory is obliged, according to the circumstances, to make the necessary arrangements as a result, and to report on this to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and to the General Consistory.

*Ibid., § 164.*

298. If the patron or patrons who elected the candidate consider the Consistory's refusal to induct him into office a violation of their rights, they may bring a complaint on this matter to the General Consistory.

*Ibid., § 165.*

299. The same procedure is observed also in the case where a candidate considers himself entitled to complain of some decision of the Consistory concerning his appointment as Pastor.

*Ibid., § 166.*

300. When a Preacher wishes to be transferred to another parish, or to leave his position, or to lay down the title of Preacher altogether, he must first request and await the permission of the Consistory for this. In doing so, he must present to it proper proof that all the duties of his office have been precisely fulfilled by him.

Note. In the transfer of a Preacher, attention is given not only to his abilities and knowledge, but also to his previous service.

*Ibid., § 167.*

301. If a Preacher is compelled, by reason of old age, infirmity, or illness, to lay down his position, his successor is obliged to allot for his maintenance a third of all the Pastoral income. However, in place of this, they may conclude between themselves some special agreement, with the confirmation of the Consistory, which sees to it that agreements of this kind are drawn up in the most precise, definite terms.

*Ibid., § 168.*

302. A Preacher may, with the permission of the Consistory, take to himself as an Assistant, for the instruction of the parishioners, a candidate for the clergy who has received the right to preach (veniam concionandi), provided no displeasure of the parishioners has been expressed against this choice for any reasons worthy of respect, but he must not entrust to him the performance of those sacred rites which are reserved to properly ordained Preachers.

*Ibid., § 169.*

303. If a Preacher, being unable, by reason of illness, infirmity, or old age, to perform his office properly himself, wishes to have, for all his official affairs, a permanent Assistant with the title of Adjunct, he must, having first obtained the consent of his parish to the appointment of the candidate chosen by him, request the Consistory to confirm this. Upon the Consistory's consent and by its arrangement, the candidate, if he has not yet been ordained, receives proper ordination, and thereafter, on a Sunday or feast day, the Preacher, addressing him in a solemn speech, presents him before the altar to the assembled parish.

Note. When a salary from the treasury is attached to the position of Adjunct, the Consistory shall submit its confirmation to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

*Ibid., § 170.*

304. The Consistory may, for well-founded reasons, refuse to confirm a Helper or Adjunct elected by the Preacher and approved by the parish; those dissatisfied may appeal to the General Consistory on the general basis.

*Ibid., § 171.*

305. If a Preacher is afflicted with a prolonged illness and has no Adjunct, then the Probst, or, where there is no Probst, the Consistory, shall make the necessary arrangements so that during this illness the duties of the Pastor are properly discharged. If, upon the physician's certification, recovery of the patient cannot be expected, or if the illness has already lasted more than a year, or finally if the Preacher, owing to infirmity or old age, is generally unable to perform all the duties of his calling, then the Consistory, after due investigation of all these circumstances and with the consent of the parish, shall appoint an Adjunct to him.

*Ibid., § 172.*

306. Upon the appointment of an Adjunct, an amicable agreement must be concluded each time between him and the Preacher concerning the share of parish income due to the former. This agreement is confirmed by the Consistory, which likewise resolves any misunderstandings that may arise from it.

*Ibid., § 173.*

307. Appointment as Adjunct confers no right whatsoever to the position of Chief Preacher (Pastor Ordinarius) when it becomes vacant, and in appointing to that position all the rules prescribed above concerning the order of filling Pastoral vacancies shall be observed.

*Ibid., § 174.*

II. On the ordination of Preachers and their induction into office.

308. A candidate is ordained as Preacher upon his confirmation in that rank. This rite is performed by the Super-Intendent, or the General Super-Intendent, or, in case of his illness or absence, by another clergyman appointed by the Consistory, and, when possible, on a Sunday or feast day, after the sermon, with the participation of several other Preachers in the performance of this rite. The newly ordained Preacher receives a certificate of his ordination. The officiant is obliged, when reporting thereon to the Consistory, to submit the oath sheet signed by the newly ordained Preacher after he has taken the oath at his ordination.

*Ibid., § 175.*

309. Candidates who have not yet received a call to any Pastoral or Adjunct position may not be ordained as Preachers.

*Ibid., § 176.*

310. Preachers moving from one place to another, as well as those who, having relinquished their office, re-enter it, are obliged, unless distance or other legitimate reasons prevent it, to submit themselves to a certain examination by means of a theological interview (colloquium) with the General Super-Intendent or Super-Intendent of the Consistorial district. However, Preachers who have relinquished their office and are returning to it do not undergo a new ordination.

*Ibid., § 177.*

311. After ordination the Preacher is solemnly inducted into office; the same is observed when a Preacher is transferred from one parish to another. Induction into office is performed, in the presence of the assembled parishioners and Church Elders or Trustees, by the General Super-Intendent, Super-Intendent, or Probst, assisted, when possible, by two other clergymen, on a Sunday or feast day, before the sermon, which is thereupon delivered by the one inducted into office. On this occasion the Preacher is handed the charter confirming him in office (constitutorium), issued by the Consistory. When, owing to distance, the induction into office cannot be performed by the General Super-Intendent, Super-Intendent, Probst, or another clergyman appointed for this by the Consistory, then the Preacher is solemnly inducted into the church by the Elders or Trustees; they likewise hand him the charter (constitutorium), and after delivering the sermon he himself enters upon the office.

Note. The parish must be notified of the induction of the Preacher into office in good time, at least one or two weeks before the performance of this rite.

*Ibid., § 178.*

312. Both the ordination of a Preacher and his induction into office are performed in the Evangelical Lutheran Church on the basis of the rules set forth in the Agenda (Art. 140).

*Ibid., § 179.*

313. After the induction into office, those who performed this rite hand over to the new Preacher the church books, the parish register, and the portion of church property kept by the Preacher; they submit a general report thereon to the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 180.*

III. On the duties of Preachers.

314. Preachers are obliged to discharge their important office with the utmost diligence and precision (mit Gewissenhaftigkeit und Treue), striving unceasingly toward the great goal appointed to them, the spread of the Kingdom of God on earth, endeavoring in every case to confirm their parishioners in the truths of Christian doctrine, edifying and encouraging them toward a pious, modest, and honest life, not only by exhortation but also by their own example, and in particular not permitting themselves to express or disseminate opinions in any way inconsistent with the teaching of their Church. They must carefully avoid everything that might give occasion to accuse them of idleness, frivolity, or intemperance (Schwelgerei), and, devoting the principal part of their free time to the extension of their knowledge of Holy Scripture and theological sciences, they must not lose sight of the dignity and sanctity of their calling even during hours of rest, and must ensure that their conduct, both in large gatherings and in friendly conversation, contains nothing scandalous or unseemly.

*Ibid., § 181.*

315. Preachers must observe strict order in their family life and in the management of their household, raising their children in the principles of true piety, encouraging all members of their household to the exact performance of Christian duties, serving in this respect, as in all others, as an example for their parishioners.

*Ibid., § 182.*

316. Preachers must, both by teaching and by example, impress upon their parishioners how important and pleasing to God are works of Christian charity, among which the care of the sick holds a foremost place.

*Ibid., § 183.*

317. Preachers are obliged to visit the sick of their parishes and to endeavor to edify and comfort them through the power of the Word of God. If they are called to the bedside of a sufferer, they may refuse only in the case where other and more important duties of office prevent it. In visiting the sick, they must not neglect the opportunities afforded them to instruct and comfort the household and relatives of the patient, to remind them of their duty to care for him, and to impress upon them that, being mindful of their own mortality, they should be ready for death at all times.

*Ibid., § 184.*

318. Preachers must in particular endeavor to exhort and admonish patients whom they know to have led a godless or dissolute life. When a sick person, feeling the weight of his sins, expresses repentance, the Preacher, at his wish, administers the Holy Sacrament to him. If, on the contrary, he does not repent and persists in his errors of godlessness until his very death, the Pastor may, in this instance, nevertheless with due caution and with expressions of Christian humility and forbearance, say a few words of admonition and edification to the parishioners, or at least to the relatives and friends of the deceased.

*Ibid., § 185. DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 319*

319. During the spread of contagious diseases, as well as in every other public danger, Preachers must not abandon their parishes or refuse the duty of visiting the sick and administering the Holy Sacrament to them. In such cases, when circumstances strongly affect people's minds and hearts, Preachers must endeavor to draw the special attention of their parishioners to Divine warnings and trials.

*Ibid., § 186.*

320. Preachers are obliged, at the request of the authorities, to visit prisoners of the Evangelical Protestant confession. A Preacher may not refuse to visit a prisoner and administer the Holy Sacrament to him, if the latter requests it; for this, only the permission of the authority under whose jurisdiction the prisoner is held is required. Upon receiving such permission, the Preacher is obliged to visit prisoners of the Evangelical Lutheran confession even without invitation, instructing and comforting them with the words of Holy Scripture.

*Ibid., § 187.*

321. The Preacher is obliged, in particular, to care for the poor of his parish. He must, as far as possible, provide for them and render them assistance, while nonetheless exercising due caution in issuing certificates of poverty.

*Ibid., § 188.*

322. Preachers must diligently visit rural schools and oversee the religious education of youth, both in the schools and generally in their parishes. Where the custom exists, or may be introduced, of visiting parishioners in their homes to examine them in their knowledge of the Law of God, they are obliged to employ this most useful means precisely and as often as possible for the enlightenment and moral improvement of the flock entrusted to them (a).

Note. For the clergy of the Saratov colonies of foreign settlers, detailed instructions concerning school and catechetical instruction (Kinderlehre und Katechisation) are contained in the Statute on Colonies (b).

(a) Ibid., [§] 189. — (b) 1840 March 5 (13233).

323. Preachers who have among their parishioners persons married to Jews or Mohammedans are obliged to see to it that these persons, as well as their children of both sexes baptized in the Evangelical Lutheran faith, diligently attend church, and that the latter, upon reaching the appropriate age, be confirmed and receive the Holy Sacrament.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 190.

324. Preachers are obliged in all cases to show respect and obedience to their superiors, and goodwill and readiness to be of service to their fellow clergy and parishioners, endeavoring to preserve peace and harmony with everyone, avoiding any occasion for discord and dispute.

*Ibid., § 191.*

325. Preachers must strictly observe the established order for the conduct of business and must not permit themselves to bypass their immediate superior and appeal to a higher one, except in those cases where this is expressly permitted by law.

*Ibid., § 192.*

326. Preachers holding office may not accept any position incompatible with their rank, nor engage in trade, crafts, or other pursuits inconsistent with their spiritual occupation or diverting them from the performance of their Pastoral duties.

*Ibid., § 193.*

327. Preachers may not engage in litigation or other judicial matters not concerning themselves or their family.

*Ibid., § 194.*

328. Preachers may accept the duties of guardians and trustees only with the permission of the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 195.*

329. In all matters pertaining to their office, Preachers are subject to the spiritual authorities alone; but when a secular public office requires them to perform some spiritual act, such as the admonition of a hardened criminal, the swearing-in of witnesses, and the like, they are obliged to perform this without delay, though not to the neglect of public worship and the performance of spiritual duties that cannot be postponed.

*Ibid., § 196.*

330. Preachers may not, without the permission of the Consistory, be absent from their parishes for more than a week. If a Preacher foresees that he must be absent for a single Sunday, he is obliged to notify his Probst and parish in good time and to arrange, if possible, for the sermon on that Sunday to be delivered by another Preacher or candidate, or, where there is no candidate in the parish, to be read from the lectern by the sexton (Küster).

*Ibid., § 197.*

331. Preachers are to submit petitions for leave through the Probst, or through the Super-Intendent or General Super-Intendent, to the Consistory, which has the right to grant them leave, but not for more than twenty-eight days. If a Preacher requests leave for a longer period, the Consistory shall submit the matter to the Ministry of Internal Affairs (a).

Note. The rule established specifically for civil officials, prohibiting leave of more than four months, cannot be consistently applied to persons of the clergy (b).

(a) Ibid., § 198. — (b) 1836 May 19 (9182).

332. In requesting leave for himself, a Preacher is obliged to take measures so that during his absence his office is properly discharged, and each time he must report this in advance to his Probst, or to the Super-Intendent, or General Super-Intendent.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 199.

333. No Preacher may perform sacred rites in the parish of another Preacher without written invitation, or at least without the expressed consent of the latter.

*Ibid., § 200. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 321*

334. Exceptions to this rule are permitted only in the case where one of the parishioners, owing to his own circumstances and upon the recommendation of the Consistory, has received from the Ministry of Internal Affairs permission to have a private Preacher for himself and his family. If this Preacher has been ordained according to the established order, he may perform all sacred rites in the house to which he is appointed; but as to what is to be entered in the church books, he must each time communicate this to the parish Preacher for that purpose.

*Ibid., § 201.*

335. If several churches are under the charge of a Preacher, he must, in performing divine services in them, strictly follow the provisions made at the founding of each church (Fundation). If there are no precise provisions on this matter, or if it proves necessary to amend them, the Preacher shall not proceed to do so except upon obtaining the consent of the parish and the authorization of the Ministry of Internal Affairs through the local and General Consistories.

*Ibid., § 202.*

336. When two Preachers are appointed to one and the same parish, with the titles of Senior (Pastor Primarius, Ober-Pastor) and Deacon (Pastor Secundarius, Comminister, Diaconus), or even without this distinction in titles, the charter of call issued to them shall precisely set forth their duties and their mutual official relations. Disputes arising between them are subject to the consideration of the Consistory. In general, the Deacon is charged with the singing of the collects before the altar and the performance of other similar liturgical rites; but in the event of a special invitation from the Chief Preacher, or of the latter's illness, absence, or other circumstances preventing him from performing his own duties, the Deacon is also charged with the performance of the other sacred rites and sacraments, as well as the delivery of sermons.

*Ibid., § 203.*

337. Every Preacher must, according to the rules and forms established in the Digest of Laws on the Estates, keep exact records of all those born, baptized, confirmed, communicated, betrothed, published (banns), married, and buried in his parish, noting in these records each such sacred act immediately upon its performance, and in such a manner that it may be seen from them where and by which Preacher each spiritual act was performed.

*Ibid., §§ 204, 209, 215; see the Digest of Laws on the Estates, Book II, Section I, Ch. 1.*

338. The Preacher must annually (in the colonies of foreigners, semi-annually) submit to the Consistory copies, certified by him, of the registers of those born, baptized, married, and buried during the year.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 210; see the Statute on Colonies.

339. The Preacher, on the basis of these registers, is obliged, at the request of the authorities and upon the petition of private persons, to furnish information about every spiritual rite performed by him, or by his predecessors, and to issue lawful (urkundliche) certificates thereof.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § [2]11.

340. These certificates must contain an exact, word-for-word extract from the church register, must be signed sub fide Pastorali by the Preacher, and confirmed with the church seal.

*Ibid., § 212.*

341. In addition to the registers mentioned in Article 337, every Preacher must keep one general list of all his parishioners (Personalbuch), according to the rules and form likewise set forth in the Digest of Laws on the Estates.

*Ibid., §§ 213, 214; see the Digest of Laws on the Estates, Book II, Section I, Ch. 1.*

342. The original registers are kept in the form of books in the church archive.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 215.

343. Preachers are obliged to issue, to those wishing to move to another parish, the appropriate certificate for this purpose (Parochialschein), on plain paper, without any charge whatsoever. No Preacher may accept a new member into his parish from another parish without the presentation of such a certificate.

Note. Foreigners not yet belonging to any Evangelical Lutheran parish in Russia and having no other proof of their confession are obliged to give the Preacher a sworn statement (an Eides-Statt) that they belong to the Evangelical Protestant confession.

*Ibid., § 216.*

344. These certificates (Art. 343) must indicate: 1) the name, surname, rank or trade, place and date of birth of the person presenting it; 2) when and from where he/she entered the parish, and whether he/she has always professed the Evangelical Protestant faith; 3) where he/she intends to move; 4) whether he/she has been confirmed and received the Holy Sacrament, or not yet, and, in the former case, when and where he/she was last admitted to Holy Communion; 5) whether single (unmarried) or betrothed, and to whom, or in lawful matrimony, and to whom, where and when the marriage ceremony was performed, or else widowed, or divorced. Everything indicated in these certificates must be based either on the church registers of the parish, or on a certificate received from the presenter upon his entry into the parish. If certain points are based only on the verbal statements of the presenter, this must be expressly noted. Certificates must be confirmed sub fide Pastorali by the Preacher and signed by him with an indication of place, year, and date. Parish certificates are kept in the church archive and are issued in the original only at the request of the appropriate public offices; in such a case, certified copies remain in the church archive.

*Ibid., § 217.*

345. Every parish Preacher is obliged to compile a so-called chronicle of the church and parish, recording in it all events, for whatever reason noteworthy, relating to the condition of the church and his flock.

*Ibid., § 218.*

346. Evangelical Lutheran Preachers wear a special official vestment, of an established form, when performing sacred rites and on all solemn occasions.

Note. Candidates of the clergy wear the same vestment both at their ordination and while preaching from the pulpit.

*Ibid., § 219. DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 323*

347. The official vestment of Evangelical Lutheran Preachers consists of: a wide talar of black woolen or silk material, made in the manner of the ancient priestly or choir vestment (Priester- oder Chor-Röcke); a white collar with hanging bands in front (Bäffchen); and a velvet biretta (Barret), which is worn only in the open air.

*Ibid., § 220.*

IV. On the rights of Preachers.

348. In addition to the personal and property rights defined in the Laws on the Estates, Preachers possess the following rights (Arts. 349–358).

Digest of Laws on the Estates, Arts. 359–393.

349. To Preachers who do not hold higher spiritual ranks, such as General Super-Intendents, Super-Intendents, Doctors of Theology, or Probsts, the following titles are assigned: to a Member of the Consistory, Consistorial Councillor, and Ober-Pastor (Pastor Primarius), Hochehrwürden; to a Pastor, Deacon, and an Adjunct discharging the duties of Pastor, Hochwohlehrwürden; to a Pastor's Helper, Wohlehrwürden.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 221.

350. The most distinguished and well-intentioned Preachers have the right to be awarded gold pectoral crosses in accordance with Article 98.

1843 May 26, Imperial Directive.

351. Preachers, in their correspondence on matters pertaining to their office, use the church seal; their letters and packets sent under this seal are dispatched without payment of weight fees.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 224.

352. Income which Preachers enjoyed prior to December 28, 1832, on the basis of laws or local customs, may not be reduced at the will of the parishioners. They are also permitted to accept, for the performance of sacred rites, the offerings customary until then, in the same amount as before December 28, 1832, pending new general regulations on this matter.

*Ibid., § 222.*

353. A Preacher has no right to refuse to perform, or to postpone, a sacred rite on account of non-payment of offerings due to him. But he may request the Consistory to recover these offerings through the secular authorities.

*Ibid., § 223.*

354. The rules set forth above in Articles 92–96 concerning the payment, from the state treasury, of travel and per diem allowances to clergy in the execution of assignments from the authorities, of allowances for departure to serve in remote regions, and of pensions and one-time allowances for service in the military department, the department of public education, and others, extend fully to the Protestant clergy as well (a).

Note 1. Travel allowances from the state treasury for travel on government business are granted as follows: to the Vice-President of the General Consistory and to the Bishop, for ten horses; to the General Super-Intendent, for eight; to the spiritual Assessor of the Consistory, the Consistorial Councillor, the Probst, and the Ober-Pastor, for four; to the Pastor, for three; and to the candidate of the clergy, for two horses (b).

Note 2. Treasury maintenance for persons of the Protestant clergy serving in the armed forces and in various branches of civil administration is provided according to established establishments (штаты) and special regulations.

(a) 1834 Feb. 20 (6825); 1835 Nov. 14 (8579); 1839 Nov. 9 (12867), present article, section II, para. 4; 1846 Nov. 4 (20581); 1847 May 14 (21222); Dec. 16 (21804); 1856 Aug. 26, Imperial Decree. — (b) 1833 Feb. 14 (5976).

355. The right of Protestant clergy to exemption from corporal punishment (Laws on the Estates, Art. 376) extends to the wives and children of Preachers. Their wives do not lose this right even in widowhood, if they have not entered into another marriage with persons not exempt from corporal punishment.

1845 Aug. 15 (19283), Appendix I, Art. 2, para. 6, and Art. 3, paras. 2, 3.

356. In addition to this (Art. 355), the children of Preachers who are not of noble origin enjoy all the rights granted to the children of personal nobles; but children born after their fathers have relinquished the clerical rank do not have these rights.

Note. Those who have relinquished the Protestant clerical rank, if by birth they did not belong to the hereditary or personal nobility, are obliged, in accordance with the laws, to choose a way of life within a fixed period.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 226.

357. To the widow and the unprovided-for children of a deceased Preacher are granted, for one so-called year of mourning (annus luctus), counted from the day of the Preacher's death, his dwelling and all Pastoral income. But they are obliged to provide board and lodging to the Preacher who is charged with discharging the duties of Pastor (a). In calculating the year of mourning, the following rules are observed:

1) The widow may remain in her husband's dwelling only from the day of his death to the same day the following year.

2) She likewise enjoys the accidental fees (акциденции) throughout the whole year.

3) If the Preacher's maintenance consisted partly in cash, then the widow is entitled, in addition to any unpaid salary owed to her husband and already earned by him up to the day of his death, to the full amount of that salary for the entire year of mourning.

4) As regards the harvest, or any other produce of the land and, in general, items included in the calculation of the Preacher's annual income, a common date of January 1st is established for this calculation. So that the widow and orphans do not suffer loss of income earned by the deceased Preacher from January 1st until the day of his death, then, once the calculation has been made of how much of it falls to each month during the year, they are compensated accordingly for the months lacking to complete the year of mourning.

5) From the income and grain collected, public taxes and seed grain (which is the property of the one who sowed it) are deducted, as well as expenses for the maintenance of the household, servants, livestock, etc., which fall proportionately both on the heirs and on the new Preacher.

6) This rule applies also to those Preachers who have left the pastorate to accept another position, and to their successors, or to the rights of the fund for Pastors' widows and orphans (Art. 358), which receives income during the vacancy of Preacher's positions. DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 325

7) The Chief Church Trusteeships shall resolve disagreements arising in the calculation of income, insofar as this matter does not properly concern the church. They are also charged with the duty, upon the entry of each new Pastor, of handing over to him, together with the church inventory, the inventory of the pastorate as well (b).

Note. On the basis of special regulations or agreements between the Preacher and the parishioners, exceptions to the above-established rules on the year of mourning may be permitted, but only with the authorization of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (c).

(a) Ibid., § 227. — (b) 1838 Apr. 11 (11132). — (c) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 227, note 1.

358. For the greater security of the position of Pastors' widows and orphans, Preachers of each Consistorial district are permitted to establish, from sums contributed by themselves or by outside persons, special Pastors' widows' and orphans' funds, according to rules drawn up by the local Consistory, with the consent of the General Consistory and the authorization of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (a). The following are directed into these funds:

1) All income from pastorates that have remained vacant for longer than the year of mourning, as well as in cases where a Preacher has died without leaving a family, or where his family has no right to enjoy the benefits of the year of mourning. This income is directed to the funds to which each pastorate is assigned. However, Pastoral positions must in no way be left vacant for indefinite periods for the sake of reinforcing the widows' and orphans' funds (such reinforcement cannot compensate for the harm done to parishioners by the lack of spiritual edification) (b).

Note 1. The income from pastorates is understood to be the income from the lands and other holdings assigned to the church for the Pastor's use, and not the Pastor's salary, if he has one, nor the accidental fees (акциденции) received by the Pastor from the parishioners (c).

Note 2. Exempted from the contribution of income from vacant Preacher's positions to the fund of the St. Petersburg Consistorial district are: <...> b) the Evangelical Lutheran Church of St. Peter and Paul [St. Peter] in St. Petersburg, which pays pensions to its own Preachers, as well as to their widows and orphans, according to special rules attached to this article (d).

2) Voluntary donations, which are permitted to be collected once a year at churches in favor of the Pastors' widows' and orphans' funds (e).

Note. In addition, the funds of the St. Petersburg and Moscow Consistorial districts have been granted the right to receive one percent above the general rate on their capital held in the Widows' Treasury of the St. Petersburg Board of Guardians (f).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 227, note 2. — (b) 1834 May 1 (7035). — (c) 1840 June 4 (13521). — (d) Ibid.; 1841 Nov. 18 (15036). — (e) 1834 May 1 (7035). — (f) 1841 Dec. 30 (15170); 1852 March 5, Imperial Directive.

V. On the jurisdiction over, and measures for the correction and punishment of, Preachers.

359. In matters relating to the clerical rank and to the duties of that rank, Preachers answer before the Consistories, according to the established order for this; in all other matters they are subject to the secular public offices, as appropriate.

• 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 225.

360. Preachers, for omissions and offenses in office or rank, are punished, depending on the seriousness of these offenses and the circumstances accompanying them, either 1) by reprimand, or 2) by removal from office, or finally 3) by deprivation of clerical rank.

*Ibid., § 228.*

361. A reprimand may be of two kinds: ordinary and severe.

*Ibid., § 229.*

362. An ordinary reprimand (einfacher Verweis) consists: 1) In a verbal or written remark from the appropriate Probst, Super-Intendent, or General Super-Intendent, in which the greater or lesser gravity of the Preacher's fault is pointed out to him, with an exhortation to be more careful in future. The Probst, Super-Intendent, or General Super-Intendent reports this to the Consistory. 2) In a written remark of the same kind from the Consistory. This reprimand may be accompanied by the imposition of a monetary fine, but not exceeding fifteen silver rubles.

*Ibid., § 230; 1839 Nov. 9 (12867).*

363. An ordinary reprimand from the Probst, Super-Intendent, or General Super-Intendent is given for minor offenses arising from thoughtlessness or negligence, which have given no occasion either for scandal or for complaint of infringement of anyone's rights. An ordinary reprimand from the Consistory is given for more serious offenses, as well as in cases where a Preacher is again found guilty of an omission for which he has already received a reprimand from his Probst, Super-Intendent, or General Super-Intendent.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 231.

364. A severe reprimand (scharfer Verweis) is given at a full session of the Consistory and is entered in the service record. This reprimand may, depending on the circumstances, be accompanied by a written announcement of the Preacher's fault to the clergy of the Probst district in which he is located, or even to the entire jurisdiction of the Consistory. — A severe reprimand may also, in some cases, be accompanied by the imposition of a monetary fine, not exceeding forty-five silver rubles (cf. Art. 362).

Note. If, owing to the remoteness of his residence, the Preacher cannot appear in person before the Consistory without significant difficulty, the reprimand is given to him in writing, and instead of summoning him to the Consistory it is ordered that this reprimand be announced to all Preachers of the Probst district in which the guilty party is located, or to the entire jurisdiction of the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 232; 1839 Nov. 9 (12867).*

365. A severe reprimand is imposed for a breach of duty (Disciplinar-Vergehen) confirmed by the offender's own admission or otherwise proven, especially for disobedience to the orders of the authorities and for offensive written or verbal remarks about such orders, as well as for other more serious offenses, provided it is reliably known that they were committed not out of malicious intent, but through carelessness or misunderstanding.

Note. When by a violation of the duties of subordination the higher spiritual or secular authority is insulted, the guilty party is subjected to the strictest punishment; but if, in showing disobedience to his superior, the Preacher has also dared to insult his honor, then for this he is subjected to a further special penalty on the basis of the general laws on this subject.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 233. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 327

366. Removal from office (remotio) is imposed for more serious offenses against one's office or rank, or for numerous offenses that have become publicly known at the same time. It is also imposed on Preachers found guilty anew of offenses for which they had already received a strict reprimand from the Consistory, as well as those who, by a sentence of the secular court that has entered into legal force, have been sentenced for a criminal offense to a punishment which, although it does not deprive them of honor, may nonetheless demean the clerical rank. Together with the removal of a Preacher from office, depending on the circumstances of the case, there may also be joined a prohibition against ever again appointing him to any Pastoral position, and a special announcement thereof to all Preachers subordinate to the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 234.*

367. Deprivation of clerical rank (Cassation) is imposed for the most serious offenses against one's office or rank, or when a Preacher is sentenced by the secular court for a criminal offense to deprivation of all rights of status, or to the loss of all special rights and privileges attached to him personally and by status, or of certain personal rights and privileges.

*Ibid., § 235; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Arts. 19, 24, 46, 53.*

368. Preachers may not be deprived of clerical rank, nor removed from office, except by a formal judicial sentence, or by a special Supreme command.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 236.

369. A criminal case in which a Preacher has been sentenced by the secular court to one of the punishments specified in Article 367, after review by the higher local criminal court and examination by the Governor of the province, is submitted, before execution of the sentence, for review to the Governing Senate, and from the Governing Senate is presented for the Supreme consideration, and is not finalized without the confirmation of His Imperial Majesty.

1785 Apr. 21 (16187) Art. 13; 1799 Mar. 18 (18894); 1802 Sept. 8 (20405) Art. 20; 1806 Jan. 10 (21991); 1814 Aug. 29 (25668) Art. 4; 1820 Jul. 15 (28358); 1826 Sept. 24 (596) Art. 4; 1829 Oct. 26 (3261); 1846 Jan. 21 (19640); cf. Digest of Local Statutes of the Baltic (Ostsee) Governorates, part II, Arts. 924 and 925, per the Continuation.

370. Upon the Supreme confirmation of the sentence (Art. 369) and its return to the proper local court for execution, that court notifies the Consistory thereof, so that it may deprive the condemned Preacher of his clerical rank before the sentence is carried out in its other parts.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 238, item 1; cf. the enactments cited under Art. 369.

371. The decree on deprivation of clerical rank is carried into execution in one of two ways: either 1) by demanding from the condemned man his charter of clerical rank (Ordinations-Schein) and the insignia thereof, or 2) by the solemn removal of these insignia from him and the confiscation of the charter in a full session of the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 237; cf. the enactments cited under Art. 369.*

372. If, owing to the remoteness of the Consistory's residence, important delay might result from communicating with it under Article 370, then the provincial authority announces to the condemned man that, by force of the judicial sentence concerning him confirmed by the Supreme authority, he is deprived of his clerical rank, and communicates this to the proper Consistory for information.

*Ibid., § 238, item 2; cf. the enactments cited under Art. 369.*

373. A Preacher deprived of clerical rank under Articles 367-372, even if he should subsequently receive a pardon, remains forever deprived of that rank.

*Ibid., § 239; cf. the enactments cited under Arts. 367-372.*

374. In addition to the punishments established by the preceding articles, Preachers may, in certain cases specified below, be subjected to temporary removal from office (suspension). This, however, is not considered a punishment, but only a necessary precautionary measure.

*Ibid. § 240.*

375. A Preacher is temporarily removed from office: 1) when he is caught in the very commission of a criminal offense, or 2) when, on strong suspicion of such an offense, he is taken into custody by the secular court, or 3) when he falls under investigation for a grave offense against his office or rank entailing removal from office or even deprivation of clerical rank, or 4) when he is accused of committing such an offense and has confessed to it, or finally 5) when so strong a suspicion rests upon him that, during the course of the investigation, scandal to the parish might result from his continuing to perform the Preacher's duties.

*Ibid., § 241.*

376. Of any necessary arrest of a Preacher for a criminal offense, the secular authorities notify the Consistory, in advance where possible, or at least immediately after the arrest, so that the Consistory, having at the same time removed him from office, may take the necessary measures to entrust the performance of his duties to another and to dispatch one of its own members, or another clerical dignitary, to the investigation [(a)].

Note. The vote of the deputy in adjudicating a case in court is counted equally with the votes of the other members of the court (b).

(a) Ibid., § 242. — (b) Digest of Local Statutes of the Baltic (Ostsee) Governorates, part II, Art. 922.

377. A Preacher removed from office is obliged to give to whoever performs his duties during that time one half of everything received in that position, both the fixed maintenance and the special incomes (casuelle Einkünfte) for the performance of spiritual rites.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 243.

378. Of every Preacher temporarily removed from office, or entirely removed therefrom, as well as of the deprivation of his clerical rank, the Consistory immediately and in detail reports to the General Consistory, which presents this report to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

*Ibid., § 244.*

379. For disseminating a doctrine not in accord with Holy Scripture as explained in the Symbolic Books of the Evangelical Lutheran Church (Art. 134), and with the rules of that Church, a Preacher is punished either with an ordinary or a strict reprimand, or even with removal from office, DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 329

depending on the seriousness of the fault, that is, on the nature and tendency of the false opinions disseminated by him, and on whether he had in doing so any unlawful evil intent.

*Ibid., § 245.*

380. A Preacher who disseminates false opinions and doctrine not deliberately, but out of thoughtlessness or incomplete understanding of the force of the words of Holy Scripture or of the expressions used by himself, is to be first admonished and instructed by his immediate superiors; if these instructions and admonitions prove unsuccessful and he is again found guilty of the same carelessness, then, depending on the circumstances, he may be subjected to an ordinary or even a strict reprimand, and finally, in case of persistence, in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article 379, to removal from office.

*Ibid., § 246.*

381. Deviation from the order of public worship and sacred rites established in the Church Agenda (Art. 140, note) is punished, depending on its seriousness, with an ordinary or strict reprimand, if indeed it is found by the immediate superiors of the Preacher and the local Consistory that it is not sufficient to confine matters to mere light remarks or admonitions through the Probst or Superintendent. But for repeated violation of the rules prescribed in the Liturgical Agenda, especially the most important ones, if the admonitions and other corrective measures employed prove unsuccessful, the guilty party may be sentenced to removal from office.

*Ibid., § 247.*

382. If the order of worship is violated by a Preacher, even without overt unlawful evil intent, to such a degree that strong scandal results among his parishioners to the detriment of piety and of the due reverence for the sacred rites, then he is immediately sentenced to removal from office, and, depending on the circumstances, even to deprivation of rank.

*Ibid., § 248.*

383. If a Preacher, out of negligence or laziness, avoids fulfilling the duty of visiting the sick in order to ease their sufferings through spiritual ministration, he is punished for this, first with an ordinary and then with a strict reprimand from the Consistory, and, should he fail to correct himself, with removal from office.

*Ibid., § 249.*

384. For the performance of invalid marriages the following punishments are imposed on a Preacher:

1) For performing a marriage which by law must be recognized as invalid, the Preacher, in the case where he has done so knowingly, is sentenced to deprivation of clerical rank and to imprisonment for a term of one to two years. When, however, he is found guilty only of an excusable error, arising more or less from a concurrence of particular circumstances, he is subjected: the first time to a strict reprimand, and the second time to removal from office (a).

2) For joining in marriage persons already bound by a marital union, in the case where this has been done by the Preacher through an excusable error, arising more or less from a concurrence of particular circumstances, he is subjected the first time to a strict reprimand, the second time to a monetary fine of from fifty to two hundred rubles, and the third time to deprivation of clerical rank. But if the Preacher is found to have known of the unlawfulness of the marriage he performed, then even the first time he is sentenced to deprivation of rank and to imprisonment for a term of six months to one year. And when it is proven that the Preacher also assisted the person bound by a prior marriage in deceiving the other person, who, unaware of this, entered into the unlawful marriage with him, then he is sentenced to the punishments established in the Code of Punishments, Article 133, for complicity in a crime (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 250; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2067. — (b) 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2048.

385. If a Preacher, contrary to the rules established above in Chapter Four, performs, out of some mercenary or other personal motive, a marriage forbidden by the laws, even though not considered invalid, he is immediately removed from office and subjected to deprivation of clerical rank; when, on the contrary, he was merely led into an error excusable given the circumstances of the case, then the first time he receives only a strict reprimand; but in case of a further such carelessness, he, as unreliable, is removed from office with a prohibition against ever again appointing him to a position.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 251; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2067.

386. To the punishments established in Article 384, item 1, and in Article 385, and on the same basis, is also subjected that Preacher who, although he did not himself perform the marriage forbidden by the laws, nevertheless by testimony, by an announcement in church, or by some other action pertaining to his office, gave another Preacher occasion to perform it.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 252; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2067.

387. For performing a marriage without observing the rules prescribed above in Chapter Four regarding the announcement of banns and other precautionary measures, when there was no special permission for this, a Preacher is subjected, depending on the circumstances that more or less aggravate or diminish his fault, the first time to a reprimand, more or less strict, and the second time to removal from office, with a prohibition against ever again appointing him to a parish. He is subjected to the same punishments for marrying anyone who has arrived temporarily in his parish, without proper certification that this person is not already married.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 253; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2069.

388. If a Preacher, without the authorization of the higher authority empowered to grant it, permits himself to declare any marriage dissolved, or to bless the separation, even if only temporary, of spouses from bed and board, then he is subjected for this either to a strict reprimand, or to removal from office, or to deprivation of rank, at the discretion of his ecclesiastical superiors.

1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2070.

389. If an Evangelical Lutheran Preacher receives into his Church a member of the Orthodox Church, he is immediately removed from office and deprived of rank in the manner established above (Arts. 367-372).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 254. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 332

390. If a Preacher (Art. 389) knowingly admits Orthodox persons to confession or communion, or their children to baptism according to the rites of the Evangelical Lutheran Church, he is subjected for this, the first time to removal from his position for a term of six months to one year, and the second time to deprivation of clerical rank and being placed under police supervision. For performing any of these spiritual rites for Orthodox persons through ignorance, he is subjected to a strict reprimand, as for carelessness inconsistent with the importance of his rank (a). For performing a marriage between a person of the Orthodox and a person of the Protestant confession, before it has been performed by an Orthodox Priest, when there is no formal certification available from the proper ecclesiastical authority that, under the rules of the Orthodox Church, no obstacles exist to this marriage, the Preacher, depending on whether or not obstacles to that marriage subsequently appeared, and on other circumstances more or less aggravating or diminishing his fault, is subjected: either to a monetary fine of ten to fifty rubles, or to temporary removal from office for a term of two to six months, or to removal from his position (b).

(a) 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 201. — (b) Ibid., Art. 2068.

391. A Preacher who, without proper permission, receives into the Evangelical Lutheran Church a member of one of the other Christian Churches (besides the Orthodox Church, per Art. 389) that enjoy equal freedom of confession of their faith in Russia, is removed from office. — For performing spiritual rites for members of these Churches, without proper permission to do so, if this is done not by mistake but knowingly, especially when there is also revealed an intention to induce a change of faith, the Preacher is punished with removal from office.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 255.

<...>

393. If a Preacher leads a scandalous and depraved life, and repeated admonitions from his superiors and ordinary and strict reprimands from them and from the Consistory fail to produce in him the desired correction, then the local Consistory sentences him to removal from his position, or, depending on the seriousness of the accusation and the scandal, even to deprivation of clerical rank.

*Ibid., § 257.*

394. If a Preacher is accused of some violation of his official duties not specifically named in the preceding articles, then the Consistory, in examining this accusation, takes into consideration: 1) the greater or lesser importance of the duty he violated and the scandal, harm, or infringement of rights resulting therefrom; 2) his motives in committing the offense, whether from thoughtlessness or from unlawful evil intent; 3) the opinion of his parishioners about him and the degree of their attachment to him; and finally, 4) the reports about him from the Probst and the Superintendent, or the General Superintendent. On the basis of these considerations, the Consistory either instructs the Preacher's immediate superior to admonish and instruct him, or issues him, on its own part, a more or less strict reprimand, or finally, should all these corrective measures prove insufficient, sentences him to removal from his position, and, for very serious offenses harmful in their consequences to the whole parish or to the whole Evangelical Lutheran Church, even to deprivation of clerical rank.

*Ibid., § 258.*

Section Three.

On Sextons and Organists.

395. The sextons, cantors, organists, bell-ringers, and the like, attached to churches of the Protestant confession, although called church servants, serve by hire and are not counted among the clergy.

1850 Jan. 11 (23817) § 5, note 3; 1857 Jun. 3, Statute on the National Census, § 5, note 3.

396. For the position of sexton, literate people, knowledgeable in choral singing and having presented proper guarantees of their reliability, are chosen by the parish Preacher together with the Church Councils.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 259.

397. The sexton must assist the Preacher in everything pertaining to church service, and must show due obedience both to him and to the Church Council.

*Ibid., § 260.*

398. The Preacher, together with the Church Councils, may dismiss and remove a sexton from office. In case of disagreement between them regarding the choice, dismissal, or removal of a sexton, they seek the resolution of the Consistory (a).

Note. Those sextons of the Protestant confession who at the same time perform the duties of school teachers are exempted from conscription duty while holding these positions, though they are not exempted from paying the poll tax (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 261. — (b) 1839 Jun. 30 (12496).

399. Organists are appointed, dismissed, or removed in the same manner as sextons (Arts. 396 and 398).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 262.

400. Organists, in the performance of their office, are obliged to carry out exactly the instructions of the Preacher and of the Church Councils.

*Ibid., § 263.*

##### CHAPTER SIX.

On the Higher Clerical Dignitaries.

Section One.

On Probsts.

401. Probst districts in the Empire are formed, in consideration of local circumstances, from a greater or lesser number of Evangelical Lutheran parishes. In 1832 the following were designated: three in the Governorate of St. Petersburg, eight in Livland, eight in Estland, seven in Courland, DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 333

one in Vilna, two in the Saratov colonies, and two in the German colonies of the southern region.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 264.

402. Preachers of those Evangelical Lutheran parishes which, in 1832, were not attached to any Probst district, remain, until further arrangements, under the direct authority of the Consistories and the General Superintendents or Superintendents. If the establishment of a new Probstship, or any change in the extent of existing Probst districts, should prove necessary, the local Consistories report this to the General Consistory, which presents its opinion thereon to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, for report to His Imperial Majesty.

*Ibid., § 265.*

403. In the event of the death of a Probst, or of a grave illness preventing him from performing his office, his place is taken, until the appointment of a new Probst, by the senior in service in that district, or by another Preacher chosen by the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 266.*

404. When a vacancy arises for a Probst, the Consistory summons all the Preachers of that Probst district to elect two candidates for the vacant position, or requests their opinions in writing. The Consistory, through the General Consistory, presents these candidates, with its own conclusion, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs for the confirmation of one of them.

*Ibid., § 267.*

405. Probsts are subordinate directly to the General Superintendents and Consistories, and are themselves the immediate superiors of the Preachers belonging to their districts. They convey to them all the instructions of the ecclesiastical authorities, receive from them reports for presentation to the higher authorities, and, as their closest overseers and mentors, observe their teaching, moral life, and exactness in the performance of their duties. Probsts submit annually to the General Superintendents brief lists of themselves and of the Preachers subordinate to them, as well as conduct reports on the candidates for the clergy located in their district, according to the prescribed form.

*Ibid., § 268.*

406. If a Probst, without harmful loss of time to the matter, or for other reasons, cannot address his submission to the General Superintendent, he has the right to apply directly to the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 269.*

407. A Probst is obliged to conduct, at least once every three years, visitations of all the churches belonging to his district, having with him, if possible, Ecclesiastical assistants.

*Ibid., § 270, item 1.*

408. Visitations must be conducted, as far as possible, on Sundays, and each time, at least a week before the visitation, the Preacher must be notified thereof; he announces this to the parish from the pulpit. The Probst, for his part, also notifies the patrons and the Church Council of that parish of the intended visitation.

*Ibid., items 2 and 3.*

409. A visitation always begins with a solemn service. The sermon is delivered by the parish Preacher, on a text given by the Probst; then he explains a brief catechism to the assembled youth, in order to demonstrate his method of teaching it; after him the Probst himself examines the youth, and, if he considers it necessary, also other parishioners, in their knowledge of the Law of God. The Probst asks the Preacher whether he has anything to declare about the state of his parish in general. Thereupon the Preacher leaves the church, and the Probst puts the same question to the parishioners, records the answer, and dismisses them, having given them a suitable admonition on this occasion. He detains those who say that they have something in particular to declare to him. After this the Probst requires from the Preacher, the church servants, and the peasant church elders detailed and precise information as to how they perform their duties, in what relations they stand to one another and to the parish, and likewise concerning the religious and moral condition of the parishioners, the state of the schools and charitable institutions, the number and behavior of the clerical candidates present in that parish, the observance of Sundays and other solemn days, the order of divine service and the administration of the sacraments, burials, and generally everything pertaining to the church. He also requires information as to whether the payments due to the Preacher and church servants are being properly made; he then examines the church books, the church chronicle, the parish archive, and the church plate in the possession of the Preacher.

*Ibid., items 4 and 7.*

410. The Probst may, if he considers it necessary, require from the Preacher the drafts or outlines (Dispositionen) of his sermons as well.

*Ibid., item 8.*

411. The Probst is obliged, by means of advice and admonitions, to correct any omissions or disorders he finds during the visitation; of those which he cannot correct or stop in this manner, he reports to the Consistory.

*Ibid., item 9.*

412. The Probst must keep a record of everything that takes place at the visitation. This record is signed by him, by the Preacher, and, as witnesses, by some of those Church Wardens or other persons present at the visitation. The record remains in the church archive and serves as the basis for the next visitation; the Probst submits to the Consistory a copy thereof and the draft of the sermon delivered on this occasion by the parish Pastor.

*Ibid., item 10.*

413. In parishes not subordinate to Probsts, visitations are conducted by the General Superintendents or Superintendents; but in the case of very great distance from the residence of the General Superintendent or Superintendent, the Consistories entrust this to one of the Preachers.

Note 1. In those parishes where special rules for visitation had been established prior to 28 December 1832, the former order in this respect continues to be observed thereafter as well (a). DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 335

Note 2. During the visitation of their districts, Probsts receive relay conveyances (Vorspann) from the parishes. Each Probst in the colonies of the southern region is granted from the treasury, once every three years, a fixed monetary allowance for travel expenses during visitation journeys (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 270, note. — (b) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870), establishment tables, Art. VII, note; 1838 Jan. 18 (10899).

414. Probsts hold the title: Hochehrwürden; during divine service and on other solemn occasions they wear the official vestment established for Preachers (Art. 347).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 271.

415. Complaints of a Probst against Preachers, and of Preachers against a Probst, are submitted to the General Superintendent, as appropriate. He endeavors to settle their disputes amicably, and, failing success, submits the complaints for resolution to the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 272.*

416. If parishioners, a patron, or Church Wardens are dissatisfied with an order of the Probst, or believe that their rights with respect to church property are being violated, they turn with a complaint about this to the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 273.*

417. Probsts, like all other Evangelical Lutheran Preachers, use the seal of their church in official correspondence; their letters and packages sent under this seal are dispatched without payment of postage by weight.

*Ibid., § 274.*

Section Two.

On the General Superintendents, Superintendents,

and on the title of Evangelical Lutheran Bishops.

418. The higher ecclesiastical superiors of the Probsts in the Governorates of Livland, Estland, and Courland, and in the districts of the St. Petersburg and Moscow Consistories, are called General Superintendents, and the superiors of the Preachers on the island of Ösel and in the cities of Riga and Reval are called Superintendents.

Note. The General Superintendent of the Estland clergy is always also the Pastor of the Reval Cathedral church (Domkirche).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 275 and note.

419. For the positions of General Superintendent of Livland, Courland, and Estland, and of the Superintendent of Ösel, two candidates each are elected by the local nobility, and for the positions of Superintendent in Riga and Reval, likewise two candidates each, by the Magistrates of those cities. The elected candidates are presented, through the Governor-General of the Baltic Governorates and the Ministry of Internal Affairs, for the Supreme consideration of His Imperial Majesty. — The Ministry, in its report on these candidates, also presents the opinion of the General Consistory obtained regarding them. — For the positions of the St. Petersburg and Moscow General Superintendents, the General Consistory likewise presents to the Ministry of Internal Affairs two candidates each, for report to His Imperial Majesty.

*Ibid., § 276.*

420. The installation of General Superintendents and Superintendents into office is performed solemnly, by order of the General Consistory, in accordance with the order set forth in the Church Agenda.

*Ibid., § 277.*

421. General Superintendents and Superintendents, as the highest ecclesiastical superiors of the Probsts and other Evangelical Lutheran clergy belonging to their Consistorial districts, as well as of the clerical candidates, and as representatives of the Consistories, are obliged, in their personal dealings with subordinate clergy, to promote by all means at their disposal the exact fulfillment of the instructions of these bodies and their general duty of overseeing the proper course of all church affairs in the district. They must ensure that the teaching of the Preachers, in its spirit and in all particulars, accords with Holy Scripture and the explanations of the Symbolic Books, and that all clergy properly perform their duties, edifying their parishioners by the example of a moral life, ceaselessly perfecting themselves in the sciences necessary to their rank, and, in performing spiritual rites and sacred ceremonies, not departing arbitrarily from the rules of the Church Agenda. They must endeavor, without delay, to eliminate, stop, or prevent and correct anything in the official conduct and manner of life of the clergy subordinate to them that is contrary to this Church Statute or to the provisions of the Agenda; but they are obliged to notify the Consistory both of this, and of those cases in which they are unable by their own authority to stop some disorder, as well as, generally, of all their observations of importance for any reason with respect to the district entrusted to them.

*Ibid., § 278.*

422. General Superintendents and Superintendents ordinarily direct the candidate examinations and spiritual conferences (colloquium). They also, upon the transfer of Preachers, satisfy themselves by means of spiritual conferences as to their merit and knowledge.

*Ibid., § 279.*

423.
