889. The freedom granted to the Sarepta Evangelical Brethren Society in the practice of its faith according to the statute, doctrine, and rites existing among the Evangelical Brethren extends also to members of the Evangelical Brethren societies in the Baltic governorates.

Note. In the Highest decree of May 3, 1834, it was explained, among other things, that the proposal of the Evangelical Lutheran Consistory to admit those wishing to become members of the Brethren society, with a solemn declaration to that effect, could not be permitted, firstly because the Herrnhuters living in the Baltic governorates do not constitute either a separate colony or a distinct religious community, professing generally the Evangelical Lutheran faith, and secondly because all the rights and privileges specified in the Highest charters of October 27, 1817 and October 10, 1826 were, and could only have been, granted to actual members of the Brethren society, that is, to those who arrived in Russia already holding this status, and not to those who might arbitrarily choose to assume this designation.

1817 Oct. 27 (27113) art. 1; 1826 Oct. 10 (611); 1834 May 3 (7049) art. 6; see also the Statute on Colonies.

890. Members of the Evangelical Brethren Society in the Baltic governorates are permitted to maintain under their supervision, for spiritual benefit, prayer houses or meetings for Latvians, Estonians, and other willing persons in towns, settlements, and villages, with the consent of the landowner and with the knowledge of the town authorities, without any hindrance otherwise. All who wish may freely gather in these prayer houses or meetings, during time free from work, except during the hours designated for ordinary church worship.

1817 Oct. 27 (27113) art. 2; 1834 May 3 (7049) art. 1.

891. The above-mentioned (art. 890) prayer houses and meetings are under the direction and management of the Elders and members of the Evangelical Brethren Society.

1817 Oct. 27 (27113) art. 2.

892. Those in charge of the prayer houses and meetings (art. 891) must be Russian subjects, unless they entered upon these positions before May 3, 1834.

1834 May 3 (7049) art. 1.

893. New prayer houses and meetings of the Evangelical Brethren Society in the Baltic governorates may be established only in compliance with the conditions established above, in articles 150, 690, and 691, regarding the establishment of such private prayer meetings as go beyond the bounds of family or household communal prayer, namely:

1) New prayer houses and meetings may be established only with the authorization of the local Evangelical Lutheran Consistories.

2) The Consistories are obliged, upon any intention to establish a prayer house or meeting under their jurisdiction, to bring this to the attention, beforehand and with their opinion, through the chief local authority and the General Consistory, of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, for report to His Imperial Majesty.

3) The Consistories, in authorizing the establishment of new prayer houses and meetings, notify both the local civil authority and the Preacher in whose parish the prayer house or meeting to be established is to be located.

4) The Consistories permit the establishment of prayer houses or meetings only to persons who enjoy general respect in their parishes, who have not been noted for any unlawful acts or acts bringing shame and dishonor, who are Russian subjects, and who are permanent residents of the place where they intend to hold meetings.

1832 Dec. 28 (5871) § 23; 1834 May 3 (7049) art. 1. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 419

894. Priests ordained by Bishops of the Evangelical Brethren Society in the Baltic governorates are permitted, among their brethren of German origin who are actual members of that society, to perform in accordance with their office all spiritual rites which, under the statutes of the society, they are to perform.

1817 Oct. 27 (27113) art. 5; see the Statute on Colonies.

895. In all prayer houses and meetings without exception (arts. 890—893), only Pastors have the right to preach (freie Vortraege zu halten), and those candidates in Theology who, after due examination by the Evangelical Lutheran Consistory, in accordance with article 274 of this Code, have received a certificate of permission to preach (pro venia concionandi), or Priests properly ordained by Bishops of the Brethren society.

1817 Oct. 27 (27113) art. 5; 1826 Oct. 10 (611); 1834 May 3 (7049) art. 2.

896. Preceptors (Vorbeter) elected by members of the Evangelical Brethren Society in the Baltic governorates for prayer meetings, if they do not have from the Evangelical Lutheran Consistory the certificate of permission to preach (pro venia concionandi) specified in article 274 of this Code, must, on the basis of article 150, confine themselves to reading Holy Scripture without any interpretation, or to prayers, hymns, and spiritual discourses from books approved by the Evangelical Lutheran Consistories, likewise without any interpretation.

1834 May 3 (7049) art. 3.

897. In accordance with article 691 of this Code, parish Pastors and district Probsts in the Baltic governorates not only have the right, but are obliged, under strict personal responsibility, to visit the prayer meetings of the Evangelical Brethren Society as often as possible, and to observe the precise fulfillment of everything established in article 691.

*Ibid., art. 4.*

898. All gatherings not held in properly established prayer houses, but in private homes, must be forbidden, but with strict observance that this pretext not be used for harassment and oppression.

*Ibid., art. 5.*

##### CHAPTER FIVE.

On the administration of the spiritual affairs of the Scottish colonists at Karras,

the Basel colonists at Shusha, and the Mennonites.

899. Members of the Scottish colony of Karras near the mineral waters in Stavropol governorate are granted the practice of their faith according to the statute, doctrine, and rites existing in their society.

1806 Dec. 25 (22410) art. 2; 1828 Dec. 15 (2517) art. 1; 1835 Jun. 26 (8271).

900. The public affairs of this colony (art. 899), including those relating to matters of faith, are handled by a special Administration composed of persons elected by the society of colonists.

1806 Dec. 25 (22410) art. 5; 1828 Dec. 15 (2517) art. 1; 1835 Jun. 26 (8271).

901. Members of the Scottish colony of Karras and the Basel missionaries settled in Shusha are forbidden all missionary activity (they are permitted to engage in agriculture, manufacturing, and crafts, but not in the conversion of persons of other faiths to Christianity).

1806 Dec. 25 (22410) arts. 12, 13; 1828 Dec. 15 (2517) art. 1; 1835 Jun. 26 (8271).

<...>

903. The Mennonites conduct their affairs of faith without hindrance, according to their church institutions and customs.

1800 Apr. 6 (19372); Sept. 6 (19546); 1801 May 23 (19887).

904. Spiritual teachers of the Mennonites, in performing the duties of their office according to the rules of their confession, must not under any circumstances interfere in secular or other matters unbecoming to the priestly rank.

1801 May 16 (19873) §3.

Digest of Laws of the Russian Empire (SZRI). 1857. Vol. XI. Part I. Pp. 7—171.

## No. 115. STATUTE ON COLONIES OF FOREIGNERS IN THE RUSSIAN EMPIRE (1857)

**STATUTE**

**ON COLONIES OF FOREIGNERS IN THE EMPIRE.**

**COMPENDIUM**

**OF INSTITUTIONS AND STATUTES**

**ON COLONIES OF FOREIGNERS IN THE EMPIRE.**

#### PART ONE. THE DIVISION OF COLONIES AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THEIR ADMINISTRATION.

##### CHAPTER ONE.

Division of colonies.

Art. 1. The colonies of foreigners settled in the Russian Empire are: 1) colonies established on state lands (a); 2) colonies settled on lands acquired in ownership by foreign immigrants (b); and 3) colonies settled on private lands, under contracts with their owners (v).

Note. Provisions concerning colonies of foreigners settled on lands allotted to them from the treasury constitute properly the subject of the first eight parts of this Compendium; while the rules concerning other settlers, as exceptions from the general provisions, are set forth separately in Part IX.

(a) Cf. the enactments cited in Chapter III [II] of this part. — (b) 1804 Mar. 1 (21192). - (v) 1765 Nov. 1 (12503): 1804 Apr. 12 (21254); 1817 Aug. 25 (27022); Oct. 1 (27072); 1837 Dec. 26 (10834).

2. The colonies settled on state lands are the following:

I. The colonies of the southern region of Russia, by which are meant all existing colonies of foreigners in the three New Russia governorates and in the Bessarabian region (a).

II. The Saratov colonies (b). DOCUMENTS_______________________________ ____________________________________________ 421

III. The Northern colonies, namely those established in St. Petersburg Governorate (v).

IV. The Livonia colony, settled in Wenden district of Livonia Governorate, on the estates of Hirschenhof and Helfreichshof (g).

V. The colonies of Members of the Evangelical Brethren Society, established in Sarepta and in the three Baltic governorates (d).

VI. The Belovezh colony, in Chernigov Governorate (e).

VII. The Rybensdorf colony, in Voronezh Governorate (zh).

VIII. The colonies of Württemberg settlers, in the Transcaucasus region (z).

IX. The German colony, in Stavropol Governorate near the mineral waters (k).

X. The German colony, settled near the town of St. Krest (l).

XI. The Karras colony, near the mineral waters in Stavropol Governorate, founded by Scottish missionaries (m).

XII. The colony of the Basel missionaries, settled near the town of Shusha (n).

XIII. The German colony near the town of Yeysk (o).

Note I. The woolen manufacturers settled near the towns of Poltava and Konstantinograd (p), although they had been received into the charge of the Poltava Chamber of State Domains, nevertheless, since these manufacturers occupy land within the town boundary, are under the jurisdiction of the town police for police matters, and since a special Committee of six members, elected by the society of these manufacturers from among themselves, under the chairmanship of a Guardian of the colonies appointed to that office by the local authorities (r), has been established to direct their affairs, these manufacturers have been removed from the department of the Chamber of State Domains (s).

Note 2. In 1851 it was Most Highly permitted for Prussian Mennonites, numbering one hundred families, to settle in Samara Governorate, under specially established rules on the matter (t).

3. In addition to the foreign colonies enumerated in the preceding article, Jewish colonies have been settled in the New Russia governorates, on state land.

1829 Jul. 24 (3034); 1837 Nov. 4 (10668); 1852 Oct. 27 (26704).

##### CHAPTER TWO.

On the department and administration of the colonies.

4. Foreign settlers (art. 2) are under the guardianship of the Ministry of State Domains (a), through the First or Second Department of this Ministry, depending on the governorate in which the colonies of foreign settlers have been established (b). In the governorate administration, foreign settlers, in each governorate where they are located, are either under the guardianship of the Chamber of State Domains, through its Economic Division (v); or are subordinate to the Guardianship Committee for Foreign Settlers of the southern region, or to the Saratov Office of Foreign Settlers, and beyond the Caucasus to the Expedition of State Domains under the Main Administration of the Transcaucasus Region (g).

Note. In the district administration, foreign settlements are subject to District Chiefs only in those governorates in which the Chambers of State Domains are subordinate to the Second Department of State Domains (d).

(a) 1837 Dec. 26 (10834) para. 3. -(b) 1838 Apr. 30 (11189) para. 1: 1839 Dec. 28 (13035) para. 1; 1841 Jun. 12 (16643|146431) para. 1. - (v) 1838 Apr. 30 (11189) para. 8; 1839 Dec. 28 (13035) para. 8,33; 1841 Jun. 12 (16643|14643|) para. 22. - (g) 1833 Jul. 1 (6298); 1838 Apr. 30 (11189); 1840 (14103) staff [establishment] para. 9, 26, 27; 1845 Nov. 1 (19434); 1849 Dec. 21 (23753). - (d) 1839 Dec. 28 (13035) pt. II, §64; 1841 Jun. 12 (16642|14642|) pt. II. §21.

<...>

6. The Chambers of State Domains subordinate (art. 957 of the Establishment of the Ministries) to the First Department of State Domains administer the foreign settlers, where such are in their department, under those rules which have been established for the Saratov Office of Foreign Settlers and the Guardianship Committee for Foreign Settlers of the southern region (a); in those governorates in which the Chambers of State Domains are subordinate (article 969 of the Establishment of the Ministries) to the Second Department of State Domains, foreign colonists are administered by these Chambers and District Chiefs under the rules established for these settlers (b).

(a) 1838 Apr. 30 (11189) pt. I, §§ 57, 364. - (b) 1839 Dec. 28 (13035) pt. I. §§ 68,471; 1841 Jun. 12 (14643) pt. I, §§ 22, 41; pt. II. § 39.

Division One.

On the local administration of the colonies of the southern region.

I. Composition of the local administration.

7. For the administration of the New Russia and Bessarabian foreign and Jewish settlements there exist: 1) the Guardianship Committee for Foreign Settlers of the southern region; 2) the Administration of the Trans-Danubian immigrants.

1845 Nov. 1 (19434).

8. The Guardianship Committee consists of a Chairman and two Members.

1845 Nov. 1 (19434) staff [establishment] I.

9. Attached to the Committee are: a Secretary, Desk Officers, an Accountant with Assistants, a Registrar of Records, an Archivist, a Translator, Officials for Special Assignments, a Surveyor, a Physician, a Veterinary Physician, and clerical staff per establishment.

1845 Nov. 1 (19434) staff [establishment] I; 1850 Jan. 25 (23873) para. 1.

<...>

11. Under the department of the Guardianship Committee are the Overseers of the settlements (colonies).

1833 Jul. 1 (6298). DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 423

12. There are to be nine Overseers of colonies.

1845 Nov. 1 (19434) I.

13. District and Village Boards are established in the colonies.

Cf. the enactments cited below, and 1838 Apr. 30 (11189) pt. IV, § 9 and 16, note.

14. The division of colonies into districts is at the discretion of the Guardianship Committee.

1818 Mar. 22 (27312) art. III, para. 3; 1819 Dec. 29 (22054[280541).

15. A District Board is established in each district, and consists of a Board Head (Vorsteher) or Elected Representative and two Beisitzers.

1801 May 16 (19873) §8; 1803 Jul. 7 (20841) § 15 [16].

16. A Village Board is established in each settlement and consists of a Schulz and two Beisitzers; one Tithingman is provided for every ten households.

The same enactments.

17. In the District and Village Board there must be a clerk, under whose supervision young people of the colony are employed for correspondence work (a).

Note. For the training of capable teachers from among colonist boys for village schools and clerks for the Boards, as well as Surveyors and Architects, with the aim moreover of spreading through them knowledge of the Russian language in the colonies, a school has been established in the Bessarabian colony of Sarata, under a special regulation concerning it (b).

(a) The same enactments. — (b) 1842 Oct. 23 (16177|16117)).

18. The colonists of each settlement constitute its communal society.

1801 May 16 (19873).

19. In each communal society a village communal assembly is established.

*Ibid.*

20. Colonists, at least one from each household, are summoned to the assembly by the Head or Schulz, sent for this purpose through Tithingmen with notices.

*Ibid.*

21. Colonists, having assembled for the meeting, must maintain quiet and attentively occupy themselves with what is proposed to them.

*Ibid.*

II. Procedure for the appointment of officials.

22. The appointment and dismissal of members of the Guardianship Committee and of the Administrator of the Trans-Danubian immigrants is at the discretion of the Minister of State Domains.

*Ibid. and 1837 Dec. 26 (10834).*

23. All other officials and clerical staff are appointed and dismissed by the Guardianship Committee itself.

*Ibid.*

24. Heads, Schulzes, and Beisitzers are appointed by election by the society of colonists.

1801 May 16 (19873) § 9.

25. The Head is elected for three years, and District Beisitzers for two years, from all the villages of the colony assigned to the Board. After a year has passed following the initial election, one of the Beisitzers is dismissed, and whoever is to take his place then remains in office for a full two years without fail. For Village Schulzes and Beisitzers, the election is held for two years, under the special supervision of the Heads, with the consent of each settlement, but with the same annual rotation of Beisitzers as in the District Board.

*Ibid., § 10.*

26. Those settlements which, because of their distance from others, cannot conveniently be assigned to any of the District Boards, elect a Schulz for three years, and two Beisitzers for two; those thus elected perform all the duties assigned to a District Board, independently of it.

*Ibid., §11.*

27. In electing district and village officials, in addition to the three persons appointed for each Board, two more should be elected to fill the posts in case of absence or illness.

1803 Jul. 7 (20841) § 16.

28. Elections are conducted by majority vote, from among adult colonists who have their own household, who are prudent, just, of good behavior, diligent and exemplary in their household management, and above all skilled in agriculture, horticulture, and animal husbandry.

1801 May 16 (19873) §9.

29. In the election, each casts his vote in turn, for whomever he chooses for whatever office, without any servility and following neither friendship nor enmity.

*Ibid.*

30. At the conclusion of the elections, those who have received the most votes are confirmed by the signed agreement of all, and are submitted for final confirmation by the Guardianship Committee.

*Ibid., §§ 9 and 10; 1833 Jul. 1 (6298).*

31. Tithingmen are rotated monthly.

1801 May 10 (19873) § 10.

32. Clerks are appointed for a special wage by voluntary hire.

1803 Jul. 7 (20841) § 15.

III. Salary.

33. The Chairman, the members of the Committee, the Administrator, and all other officials of the administration of the New Russia and Bessarabian foreign settlements receive maintenance in the amount fixed by the establishment. The establishment sum is made up by a levy on the New Russia and Bessarabian foreign settlers under the Committee's jurisdiction, and from revenues of the leasehold items in the foreign settlements (a).

Note. The levy on the New Russia and Bessarabian foreign settlers has been increased by three kopecks for every male revision soul released from the exemption period, to cover the expenses under the establishment of a special Control Division of the Committee, set up in 1850. This additional levy is paid into the District Treasuries within the time limits established for the payment of taxes, while the sum fixed by the establishment is disbursed from the state treasury on the general basis (b).

(a) 1845 Nov. 1 (19434) staff [establishment] I, II, note 1,2. — (b) 1850 Jan. 25 (23873) para. 2, 3. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 425

34. Surpluses from the establishment allocation are used, with the permission of the Minister of State Domains, for those purposes to which a similar sum is applied, made up of surpluses from the establishment allocations for the Chambers and District Administrations of State Domains.

1845 Nov. 1 (19434) note 3.

35. The Head receives a salary of five rubles seventy-two kopecks, and the District Beisitzers four rubles twenty-nine kopecks, from all the settlements belonging to the Board; the Schulz is allotted two rubles eighty-eight kopecks from the settlement in which he was elected.

1801 May 16 (19873) § 13; 1839 Nov. 9 (12867).

36. Village Beisitzers and Tithingmen perform their duties without any pay.

1801 May 16 (19873) § 13.

IV. Subjects and duties.

37. The subjects of the Guardianship Committee are:

1) The reception of foreign settlers establishing themselves in the status of colonists.

2) Their settlement on the basis of the rules established for this purpose.

3) The department of lands allotted or hereafter to be allotted for the settlement of colonists.

4) The protection of all benefits, rights, and privileges granted and hereafter to be granted to colonists.

5) Supervision of the fulfillment of the obligations they have undertaken.

6) The inspection of the colonies and the examination of complaints and petitions submitted by colonists (a).

Note. The authorities of the foreign settlers of the southern region also participate in the arrangements for the provisioning of local horses, for the travel of Their Highest Highnesses, on an equal footing with the other persons designated for this purpose (b).

(a) 1818 Mar. 22 (27312), art. I, para. 6, 7, 11 and 14; art. 11, para. 16 and 17. - (b) 1846 Jul. 23 (20242).

38. In addition to this, the following are assigned to the department of the Guardianship Committee:

1) All matters of rural police in relation to the colonies entrusted to them; the timely and proper collection of taxes due to the treasury; the conduct of investigations in the colonies; fines, penalties, etc.

2) Care of the economy and household management in the colonies.

3) Encouragement of the improvement of agriculture, horticulture, and animal husbandry, and of the establishment of factories suited to the climate and local possibilities.

4) The apportionment of state debt sums among families, the safekeeping of payments made, their verification, and their forwarding as appropriate.

5) The issuance of passports to colonists, their release into other statuses, and their departure abroad.

6) The confirmation of district and village officials in the manner established for this.

7) Judicial matters among colonists under the rules set forth in Part VIII of this Compendium.

In addition to the above-cited enactments: 1800 Jul. 26 (19492) art. 1, 6, 7, 8 and 9; 1812 Nov. 27 (24276[25276]) para. 4 and 8; 1817 Apr. 30 (26823); 1818 Mar. 22 (27312) art. III, para. 4 and 9; 1833 Jul. 1 (6298); 1849 Feb. 28 (23051).

39. The subjects and duties of the Overseers in the colonies are determined by the Chairman of the Committee for Foreign Settlers of the Southern Region.

1818 Mar. 22 (27312) art. III. para. 12; 1833 Jul. 1 (6298); 1845 Nov. 1 (19434).

40. The subjects of the District and Village Boards are the same as those assigned in state-owned settlements to village authorities.

This is evident from the general consideration of the Instruction for the internal organization of the New Russia] Colon[ies] 1801 May 16 (19873) and the addend[um] to it, 1803 Jul. 7 (20841).

41. Heads, Schulzes, and Beisitzers, being distinguished and respected above all other villagers, are obliged to promote their welfare and warn them against any harm; in the performance of their office, they must exact compliance strictly but with order, treat the villagers kindly, receive all their petitions patiently and attend to all their needs, be direct advocates for them, and by no means engage in bribe-taking, since they will be subject to prosecution and punishment under the laws both for neglect of their duties and for oppression of their subordinates.

1801 May 16 (19873) § 17.

42. The subjects of the village communal assembly are:

1) Village elections (a).

2) The release of colonists into other statuses (b).

3) The confirmation of agreements for the invitation of Priests (v).

4) The examination of petitions and complaints concerning communal needs and the issuance of rulings thereon (g).

5) The apportionment of taxes and dues (d).

6) The exclusion and removal from the colonies of settlers of dissolute conduct (e).

(a) 1801 May 16 (19873) §§ 9-11. - (b) 1812 Nov. 27 (25276). - (v) 1810 Dec. 3, Most Highly] confirmed] regulation] of the Comm[ittee] of Min[isters]; 1821 Dec. 31, Mo[st Highly] confirmed] regulation] of the Comm[ittee] of Min[isters]. — (g) 1801 May 16 (19873) § 38. - (d) 1808 Dec. 18 (23408); 1812 Mar. 12 (25031); 1818 Aug. 9 (27462). - (e) 1837 Jan. 11 (9857).

V. Procedure for the conduct of business.

43. In the conduct of business the Committee follows the procedure established in the Chambers of State Domains; matters are brought before the General Presence at the direction of the Chairman.

1845 Nov. 1 (19434) para. 5.

44. Boards must have: 1) special books for recording verbal orders, directives, and disputes among villagers and all matters generally within their administration; 2) protocols for recording received directives and dispatched reports, with numbers indicated on them.

1801 May 16 (19873) § 27.

45. Village Beisitzers meet once or twice a week, depending on need and at the summons of the Head and Schulz.

*Ibid., § 10.*

46. No resolution of a District or Village Board shall be recognized as valid unless the matter has been heard, deliberated, and decided by all the members together.

1803 Jul. 7 (20841) § 16. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 427

47. At the request of a District or Village Board, every colonist must appear before it immediately; upon the summoned colonist's arrival in the room in which the Schulzes and Beisitzers perform their office, he must, with due respect and without his hat, approach the village authorities, ask permission to explain his matter, and then decorously and without any commotion present his need; and when, after being heard, he is told to leave the room, he must do so at once and wait until he is called back in.

*Ibid., § 17.*

48. Whoever, upon being summoned by a District or Village Board, fails to appear before it at once without good cause, shall be liable under article 307 of the Code of Punishments; and in cases requiring urgency admitting of no delay, he may be brought to the Board under guard, and such disobedience is to be reported to the Guardianship Committee.

1803 Jul. 7 (20841) § 17; 1833 Jul. 1 (6298); 1840 Aug. 31 (13750); 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) art. 295.

VI. Nature and limits of authority.

49. The jurisdiction of the Guardianship Committee extends to all colonies already existing or hereafter to be settled on state lands in the three New Russia governorates and in the Bessarabian region, of whatever nation they may be, and to settlers from among Russian subjects, settled under the rules issued for colonists, only until such time as they are transferred to the general governorate department.

1818 Mar. 22 (27312) art. I, para. 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10; 1833 Jul. 1 (6298); 1846 Nov. 5 (20582); 1847 Mar. 5 (20977) para. 18.

50. The jurisdiction of a District Board embraces all settlements assigned to it. Village Boards, in turn, each administer the settlement in which they were established.

1801 May 16 (19873) §§8,9, 10, 13; 1803 Jul. 7 (20841) §§ 15, 16, 17.

VII. Subordination and procedure of communications.

51. The Guardianship Committee is directly subordinate to the Minister of State Domains.

1818 Mar. 22 (27312) art. II [II], para. 1; 1837 Dec. 26 (10834) para. 3.

52. The Committee receives instructions and proposals from the Minister of State Domains, and carries them out precisely.

The same enactments.

53. In all matters for which there is no exact enactment or instruction of the Minister, the Committee requests authorization from him.

*Ibid.*

54. In matters admitting of no delay, the Committee is guided by the interest of the treasury or the necessity of the settlers, reporting nevertheless immediately on everything to the Minister.

*Ibid.*

55. Communications between the Minister and the Committee are conducted according to the forms generally established for ministerial correspondence.

1818 Mar. 22 (27312) art. II, para. 5.

56. The Committee has no direct communication with other higher authorities, except for reports to the Senate on the receipt of decrees, which are sent to the Committee on an equal footing with other higher government offices. In all cases requiring communication with other offices, the Committee submits to the Minister of State Domains.

*Ibid., para. 8; 1837 Dec. 26 (10834) para. 3.*

57. Necessary communications with the Governor-General of New Russia and Bessarabia, as the chief local authority in civil matters, are conducted either directly by the Committee according to the forms used in the Ministries, or, by its resolutions, in the name of the Committee's Chairman. The Governor-General is obliged to satisfy all lawful requirements of the Committee in matters concerning colonists, while notifying it at the same time of his own dispositions.

1818 Mar. 22 (27312) art. II, para. 9-11.

58. In like manner the Committee communicates with the military authorities, whenever a matter touches upon their department.

*Ibid., para. 12.*

59. In matters depending on Governorate Chiefs and higher government offices, both of those governorates in which the colonies are located and of others, the Committee communicates on a footing of equality, and requests assistance or necessary information, and if it does not receive these in due time, applies to the chief authorities, and in necessary cases reports to the Minister of State Domains. The lower officials of the governorate in which the subordinate colonies are located, such as Town Governors, District Police Officers, and others, are obliged to comply immediately with the requirements of the Committee or of its Chairman in all cases in which such requirements pertain to their duties.

*Ibid., para. 13 and 14; 1837 Dec. 26 (10834) para. 3.*

60. The Chairman of the Committee, or, by his commission, a Member of the Committee, during the inspection of the colonies receives the complaints and petitions of colonists, resolves their requests, provided this is not contrary to the general provisions concerning colonists, and issues instructions to the local colonist authorities, on the condition only that such instructions and proposals remain in force until his return to the Committee, on whose confirmation their further effect depends.

1818 Mar. 22 (27312) art. II, para. 16 and 17.

61. The Committee sends to the Ministry weekly brief memoranda on the conduct of business and monthly statements both of matters decided and undecided, and of the sums in its disposal.

*Ibid., para. 6.*

62. All Schulzes within his Board are subordinate to the Head, and he must therefore diligently see to it that each of them carries out what is entrusted to him and performs his duty carefully.

*Ibid., para. 15.*

63. It is strictly prescribed that all orders or instructions sent by the authorities be carried out everywhere in all colonies with the utmost exactness, without delay or omission.

*Ibid. [1801 May 16 (19873)], § 34.*

64. An account of communal affairs is rendered by the Head and Schulzes upon their replacement by a new election.

<...>

*Ibid., § 12.*

Division Two.

On the local administration of the Saratov colonies.

65. The Saratov colonies are administered by the Saratov Office of Foreign Settlers, whose seat is fixed at Saratov.

1797 Jun. 30 (18021); 1833 Jul. 1 (6298) para. 3.

66. The Office consists of an Administrator and two Members.

1833 Jul. 1 (6298) staff [establishment]; 1840 (14108) staff [establishment], para. 26.

67. Attached to the Office are: a Secretary, Desk Officers, an Assessor, a Controller with an Assistant, an Accountant with an Assistant, a Registrar of Records, an Archivist, a Translator, an Official for Special Assignments, a Surveyor, Physicians, and clerical staff per establishment.

1845 Nov. 1 (19434) staff [establishment]; 1854 Jan. 6 (27841) staff [establishment].

68. The appointment and dismissal of the Administrator of the Saratov Office of Foreign Settlers and of its Members is at the discretion of the Minister of State Domains; all other officials of the Office and clerical staff are appointed and dismissed by the Office itself.

1833 Jul. 1 (6298); 1837 Dec. 26 (10834) para. 3.

69. The Office of the Saratov Foreign Settlers combines, in respect of the administration of the colonists, all the matters which in the southern colonies are handled by the Guardianship Committee.

1797 Jun. 30 (18021), (18022); 1802 Oct. 27 (20470).

70. The Office is placed in the same relation of dependence on the Governorate Chief as the Chambers of State Domains, in accordance with the general establishment concerning them.

1841 Nov. 3 (14989) para. 2.

71. In the conduct of business, the Office follows the procedure established in the Chambers of State Domains; matters are brought before the General Presence at the direction of the Administrator.

1845 Nov. 1 (19434) para. 5.

72. The Office is answerable for everything pertaining to the colonies; therefore the proper collection of taxes due to the treasury, matters of police and public order, inquiries and investigations occurring in the settlements, and the actual forwarding of all legally established levies to the Treasuries and to the Chamber of State Domains, remain under its special accountability.

1797 Jun. 30 (18022) art. 9.

73. The jurisdiction of the Saratov Office extends to all foreign colonies located in that governorate, excluding the Sarepta colony, whose local administration is defined below in Division V of this chapter.

*Ibid., art. 1 and 2.*

74. Under the department of the Office are: 1) Overseers of the settlements (colonies) (a), and 2) District and Village Boards (b).

(a) 1833 Jul. 1 (6298) staff [establishment]. — (b) 1800 Sept. 17 (19562); 1840 (14108) staff [establishment], para. 27.

75. Overseers of colonies are appointed and dismissed by the Office.

1833 Jul. 1 (6298) staff [establishment], note 1.

76. Overseers of colonies must assist the Office in the further improvement of the colonists' welfare and, without arbitrarily introducing any measures of their own, are obliged to endeavor to maintain proper subordination among the settlers toward the authorities, through constant observation that the order established in the colonies is unfailingly preserved, and to report to the Office any violation thereof, furnishing it with monthly statements of all special occurrences.

*Ibid.*

77. The Administrator of the Office, its Members, and all other officials receive maintenance fixed by the establishment. The establishment sum is made up by an eighteen-kopeck levy on the colonists subordinate to the Office. Surpluses from the establishment allocation are used, with the permission of the Minister of State Domains, for those purposes to which a similar sum is applied, made up of surpluses from the establishment allocations for the Chambers and District Administrations of State Domains.

1845 Nov. 1 (19434) staff [establishment], note; 1854 Jan. 6 (27841) staff [establishment], note.

78. District and Village Boards are organized entirely in conformity with those established in the colonies of the southern region, and likewise, in various particulars of administration, are obliged to conform to the rules prescribed for the local administration of the southern colonies.

This is evident from a comparison of the Instructions for the Saratov and New Russia colonists.

Division Three.

On the local administration of the St. Petersburg colonies.

79. For the administration of the St. Petersburg colonies an Overseer with an Assistant is appointed; one clerical servant is allotted to them.

1833 Jul. 1 (6298) staff [establishment]; 1840 (14108) staff [establishment].

80. The appointment and dismissal of the Overseer of the St. Petersburg Settlements and his Assistant is at the discretion of the Minister of State Domains.

1833 Jul. 1 (6298); 1837 Dec. 26 (10834).

81. The Overseer, his Assistant, and the Boards administer the colonists in application of the rules prescribed for the local administrations of colonists of the southern region and of Saratov.

1797 Jun. 20 (18006) para. 7-9; 1803 Jun. 16 (20798); 1809 Aug. 7 (23773).

82. Under the department of the Overseer are District and Village Boards, which are established on the same basis as those existing in the colonies of the southern region of Russia.

1803 Jun. 16 (20798) art. II, §§ 8-11.

83. The Overseer, his Assistant, and the clerical servant receive their salary at the expense of the settlers themselves, per establishment.

1833 Jul. 1 (6298) para. 8; 1840 (14108) staff [establishment]. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 432

84. The colonist-manufacturers of Tsarskoye Selo are not under the general administration of the St. Petersburg colonists, but are administered by the town authorities of Tsarskoye Selo (a), while the colonists of the Alexandria colony, settled on land of the palace department near Peterhof, are entirely under the jurisdiction of the Peterhof town authorities (b).

(a) 1819 May 28 (27818); 1825 Aug. 20 (30459). - (b) 1852 Jun. 9, Most Highest] command].

Division Four.

On the local administration of the Livonia colony,

settled in Wenden district.

85. The Livonia colonists are administered by Elders chosen from among themselves, whose confirmation they must submit, through the District Chief under whose department they are, to the Livonia Chamber of State Domains; they are subject to the general oversight of the rural police.

Conditions concluded with these settlers upon their establishment, 1766 Nov. 21, para. 17; 1783 Nov. 14 (15873); 1798 Jun. 14, rescript addressed to the Livonia] Civil] Governor] Richter; 1830 Sept. 23 (3938) art. 56 [6], para. 4 and 6; 1841 Jun. 12 (14643).

Division Five.

On the local administration of the colonies

of Members of the Evangelical Brethren Society, established in Sarepta

and in the three Baltic governorates.

I. Local administration of the Sarepta colony.

86. The Sarepta colony is administered solely by the Administrator of the Office of Saratov Foreign Settlers; it has, moreover, its own special Board, whose composition, under the name of the Board of the Evangelical Brethren Society, is defined in Part VIII of this Compendium.

1797 Jun. 20 (18011) para. 4; 1833 Jul. 1 (6298) staff [establishment]; 1834 Aug. 8 (7337).

II. Local administration of Members of the Evangelical Brethren Society

living in the Baltic governorates.

87. Members of the Brethren Society in the Baltic governorates are permitted to have their own authority among themselves, consisting of Elders.

1817 Oct. 27 (27113) para. 8.

88. These Elders are granted the right to have a special seal.

*Ibid.*

Division Six.

Local administration of the Belovezh colony

in Chernigov Governorate.

89. The Belovezh colony is under the authority of the Chernigov Chamber of State Domains, which is obliged to administer it according to the laws generally issued concerning colonists.

*PSZRI. Coll. 1809 Jul. 2 (23737) pt. 1; 1838 Apr. 30 (11189) pt. I, § 57; 1844 Aug. 8 (18132).*

Section Seven.

Local administration of the Ryebensdorf colony

in Voronezh Governorate.

90. The Ryebensdorf colony is subordinate to the Voronezh Chamber of State Domains.

*1833 Jul. 1 (6298) pt. 3; 1838 Apr. 30 (11189) pt. I, § 57.*

91. The colonists elect from among themselves a Vorsteher, who in everything relating to rural administration acts according to the rules prescribed for Volost Heads in state-owned villages.

*1833 Jul. 1 (6298).*

Section Eight.

Local administration of the colony of Württemberg settlers

in the Transcaucasian Territory.

92. Supervision of the Transcaucasian settlers is entrusted to the Expedition of State Domains under the Main Administration of the Transcaucasian Territory (a).

Note. The German colony located near Tiflis, beyond the Kuki suburb, has been assigned to the city of Tiflis, and moreover in 1852 it was decreed: having secured the colonists' present rights, to grant to each householder as private property the land and houses individually held by them, provided, however, that these may not be transferred to outside persons not belonging to the membership of the colony; 2) to permit colonists to resettle in other places and to pass into other estates; those who are discharged into another estate may remain in the estate of colonists only if they undertake to fulfill the obligations of both statuses, in accordance with articles 139 and 140 of this Statute; 3) to grant them, for internal administration, the right to have their own Board [Prikaz], on the model of the Rural [Board], on the former basis and with the former rights, on condition that the Board collect from them all state and municipal taxes and dues and remit them where required; 4) with the assignment of the German colony to the city of Tiflis, to place it under the jurisdiction of the Tiflis municipal police, on condition that the police adjudicate complaints against the actions of the Board according to the rules set forth in this Statute, within the limits of authority granted to the Colony Warden, and refer matters requiring the decision of higher authority to the Tiflis Provincial Board. The Viceroy of the Caucasus has been authorized, on this basis, to define in special rules the relations of the Tiflis police to the colonists and their Board (b).

(a) 1833 Jul. 1 (6298) pt. 2; 1841 Jan. 5 (14157) § 17; 1846 Dec. 14 (20701) pt. 7; 1849 Dec. 21 (23753) §§ 1, 2, 31, 32. - (b) 1852 Sept. 11 (26578).

93. The Colony Warden, the Bookkeeper — who is at the same time the officer in charge of colony affairs — and the clerical staff are appointed and dismissed by the Expedition of State Domains and receive salaries according to the staff schedule at the expense of the settlers themselves.

*1833 Jul. 1 (6298); 1838 Apr. 30 (11189); 1841 Jan. 5 (14157) § 17.*

94. The Colony Warden, being directly subordinate to the Expedition, acts under its direction on the basis of instructions given to him with the approval of the Viceroy of the Caucasus.

*1849 Dec. 21 (23753) §§ 1, 2, 31, 32.*

Section Nine.

Local administration of the German colony

settled in Stavropol Governorate near the mineral waters.

95. The German colony near the mineral waters, formed of settlers from Saratov, is under the authority of the Chamber of State Domains and is administered according to the general rules established for the administration of the Saratov foreign settlers and the colonists of the southern territory.

*1835 Jun. 26 (8271); 1838 Apr. 30 (11189).*

Section Ten.

Local administration of the German colony

near the town of St. Cross [Svyatoi Krest].

96. These colonists have a special Warden, maintained at their own expense, for their administration; in other respects they remain under the direct authority of the Chamber of State Domains.

*1817 Sept. 29 (27070) pt. 3; 1838 Apr. 30 (11189) pt. I, § 57.*

Section Eleven.

Local administration of the colony

founded by Scottish missionaries at Karras.

97. For the administration of the public affairs of the Karras colony, the colonists are granted the right to establish a Board [Uprava] by electing from among themselves one Elder and two members.

*1835 Jun. 26 (8271) pt. 4.*

98. The election is renewed every three years, and the Elder is chosen in turn: once from the Scottish and once from the Saratov colonists.

*Ibid.*

99. This colony is under the direct authority and protection of the Chamber of State Domains, which is obliged to watch over the welfare of the colonists and to prevent all discord among them.

*Ibid., pt. 5; 1838 Apr. 30 (11189) pt. I, § 57.*

Section Twelve.

Local administration of the colony of Basel missionaries

settled near the town of Shusha.

100. The local administration of the colony of Basel missionaries is in every respect based on the same rules as the administration of the Scottish colony (a). This colony is under the Administration of the Expedition of State Domains under the Main Administration of the Transcaucasian Territory (b).

(a) 1821 Dec. 17, Highest Order; 1828 Dec. 15 (2517). - (b) 1841 Jan. 5 (14157) § 17; 1846 Dec. 14 (20701) pt. 8.

Section Thirteen.

On the administration of the German colony near the town of Yeysk.

101. The German colony near the town of Yeysk is under the immediate subordination of the Investigative Authority of the Yeysk district, where it has been settled under the general authority and protection of the Host Administration of the Black Sea Host.

*1852 Mar. 20 (26077), pt. 5.*

102. For the settlement of cases, the observance of order, and the exact fulfillment of everything relating to the economy, police, and moral condition of the colonists, they appoint from among themselves Elders and Deputies.

*Ibid.*

103. The Elders and Deputies act on the basis of the duties defined above (arts. 16, 45, etc.) for Schulzes and Beisitzers.

*Ibid.*

104. The Investigative Authority acts with the powers of the Colony Warden (art. 75), and the Host Administration with the powers of the Guardianship Committee for Foreign Settlers of the southern territory.

*Ibid.*

105. Criminal cases of the colonists are referred for decision to the Host judicial bodies.

*Ibid.*

Section Fourteen.

On the administration of the Jewish colonies

located in the New Russia governorates.

106. The administration of the Jews in the New Russia governorates is subordinate to the Guardianship Committee for Foreign Settlers.

*1846 Nov. 5 (20582); 1847 Mar. 5 (20977) pt. 16.*

107. For local oversight, the Guardianship Committee appoints in each of the New Russia governorates a special Trustee with an Assistant, and in the settlements Boards [Prikazy] are established on the same basis on which they exist in the German colonies, under the direction of one of the best German colonists, or, in the absence of such, of trustworthy persons of another estate. Jewish settlements situated among the colonies of foreign settlers may be placed under the nearest Colony Warden (a).

<...>

(a) 1847 Mar. 5 (20977) pt. 17. <...>

108. In order to attract to the Jewish settlements German colonists who, by the example of their husbandry, might be of benefit to the Jews and, moreover, might be appointed to the offices of rural officials, the Guardianship Committee is authorized to invite the best householders among the German colonists to move to the Jewish settlements, as leaseholders, for an extended term, granting them plots of land from twenty to forty desyatinas for the first ten years, on an equal footing with the Jews, free of charge, and thereafter, over the course of the next DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 435

ten years, upon payment of half the quitrent. If, however, the colonists wish to remain on these plots beyond the twenty-year term, they shall be required to pay the full quitrent (a).

#### SECTION TWO. ON THE CIVIL STATUS OF COLONISTS.

##### CHAPTER ONE.

On entry into the estate of colonists.

110. Only those foreigners are recognized as colonists who are settled either on state-owned, or private, or purchased lands, in the capacity of farmers or of craftsmen needed in the agricultural condition; foreigners arriving singly or with families for trade and crafts, or for registration in some estate within towns, are in no way to be counted among them (a).

Note. From 1819, the recruitment of foreigners was firmly discontinued (b), but subsequently, at various times, the resettlement of foreigners to Russia was again permitted (v).

(a) 1763 Jul. 22 (11880); 1804 Feb. 20 (21163); Mar. 1 (21192); Apr. 12 (21254); 1817 Aug. 25 (27022); 1818 Mar. 22 (27312) art. 1, pt. 8; 1827 Oct. 5 (1443). - (b) 1819 Oct. 25 (27954); 1831 Jun. 2 (4617). - (v) 1842 Jan. 27 (15248); 1851 Nov. 19 (25752, a); 1852 Mar. 20 (26077).

111. The Ministry of State Domains is granted the right to admit into the number of colonists, singly and without any assistance from the treasury for settlement, but with the grant of the statutory allotment of land, such foreign émigrés as, having arrived from abroad to visit relatives long settled in Russia in the estate of colonists, or having been summoned by the latter, should for whatever reason wish to remain permanently in Russia in this same estate (a), and to authorize, at its discretion, the admission into the estate of colonists of foreign craftsmen useful to the colonies who, according to the certification of the local authorities, will be able to settle without assistance from the treasury, provided the colony community consents to their admission (b).

Note. In 1832 and 1837 the Chief Trustee of the colonies of the southern territory was authorized to admit into the said colonies, in order to replace families lost to plague and cholera, German emigrants departing from the Kingdom of Poland, without requesting special permission of the Ministry of State Domains for this, provided, however, that such emigrants be admitted to the class of colonists only with the consent of the communities and if they prove able to settle without any assistance from the treasury, taking care that, in order to avoid overcrowding in the settlement, their number should not exceed the number of colonists lost (v).

(a) 1831 May 6 (4539) pt. 4; 1837 Dec. 26 (10834). - (b) 1832 May 31 (5404); 1837 Dec. 26 (10834). - (v) 1832 Oct. 18 (5684); 1837 Dec. 26 (10834).

112. The rural craftsmen who are permitted to be enrolled among the colonists (art. 111) are: tailors, shoemakers, carpenters, blacksmiths, potters, coppersmiths, weavers, and masons; all other artisans and craftsmen who are of no use for village life may not be recognized as colonists.

*1804 Feb. 20 (21163).*

113. Upon entry into the estate of colonist, the foreigner must give a signed undertaking to observe the internal laws of the colony.

*1763 Jul. 22 (11880) pt. 5; 1764 Mar. 19 (12095) art. 4.*

114. Each colonist takes the oath of allegiance according to his own faith and rites.

*1763 Jul. 22 (11880) pt. 5.*

<...>

116. Mennonites, as well as Württemberg colonists of the Separatist sect, are not required to take the oath of allegiance, but are permitted to perform it in accordance with the rules of their faith, by a single verbal affirmation consisting in the pronouncement of the word "yes."

*1800 Sept. 6 (19546) pt. 1; 1819 Dec. 2 (28012).*

117. Should any colonist refuse to take the oath of allegiance, such persons, after everything that may have been given to them for their settlement has been taken back, shall be sent abroad immediately.

*1814 Jul. 17 (25622).*

118. The formal admission of persons wishing to join as members of the Evangelical Brotherhood Society in the Baltic governorates, and their solemn declaration thereof, is prohibited.

*1834 May 3 (7089) pt. 6.*

<...>

##### CHAPTER TWO.

On the civil rights of colonists.

120. All colonists settled in Russia enjoy freedom in the practice of their faith according to its statutes, teachings, and rites.

*1763 Jul. 22 (11880) art. 6; 1764 Feb. 25 (12057); 1800 Sept. 6 (19546) pt. 1; 1804 Feb. 20 (21163); 1806 Dec. 25 (22410) pt. 2; 1814 Jan., Privilege to the Warsaw colonists settled in Bessarabia, pt. 6; 1817 Oct. 27 (27113) pt. 1; <...>*

121. Colonists are permitted to establish churches on the lands allotted to them and to maintain at these the requisite number of Priests, Pastors, and other clergy; the construction of monasteries, however, is prohibited.

*1763 Jul. 22 (11880) art. 6; 1767 Mar. 27 (12852) art. 2; 1814 Jan. b. pt. Privilege to the Warsaw colonists settled in Bessarabia, pt. 6.*

122. Under pain of the full rigor of the law, colonists are forbidden to entice and draw into agreement with their own faith or society any persons living in Russia who profess the Orthodox faith or, in general, any other Christian faith.

*1763 Jul. 22 (11880) art. 6. — Cf. Statutes on Foreign Confessions.*

**<...> DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 437**

124. Colonists and their descendants are granted civil rights not only in their colonies, but throughout the Empire.

*1763 Jul. 22 (11880) art. 6; 1767 Mar. 27 (12852) art. 4; 1797 Jun. 20 (18011) pt. 5; 1800 Sept. 6 (19546).*

125. Colonists and their descendants enjoy full freedom and power to dispose of their own property within the state as they see fit.

*1797 Jun. 20 (18011) pt. 9; 1800 Sept. 6 (19546) pt. 8.*

126. In the event that a colonist exports acquired property abroad, he is obligated to pay a three-year tax on the capital accumulated in Russia, in whatever amount is declared according to his conscience and that of the authorities of the settlement in which he resides (a).

Note 1. The particular civil rights of colonists, both personal and in respect of property and obligations, are set forth in detail in Section III; the rights of colonists to engage in trade and to establish factories and works are set forth in Section V of this Code.

Note 2. Concerning the rights granted to foreign armorers of the Zlatoust factory, see the Mining Statute (b).

(a) 1797 Jun. 20 (18011) pt. 9; 1800 Sept. 6 (19546) pt. 8. - (b) 1832 Mar. 11 (5224); 1833 Feb. 28 (6018).

##### CHAPTER THREE.

On the acts of civil status of colonists.

127. The acts of civil status of colonists are: 1) revision tales [census lists], and 2) parish registers.

Cf. the laws cited in the following articles.

Section One.

Revision tales.

128. The census of colonists is conducted at the same intervals and on the same rules as the general census; and therefore the compilation and form of the revision tales, as well as their submission, is carried out in the same manner as prescribed by the Statute on the Census generally for all taxable estates subject to enumeration.

*1802 May 9 (20259); 1815 Dec. 8 (26013).*

Section Two.

Parish registers.

129. The duty of keeping accurate parish registers in the colonies, both of those married and of those born and deceased, is placed upon the Priests and Pastors, who must submit copies of them to the authorities at the end of each half-year.

*1800 Sept. 17 (18562[19562]) art. 3; 1801 May 16 (19873) § 8 [6]; 1803 Jun. 16 (20798) § 6.*

130. Heads and Schulzes are obliged to send lists and summary registers of births, marriages, and deaths annually by the first day of January.

*1801 May 16 (19873) § 26; 1803 Jun. 16 (20798) § 24.*

##### CHAPTER FOUR.

On the termination of the civil status of colonists.

131. The rights of civil status of colonists are terminated by: 1) transfer into other estates (a); 2) departure abroad (b); 3) a crime entailing the deprivation of all rights of status (v).

(a) Cf. the laws cited in the following articles. — (b) Cf. the laws cited in Sect. II, Ch. IV, Section VI. — (v) 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) art. 24.

132. It is forbidden to discharge colonists into other estates by entire settlements, or in such numbers from a single settlement that it might thereby fall into disorder.

*1812 Nov. 27 (25276) pt. 1.*

133. A colonist wishing to transfer into another estate must have: 1) a discharge from the local authorities, and 2) the written consent of the entire community.

*Ibid., pts. 2, 4 and 8; 1826 Jan. 31 (116).*

134. A discharge may be granted to a colonist by his authorities only when he has definitely chosen another way of life and presents a receipt from the Colony Warden for payment of the portion of the state debt owed by him.

*1812 Nov. 27 (25276) pts. 3 and 4.*

135. Should it be found that the reckoning of the debt of a discharged colonist was made incorrectly, responsibility shall be borne by the Warden who issued the receipt; once all accounts have been put in order, however, responsibility passes, in the colonies of the southern territory, to the Guardianship Committee, and in the Saratov colonies, to the local Office.

*Ibid., pt. 4; 1833 Jul. 1 (6298).*

136. The community has no right to detain a colonist if he presents someone else in his place to continue his husbandry.

*1812 Nov. 27 (25276) pt. 3 [2].*

137. One who has received a discharge, upon entry into another estate, enjoys, equally with others, all the rights and privileges granted to that estate.

*Ibid., pt. 5.*

138. On the basis of these rules, the local authorities discharge colonists into other estates on their own authority, without prior communication on the matter with the Minister of State Domains.

*Ibid., pt. 8; 1837 Dec. 26 (10834).*

139. Those discharged into another estate may at the same time remain in the estate of colonist, fulfilling the obligations of both statuses.

*1812 Nov. 27 (25276) pt. 6.*

140. On this basis, that is, with the fulfillment of the obligations of both statuses, colonists are permitted to be registered into other statuses both by entire settlements and in unlimited numbers.

*Ibid.*

< >

#### SECTION THREE. ON THE CIVIL RIGHTS OF COLONISTS.

##### CHAPTER ONE.

On the family customs of colonists.

Section One.

On marriage and divorce.

142. The necessary conditions for the marriage of colonists of the Protestant faith and the lawful impediments thereto, likewise the contracting of marriage, its dissolution, and matters of divorce generally, are defined in the Statute on Spiritual Affairs of Foreign Confessions, Book II.

*1832 Dec. 28 (5870) §§ 66-135.*

143. Divorce cases of colonists of the Protestant faith are conducted in the local Consistories.

*1808 Nov. 3 (23339); 1825 Mar. 13 (30292); 1828 Aug. 7 (2217 a).*

144. Colonists are exempted from payment of fees for stamped paper in dispensation cases.

*1828 Aug. 7 (2217 a) pt. 1.*

145. For the Württemberg settlers in the Transcaucasian Territory belonging to the Separatist sect, it has been decreed with regard to marriage that every one of them is free, upon reaching the age of majority — that is, seventeen or eighteen years for males, and fifteen or sixteen years for females — to enter into marriage with bridegrooms or brides of any age, provided they too have reached the age of majority.

*1829 Feb. 7 (2659) pt. 7; 1835 Feb. 12 (7853); 1841 Nov. 25 (15509[15059]).*

146. The term for entering into a new marriage, in the event that the whereabouts of one of the spouses is unknown, is set for these same colonists at five years from the time of their absence.

*1829 Dec. 3, Resolution of the Committee of Ministers.*

147. Such permission to enter into marriage is also allowed in cases where the remaining husband or wife, although the whereabouts of the other party may be known, has no prospect whatsoever of that party's return.

*Ibid.*

148. The investigation of the veracity of the statements of those settlers who, owing to the prolonged absence of a husband or wife, request permission to enter into another marriage, as well as the determination of the cases in which permission may be granted for the dissolution of a marriage on account of the prolonged absence of one of the spouses, is entrusted to the Transcaucasian Expedition together with a deputy from the ecclesiastical side.

*Ibid., and 1841 Jan. 5 (14157) § 17; 1849 Dec. 21 (23753).*

Section Two.

On guardianship and majority.

149. District Heads and Schulzes are obliged to appoint guardians over widows and orphans, and likewise over the idle and negligent, with the consent of their relatives and other householders; they themselves exercise chief guardianship over such persons.

*1800 Sept. 17 (19562) art. 16, pt. 2; 1801 May 16 (19873) § 29; 1803 Jun. 16 (20798) § 27.*

150. Heads and Schulzes must see to it that guardians perform their duty with diligence and honesty, and must require of them, twice a year, an accounting both of the increase and decrease of their household and of their conduct and diligence, personally, or through Beisitzers and Deputies, verifying their statements as often as possible and reporting everything to the authorities.

*Ibid.*

151. Heads and Schulzes must likewise appoint guardians over the estates remaining after extinct families, and, having handed over to them, by inventory, all the remaining property, report thereon to the authorities without delay.

*1800 Sept. 17 (19562) art. 16, pt. 2; 1801 May 16 (19873) § 27 [29]; 1803 Jun. 16 (20798) § 27.*

152. Guardianship over a minor ceases upon his reaching the age of twenty.

*1764 Mar. 19 (12095) art. 4.*

153. At that time the minor enters into all the rights of an adult, and the guardian is obliged to render a full accounting, receiving as a reward one-quarter of the movable property acquired under his administration.

*Ibid.*

154. Mennonites are granted the freedom to choose guardians according to their own rules.

*1800 Sept. 6 (19546) art. 8.*

##### CHAPTER TWO.

On the right to property.

Section One.

On the allotment of land to colonists from the treasury.

155. Colonists are allotted plots of land from the treasury in a quantity commensurate with the conditions concluded at the time of their settlement.

Note. The quantity of plots with which colonists have been allotted is as follows: 1) the Saratov colonists were allotted, for each soul according to the fifth revision, twenty desyatinas of land (a); 2) of the St. Petersburg colonists, the Sredniaya Rogatka and Izhora colonists were allotted thirty desyatinas each, while the Novo-Saratov, Strelna, Peterhof, Oranienbaum, Kronstadt, Kipen, and Yamburg colonists were allotted thirty-five desyatinas per family (б); 3) the Livonian colonists were allotted thirty desyatinas per family, or, by Livonian measure, sixty so-called "tonnenstellen" (в); 4) of the colonists of the Southern Territory: the Danzig, Swedish, and Yamburg colonists received land at fifteen desyatinas per soul (г); the Josephstal colonists were provided thirty-two and a half desyatinas per family (д); <...> while all the rest, both the New Russia and Bessarabia colonists, were allotted sixty desyatinas of land (ж); and the Mennonites sixty-five desyatinas per family (з); 5) the Scottish missionaries settled in Stavropol Governorate, the Basel missionaries located in the town of Shusha, and the colonists settled near the mineral waters in Stavropol Governorate, as well as near the town of St. Krest, were allotted sixty desyatinas per family (i); 6) the Chernigov colonists were assigned thirty desyatinas per family at the time of their settlement (и); 7) the Lutheran and Reformed pastors in the colonies were assigned one hundred twenty desyatinas of arable and hay-mowing land, and the [Catholic] priests sixty desyatinas, plus three desyatinas for a house and garden. Should DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 441

any of the priests wish to farm on a larger scale, they may be given a number of desyatinas equal to that assigned to the pastors; otherwise the excess is to be taken back from them (к).

(a) 1797 Jun. 30 (18[0]22) art. 8; 1797 Dec. 4 (18263); 1800 Sept. 17 (19562) para. 13; 1802 Sept. 4 (20403) para. 1, and Dec. 19 (20556) para. 1; 1808 Dec. 18 (23408). — (б) 1797 Jun. 20 (18006); 1805 Jul. 18 (21837); 1811 Sept. 12 (24776[24766]). — (в) Conditions concluded with the Livonian colonists, 1766 Nov. 21, art. 2. — (г) 1800 Apr. 6 (19372) arts. III, IV, V. — (д) Ibid., art. II. <...> — (ж) 1804 Feb. 20 (21163) para. 6; 1814 Jan., Privilege granted to the German colonists who relocated to Bessarabia from the former Duchy of Warsaw, para. 3. — (з) 1800 Apr. 6 (19372) art. 1, and Sept. 6 (19546) para. 2; 1801 May 23 (19887). — (i) 1817 Sept. 29 (27070); 1828 Dec. 16[15] (2517). — (и) This is evident from the special conditions concluded with these colonists at the time of their settlement. — (к) 1809 Aug. 25 (23807); 1810 Mar. 23 (24166); 1814 Jul. 17 (25622); 1817 Sept. 18 (27056).

156. In the plots of land allotted to colonists, only usable land is counted (a); all other lands, such as: rivers, lakes, marshes, bogs, chalk deposits, salt flats, clayey, sandy, and other places unsuitable for plowing and haymaking, are not counted at all, but are given over to the common possession of the whole village or hamlet (б).

(a) Cf. all the enactments cited above in this section. — (б) 1764 Mar. 19 (12095) art. 4, para. 6; 1802 Dec. 19 (20556) paras. 4 and 5.

157. Should precious metals be found anywhere, such places are excluded from the allotted holdings.

1764 Mar. 19 (12095) art. 4, para. 6.

158. For the Saratov colonists in particular it is prescribed that unusable lands be considered not only those recognized as such by the Land-Surveying Instruction, but also all those which, through trials conducted by the colonists over the course of several years, proved unsuitable either for plowing or for haymaking (a).

Note. In general, it has been decreed that the Saratov colonists be allotted, in addition to making up the existing shortfall against the twenty-desyatina proportion per soul of the fifth revision, such a quantity of land that a total of fifteen desyatinas would fall to each soul of the eighth revision (б).

(a) 1802 Dec. 19 (25556[20556]) paras. 4 and 5. — (б) 1840 Mar. 12 (13255).

Section Two.

On the colonists' right of possession of lands

allotted to them by the treasury.

159. All lands allotted for the settlement of colonists are assigned to them in indisputable and perpetually hereditary possession, but not as the personal property of any individual, but as the communal property of each colony.

1764 Mar. 19 (12095) art. 4, para. 4; 1767 Mar. 27 (12852) art. 1; 1797 Jun. 20 (18011) para. 2; 1800 Sept. 6 (19546) para. 2; 1806 Dec. 25 (22410) para. 3; 1817 Oct. 27 (27113) para. 3; <...>

160. Therefore the colonists may not, under any pretext whatsoever, sell or cede even the smallest portion of their land, nor execute any deeds thereof, without the will of the authority established over them, so that such lands may never fall into outside hands.

The same enactments.

161. All water mills situated on lands allotted to the colonies, regardless of whose funds were used to build them, constitute the property of the colonist communities of the very settlements to which the land belongs.

1801 Aug. 7 (19967); 1803 Mar. 28 (20692); 1808 Nov. 26 (23371).

162. Every colonist is permitted, without hindrance, to build a windmill on his own plot.

1808 Nov. 26 (23371).

163. Whoever wishes to build a windmill on communal land must without fail have permission from the entire settlement for this, and must pay it an annual quitrent for the site, not exceeding, however, sixty kopecks.

*Ibid.; 1829[1839] Nov. 19[9] (12867).*

164. Persons not belonging to the estate of colonists may under no circumstances have this right.

1808 Nov. 26 (23371).

165. Should, contrary to expectation, the peaceful possession within the colonies be disturbed by anyone, the Schulzes must immediately report to the Head or Overseer, describing the localities in which, by whom, and precisely what occurred, and these officials must report to their local administration, which is obliged to intervene and initiate proceedings in the order prescribed by law.

1800 Sept. 17 (19562); 1801 May 16 (19873) § 41; 1803 Jun. 16 (20798) § 39.

Section Three.

On the right to acquire land as property.

166. Colonists are permitted, for the expansion and improvement of their farming, to purchase and in general acquire land as property from private individuals.

1804 Mar. 1 (21192); <...>

167. With respect to such lands, colonists enjoy all the rights assigned to other rural inhabitants over their private property.

*Ibid.*

<...>

Section Four.

On inheritance and division of property.

169. The right of inheritance in lands allotted to colonists from the treasury is established on the following rules.

170. In plots of land allotted from the treasury, the youngest son generally inherits, and only in the case of his incapacity may the father designate another heir from among his elder sons, or from among relatives.

1764 Mar. 19 (12095) art. 4, paras. 1, 2.

171. When the father fails to do this during his lifetime, then, owing to the complete incapacity of the lawful heir, the local authority gives the plot to those of the near relatives who do not have plots of their own, or, in the case of equal rights among several persons, disposes of it by lot.

*Ibid., art. 4, para. 2. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 443*

172. Brothers and relatives are permitted, by mutual consent, to live in one household, on the condition, however, that one person alone, not all of them, be the master of that household.

*Ibid.*

173. Should colonists wish to divide their household, this may be permitted only with the authorities' permission; the Heads and Schulzes must ensure that such divisions serve the direct benefit of the settlers and do not disrupt their farming, and to this end, in presenting the names of those wishing to divide, they must specifically explain the good will of the parents or relatives toward this; also whether the party being separated off will have sufficient land, implements, and livestock to set up a household, and, in short, on this occasion it must without fail be observed that the first household is preserved intact and the latter is successfully established.

1800 Sept. 17 (19562) art. 38; 1801 May 16 (19873) § 31; 1803 Jun. 16 (20798) § 29.

174. If, after a colonist's death, only a widow with daughters remains, they hold the land plot jointly until the marriage of the mother herself, or of one of the daughters. The first man to enter such a household through marriage receives the hereditary land into permanent possession; however, before the marriage is concluded, he must give a written undertaking, witnessed by the Pastor and the elders of the settlement, that he will keep and support his mother-in-law in his household until her death, and his wife's stepdaughters and sisters until their marriage, unless they themselves wish to leave earlier than that time.

1764 Mar. 19 (12095) art. 4, para. 4.

175. Lands allotted to church servants of a colonist settlement do not pass by inheritance to their children, but fall to their successors in office.

*Ibid., para. 5.*

176. Each colonist may bequeath his own personal property according to his own will, without any restriction.

*Ibid., para. 3; 1797 Jun. 20 (18011) para. 9; 1800 Sept. 6 (19546) para. 8; 1817 Oct. 27 (27113) para. 9.*

177. If, by a will, movable property lawfully acquired in Russia by a colonist is bequeathed to his relatives residing abroad, the authorities of the settlement where the testator resided, having appraised such property in good conscience, are obliged first to pay out of it all debts, both to the treasury and private, and to deduct a three-year tax on the whole of the acquired capital.

1767 Mar. 27 (12852) art. 10; 1797 Jun. 20 (18011) para. 9; 1800 Sept. 6 (19546) para. 8; 1817 Oct. 27 (27113) para. 9.

178. In the event of a colonist's death without a will, the movable property remaining after him is divided on the following basis: the widow of the deceased is given one-fourth of it, all the daughters together receive an equal fourth, and the remainder is divided in equal shares among the sons.

1764 Mar. 19 (12095) art. 4, para. 3.

179. If a colonist of the Sarepta or Baltic Evangelical community dies without leaving heirs and without making a will, his estate is given over into the possession of the community of the whole colony without any levy to the treasury, subject only to the obligation to pay the debts of the deceased.

1797 Jun. 20 (18011) para. 9; 1817 Oct. 27 (27113) para. 9.

##### CHAPTER THREE.

On obligations.

180. Colonists may not, of their own accord, without the knowledge and permission of their authorities, enter into written obligations; the Heads and Schulzes must exercise oversight in this regard.

1800 Sept. 17 (19562) art. 31; 1801 May 16 (19873) § 21; 1803 Jun. 16 (20798) § 19; 1827 Dec. 31 (1673).

181. Colonists, especially those with small families, the sick, and those of insufficient means, are permitted to hire workers; but anyone unable to pay wages to workers is forbidden to hire them.

1800 Sept. 17 (19562) art. 23; 1801 May 16 (19873) § 37; 1803 Jun. 16 (20798) § 35.

182. Colonists enter into obligations with the treasury only in matters pertaining to their trade, according to the rules laid down in the Civil Laws.

1830 Oct. 17 (4007) §7.

183. Written obligations of colonists must be executed at public offices and with the permission of their authorities.

1827 Dec. 31 (1673).

184. Should it be discovered that any written obligation of a colonist was executed without the permission of his authorities, the entire responsibility for it must fall upon the person or office that approved it, and the act itself is deemed invalid.

*Ibid.*

185. A contract for leasing out water mills on a farming-out basis may be executed only with the general consent of the colonists of the settlement to which the mill belongs, and for a term of not less than one year and not more than twelve years.

1803 Mar. 28 (20692); 1808 Nov. 26 (23371).

186. All written obligations or contracts, agreements, promissory notes, powers of attorney, wills, accounts, and other instruments, whether executed among colonists themselves or with outside persons, must be written on the prescribed stamped paper, without which no public office or authority of theirs shall accept them or take any action upon them.

1800 Sept. 17 (19562) art. 81[31]; 1801 May 16 (19873) § 21; 1803 Jun. 16 (20798) § 19.

#### PART FOUR. ON THE DUTIES AND TAXES OF THE COLONISTS.

##### CHAPTER ONE.

On exemption.

187. Colonist communities, at the time of their initial settlement, are granted years of exemption from the performance of duties and the payment of all kinds of taxes.

1763 Jul. 22 (11880) art. 6, para. 2; 1767 Mar. 27 (12852) art. 8; 1797 Jun. 20 (18011) para. 11; 1800 Sept. 6 (19546) para. 9; 1804 Feb. 20 (21163) para. 2; 1806 Dec. 25 (22401[22410]) para. 4. DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 445

188. The term of exemption established for the colonies is determined by the conditions concluded at the time of the colonists' settlement and in the charters granted to them.

Note. Although the manifesto of 1763 Jul. 22 (11880) granted settlers coming to Russia a thirty-year exemption, and subsequently, by the decree of 1806, Sept. 27 (22293), a ten-year exemption from the payment of taxes was established for all foreigners in general wishing to settle in the Empire; nevertheless, from the particular conditions concluded with the colonists at their settlement and from the charters granted to them, it appears that the term of exemption established for each colony differs, namely: the Saratov and Sarepta colonists enjoyed a thirty-year exemption (**) (a). Of the St. Petersburg colonists, the Sredniaya Rogatka, Izhora, and Novo-Saratov colonists received five years of exemption, while the Yamburg colonists received thirteen years (б); all the rest, namely: the Strelna, Kipen, Peterhof, Oranienbaum, and Kronstadt colonists, as well as the manufacturer-colonists of Tsarskoye Selo, were given ten years of exemption (в). Of the Livonian colonists, those who received into their possession fully cultivated lands were assigned four years of exemption, while those who received lands partly cultivated and partly uncultivated were assigned six years; the rest, who received one-third or one-quarter cultivated land and two-thirds or three-quarters uncultivated land, were given eight years of exemption; while those who settled on vacant and wholly uncultivated land enjoyed an exemption of from nine to ten years (г). The Scottish missionaries settled at Karras in Stavropol Governorate, and the Basel missionaries settled near the town of Shusha, were granted thirty years of exemption (д). The Mennonites and all the other New Russia and Bessarabia colonists received ten years of exemption (*[**]) (е); with the exception of: 1) the Württemberg and Bavarian émigrés who settled in Bessarabia in 1817 and received seven years of exemption, (ж) <...>

Note 2. To the Marienfeld colonists settled beyond the Caucasus, a ten-year exemption from the payment of taxes and duties was Most Graciously granted, counting it from 1849; and to the six-year term for which they were given in 1845 a loan of one thousand five hundred rubles interest-free for setting up their households, a further four years of exemption were added, after which it was prescribed that the collection of the loan monies should begin in 1856, over the course of ten years, in equal annual installments [(и)].

(a) 1763 Jul. 22 (11880); 1767 Mar. 27 (12852); 1808 Dec. 18 (23408). — (б) 1797 Jun. 20 (18006); 1805 Jul. 18 (21387[21837]); 1807 Dec. 4 (22706). — (в) 1820 Feb. 2 (28124) and Apr. 24 (28252); 1823 Jul. 13 (29541); 1825 Aug. 20 (30459). — (г) Conditions concluded with these colonists, 1766 Nov. 21, art. 3. — (д) 1806 Dec. 25 (22410) para. 4; 1828 Dec. 15 (2517); 1840 Apr. 10 (13386[13368]) § 5. — (е) 1809[1800] Apr. 6 (19372); Sept. 6 (19546) para. 9; 1804 Feb. 20 (21163) para. 2: Privilege to the Warsaw colonists settled in Bessarabia in 1841[1814], para. 1; <...> 1825 Mar. 9 (30281); 1830 Oct. 14 (3993). — (ж) 1817 Aug. 2[28] (27029). <...> — (и) 1852 May 2, resolution of the Committee of Ministers.

(**) Subsequently, the exemption for the Sarepta colony was extended to 1806; 1797 Jun. 20 (18111[18011]) para. 11.

(*[**]) As, according to the inspection of the Mennonite settlements conducted in 1800, they were found to be in a state of poverty, and, owing to the cramped conditions in the Khortitsa area, some families were at that time relocated to other lands, the ten-year exemption granted to the Mennonites was extended for those who remained on the sites of their earlier settlement by a further five years, and for those relocated, by ten years (1800 Sept. 6, Charter granted to the Mennonites [19546] art. 9).

189. Colonists relocating to Stavropol Governorate to the mineral waters are given a five-year exemption from the payment of taxes and the performance of all duties, counted for each family from the day of arrival in Stavropol Governorate.

1828 Dec. 15 (2517).

##### CHAPTER TWO.

On the duties in kind of the colonists.

Section One.

On the recruitment duty.

190. All colonists settled in Russia, together with their descendants, are forever exempted from the recruitment duty, both in kind and in money (a).

Note. In 1851 it was decreed: that the Mennonites, who in future may be permitted by the government to settle in Russia in new colonies under the rules set forth in this Statute, be granted exemption from military service for a period of twenty years from the time of settlement, and that, upon the expiry of this term, they be assessed, by calculation, a permanent monetary levy, under the name of recruitment money [(б)].
