## No. 116. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A RUSSIAN CENTRAL SCHOOL IN THE VOLGA COLONY OF KATHARINENSTADT, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1858)

33341. — June 27. Most highly confirmed decision of the Committee of Ministers, announced to the Senate by the Minister of State Domains. — On the establishment, in the colony of Katharinenstadt, of a single central school, in place of the two schools existing in the colonies of Saratov and Samara governorates, for the training of teachers proficient in the Russian language.

On the basis of the Most highly confirmed decision of the Committee of Ministers of November 7, 1833 (6551), explained in the note to article 258 of Volume XII of the regulation on colonies of foreigners in the Empire, there existed in the Volga colonies of foreign settlers two schools for teaching the Russian language, with the aim that the pupils, upon completion of the course, should teach the children of colonists in Russian in the village colonist schools, in which the schoolmasters teach in German, with the time divided between both languages in all grades.

In order to better achieve this useful goal, as a result of personal discussions with the Administrator of the Saratov Office of Foreign Settlers, as well as with the local clergy and the elders of the colonist communities, having recognized it useful, instead of the two aforementioned schools, each accommodating twenty-five pupils, to establish one school in the colony of Katharinenstadt for fifty pupils and to somewhat expand the course of instruction by introducing subjects necessary for the training of teachers and useful in rural life, the Minister of State Domains submitted a report on this subject to the Committee of Ministers, proposing:

1. Instead of the two schools existing in the colonies of Saratov and Samara governorates for the training of teachers proficient in the Russian language, to establish one central school in the colony of Katharinenstadt for fifty pupils, — and

2. While maintaining in force the procedure, indicated in the Most highly confirmed decision of the Committee of Ministers of November 7, 1833, for the assignment of colonist children to the school and their maintenance, to introduce in this school, in addition to the subjects of instruction already established therein, in accordance with the petition of the local authorities and for the benefit of the pupils, also the teaching of History and Geography, with regard to Russia, in as brief a form as possible, as well as a general concept of Natural History, leaving it to the Ministry of State Domains to determine the scope of instruction in these subjects by a special program.

Now, by an extract from the journals of the Committee of Ministers of June 3 and 27 of this year 1858, the Minister of State Domains has been informed that the Committee resolved: to confirm his report, and that the Sovereign Emperor Most highly deigned to approve the Committee's decision.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXII. P. 796.*

## No. 117. DECREE OF ALEXANDER II ON THE TAXES AND OBLIGATIONS OF THE NOVGOROD COLONISTS (1858)

33951. — December 24. Personal decree, announced to the Senate by the Chairman of the Department of Appanages on March 31, 1859. — On the taxes and obligations levied on the colonists of the villages of Gorelovo, Nikolaevskoye, and Aleksandrovskoye, which have passed into appanage administration from the former districts of plowman-soldiers of Novgorod governorate.

Together with the former districts of plowman-soldiers in Novgorod governorate, there also passed into appanage administration the three colonies of foreign settlers located in these districts — the villages of Gorelovo, Nikolaevskoye, and Aleksandrovskoye — in which, according to the tenth census, there are registered six hundred nineteen male souls and four thousand one hundred fifty desyatinas of arable land.

Upon the most humble report of the Minister of the Imperial Court, the Sovereign Emperor, on December 24, 1858, Most highly deigned to command: that the following taxes be levied henceforth on the colonists settled in the aforementioned villages:

1. The general poll tax at eighty-six kopecks and, for the construction of means of communication, at nine kopecks per soul, on an equal footing with all colonists who, residing on state lands, have been equalized with state peasants, namely: the Saratov, the German colonists of Stavropol governorate, the New Russian, and the Bessarabian colonists.

2. General zemstvo monetary obligations — on an equal footing with the other rural inhabitants of Novgorod governorate, since all colonists settled in the Empire participate in the payment of monetary zemstvo obligations, except for members of the Evangelical Brotherhood in Sarepta and in the Baltic governorates, the Livonian colonists of Wenden district, the Scottish colonists of Stavropol, and the Srednyaya Rogatka, Izhora, Novosaratovka, and Yamburg colonists of St. Petersburg governorate.

3. A land tax at the rate established for the Novosaratovka and Strelna colonists, at fifty-seven and a quarter kopecks per desyatina of arable land in their use; the collection of this tax in full is to begin on January 1, 1862, and until then only two-thirds thereof is to be collected, that is, thirty-eight kopecks per desyatina, in order thereby to ease the colonists' transition to their future payments.

Accordingly, payments in the aforementioned colonies will amount, until 1862, to four rubles nine and three-quarter kopecks per soul, including in this figure treasury taxes, zemstvo obligations, and the land tax calculated according to the land due to each soul, and from 1862 this sum will rise to five rubles thirty-eight kopecks.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXIII. Part 2. P. 559.*

## No. 118. DECREE OF ALEXANDER II ON THE SETTLEMENT OF PRUSSIAN MENNONITES IN SAMARA GOVERNORATE (1859)

34077a. — January 22. Personal decree, announced to the Senate by the Administrator of the Ministry of State Domains on July 30 of this year. — On the settlement of Prussian Mennonites on the Samara-Stavropol lands.

On the occasion of the transfer to the jurisdiction of the Ministry of State Domains of lands of Samara governorate, formerly used by the Kalmyks of Stavropol governorate and the Orenburg Cossack Host, amounting to more than three hundred thousand desyatinas, it was Most highly commanded, on February 14, 1844 (17716), that from among these lands, named the Samara-Stavropol lands, there be set aside, among other things, a special plot of up to thirty thousand desyatinas for foreign colonists from among the Mennonites and Scots.

As a result, the Minister of State Domains, while in Samara governorate in 1857, after preliminary discussions with the representatives of the Prussian Mennonites, instructed the Head of Samara governorate to enter into closer agreement with them concerning the conditions under which this settlement of Mennonites might be permitted, DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 495

and then, upon receiving a reply, submitted this proposal for the Most High consideration of His Imperial Majesty, proposing for his own part:

1. For the first instance, to settle on the Samara-Stavropol lands only one hundred Mennonite families, with the Ministry being allowed, subsequently, when the success of this undertaking corresponds to expectations, to increase this settlement with new arrivals from abroad.

2. To carry out the settlement of the Mennonites on the aforementioned lands on the same basis on which the settlement of their co-religionists in Novouzensk district was permitted in 1851, but with the provision that those resettling be granted an exemption from the payment of taxes and obligations for three years, this term being reckoned from the expiration of one year from the time of arrival at the places designated for them.

3. Upon the expiration of this term, to subject these Mennonites to taxes and obligations on an equal footing with state peasants, including a quitrent tax for the land based on an assessment of its profitability; — and

4. In case of approval of this proposal, to communicate with the Minister of Foreign Affairs regarding the recruitment of Mennonites from abroad.

This matter, by Most High command, was submitted for consideration to the Council [Committee] of Ministers, and, upon its report, the Sovereign Emperor, on January 22 of this year, Most highly deigned to command that the aforesaid proposal be carried out.

On this basis a draft of the conditions was drawn up, on which it was proposed to permit the settlement in Samara governorate of up to one hundred Prussian Mennonite families, and thereupon, through the mediation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Russian Consulate General in Danzig was authorized to issue passports for travel to Russia to Mennonites undertaking resettlement, subject to the following procedure:

1. Prior to the issuance of a passport, to present to each family wishing to resettle the conditions under which this resettlement is permitted, together with a signed statement expressing full agreement to submit to these conditions, and likewise to require from each such family, as security for their firm settlement in Russia, a deposit of not less than three hundred fifty Prussian thalers and a release consent from the Prussian government.

2. To forward the signed statements and the money to the Ministry of State Domains for further disposition, both regarding the reception of the settlers and the payment of the money to them upon arrival at the place of settlement; — and

3. To begin issuing passports not before a party of not less than twenty families has been formed (by special agreement of the Ministries of Foreign Affairs and State Domains, however, it was permitted to issue passports to fifteen families for the first party), bearing in mind that the resettlement, for the first instance, should be limited to one hundred families.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs now reports that the Russian Consulate General in Danzig has forwarded: a) the signed statement of fifteen Prussian Mennonite families agreeing to submit to the conditions under which their resettlement to the Empire is permitted; b) a list of the Mennonite families to whom passports have been issued; and c) a bill of exchange for five thousand four hundred sixty-eight rubles seventy-five kopecks in silver, constituting the required deposit from each family.

Seeing from this report that the implementation of the proposed resettlement of Mennonites to Samara governorate, with the Most High consent, has already begun, I have the honor to report the foregoing to the Governing Senate for its information, and to submit herewith a copy of the conditions under which this resettlement is being carried out.

Conditions under which, on the basis of the Most High command of January 22, 1859, the settlement, for the first instance, of up to one hundred Prussian Mennonite families in Samara governorate is permitted, on the free treasury plot designated for this purpose.

1. Mennonites who, on the basis of the Most High command of January 22, 1859, wish to resettle in Russia on the plot of the Samara-Stavropol treasury lands, are obliged to obtain a release consent from their Government, and, upon presenting it to the Russian Consulate General in Danzig, on which will depend the issuance of their passports, to deposit therewith, as security for the settlement of each family, not less than three hundred fifty Prussian thalers, which, after deduction of forwarding expenses, will be returned to them upon arrival at the place of settlement.

2. Likewise, they must give a signed statement that they will constantly bear in mind the purpose of their being called to Russia — to serve as models for other agricultural classes, following in this respect the example of their Molochna brethren.

3. For the first step toward resettlement, a party consisting of not less than twenty families must be formed, since only under this condition will it be possible to lay a firm foundation for the colony.

4. All rules existing in the Statute on Colonies, both in general for foreign settlers and in particular for Mennonites, concerning which no reservation is made in the present conditions, shall extend also to the resettling Mennonites.

5. They and their descendants shall be granted the freedom of exemption from entering military service. In place of the fulfillment of this obligation, they shall be subject, upon the expiration of twenty years of exemption reckoned from the time of their assignment to the estate of foreign settlers, to a permanent levy known as the recruit levy. This levy shall be calculated according to the value of a recruit as established by the Government, which is presently set at three hundred rubles in silver.

6. They shall be granted an exemption from the payment of taxes and obligations for three years, this term being reckoned from the expiration of one year from the time of arrival at the places designated for them, such exemption, however, not extending to the levies for the maintenance of the administration and the communal levy, with which the resettling Mennonites must be charged from the time of their assignment to the estate of foreign settlers, and of which the latter levy is apportioned by the communities themselves for private needs relating to their internal organization.

7. Then, upon the expiration of these years of exemption, in addition to the aforementioned payments, they must be charged with all taxes and obligations on an equal footing with state peasants, including the quitrent tax for the land, which shall be due according to an assessment of the profitability of the lands designated for them, which assessment may itself change according to circumstances affecting the profitability of the land.

8. On the plot designated for the Mennonites, up to sixty-five desyatinas shall be allotted for each family, provided that the survey of family plots be carried out at the expense of the resettlers and in accordance with the requirements of model farming. One-twentieth of the total amount of land, however, may be allotted DOCUMENTS_______________________________________________________________________________ 497

in plots of a smaller size per family than the sixty-five-desyatina proportion.

9. The plot designated for the settlement, for the first instance, of one hundred Mennonite families, shall be withdrawn from other use, but only the amount of land actually needed for each family shall be allotted to the Mennonites as they arrive; the remaining area, pending settlement, shall be let out as a treasury quitrent item, with the Mennonites being permitted to retain about two thousand desyatinas thereof for themselves upon payment of the existing quitrent. In general, one year before resettlement, the Mennonites must announce how much land they will need for the following year for settlement, so that this land may be allotted without delay upon their arrival.

10. The resettlement of Mennonites to the aforementioned lands, should there prove to be no fewer than twenty families willing, may be begun in the spring of 1859.

11. The right of distilling and selling beverages in the districts of their settlement, granted to Mennonites already settled in Russia, may not extend to Mennonites resettling under these conditions: they must submit in this respect to the tax-farming conditions in force in Russia; — and

12. Should the settlers so desire, the Ministry may petition for them to be granted the right of duty-free import into Russia of goods to the value of duties of up to one hundred rubles in silver per family, in addition to used clothing, linen, agricultural implements, and the like, which are subject, under customs regulations, to free passage.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXIV. Part 3. Suppl. Pp. 3-5.*

## No. 119. DECREE OF ALEXANDER II ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AUXILIARY FUNDS IN THE VOLGA COLONIES (1859)

35266. — December 21. Imperial decree, announced to the Senate by the Minister of State Domains. — On the establishment of auxiliary funds attached to the colonist districts of the Saratov-Samara colonies.

The Sovereign Emperor, upon the most loyal report of the Minister of State Domains, on the 21st day of December 1859, was Most Highly pleased to command:

1. To open auxiliary funds attached to those colonist districts of the Saratov-Samara colonies in which there are on hand communal or orphan and other capital sums belonging to the colonists, in the amount of not less than one thousand rubles per district.

2. To apply to these funds, which combine the operations of receiving deposits and issuing loans, the regulation on peasant auxiliary and savings funds, with the admission, subject to the authorization of the Minister of State Domains, of such changes as may, owing to local circumstances, be recognized as useful, chiefly with regard to the amount of loans, which, in view of the solvency and degree of prosperity of the colonists, ought to be increased above the amount established for state peasants.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXIV. P. 373.*

## No. 120. DECREE OF ALEXANDER II ON THE ECONOMIC RIGHTS OF FOREIGNERS IN RUSSIA (1860)

35880. — June 7. Imperial decree, given to the Senate, published on 20 June. — On the rights of foreigners residing in Russia.

The Manifesto of 1 January 1807 (22418) established certain restrictions on the trading rights of foreigners permanently or temporarily residing in Russia. At present, with the gradual improvement of means of communication and the rapid development of international trade relations, these restrictions no longer correspond to the needs of the time. On the other hand, in the principal European states Our subjects, like all foreigners in general, are permitted to engage in commercial affairs on equal terms with native inhabitants. Taking into consideration the beneficial influence which affording greater convenience for the use of foreign capital as well, in enterprises of every kind, may have on all branches of the national wealth, and desiring to give a new token of Our particular concern for the prosperity of trade, agriculture, and industry generally in the Empire, as well as to show foreign Powers just reciprocity, We have deemed it right to grant to foreigners residing in Russia the same rights in this respect as are already enjoyed by Our subjects in the principal European states.

In consequence of this, in accordance with the opinion of the State Council, We command:

1. Foreigners are permitted to enter all merchant guilds on an equal footing with native subjects of the Empire, and thereafter to enjoy all trading rights by guild granted to the Russian merchantry (Articles 77–107 of the Trade Statute of the Digest of Laws, ed. 1857, Vol. XI).

<...>

2. The dwellings and stores of foreigners and all lands belonging to them are protected by the general laws. The search of their homes and the examination of their trading books may be undertaken only on the basis of the same rules as are prescribed for Russian subjects of the same estate.

3. Foreigners may acquire, whether by purchase or by inheritance, testament, deed of gift, grant from the treasury, and the like, movable and immovable property of every kind, with the sole exception of those which, under the laws in force, may be owned only by persons belonging to the Russian hereditary nobility and by foreigners who have obtained the rights thereof; — and

4. Foreigners, except Jews, may, by power of attorney from the owners of populated estates, administer such estates in the capacity of stewards. They may also rent and hold in lease, on possessory tenure, and generally, on the basis of any obligations not forbidden by law, immovable populated and unpopulated properties, subject only to those conditions and restrictions established for native subjects of the Empire (Civil Laws, Book IV, Part III, Chapter 2).

The Governing Senate will not fail to make the appropriate arrangements for the execution of the foregoing.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXV. P. 706–707.*

## No. 121. RULES FOR THE SETTLEMENT OF PRIVATELY OWNED LANDS IN CRIMEA BY FOREIGN IMMIGRANTS, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II

36298. — November 8. Most Highly confirmed Rules on the procedure for settling proprietary lands in Crimea by immigrants from abroad.

Resolution of the Committee of Ministers, Most Highly confirmed on 8 November 1860, announced in a Senate decree of 27 January 1861. — The Governing Senate heard: a report of the Minister of State Domains, of the 4th of this January, that in consequence of a petition of the nobles of the Crimean peninsula concerning the provision of various means for maintaining the order of the proprietary estates there, he, the Minister, submitted to the Committee of Ministers a proposal on measures for the settlement of the peninsula in view of the departure of Tatars abroad, together with a draft of Rules on the settlement of proprietary lands in Crimea by foreign immigrants. By extracts from the journals of the Committee of Ministers, of 25 October and 8 November 1860, he, the Minister, was informed, first, that the Committee, independently of these rules, resolved: to allow Crimean landowners to hire foreign workers on the basis of the general regulations in force in Russia concerning personal hire, permitting the issuance to such foreigners of passports for the entire term of hire, which by law may not extend beyond five years; and second, to grant to those foreigners who wish to settle permanently in Crimea and adopt Russian subjecthood all the rights and privileges provided for this case in the draft Rules drawn up by the Ministry of State Domains. The Sovereign Emperor was Most Highly pleased to confirm the Resolutions of the Committee. He, the Minister of State Domains, in reporting such Most High commands to the Governing Senate, also submits the above-mentioned Rules for the settlement of proprietary lands in Crimea by foreign immigrants, with the request that the Governing Senate be so good as to make the appropriate arrangement for their publication. — Ordered: For the due execution of this Most High command, to instruct by decree the Taurida Provincial Board and Treasury Chamber, which decrees are to inform the Chamber of Criminal and Civil Court there and to notify the Governor-General of New Russia and Bessarabia and the Ministers of State Domains, Internal Affairs, and Finance, with the Rules attached, as submitted with the aforementioned report of the Minister of State Domains.

Rules.

1. The settlement of proprietary lands in Crimea by foreigners, by voluntary agreement with the owners, is carried out on the basis of the right already granted to all landowners under Article 510 of the Statute on Colonies of Foreigners in Russia; but for the purpose of facilitating this matter, the following are established, in addition to and amendment of the existing rules:

2. Landowners are permitted to enter into preliminary agreements with foreigners who present a certificate from the appropriate Russian Imperial Mission that there are no obstacles to their settlement in Russia, with the exclusion thereafter of any mediation of the Government in this matter, which, in particular, will make no solicitations of foreigners whatsoever.

3. The foreign immigrants accepted by landowners must be settled not in whole masses or contiguous districts, but only in villages and hamlets, alongside Russian settlers, or on farms and homesteads, being in every case subject not to separate but to the general local administration and management applicable to other estates.

4. All foreign immigrants who settle permanently on proprietary lands in Crimea and adopt Russian subjecthood shall enjoy freedom of religion, and, together with their sons then living, shall be exempt for life from conscription duty; but if there should be Mennonites among them, then, upon expiry of the twenty-year exemption period, they shall be subject, in place of personal performance of military service, to a permanent monetary levy, called the recruit levy, following the example of the Mennonites settled in Samara Governorate.

5. In the contracts concluded by landowners with foreign immigrants, the following must be set forth with due clarity and definiteness: First, all obligations mutually accepted, on the part of the owner, with regard to the lands, forests, and other lands granted for the use of foreigners, and, on the part of the latter, with regard to the performance by them of various duties in favor of the owner. In this connection it must be precisely indicated at whose expense the resettlement and travel costs will be borne — whether at the landlord's or the colonists' own expense; in the former case, the sum intended to be allotted for that purpose must also be indicated. Second, the mutual settlements between landowners and immigrants in the event that the latter, upon expiry of the term of the agreement, should not wish to renew it.

In this connection the following rules are to be observed:

a) The duties of the immigrants in favor of the owner of the land may be of three kinds:

a) monetary, or land quitrent; b) in kind, or remuneration of the owner with produce of the land; and c) personal, or labor in favor of the owner.

b) The amount of the monetary payment for the use of the land, as well as remuneration in produce of the land, depends on the mutual terms of the contracting parties, and is fixed in the contract itself.

c) If the immigrants undertake to perform personal agricultural labor in favor of the owner of the land, such labor must be precisely specified in the contract.

d) Contracts must be concluded, in conformity with Article 515 of Volume XII, Part 2, for a term of no more than twenty years; they are drawn up on stamped paper of the lowest denomination, under the signatures of the contracting parties and two witnesses as required by law.

e) The said contracts, concluded by landowners with foreign immigrants, must be certified in the District Courts, which, however, are obliged to certify these contracts only upon confirmation, from examination of the documents, of the actual ownership of the lands by the former.

f) The contract remains in force even if the land occupied by the immigrants should pass, for whatever reason, to another owner, and the heirs or acquirers may not alter the terms except with the consent of the settlers themselves; the immigrants, for their part, are permitted to transfer their rights and obligations under the contract to another person, but only with the consent of the owner of the land; — and

g) Disputes concerning the terms are settled by the appropriate government offices, under the general laws. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 501

6. Immigrants who, under the terms concluded with landowners, obtain permanent settlement and enter Russian subjecthood are required to be enrolled in the free taxable estate not enjoying special rights; for their enrollment in the rank of colonists, with the rights and privileges granted to the latter under former statutes, is not permitted.

7. The enrollment of these immigrants is carried out in the generally established manner, by order of the Treasury Chamber, to which the landowner must, immediately upon conclusion of the contracts, report both the number of settlers established on his lands and the time of their settlement, for its appropriate action.

8. Those of the foreign immigrants who wish to enter the free rural estate require no admission resolutions whatsoever, but upon expiry of the exemption years, they are personally liable for the timely payment of taxes and duties, which must without fail be included in the contracts concluded with landowners.

9. For the possible acceleration of the settlement of the depopulated lands of the Crimean peninsula, there is granted to foreigners who, in compliance with these conditions, conclude contracts with landowners, settle permanently on their lands, adopt Russian subjecthood, and choose their estate at that time, — exemption from payment of treasury taxes and monetary duties and from the performance of general duties in kind: to those settling in 1861, 1862, 1863, and 1864, for a period of ten years, and to later settlers, for a period of five years, from the time of the enrollment of these persons in the estate chosen by them.

10. Foreign immigrants are not deprived of the right to enjoy these privileges even if, before the expiry of the exemption period, they should move to another piece of land, or, while remaining Russian subjects, should change the estate originally chosen.

11. Upon expiry of the exemption period, these persons are subject to treasury taxes and monetary duties, and are drawn into the performance of general duties in kind, on equal terms with the estate to which they belong. For their diligence in the performance of duties in kind, as falling upon the land, the owner on whose land they are settled by contract is answerable, concerning which the immigrants enter into mutual agreement with the landowners.

12. The Minister of State Domains is authorized, in communication with the chief administration of the New Russian territory, to permit additions or changes to these rules which, according to circumstances and the indications of experience, shall be recognized as corresponding to the views of the Government and the benefit of the matter itself, with a view to the more successful settlement of Crimea.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXV, Part 2. P. 224–226.*

## No. 122. DECREE OF ALEXANDER II ON THE INCORPORATION OF THE GERMAN COLONY NEAR TIFLIS INTO THE CITY (1861)

36968. — May 3. Imperial decree, announced to the Senate by the Acting Minister of Justice. — On the conversion of the Tiflis German colony into a part of the city of Tiflis.

In 1852 the late Chairman of the Caucasus Committee, the late Adjutant General Prince Chernyshev, communicated to the Ministry of Justice the Most High command, proposed to the Governing Senate on 11 September 1852 (26578), on the incorporation into the city of Tiflis of the German colony located near it, with the concentration of the internal administration of the colony in a single Office, subordinate to the jurisdiction of the Tiflis city police.

Now the Sovereign Emperor, upon the submission of the Viceroy of the Caucasus and the resolution of the Caucasus Committee, has been Most Highly pleased to command:

1. To convert the Tiflis German colony into a part of the city of Tiflis, and to include the colonists settled therein among the city inhabitants.

2. To transfer the plots of land now held by the colonists to them in full ownership, providing each owner with a title deed.

3. Upon the alienation of a plot of land in the colony, to grant the new owner of that plot the right, proportional to the size of the land acquired, to use the water-supply ditch constituting the communal property of the colony, with the obligation imposed upon him to participate to the same extent in the maintenance of the ditch.

4. To distribute the treasury debt owed by the Tiflis colonists, subject to repayment, in the amount of 6,671 rubles 88 kopecks silver, among the owners of the plots of land, in proportion to the size of these plots; to preserve, for those of them who retain their lands for themselves, the extensions of time granted to the colonists for the repayment of the debt, but those who sell such lands are obliged, at the very time of the sale, to pay in full the portion of the debt attributable to the plot being alienated.

5. To now cancel the irrecoverable treasury debt of the Tiflis colonists, in the amount of 8,042 rubles 30¾ kopecks silver, which would have been subject to collection from them in the event of their departure from the borders of the Russian Empire or voluntary withdrawal from colonist status.

6. To subject the colonists, upon their inclusion among the city inhabitants of the city of Tiflis, to all the levies and duties established for the inhabitants of that city, at the same time abolishing the reductions in the rate of the land tax granted to the colonists on the basis of the Most High decree to the Governing Senate of 16 June 1831.

7. To allow colonists wishing to continue enjoying the personal rights granted to their estate to enter the membership of other colonist communities with the consent of the latter, expressed in a proper resolution. Such colonists are not to be deprived of the right to own immovable property in Tiflis, but on condition that they bear duties under both estates, in accordance with Article 139 of the Statute on Colonies of Foreigners in the Empire, Digest of Laws, Vol. XII, Part II, ed. 1857.

8. To leave the Tiflis colonist church, with the pastor's residence, and the school for the time being in their previous condition, for the use of colonists of various colonies residing in Tiflis, obliging these persons to keep them in proper repair; — and

9. To close the Rural Office of the Tiflis colony, with the abolition of the community of Tiflis colonists.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXVI, Part 1. P. 703–704. No. 123. RESOLUTION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON RAISING LEVIES ON THE GERMAN COLONISTS OF NEW RUSSIA AND BESSARABIA, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1861)*

37062. — May 30. Most Highly confirmed resolution of the Committee of Ministers, announced to the Senate by the Minister of State Domains. — On increasing the levy on the German colonists of the New Russian governorates and the Bessarabian region.

The Sovereign Emperor, upon the submission of the Minister of State Domains and the resolution of the Committee of Ministers, on the 30th day of May of this year, was Most Highly pleased to command: that the colonists of the three New Russian governorates and the Bessarabian region, beginning with this year 1861, be assessed, in place of the levy now paid, a levy for the repayment of the treasury debt for settlement, in the following amounts:

1. German colonists of the Bessarabian region, 10 rubles per family.

2. German colonists of Yekaterinoslav Governorate: those of Josephstal and Rybalskoye, 2 rubles 85 kopecks, except two families of the latter, now paying 4 rubles 28 kopecks, who shall pay 5 rubles, and the colonists of Yamburg, 2 rubles 30 kopecks per family.

3. German colonists of Kherson Governorate: a) of the Liebental and Berezan districts, 15 rubles per family; b) of the Kuchurgan and Glückstal districts and the separate colony of Hoffnungstal, 10 rubles; and c) of the Swedish district, 3 rubles.

4. German colonists of Taurida Governorate: a) of the Neusatz and Zürichtal districts, 3 rubles, except the colony of Hertsenberg, which for the time being remains at the former rate of 1 ruble 42¾ kopecks per family, and b) 382 families of colonists of the Molochna district, from 10 to 20 rubles per family.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XXXVI, Part 1. P. 800.*

## No. 124. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON SANCTIONS AGAINST COLONISTS WHO RESETTLED WITHOUT PERMISSION FROM ONE GOVERNORATE TO ANOTHER, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1865)

41919. — March 14. Most Highly confirmed opinion of the State Council, published on 26 April. — On depriving colonists who resettled without permission from one governorate to another of the rights granted to colonist status.

The State Council, in the Department of State Economy and in General Session, having examined the submission of the Minister of State Domains on supplementing Article 435 of the Statute on Colonies, resolved: to confirm the present submission and, in consequence thereof, to supplement Article 435 of the Statute on Colonies (Digest of Laws, Vol. XII, Part 11, ed. 1857) with a note of the following content: "Colonists who resettle without authorization and without the permission of the Minister of State Domains from one governorate to another are excluded by the chief local administration from colonist status and, forever losing the rights and privileges granted to that status, are enrolled among other taxable estates on general grounds."

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was Most Highly pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the General Session of the State Council on supplementing Article 435 of the Statute on Colonies, and commanded its execution.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XL, Part 1. P. 315.*

## No. 125. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON THE OPENING OF THE LESNOI KARAMYSH SCHOOL IN THE VOLGA REGION, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1866)

43535. — August 5. Most Highly confirmed resolution of the Committee of Ministers, announced to the Senate by the Minister of State Domains. — On authorizing the communities of colonies of foreign settlers of Saratov Governorate to open, in the colony of Lesnoi Karamysh, a school under the name: "Lesnoi Karamysh Central Russian School."

Upon the submission of the Minister of State Domains and the resolution of the Committee of Ministers, the Sovereign Emperor, on the 5th day of August of this year, was Most Highly pleased to command:

1. To authorize the communities of colonies of foreign settlers of Saratov Governorate to open, in the colony of Lesnoi Karamysh, a school, under the name "Lesnoi Karamysh Central Russian School," for approximately 150 day pupils, in two grades with a preparatory grade attached to them, with the subdivision of the latter and of the first, lowest grade each into two parallel sections, with four teachers from among persons who have completed a course at one of the higher, or at least secondary, educational institutions, and who hold approving certificates for the rank of teacher of a district school.

2. To grant the four teachers of the Lesnoi Karamysh Central Russian School the service and pension rights of teachers of district schools of the Ministry of National Enlightenment; — and

3. To authorize the Ministry of State Domains, on these principal grounds and with the funds allocated by the communities, to establish the school, conforming, with regard to the internal economic and educational organization of this institution, to the regulation and program in force in a similar school in the colony of Yekaterinenstadt, Samara Governorate.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XLI, Part 1. P. 988.*

## No. 126. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A LUTHERAN AUXILIARY FUND IN THE BESSARABIAN COLONY OF TARUTINO, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1866)

43642. — September 16. Most Highly confirmed resolution of the Committee of Ministers. — On the establishment, in the colony of Tarutino, Bessarabian region, of a District Committee of the auxiliary fund of the Evangelical Lutheran parishes.

A memorandum of the Minister of Internal Affairs, of 20 August, was heard, on the establishment in the colony of Tarutino, Bessarabian region, of a District Committee of the auxiliary fund of the Evangelical Lutheran parishes. DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 505

The Committee resolved: to request the Most High consent of His Imperial Majesty to the implementation of the conclusion of the Minister of Internal Affairs.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 16th day of September 1866, was Most Highly pleased to consent to this.

Memorandum. — On the basis of § 12 of the Most Highly confirmed Statute, of 8 August 1858 (33454), of the auxiliary fund of the Evangelical Lutheran parishes in Russia (appendix to Article 603, Vol. XI, Part I, of the Digest of Laws, per the 1863 Continuation), District Committees are established, to assist the Central Committee of the said fund, in consistorial districts, in cities where Evangelical Lutheran Consistories are located, and in other more significant places.

The Evangelical Lutheran General Consistory, reporting that five Lutheran colonial parishes in the Bessarabian region and their preachers desire the establishment of a special District Committee in the colony of Tarutino, as the largest of all the said colonies, explained that, as the population in these colonies, which already number 28,000 inhabitants, increases, new settlements are being founded and there arises a need for the establishment of new parishes. For the construction of churches and schools in these parishes, given the insufficiency of the means of the inhabitants of the new settlements, assistance from the original parishes is necessary; but the readiness to make contributions in these parishes would be strengthened by the assurance that the sums collected would be applied to the needs of their own district, in particular to providing the new settlements with churches and schools. Meanwhile, at present all contributions of the colonists of the Bessarabian region go to the Odessa District Committee, which is located across the Dniester River, at a very great distance from the Bessarabian colonies, and which could confine its activity to the colonies of Kherson Governorate. Therefore the General Consistory requests authorization for the establishment of a District Committee of the auxiliary fund in the colony of Tarutino.

Concerning this petition of the General Consistory, the Minister of Internal Affairs communicated it for the opinion of the Minister of State Domains, who, having considered all the local circumstances, replied that he not only saw no obstacle, but for his part found it very useful to open, in the Bessarabian colony of Tarutino, a District Committee of the auxiliary fund of the Evangelical Lutheran parishes in Russia.

Although, on the basis of the above-cited § 12 of the Most Highly confirmed Statute, of 8 August 1858, of the auxiliary fund of the Evangelical Lutheran parishes in Russia, District Committees of this fund are established only in cities, yet since the establishment, in accordance with the petition of the Evangelical Lutheran General Consistory, in the colony of Tarutino, Bessarabian region, of a District Committee of the auxiliary fund of the Evangelical Lutheran parishes in Russia, is recognized as very useful by the Minister of State Domains, the Minister of Internal Affairs deemed it proper to request Most High consent to this, which he has the honor to submit for the consideration of the Committee of Ministers.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XLI, Part 2. P. 25–26.*

## No. 127. DECISION ON SUBORDINATING THE COLONIES OF A NUMBER OF GOVERNORATES TO THE GENERAL INSTITUTIONS FOR PEASANT AFFAIRS, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1866)

44000. — December 17. Highest-confirmed resolution of the Main Committee on the organization of the rural estate, communicated to the Senate by the Minister of State Domains. — On the transfer of the colonies of foreign settlers to the jurisdiction of the general institutions for peasant affairs.

The Sovereign Emperor, upon the report of the Minister of State Domains and the finding of the Main Committee on the organization of the rural estate, on 17 December 1866, was Highest pleased to command:

1. The colonies of foreign settlers, which are under the jurisdiction of the Chambers of State Domains in the governorates of Voronezh, Novgorod, Samara, St. Petersburg, and Chernigov, shall henceforth be transferred to the jurisdiction of the general provincial and district institutions, as well as the local institutions for peasant affairs.

2. Until such time as the question of the organization of public administration in the colonies, as well as of the courts, is resolved in the established manner, the currently existing rules on the internal public administration of the colonies (Code of Laws, Vol. XII, Part II, Statute on Colonies) shall remain in force, while the authority belonging to the Chambers of State Domains, with respect to colonies passing out of their jurisdiction, for the adjudication of litigation among colonists (Arts. 6, 38 clause 7, 485 and 488 of the Statute on Colonies) shall be transferred to the local Provincial Presences for Peasant Affairs.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XLI. Sec. 2. P. 408.*

## No. 128. DECREE OF ALEXANDER II ON THE PROCEDURE FOR ISSUING PASSPORTS TO FOREIGN SETTLERS (1868)

45922. — May 29. By Imperial Name, communicated to the Senate by the Minister of State Domains on the 31st of that same May, published on 4 July. — On the procedure for issuing passports to foreign settlers.

The Governing Senate heard the report of the Minister of State Domains of 31 May 1868, of the following content: upon his, the Minister of State Domain's, most humble report concerning measures to remove the difficulty encountered by foreign settlers, under the temporary rules currently in force, in obtaining passports in a timely manner, the Sovereign Emperor, on the 29th day of May of this year, was Highest pleased to command: until the confirmation of a new statute on the colonies of foreign settlers, it is to be established, as an amendment to the temporary rules set forth in the note to Article 424, Vol. XII, of the Statute on Colonies, that — "The issuance of passports to foreign settlers shall be carried out by the District and Village Boards, provided that the blank forms for passports and the stamped paper for tickets, as needed, shall be obtained by the District Boards directly from the District Treasuries, for cash." ## No. 129. RULES FOR THE ORGANIZATION OF SETTLER-PROPRIETORS (FORMER COLONISTS), CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1871)

49705. — June 4/16. Highest-confirmed Rules on the organization of settler-proprietors (former colonists) settled on state lands in the governorates of St. Petersburg, Novgorod, Samara, Saratov, Voronezh, Chernigov, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav, Kherson, and Tavrida, and in the Bessarabian oblast.

Opinion of the State Council, Highest confirmed on 31 May 1871, published on 5 July. — The State Council, in General Assembly, having examined the finding of the Main Committee on the organization of the rural estate concerning the draft rules submitted by the Acting Minister of State Domains on the organization of foreign rural settlers (colonists) settled on state lands, opined:

I. The draft Rules on the organization of settler-proprietors (former colonists) settled on state lands in the governorates of St. Petersburg, Novgorod, Samara, Saratov, Voronezh, Chernigov, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav, Kherson, and Tavrida, and in the Bessarabian oblast, as corrected in accordance with the comments of the Main Committee and the State Council, shall be submitted for the Highest confirmation of His Imperial Majesty.

II. Upon the Highest confirmation of these rules following:

1) The Minister of State Domains shall be authorized to take the appropriate measures for their implementation and to draw up the necessary instructions and rules for this purpose, in agreement, where required, with the relevant Ministers, and, on matters exceeding the limits of their authority, to seek resolution through the Main Committee on the organization of the rural estate.

2) The Minister of State Domains shall be authorized, in agreement with the Chief Administrator of the Second Section of His Imperial Majesty's Own Chancellery and the Minister of Internal Affairs, to undertake a review of the Statute on Colonies of Foreigners (Code of Laws, Vol. XII) and, should there be found in this Statute such rules as would retain their force even under the operation of the new rules concerning the former colonists, to consider the possibility of transferring these rules to the relevant parts of the Code of Laws, with the subsequent repeal of the separate Statute on Colonies.

3) The Ministers of State Domains, of Internal Affairs, and of Public Education shall be authorized, by mutual agreement, in the established manner, to submit a proposal for the transfer, as appropriate, of the duties assigned to the Saratov Office and the Guardianship Committee of Foreign Settlers with respect to the chief ecclesiastical guardianship and the manner of filling vacant parishes, as well as concerning the organization of the school system in the villages of the settlers (colonists).

4) The Minister of State Domains shall be authorized to make all such changes in the composition of the Saratov Office and the Guardianship Committee, as well as of the institutions subordinate to them, as experience shall show to be necessary for the speediest completion of the matters remaining within the duties of these institutions, so that, upon the completion of such matters, all existing special institutions for the administration of foreign settlers shall be abolished.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was Highest pleased to confirm and ordered to be executed the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council, upon the draft Rules on the organization of foreign settler-proprietors (former colonists) settled on state lands in the governorates of St. Petersburg, Novgorod, Samara, Saratov, Voronezh, Chernigov, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav, Kherson, and Tavrida, and in the Bessarabian oblast.

Rules.

I. On the public organization and administration of settler-proprietors

(former colonists) and on their transfer to the jurisdiction of the general provincial and district,

as well as local institutions for peasant affairs.

1. Settler-proprietors (former colonists), whether under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of State Domains or removed from its jurisdiction on the basis of the Highest-confirmed resolution of the Main Committee on the organization of the rural estate of 17 December 1866 (44000), shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the general provincial and district, as well as local institutions for peasant affairs, on the grounds and in the manner indicated in the following articles.

Note. The present rules do not extend to the colonies of Jewish agriculturalists of the Kherson and Yekaterinoslav governorates, or to the colony of the Evangelical Brethren of Sarepta, Saratov governorate, concerning which special rules will be issued.

2. The said settlers shall be included among the rural inhabitants and, being assigned to the category of peasant-proprietors, shall retain, on the grounds indicated below, the personal privileges which they have hitherto enjoyed.

3. Rural societies and volosts (townships) of settlers shall be organized on the grounds set forth in Articles 40–45 of the General Statute on Peasants of 19 February 1861 (36657), and in the supplementary enactments thereto, subject to the following rules:

a) The colonist districts now existing shall each form a separate volost, with the exceptions indicated below in points b and c.

b) Villages (colonies) forming part of a district situated in several counties shall form separate volosts by county, which may nonetheless continue to preserve the existing connection among themselves in matters of economy.

c) A village which, owing to the distance involved, cannot be included in a volost formed by other villages, shall constitute a separate volost if it contains about three hundred or more revision souls, or else it shall be attached to the nearest peasant volost.

d) A change in the composition of volosts formed on the basis of the present rules shall be permitted, with the authorization of the provincial authorities, upon petition of the societies and in compliance with the rules of the General Statute on Peasants, as well as with what is established in point b of the present article. DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 509

4. The public rural and volost administration, as well as the volost court of the settlers, shall be organized on the basis of Articles 46–129 of the General Statute on Peasants and the supplementary enactments thereto, subject to the following rules:

a) The Village Assembly shall be composed of the settler-householders belonging to the rural society, possessing a homestead, with or without field allotments, and of all persons elected to village offices. In villages where household land tenure exists, settlers possessing neither a homestead nor a field allotment (landless) shall send to the Assembly one elected representative for every ten adult workers.

Note. Settlers assigned to the society who, without participating in the use of communal lands, acquire plots in ownership outside the boundaries of the communal allotment, as well as elected representatives of landless settlers (point a), shall have a voice at the Assembly in all matters concerning them, such as: the apportionment of state taxes and of zemstvo and public obligations, deliberations on communal needs and benefits, the election of officials, and the disposition of communal quitrent items and land holdings generally used by the whole society; but they shall not take part in matters concerning the lands of the communal allotment held by individual householders.

b) Each category of settlers among those indicated in point a and the note thereto — namely, settler-householders, settlers possessing only homesteads, settlers who, without participating in the use of communal lands, acquire plots in ownership outside the communal allotment, and finally the elected representatives of landless settlers — shall be permitted, under the chairmanship of the village elder or his deputy, to convene separately in private meetings, independently of the general Village Assembly, to discuss matters concerning exclusively themselves and not the whole society.

c) If any rural society, owing to the size of its population and its commercial and industrial activity, deems the convening of an Assembly of all householders to be difficult, such a society may entrust the resolution of certain matters within the jurisdiction of the Village Assembly to a small Village Assembly. The small Village Assembly shall be composed of the officials required to attend the Village Assembly, and of elected representatives — one for every ten households. These representatives shall be appointed for a term of one year. The matters indicated in points 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, and 17 of Article 51 of the General Statute on Peasants may not be entrusted to the small Assembly. Landless settlers shall send to the small Assembly one elected representative for every hundred adult workers, or, if their number is smaller, not less than one representative.

d) In addition to the matters indicated in Article 51 of the General Statute on Peasants, the Village Assembly shall have jurisdiction over: 1) authorizing the transfer of household plots from one householder to another; 2) the disposition of communal quitrent items; and 3) the administration of common forests and plantations.

e) Among the matters requiring the consent of not less than two-thirds of all settlers entitled to vote at the Village Assembly, in addition to those indicated in Article 54 of the General Statute on Peasants and in points a and b of Article 19 of the present rules, are: 1) the establishment of a small Village Assembly, and 2) authorization to lease out communal lands and income-producing items.

f) In villages where household land tenure exists, the landless settlers of each rural society shall send to the Volost Assembly one elected representative for every twenty adult workers. But the number of such representatives shall in no case exceed the number of representatives from householders.

g) In a volost consisting of several villages, and having a population of more than 2,000 souls, the establishment of a small Volost Assembly shall be permitted, by resolution of the Volost Assembly adopted by not less than two-thirds of all settlers entitled to vote at the Assembly. This Assembly shall be composed of the officials required to attend the Volost Assembly under Article 71 of the General Statute on Peasants, and of elected representatives: one for every twenty-five households, and one for every fifty adult workers among the landless settlers. If, however, the societies find that the small Assembly, even at such a size, would be too numerous, then, upon their resolutions, the Provincial Presence for Peasant Affairs shall authorize the appointment of representatives to the small Assembly from a greater number of households and, where there are landless settlers, from a greater number of adult workers, provided that each village and settlement has one representative at the Assembly, and that the landless do not exceed the householders in the composition of the Assembly. Representatives to the small Volost Assembly shall be replaced each year by a new election. The small Assembly may, by decision of the general Volost Assembly, be entrusted with all matters within the latter's jurisdiction, except for the election of volost officials and judges of the Volost Court.

h) Rural societies within a volost that have joint land use, or that constitute a separate parish, etc., may, in matters concerning such land tenure, parish, etc., convene, under the chairmanship of the Volost Elder or one of his assistants, private Assemblies, independently of the general Volost Assemblies. Representatives for such private Assemblies shall be appointed one for every ten households or, at the discretion of the societies concerned, in a smaller number.

i) In addition to the matters indicated in Article 89 of the General Statute on Peasants, matters within the jurisdiction of the Volost Board shall include: 1) arrangements, on the basis of resolutions of the Volost Assembly, concerning communal lands and quitrent items belonging to the whole volost or jointly to several rural societies within the volost; 2) arrangements concerning insurance against fire, hail, and the like, and the payment of compensation for damage caused; and 3) arrangements concerning the operations of savings and loan funds and the recoveries arising from these operations.

Resolutions of Village and Volost Assemblies, as well as of Volost Courts, shall be drawn up, and all record-keeping in the public administration shall be conducted, in the Russian language.

j) In volosts where the hearing of cases by the Volost Court at the seat of the Volost Board may encounter difficulty, the Volost Assembly shall be authorized either to designate in advance those villages within the volost to which the court is obliged to travel at fixed intervals for the hearing of cases, or to permit the court itself to send special divisions of the court, consisting of not less than 3 judges, with the powers of a volost court, to those villages of the volost where, owing to the accumulation of cases or the convenience of summoning the persons required for the hearing, the need for this shall arise.

k) The current officials of the present District Administrations, with the exception of those occupying positions to be abolished as a result of the reorganization of these administrations, shall remain in their positions, until the expiration of their terms of service, and shall retain the compensation they receive even if the said positions are given a different title (as, for instance, Volost Elder instead of District Head or District Elder); but the election of judges to the Volost Courts must be undertaken immediately.

l) In cases where volosts are formed consisting of settlers (former colonists) and other rural inhabitants, as well as in the case of the division of the present districts into smaller volosts, new elections of all volost administration officials must be held.

5. The payment by settlers of taxes and monetary levies, as well as the performance by them of obligations, shall be carried out on the following grounds:

a) Settlers are obliged to pay, on the existing grounds, the state taxes and, until the issuance of title deeds, the quitrent or land tax for the lands in their use, and also to perform, on general grounds, without further exemptions in this respect, the zemstvo and other monetary and labor obligations. In addition, they shall be assessed a levy for the maintenance of the local institutions for peasant affairs, on the general basis established for this levy. Likewise, until special arrangements are made, those special levies which exist in some colonies, in the form of a public levy for the maintenance of special colonist administrations, central Russian schools, clergy, etc., shall not be abolished.

Note. Exemption from the obligation of billeting troops shall be retained for the settlers, from the date of issuance of the present rules, for a further 10 years. With respect to the conscription obligation, the statutes currently in force with regard to colonists shall retain their force until the issuance of a general law on military service.

b) The calculation of the said levies and the drawing up of assessment sheets for them shall be carried out in the manner now existing, until special arrangements are made on this subject.

c) Insurance levies for the compensation of fire victims shall be made on the basis of the special statutes in force among the settlers (former colonists).

d) With respect to the communal obligations of the settlers, the provisions set forth in Articles 177–186 of the Highest-confirmed General Statute on Peasants of 19 February 1861, and the supplements thereto, shall apply.

e) The proper fulfillment by the settlers of the taxes and levies due from them, as well as of the zemstvo and communal obligations, shall be ensured in the manner indicated in Articles 187–191 of the Highest-confirmed General Statute on Peasants of 19 February 1861, and the supplementary enactments thereto.

6. Grain reserves belonging to the societies, remaining under the jurisdiction of these societies, shall, as regards the manner of their disposition, be subject to those rules established for peasant-proprietors.

7. Communal capital shall be placed at the disposal of the societies concerned on the grounds established for peasant-proprietors. Accordingly, capital belonging to individual rural societies shall be transferred directly to the communal funds of each society, as appropriate; while capital constituting the joint property of several societies shall be deposited, as contributions from the latter, in local (volost) credit institutions, on the basis of resolutions of the Volost Assemblies concerned (general or private, depending on the ownership of the capital), retaining the special purposes assigned to this capital.

8. The volost funds existing among the settlers, on various grounds and under various names (orphans' funds, savings and loan funds, etc.), shall continue their operations under the rules currently in force for them.

9. The discharge of settlers from rural societies and volosts, as well as their enrollment therein, their assessment for taxation, their removal from the tax rolls, and their transfer from one tax assessment to another, shall be carried out in the manner established in Articles 130, 132–140, 142, 146, and 147 of the General Statute on Peasants of 19 February 1861 and the supplements thereto, subject to the following rules:

a) Only persons enjoying, personally and by status, the same rights as are assigned to the members of the society into which they are being enrolled may be assigned to societies of settlers.

b) Within 10 years from the date of issuance of the present rules, settlers may: 1) enroll in other estates, remaining, if they wish, in their former estate; in this case, acquiring all rights and privileges under both estates, they shall discharge all obligations and assessed levies under both estates; 2) renounce Russian subjecthood and leave Russia, without payment into the treasury of any part of the capital they have acquired; upon the expiration of the 10-year term, however, they shall become subject to the general laws of the Empire regarding the renunciation of Russian subjecthood.

10. The reorganization and establishment, on the grounds set forth above, of the rural and volost administrations of the settlers shall be carried out, under the immediate supervision of the Governors and the Provincial Presences for Peasant Affairs, by special Commissions composed of the local Peace Mediator, an official of the Ministry of State Domains, and an official appointed by the Governor, applying the procedure indicated in Articles 10 and 11 of the Imperial Decree by Name given to the Governing Senate on 19 February 1861 on the promulgation and implementation of the Statutes on Peasants. This reorganization shall be completed within three months from the time of the distribution of the settlers' volosts among the mediation districts, and, in those mediation districts established specifically for these settlers, within three months from the appointment of the Peace Mediators.

11. As the volost and rural administration in the societies of settlers (former colonists) is reorganized, on the grounds set forth in the preceding articles, these settlers shall pass into the jurisdiction of the general provincial and district administrations, as well as the local institutions for peasant affairs, on the basis of the Highest-confirmed Statute on these institutions of 19 February 1861.

12. The distribution of the settlers' villages among the mediation districts, and the formation, where necessary, of new districts, shall be entrusted to the Provincial Presences for Peasant Affairs. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 513

13. The transfer, on the grounds set forth, of the settlers (former colonists) currently under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of State Domains to the jurisdiction of the general provincial and local institutions for peasant affairs, shall be carried out, by mutual agreement of the Ministers of Internal Affairs and of State Domains, within six months from the date of the promulgation of the present rules.

14. All contested judicial matters of the settlers, arising prior to the issuance of the present rules in the Provincial Presences for Peasant Affairs, in the Saratov Office, and in the Guardianship Committee of Foreign Settlers, and not yet concluded by proceedings, shall either be terminated on the basis of Articles 21 and 22 of the Highest-confirmed opinion of the State Council of 10 March 1869 (46840) on the procedure for the conduct of cases of former judicial establishments, or shall be transferred for resolution, as appropriate, to the newly formed public administrations of the settlers, or to the judicial establishments, with notice thereof given to the parties involved in the case.

15. The present rules, with the exception of those concerning land organization, shall also extend to settlers (former colonists) who, while remaining registered by revision in their original societies, settled, prior to the issuance of these rules, in separate villages and settlements on their own lands, or on lands acquired at the expense of the original societies, or on the lands of private owners, under term contracts with the owners. The land relations of such settlers shall be determined by the contracts concluded by them with the original societies — the owners, or the landowners; in the event that such settlers acquire the lands occupied under contract in full ownership, the manner of land use shall be established by communal resolutions, applying the present rules.

II. On the land organization of settlers (former colonists)

settled on state lands.

16. Rural societies of settlers shall retain all lands and tracts allotted to them and remaining in their permanent use. In this connection, settler societies in whose holdings there is found land in excess of the established normal allotment shall be obliged, within 10 years from the date of confirmation of the present rules, to admit into their midst, without special admission resolutions, such number of migrants from land-poor original settlements as can be provided with the normal allotment out of the surplus lands available to each society.

Note 1. The migrants mentioned in this article who wish to settle in those societies which have surplus lands shall apply with a request to that effect to the local Provincial Presence for Peasant Affairs, which shall make the appropriate arrangement in response to such requests.

Note 2. Lands set aside for settlement by migrants from the original settler (colonist) settlements, but not yet settled by them to this day, shall be deemed free state lands and shall be assigned preferentially for the allotment of settlers (former colonists) of those villages whose societies, in accordance with Article 33 of the Highest-confirmed Rules of 31 March 1867 (44418) for the drawing up and issuance of title deeds to state peasants, shall receive permission for the resettlement of part of their members onto state lands.

17. For ownership of the lands and tracts allotted to each society, a special document called a title deed shall be issued to it.

18. The settlers, holding the lands and tracts granted to them under the deeds mentioned in Article 17, shall be obliged to pay into the treasury an annual payment fixed by law, called the state quitrent tax. The amount of this tax shall be determined in the manner established in Article 25 of the present rules.

19. Settlers shall have the right to use and dispose of, at their discretion, the lands granted to them in ownership under the deeds, subject to the following rules:

a) With the consent of two-thirds of the members of the society entitled to vote at the Assembly, the society may divide the lands belonging to it into household plots; whereupon the sum of the state quitrent tax charged on the whole society shall be divided among the householders according to the size and quality of their household plots.

b) The allotment of plots to individual householders from land held in communal ownership shall likewise be permitted by resolution of two-thirds of the members of the society entitled to vote at the Assembly; whereupon the amount of quitrent tax attributable, by calculation, to the allotted plots shall also be determined.

c) Resolutions of the society concerning allotment, as well as resolutions concerning the division of land into household plots, must, before being put into effect, be certified by the Peace Mediator, who shall submit a copy of the resolution to the Provincial Presence for Peasant Affairs for information and for confirmation of the distribution of the quitrent tax among the householders made by the society.

d) Within three years from the time of receiving the title deeds, societies, in the case of communal tenure, and householders, in the case of household tenure, may not alienate their lands to persons not belonging to the same society.

e) After the expiration of three years from the issuance of the title deeds, both societies and owners of household plots may alienate the lands of their allotment, by means permitted by law, not only to fellow villagers but also to outside persons, subject to the following conditions: 1) deeds of conveyance for the acquisition of these lands shall be executed in the general manner established for the execution of such deeds; 2) a society may sell plots of land held in communal ownership only pursuant to a resolution of two-thirds of the members of the society entitled to vote at the Assembly, certified by the Peace Mediator; 3) upon the alienation of household plots held in the personal possession of their owners, the obligation to pay the state quitrent tax due on the plot shall pass to the new acquirer.

f) In the division, allotment, and alienation of land, the rules established by the Highest-confirmed opinion of the State Council of 23 November 1870 (48946) for ensuring the payment of the state quitrent tax upon the sale and division of the lands of former state peasants shall be observed.

g) Settlers shall be permitted to be guided by their local customs in matters of inheritance of land.

20. Lands allotted not to a single society but to several societies (districts or volosts) for forest plantations, farmsteads, and other economic and industrial establishments, the societies are obliged to maintain in the future as well, without changing the purpose assigned to these lands and without departing, in their disposition of them, from the DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 515

established procedure except with the special authorization of the Provincial Presence for Peasant Affairs.

21. Subject to compliance with the restrictions indicated above (Articles 19 and 20), settlers shall enjoy, in respect of the possession of the lands of their allotment, all rights granted to peasant-proprietors from among former state peasants.

22. Title deeds shall be drawn up by officials of the Ministry of State Domains and presented to the settlers, in the presence of the Peace Mediators, in the manner established by the Highest-confirmed Rules of 31 March 1867 for drawing up title deeds for state peasants.

23. The extent (number of desyatinas) of the existing allotment of the settlers, granted to them in ownership under the deeds, shall be determined according to plans of economic survey.

24. Title deeds must be drawn up and issued to the settlers within three years, counting from the date of issuance of the present rules, except in the governorates of Chernigov and Poltava, where title deeds must be issued to the settlers simultaneously with the issuance of such deeds to former state peasants.

25. The amount of the state quitrent tax due from each settler society for the lands and tracts of its allotment shall be calculated and entered into the title deed: a) in villages where valuations of those lands have already been made — in the amount determined by such valuations; and b) in the remaining villages, where valuations have not yet been made, — in the amount corresponding to the multiplication of the total quantity of usable land in those villages by the average, apportioned, quitrent tax per desyatina of usable land in the adjacent or nearest villages of state peasants, whose lands, by degree of profitability and local conditions, most closely approximate the lands of the settler (former colonist) society concerned.

Note. The Mennonites of the volosts of Khortitsa and Mariupol, Yekaterinoslav governorate, Molochna, Tavrida governorate, and Malyshinsk, Samara governorate, shall be assessed the state quitrent tax at the rate of fifteen kopecks per usable desyatina of the allotment according to the plans of economic survey, with the exception, however, of the lands of the salt-transport route additionally allotted to the Molochna Mennonites in 1869, which they accepted with the obligation of paying quitrent tax on the general basis.

26. The amount of the quitrent tax determined in the title deed, on the grounds set forth in Article 25, shall remain unchanged until the expiration of 20 years from the date of issuance of the present rules. Subsequent changes in the assessments of this tax may be made only by legislative procedure.

27. Societies and owners of household plots of land subject to the state quitrent tax shall be permitted to obtain exemption from payment of all or part of this tax, by depositing with the provincial or district treasury, in state interest-bearing securities, such capital as would yield interest equal to the amount of quitrent tax from which the society or the owner of the plot wishes to free its lands. The capital deposited in interest-bearing securities must amount to not less than one hundred rubles at the nominal value of the securities.

28. Lands which, by means of a deposit with the treasury of the corresponding capital, on the basis of the preceding Article 27, shall be freed from the whole of the state quitrent tax charged upon them, as well as plots of land sold by rural societies with the conversion into the treasury of the sum due for them on the basis of the rules indicated in point e of Article 19, shall, constituting the full property of their owners, be excluded from the number of lands subject to payment of the state quitrent tax.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XLVI. P. 813-819.*

## No. 130. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON THE PROCEDURE FOR FOREIGNERS TO RENOUNCE RUSSIAN SUBJECTHOOD, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1874)

53255. — March 15. Imperially confirmed statute of the Committee of Ministers. — On the procedure for the release of foreigners from Russian subjecthood.

The memorandum of the Minister of Internal Affairs, of February 12, 1874, together with the register for the September third of 1873 concerning the release of 162 persons from Russian subjecthood, was heard.

The Committee resolved:

1) To request His Imperial Majesty's Supreme consent to the release from Russian subjecthood of the persons named in the register, on condition that, with regard to Otton Fiebiger, Baron von Firks, Baron Simolin-Batory, Otton Löwenstein, and Nikolai, son of the Kurland nobleman Count Nikolai Lamsdorff (Nos. 116, 122, 123, 146, and 141 in the registers), of whom the first four are shown as 21 years of age and the last as 14 years of age, Articles 3 and 11 of the Imperially confirmed Statute on Military Conscription of January 1, 1874, be strictly observed; and

2) To authorize the Minister of Internal Affairs henceforth, when submitting reports to the Committee of Ministers on release from Russian subjecthood, to attach a certification that no obstacles exist to the requested release under the Statute on Military Conscription.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 15th day of March, 1874, was Graciously pleased to consent to this.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XLIX. Pt. 1. P. 368.*

## No. 131. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE PROCEDURE FOR FORMER COLONISTS TO DEPART ABROAD, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1874)

53521. — May 14. Imperially confirmed opinion of the State Council, published June 10. — On clarifying the procedure by which former colonists may be released from Russian subjecthood and emigrate from Russia prior to fulfilling their military service obligation.

The State Council, in the Special Presence on Military Conscription, having examined the report of the Minister of Internal Affairs on clarifying the procedure by which former colonists may be released from Russian subjecthood and emigrate from Russia prior to fulfilling their military service obligation, resolved to clarify: 1) that settlers-proprietors (former colonists) established on state lands who, by age, are subject to military conscription must be entered, on the general basis, in the conscription lists; 2) that those of them who wish to exercise the right granted to them by the Imperially confirmed Statute on the Organization of Their Life of July [June] 4, 1871, to leave Russia, must declare such intention before September 1 of the year in which they are subject to conscription; and 3) that those former colonists of conscription age who, having declared within the specified period their intention to emigrate from Russia, fail to carry this out by the day their peers draw lots, and fail to notify the competent Presence on Military Conscription thereof, shall be compelled to perform this obligation, as persons evading it, without the drawing of lots; whereas those who have duly declared that they will not leave Russia shall be permitted to participate in the drawing of lots on the general basis.

Resolution.
