His Imperial Majesty was Graciously pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the Special Presence on Military Conscription, established under the State Council, on clarifying the procedure by which former colonists may be released from Russian subjecthood and emigrate from Russia prior to fulfilling their military service obligation, and commanded that it be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. XLIX. P. 772.*

## No. 132. SENATE DECREE ON THE APPLICATION OF THE RULES ON THE ORGANIZATION OF SETTLERS-PROPRIETORS TO THE VOLHYNIAN MENNONITE COLONY OF MIKHALIN, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II

857. — July 26, 1874. — Decree of the Governing Senate (1st Department). — On applying to the Mennonite colonists of the village of Mikhalin, Berdichev district, Kiev governorate, the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 9 of the Imperially confirmed Rules of June 4, 1871, on the organization of settlers-proprietors (former colonists) established on state lands.

By Decree of HIS IMPERIAL MAJESTY, the Governing Senate heard the report of the Acting Minister of Internal Affairs, of July 1, 1874, No. 1290, whereby he submits to the Governing Senate a copy of the Imperially confirmed opinion of the State Council of June 14 of this year, of the following content: The State Council, in the Special Presence on Military Conscription, having examined the report of the Minister of Internal Affairs on applying to the Mennonite colonists of the village of Mikhalin, Berdichev district, Kiev governorate, the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 9 of the Imperially confirmed Rules of June 4, 1871, on the organization of settlers-proprietors (former colonists) established on state lands, and concurring in substance with the Minister's conclusion, resolved: to apply to the Mennonite colonists of the village of Mikhalin, Berdichev district, Kiev governorate, the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 9 of the Imperially confirmed Rules of June 4, 1871, on the organization of settlers-proprietors (former colonists) established on state lands, while observing the procedure established for releasing former colonists from Russian subjecthood and their emigration from Russia prior to fulfilling their military service obligation. Endorsed on the opinion: HIS IMPERIAL MAJESTY was Graciously pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the Special Presence on Military Conscription, established under the State Council, on applying to the Mennonite colonists of the village of Mikhalin, Berdichev district, Kiev governorate, the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 9 of the Imperially confirmed Rules of June 4, 1871, on the organization of settlers-proprietors (former colonists) established on state lands, and commanded that it be carried out. Signed: Chairman of the State Council CONSTANTINE. June 14, 1874. Ordered: That, regarding this Imperially confirmed opinion of the State Council, for information and due execution by whom it may concern, His Imperial Highness the Viceroy of the Caucasus, the Ministers, and the Chief Administrators of separate departments be notified, some by decrees and others by transmission to the files of the Chief Procurator of the 1st Department of the Governing Senate of copies of the Senate's ruling; likewise that decrees be sent to: the Governors-General, Military Governors, Governors, Treasury Chambers, and Provincial, Cossack Host, and Regional Boards; and that notices be communicated to the Most Holy Governing Synod and to all Departments and General Assemblies of the Governing Senate, and that a copy of the ruling be transmitted to the Department of the Ministry of Justice, and that notice be given to the Office of the Senate Printing House for publication in the established manner.

(Signed: For the Chief Secretary, Shcheglov.)

Collection of Government Statutes and Orders (SURP). 1874. 2nd half-year. No. 63. Pp. 955-956.

## No. 133. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE PERFORMANCE OF MILITARY SERVICE BY MENNONITES, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1875)

54568. — April 8. Imperially confirmed opinion of the State Council, published May 14. — On the performance of obligatory service by Mennonites.

The State Council, in the Special Presence on Military Conscription and in General Assembly, having examined the report of the Minister of Internal Affairs on the performance of obligatory service by Mennonites, and concurring in substance with the Minister's conclusion, resolved: I. To set forth Article 157 of the Statute on Military Conscription as follows: "Mennonites, being exempted from bearing arms, shall perform their service in the workshops of the naval department, in fire brigades, and in special mobile units of the forestry department, on the basis of specially established rules. This, however, does not apply to those Mennonites who joined the sect, or arrived from abroad to settle in the Empire, after January 1, 1874." II. To submit the draft rules on the performance of obligatory service by Mennonites for the Supreme confirmation of His Imperial Majesty.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was Graciously pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the performance of obligatory service by Mennonites, and commanded that it be carried out.

(See the Rules at the end of the Volume.)

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. L. Pt. 1. Pp. 340-341.*

## No. 134. DECISION ON THE REDEMPTION OF LAND BY THE IZHORA COLONY NEAR ST. PETERSBURG, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1877)

56910. — February 1. Imperially confirmed statute of the Main Committee on the Organization of the Rural Estate, announced to the Senate, on behalf of the Minister of Justice, by the Deputy Minister of Justice on the 28th of the same February. — On the redemption by the colonists of the Izhora colony of the land in their use.

By the sense of the Imperially confirmed enactment of the Main Committee on the Organization of the Rural Estate of November 2, 1863 (40183), incorporated into the note to Article 159 of the Digest of Laws, 1857 edition, Vol. XII, Part II, Statute on Colonies of Foreigners in the Empire, per the 1868 Continuation, the law set forth in the said enactment concerning the redemption of land by colonists settled on palace lands must apply to all colonists to whose use palace lands were allotted. Meanwhile, this law names the colonies of Strelna, Znamenka, Oranienbaum, Alexandria, Srednyaya Rogatka, and Kipen, but does not mention the Izhora colony, settled on the lands of the Sovereign's Tsarskoye Selo estate, St. Petersburg governorate. Therefore, deeming it necessary to extend the force of the above-mentioned law to the Izhora colony, the Minister of the Imperial Court and Crown Lands applied to the Main Committee on the Organization of the Rural Estate with a submission to permit the redemption of the palace land in the use of the colonists of the Izhora colony, by agreement of these colonists with the Crown Lands Department and with the confirmation of the Minister of the Imperial Court and Crown Lands, in the same manner as was granted to the colonists of the Srednyaya Rogatka and Kipen colonies by the Imperially confirmed journal of the Main Committee of November 2, 1863.

The Administrator of the Affairs of the Main Committee on the Organization of the Rural Estate, State Secretary Zhukovsky, has now communicated to the Minister of the Imperial Court and Crown Lands, for due execution, an extract from the Imperially confirmed journal of the Main Committee of February 1, 1877, whereby the Main Committee resolved: to confirm the said submission of the Minister of the Imperial Court and Crown Lands.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. LII. Pt. 1. P. 99.*

## No. 135. DECREE OF ALEXANDER II ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE LIPPERT SCHOLARSHIPS (1877)

57046. — March 11. Personal decree, announced to the Senate by the Minister of Internal Affairs on April 22. — On assigning to the scholarships established from the interest on the capital donated by the colonist Lippert the designation "Lippert Scholarships."

Peter Lippert, a former colonist of Ekaterinenstadt, Samara governorate, by his testament of January 24, 1861, donated 5,000 rubles for the establishment, from the interest on this capital, of scholarships for the purpose of teaching various trades to poor children of settlers-proprietors of the Samara and Saratov governorates.

The Saratov Governor communicated to the Ministry of Internal Affairs a petition of the Congress of Delegates from the society of settlers-proprietors (former colonists) of the said governorates requesting permission to assign to these scholarships the designation "Lippert Scholarships," in memory of the deceased benefactor, as their original founder.

Upon the most loyal report on this matter, His Imperial Majesty, on the 11th day of March of this year, was Graciously pleased to grant the said petition.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. LII. Pt. 1. P. 187.*

## No. 136. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE ORGANIZATION AND ADMINISTRATION OF THE VOLGA COLONY OF SAREPTA, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II (1877)

57437. — June 6. Imperially confirmed opinion of the State Council. — On the communal organization and administration of the Evangelical Brotherhood Community of the settlement of Sarepta.

The Acting Administrator of the Affairs of the Main Committee on the Organization of the Rural Estate, having forwarded to the Minister of State Domains, by communication of June 14 of this year, the Imperially confirmed opinion of the State Council of June 6 of this year on the communal organization and administration of the Evangelical Brotherhood Community of the settlement of Sarepta, notified that the State Council, together with rendering the said opinion, resolved: to authorize the Minister of State Domains to reconcile the proposals he has drawn up concerning the land organization of the settlement of Sarepta as closely as possible with the rights to lands granted to the Sarepta community upon its establishment in Russia by special Imperial charters, as well as with the provisions of the Digest of Laws, 1857 edition, Vol. XII, Part II, Statute on Colonies (Articles 159 and 160), and thereafter, having communicated with the Chief Administrator of the Second Section of His Imperial Majesty's Own Chancery and the Minister of Finance, to submit the final proposals on this subject for the consideration of the Main Committee on the Organization of the Rural Estate; and that this resolution of the State Council has likewise been honored with His Imperial Majesty's Supreme confirmation.

The Minister of State Domains, in reporting the foregoing to the Governing Senate, submitted the Imperially confirmed opinion of the State Council of June 6 of this year.

The State Council, in General Assembly, having examined the conclusion of the Joint Presence of the Main Committee on the Organization of the Rural Estate and the Department of Laws, on the draft rules submitted by the Minister of State Domains for the organization of the Evangelical Brotherhood Community of the settlement of Sarepta, resolved:

I. To establish the following rules for the communal organization and administration of the Evangelical Brotherhood Community of the settlement of Sarepta:

1. Members of the Evangelical Brotherhood Society of the settlement of Sarepta shall be included among the rural inhabitants and shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the general provincial and district institutions, as well as the local institutions for peasant affairs, on the bases and in the manner indicated in the following articles.

2. The Sarepta community, in its internal religious-communal and church-school affairs, shall be governed in accordance with the statutes of the Evangelical Brotherhood Community, remaining under the immediate authority of its presiding clergyman.

3. In administrative respects, the settlement of Sarepta shall constitute a separate volost.

4. The communal and economic affairs of the settlement of Sarepta shall be managed by the local assembly, consisting of two-thirds of the adult members of the society not disqualified by court judgment, elected by the society.

5. The execution of the assembly's decisions shall be entrusted to a special Committee, consisting of: the Elder, who shall also serve as Chairman of the Committee, the Justiciar, the Guardian of the Widows' House, the Guardian of the Maidens' House, the Superior of the Brotherhood House, and six members elected by the assembly for three years.

6. The Volost Administration of the settlement of Sarepta shall consist, under the chairmanship of the Elder, of three Assessors elected by the assembly for three years, and the Justiciar.

7. The Sarepta Elder and Volost Administration shall be granted, in police matters, all the rights and duties of volost elders and administrations among peasant-proprietors, while in matters of judicature and settlement of disputes the said Administration shall be granted the rights of a volost court (Articles 95-110 of the General Statute of February 19, 1861 (36657)). But cases involving persons who do not belong to the Sarepta community shall, at the request of either party, be subject to review by the general courts of law, strictly on the basis of the laws (General Statute, Article 97 and note to Article 101). Likewise, in all matters of civil suits and disputes exceeding the competence of the volost court, members of the Sarepta community shall be permitted to seek their rights either locally, by way of arbitration (Articles 99 and 110 of the General Statute), or in the general courts of law, as appropriate.

Note. In place of the official agent formerly maintained by the Sarepta community, this community shall be permitted to have its own special attorney for representing it in all its affairs.

8. The Elder and the local presiding clergyman shall be confirmed in and dismissed from their offices, upon submission of the Sarepta Administration, the former by the Saratov Governor, and the latter by the Minister of Internal Affairs, submissions to the Minister being made through the Governor.

Note. In the event that foreigners are appointed to these offices, such persons, together with their confirmation in office, shall be sworn in as subjects of Russia and shall become members of the Sarepta community. This rule shall likewise extend to other office-holders appointed from among foreigners, namely: the second pastor in Sarepta, the pastor of the Brotherhood church in St. Petersburg, the superintendents of the communal residence houses, and the teachers of the local schools; and all persons named in this note, upon their release from the said duties, shall thereby also acquire the right to renounce Russian subjecthood.

9. The enrollment of new members into the Brotherhood community and their release therefrom shall be carried out in the manner established in Article 9 of the Imperially confirmed Rules of June 4/16, 1871 (49705), on the organization of settlers-proprietors, former colonists.

10. For ten years from the confirmation of these rules, the Evangelical Brethren of the settlement of Sarepta may, upon renouncing Russian subjecthood, leave Russia without hindrance and without payment to the treasury of any portion of the capital they have acquired. As regards the entry of foreign members of the Brotherhood community into Russian subjecthood, as well as their release therefrom, after the expiration of the said ten-year term, apart from the exemption already established in the note to Article 8 of these rules, a special enactment shall be issued in due course.

11. Members of the Brotherhood community shall be obligated, on the general basis, to pay state taxes and perform military, zemstvo, and other monetary and in-kind obligations.

Note 1. Exemption from the billeting obligation shall be maintained from the date of issuance of this enactment for ten years going forward. Church buildings, hospitals, school and communal residence buildings (almshouses for the elderly and indigent) situated within the boundaries of the settlement of Sarepta that yield no income shall be permanently exempted, on the general basis (note 2 to Article 1 of the Statute on the Reorganization of the Military Billeting Obligation and Article 2 of the Temporary Rules for Zemstvo Institutions, per the 1869 Continuation), from military billeting and from zemstvo taxation.

Note 2. Educational and charitable institutions, and sanitary and fire-fighting establishments, existing in Sarepta and any that may be established there in future, if maintained exclusively at the expense of the local community, without participation of zemstvo funds, shall be subject directly to local administration and shall not fall under the jurisdiction of the zemstvo.

Note 3. With respect to military conscription, the settlement of Sarepta shall be attached, without division, on the rights of a separate volost, to one of the nearest conscription districts, and the compilation of conscription lists shall be entrusted to the Sarepta Administration (Articles 67, 72(1), and 102 of the Statute on Military Conscription).

12. The Brotherhood community of the settlement of Sarepta, holding its communal property undivided, shall participate, through its attorney, in the congress of district landowners, in which individual members of the community shall also participate in accordance with the property personally held by each of them (Statute on Zemstvo Institutions, Articles 19 and 23), sending representatives to the zemstvo assemblies on the bases and in the manner established for this purpose in the Statute on Zemstvo Institutions.

13. The Brotherhood community and each of its members shall retain the right to conduct internal and foreign trade, and all kinds of trades and crafts, both within the lands allotted to Sarepta and throughout the Empire on the general basis, that is, upon payment of the guild and trade dues, excises, and duties established by law.

II. To authorize the Minister of State Domains to take, by mutual agreement with the Minister of Internal Affairs, measures for transferring the settlement of Sarepta to the jurisdiction of the general institutions within three months from the date of issuance of these rules.

III. To authorize the Minister of Internal Affairs, on the question of applying, upon expiration of the ten-year term established by Article 10 of the said rules, the general laws concerning the acceptance and renunciation of Russian subjecthood to members of the Sarepta community, to submit his conclusion, in the established manner, by the end of the said term.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was Graciously pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the communal organization and administration of the Evangelical Brotherhood Community of the settlement of Sarepta, and commanded that it be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. LII. Pt. 1. Pp. 698-700.*

## No. 137. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE ORGANIZATION OF LUTHERAN PARISHES IN THE SETTLEMENTS OF FORMER COLONISTS, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER II

76. — December 27, 1877. — Imperially confirmed opinion of the State Council, submitted to the Governing Senate by the Minister of State Domains on January 11, 1878. — On the administration of the properties of Evangelical-Lutheran churches in the settlements of settlers-proprietors (former colonists) and on the procedure for appointing preachers to them.

HIS IMPERIAL MAJESTY was Graciously pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the administration of the properties of Evangelical-Lutheran churches in the settlements of settlers-proprietors (former colonists) and on the procedure for appointing preachers to them, and commanded that it be carried out.

Signed: Chairman of the State Council CONSTANTINE.

OPINION OF THE STATE COUNCIL. December 27, 1877.

Extracted from the journals of: the Joint Departments of Laws and State Economy of October 7, and the General Assembly of December 5, 1877.

The State Council, in the Joint Departments of Laws and State Economy and in General Assembly, having examined the submission of the Minister of State Domains on the administration of the properties of Evangelical-Lutheran churches in the settlements of settlers-proprietors (former colonists) and on the procedure for appointing preachers to them, and concurring in substance with the Minister's conclusion, resolved:

I. In amendment and supplement of the relevant statutes, to enact:

1) The administration of the properties of Evangelical-Lutheran churches in the settlements of settlers-proprietors (former colonies of foreign settlers) in the governorates of Samara, Saratov, Ekaterinoslav, Tavrida, Kherson, Bessarabia, and Voronezh (the settlement of Rybensdorf) shall be entrusted to church councils established in each parish, attached to the parish church, with the same rights granted to them and the same duties imposed upon them as are defined in the statutes in force for church councils in cities.

2) The said church councils must consist of no fewer than four members, namely: the parish preacher and three lay persons elected by the parishioners of the parish church; furthermore, the parishioners of filial churches shall be granted the right to elect one member to the church council from each filial church. The chairmanship of these councils shall, until further order, be entrusted to the parish preacher.

3) At filial churches, special church councils may be established, by resolution of the parishioners and with the permission of the General Evangelical-Lutheran Consistory, on the same bases as at parish churches. In such case the parishioners of the filial church shall not elect a member to the council of the parish church.

4) To parishes in the settlements of settlers-proprietors (former colonies of foreign settlers) shall be extended the effect of Article 294 of the Statutes on the Spiritual Affairs of Foreign Confessions (Digest of Laws, Vol. XI), granting parishioners the right to call and appoint preachers.

II. To disburse, at the disposal of the Minister of Internal Affairs, for augmenting the resources of the Evangelical-Lutheran General Consistory, from January 1, 1878, the sum of two thousand seven hundred ninety-two rubles and eighty-seven kopecks per year, charging this expenditure to the account of the public levy entered in the estimates of the Ministry of State Domains, collected from settlers-proprietors (former colonists) for the maintenance of the colonial administration.

III. The implementation of the enactments set forth in Article I shall be entrusted to the Minister of Internal Affairs. Arrangements for the review and transfer, as appropriate, of matters previously conducted within the Ministry of State Domains regarding the chief ecclesiastical trusteeship in the former colonies of foreign settlers, and regarding the filling of vacant parishes therein, shall be left to the mutual agreement of the Ministers of State Domains and Internal Affairs.

The original opinion is signed in the journals by the Chairmen and Members.

*SURP. 1878. 1st half-year. No. 20. Pp. 148-149.*

## No. 138. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE SCHOOL AT THE MOSCOW LUTHERAN CHURCH OF SS. PETER AND PAUL, APPROVED BY ALEXANDER II (1878)

59059. — November 28. Opinion of the State Council, Highest confirmed. — On the reorganization of the school attached to the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of SS. Peter and Paul in Moscow.

The State Council, in the Joint Departments of Laws and of State Economy and in General Assembly, having examined the submission of the Minister of National Enlightenment on the reorganization of the school attached to the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of SS. Peter and Paul in Moscow, and agreeing in substance with the Minister's conclusion, resolved as its opinion:

I. To authorize the Church Council of the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of SS. Peter and Paul in Moscow, beginning with the 1878/79 academic year, to reorganize the school maintained at the expense of the said church on the following bases:

1. The said school, while under the general administration of the Church Council of the Church of SS. Peter and Paul, is subject to the authority of the Trustee of the Moscow educational district. It is divided into three sections: a) an elementary school, b) a Realschule with a commercial department, and c) a Gymnasium. As regards the organization of instruction and upbringing, the school is governed by the Statutes of Gymnasiums and Progymnasiums and of Realschulen, Highest confirmed on 30 July 1871 and 15 May 1872 (49860 and 50834), with the rules prescribed for Gymnasiums and Progymnasiums observed in respect of the elementary school and the gymnasium section, and the rules of the Statute on Realschulen observed in respect of the Realschule section, subject to the following exceptions:

2. The elementary school of the institution, corresponding to the preparatory class of government Gymnasiums and Progymnasiums, is divided into three annual courses and consists of two sections: one for children speaking Russian, and the other for those speaking German. Children who cannot yet read or write are admitted to the first course. In addition to the subjects taught in the preparatory class of Gymnasiums, German is added in the elementary school.

3. In the Realschule section, the teaching of general history and geography, arithmetic, correspondence and bookkeeping, and German may be conducted in German, and in the Gymnasium, the teaching of ancient languages and German, of general history and geography in all classes, and of arithmetic in the 1st and 2nd classes, may likewise be conducted in German.

4. Immediate administration of the school belongs to the School Council, composed of: the President of the Church Council, the senior pastor, the second preacher, two members of the Church Council chosen by it, one member elected by the general assembly of the church's parishioners for a term of three years, and the Director and Inspector of the school.

5. The School Council reviews the resolutions of the Pedagogical Council, receives and verifies the reports on the academic and educational condition of the school submitted by the Director, elects, upon the Director's proposals, teachers, tutors, and other persons employed at the school, grants employees leave within the limits of authority granted to Directors of government Gymnasiums and Realschulen, submits recommendations for the dismissal of employees, exempts needy and deserving pupils from tuition fees, and awards stipends.

6. The Director and Inspector of the school are elected upon the proposal of the School Council at a joint session of the Church Council and the School Council. The Church Council submits, through the Trustee of the Moscow educational district, the confirmation of the Director of the school in office to the Minister of National Enlightenment. The Inspector and other officials of the school, in a number not exceeding that established by the Statutes and staff tables of Gymnasiums, Progymnasiums, and Realschulen, are confirmed in office by the Trustee of the district.

II. To grant the employees of the School of SS. Peter and Paul all the service rights bestowed by the Statutes of 30 July 1871 and 15 May 1872, Highest confirmed, upon employees of government Gymnasiums, Progymnasiums, and Realschulen, except for the right to receive from the treasury a third of a term's salary not counted toward pay upon appointment to service, as well as the right to lump-sum benefits and pensions for service at the school, applying in this regard the provisions of the Statute on Gymnasiums and Progymnasiums to employees of the elementary school and gymnasium section of the school, and the provisions of the Statute on Realschulen to employees of the Realschule section.

III. To extend to pupils studying in the Realschule and gymnasium sections of the School of SS. Peter and Paul the rights enjoyed by pupils of the corresponding government educational institutions of the Department of the Ministry of National Enlightenment.

IV. To authorize the Minister of National Enlightenment to confirm, on these bases, the Statute of the School of SS. Peter and Paul in Moscow.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was pleased to confirm, Highest, the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the reorganization of the school attached to the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of SS. Peter and Paul in Moscow, and commanded that it be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. LIII. Pt. 2. Pp. 256-257.*

## No. 139. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON EXEMPTIONS FROM MILITARY SERVICE FOR FOREIGN SETTLERS, APPROVED BY ALEXANDER II (1878)

59120. — December 12. Opinion of the State Council, Highest confirmed, published 3 January 1879. — On granting exemption from military conscription to foreign settlers who settled in Russia on the same terms as the persons named in point 1 of note 1 to Article 62 of the Statute on Military Conscription (1876 edition).

The State Council, in the Special Presence on Military Conscription and in General Assembly, having examined the submission of the Acting Minister of Internal Affairs on granting exemption from military conscription to peasant-proprietors, former Austrian subjects of Czech nationality, who settled in 1860–1870 in Perekop county, Tavrida governorate, resolved as its opinion to decree: "The exemption from military conscription specified in point 1 of note 1 to Article 62 of the Statute on Military Conscription, 1876 edition, shall be enjoyed, in addition to the persons named in that point, also by all other foreign settlers who settled in Russia on the same terms as those persons. Should any doubts arise in applying this rule, the Ministers of Internal Affairs and of War shall submit reports to the Special Presence on Military Conscription."

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was pleased to confirm, Highest, the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on granting exemption from military conscription to foreign settlers who settled in Russia on the same terms as the persons named in point 1 of note 1 to Article 62 of the Statute on Military Conscription (1876 edition), and commanded that it be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. LIII. Pt. 2. P. 301.*

## No. 140. DECREE OF ALEXANDER II ON THE GIRLS' GYMNASIUM AT THE MOSCOW LUTHERAN CHURCH OF SS. PETER AND PAUL (1880)

60504. — February 15. Personal decree, published 14 March. — On the reorganization of the girls' school at the Lutheran Church of SS. Peter and Paul in Moscow into a girls' Gymnasium.

The Sovereign Emperor, upon the most loyal report of the Minister of National Enlightenment, on the 15th day of February 1880, was Highest pleased to command:

1. To reorganize the girls' school at the Lutheran Church of SS. Peter and Paul in Moscow into a girls' Gymnasium on the basis of the following principal provisions:

a) German is added to the compulsory subjects of instruction in the Peter-and-Paul Girls' Gymnasium for all classes.

b) The teaching of general history and geography, arithmetic in the preparatory, first, and second classes, and likewise pedagogy, is conducted in German.

c) The Peter-and-Paul Girls' Gymnasium is under the general administration of the Church Council of the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of SS. Peter and Paul. Immediate administration of the Gymnasium belongs to the School Council, which enjoys the rights granted to the Guardian Council of girls' Gymnasiums of the Department of the Ministry of National Enlightenment.

d) The Director of the Peter-and-Paul boys' school, with respect to the said Gymnasium, enjoys the rights granted to Directors of boys' Gymnasiums by the Statute of 24 May 1870 (48406).

e) The Headmistress of the girls' Gymnasium is elected upon the proposal of the School Council at a joint meeting of the School and Church Councils and is submitted, through the Trustee of the Moscow educational district, for confirmation by the Minister of National Enlightenment. All other officials, upon meeting the established requirements, are confirmed in office by the Trustee of the Moscow educational district.

g) Employees of the Peter-and-Paul Girls' Gymnasium are granted the service rights bestowed by the Statute of 24 May 1870, Highest confirmed, upon employees of government girls' Gymnasiums, except for the right to lump-sum benefits and pensions for service;

and z) The female pupils of this Gymnasium are granted the rights enjoyed by female pupils of Gymnasiums of the Department of the Ministry of National Enlightenment; — and

2. To authorize the Minister of National Enlightenment to confirm, on the basis of such principles, the Statute for this institution.

*PSZRI. Coll. 2. Vol. LIV. Pt. 2. Pp. 454-455.*

## No. 141. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE PERFORMANCE OF MILITARY SERVICE BY MENNONITES IN FOREST DETACHMENTS, APPROVED BY ALEXANDER III (1882)

432. On the performance by Mennonites of compulsory service in forest detachments of the Department of the Ministry of State Domains.

HIS IMPERIAL MAJESTY was pleased to confirm, Highest, the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the performance by Mennonites of compulsory service in forest detachments of the Department of the Ministry of State Domains, and commanded that it be carried out.

Signed: Chairman of the State Council, MIKHAIL.

OPINION OF THE STATE COUNCIL. 25 May 1882.

Extracted from the journals: of the Joint Departments of Laws, of State Economy, and of Civil and Ecclesiastical Affairs of 23 April, and of the General Assembly of 10 May 1882.

The State Council, in the Joint Departments of Laws, of State Economy, and of Civil and Ecclesiastical Affairs and in General Assembly, having examined the submission of the Ministry of State Domains on the performance by Mennonites of compulsory service in forest detachments of the Department of the Ministry of State Domains, resolved as its opinion:

I. In addition to the appendix to Article 157 of the Statute on Military Conscription (Digest of Laws, vol. IV, book I, 1876 edition), to establish the following rules concerning the performance of compulsory service by Mennonites belonging to this sect and settled in the governorates of Volhynia, Yekaterinoslav, Samara, Tavrida, and Kherson prior to 1 January 1874:

1) The said Mennonites, upon being called up for compulsory service, shall be assigned to forest detachments of the Department of the Ministry of State Domains.

2) Recruits shall join the detachments by 1 March of the year following their call-up and shall be designated as obligated workers.

3) The discharge of obligated workers into the reserve shall be carried out by order of the Ministry of State Domains, on the basis of the rules in force in the military department.

4) Workers may be granted leave, at the discretion of the Minister of State Domains, during the period from September to March.

5) Sick workers shall be placed, for treatment, in military medical establishments, on the bases determined by Articles 1471–1517 of Part IV, Book III of the Digest of Military Regulations (1859 edition).

6) The detachments are assigned to forest work in the governorates of Yekaterinoslav, Tavrida, and Kherson and are placed under the complete authority of the foresters within whose jurisdiction they are located.

7) The detachments are assigned a uniform dress, of a pattern approved by the Minister of State Domains.

8) For each day actually worked, obligated workers shall receive pay in the amount of twenty kopecks per person.

9) The times for beginning and ending work, as well as the number of working hours per day, shall be determined on the basis of Table III, § 3 of the schedule of piece-work norms for construction work, Highest confirmed 7 April 1869 (Complete Collection of Laws, vol. XLIV, No. 46978).

10) During time free from state work, the governorate forester may release a portion of the workers for agricultural occupations on plots allotted for the use of the forest detachments.

11) While serving in the detachments, workers shall, for minor offenses, be subject to the following disciplinary penalties:

a) by order of the local foresters — reprimand, censure, simple arrest of up to seven days, and strict arrest of up to five days;

b) by order of the governorate foresters — reprimand, censure, simple arrest of up to one month, and strict arrest of up to twenty days.

12) Under simple arrest, the guilty shall be held, each separately, in a lighted guardroom; they shall receive ordinary food but shall sleep on bare plank beds. Under strict arrest, workers shall likewise be held singly in a lighted guardroom and shall sleep on bare plank beds; they shall be issued only bread and salt daily, and hot food every third day.

13) Workers subjected to arrest shall be forbidden to smoke tobacco, consume spirits, play games, or sing, and shall likewise be forbidden contact with outside persons.

14) The internal organization and administration of the detachments shall be established by rules approved by the Minister of State Domains.

15) The costs of maintaining the detachments shall be borne partly by the treasury and partly by the Mennonite communities' own resources.

16) The following expenditures shall be made from the funds of the State Treasury:

a) daily wages of workers;

b) rental, heating, and lighting of quarters for workers until the expiration of one year after the construction of barracks, and also during forest-management work in locations remote from the barracks;

c) treatment of sick workers in medical establishments of the military department;

d) the construction and repair of workshops for the manufacture and repair, by the labor of the workers themselves, of tools and instruments needed for state work.

Note. The expenditures enumerated in Article 16 shall be covered from the funds allotted under the estimate of the Ministry of State Domains for forest work.

17) Independently of this, each detachment shall be allotted from the state lands: a) free of charge — five desyatinas each for a homestead and kitchen garden, and b) for special payment — from one hundred to two hundred desyatinas, for agricultural use. The selection of plots, the more precise determination of the amount of land to be allotted to each detachment for agricultural needs, and the fixing of payment for it, shall depend on the discretion of the Minister of State Domains, who is authorized to reduce this payment by not more than fifty percent below the prices prevailing in that locality for the rental of land.

18) For heating the barracks and preparing food, the detachments shall be issued fuel by the Department of State Domains at reduced prices, not, however, lower than fifty percent below the rates established for the sale of timber from state forest tracts.

19) The following shall be the obligations and expense of the Mennonite communities:

a) construction, repair, heating, and lighting of barracks for housing the forest detachments, together with the necessary outbuildings attached to these barracks;

b) the household equipping, uniforms, and provisioning of the detachments;

c) the transport of obligated workers from their place of residence to the forestry districts and back, upon discharge into the reserve;

d) the rental payment for land allotted to the detachments by the treasury for agricultural use.

20) After the expiration of twenty years (counting from 1882), the barrack buildings constructed by the Mennonites shall pass into the ownership of the treasury, without any compensation whatsoever on its part. Should the Ministry of State Domains, before the expiration of the said term, find it necessary to change any of the locations chosen for the settlement of the detachments, the barrack structures erected there by the Mennonite communities shall be acquired by the treasury at a price determined by sworn appraisers.

II. As assistance toward the construction of six barracks for the housing of the forest detachments, an interest-free loan shall be issued, during the course of 1882 and 1883, to the Mennonite communities settled in the governorates of Volhynia, Yekaterinoslav, Samara, Tavrida, and Kherson, in the amount of four thousand rubles for each barrack, with the disbursement of this money from the funds allotted under the estimate of the Ministry of State Domains for forest-management work. The procedure and conditions for the repayment of the said loan, under the joint liability of all the aforementioned communities, shall be established by agreement between the Ministry and these communities.

The genuine opinion was signed in the journals by the Chairmen and Members.

*SURP. 1882. 2nd half-year. No. 62. Pp. 820-824.*

## No. 142. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE SCHOOL AT THE LUTHERAN CHURCH OF ST. CATHERINE IN ST. PETERSBURG, APPROVED BY ALEXANDER III (1882)

55. On the reorganization and rights of the school attached to the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of St. Catherine in St. Petersburg.

HIS IMPERIAL MAJESTY was pleased to confirm, Highest, the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the reorganization and rights of the school attached to the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of St. Catherine in St. Petersburg, and commanded that it be carried out.

Signed: Chairman of the State Council, MIKHAIL.

OPINION OF THE STATE COUNCIL. 16 November 1882.

Extracted from the journals: of the Department of Laws of 9 October and of the General Assembly of 1 November 1882.

The State Council, in the Department of Laws and in General Assembly, having examined the submission of the Ministry of National Enlightenment on the reorganization and rights of the school attached to the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of St. Catherine in St. Petersburg, resolved as its opinion:

I. To authorize the church council of the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of St. Catherine in St. Petersburg to reorganize the school attached to this church, under the supervision of the Trustee of the St. Petersburg educational district, on the bases on which the school at the Reformed church in St. Petersburg exists, so that instruction in the former shall correspond, in scope, to the curriculum of Gymnasiums and Realschulen established by the Statutes of these educational institutions, Highest confirmed on 30 July 1871 and 15 May 1872.

II. Upon the completion of the reorganization specified in Article I: 1) the employees of the School of St. Catherine shall be granted all the service advantages bestowed by the Statutes on Gymnasiums and Realschulen of the Department of the Ministry of National Enlightenment upon the corresponding officials, except for the right to receive from the treasury a third of a term's salary not counted toward pay, as well as the right to lump-sum benefits and pensions for service at the school; and 2) the pupils studying in the classical and Realschule sections of the School of St. Catherine shall be granted the rights enjoyed by pupils of the corresponding educational institutions established by the Ministry of National Enlightenment.

III. To authorize the Minister of National Enlightenment to put the measures specified in Article II into effect upon due verification that the School of St. Catherine has in fact been reorganized on the bases determined by Article I of the present enactment.

The genuine opinion was signed in the journals by the Chairmen and Members.

*SURP. 1883. 1st half-year. No. 6. Pp. 95-96.*

## No. 143. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE PERFORMANCE OF MILITARY SERVICE BY MENNONITES, APPROVED BY ALEXANDER III (1883)

1316. — January 19. Opinion of the State Council, Highest confirmed (Collection of Statutes, 1883, 11 March, Art. 242). — On the performance of compulsory service by Mennonites.

The State Council, in the Department of Laws and in General Assembly, having examined the submission of the Minister of State Domains on the performance of compulsory service by Mennonites, resolved as its opinion:

The effect of the rules established by the opinion of the State Council, Highest confirmed 25 May 1882 (914), concerning the compulsory service of Mennonites residing in the governorates of Volhynia, Yekaterinoslav, Samara, Tavrida, and Kherson, shall be extended also to Mennonites who settled prior to 1 January 1874 in all other governorates and regions of the Empire.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was pleased to confirm, Highest, the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the performance of compulsory service by Mennonites, and commanded that it be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 3. Vol. III. Pp. 9-10.*

## No. 144. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE ALEXANDER EVANGELICAL SCHOOL IN MOSCOW, APPROVED BY ALEXANDER III (1883)

1868. — November 29. Opinion of the State Council, Highest confirmed (Collection of Statutes, 1884, 24 January, Art. 80). — On the establishment of the Alexander Evangelical School in the city of Moscow.

The State Council, in the Department of Laws and in General Assembly, having examined the submission of the Minister of National Enlightenment on the establishment of the Alexander Evangelical School in the city of Moscow, resolved as its opinion:

To authorize the Evangelical parishes in the city of Moscow to establish in this city a two-class school on the basis of the Statute on Municipal Schools, Highest confirmed 31 May 1872 (Complete Collection of Laws, vol. XLVII, No. 50909), and the following special rules:

1. The institution shall be named the "Alexander Evangelical School" and shall have as its purpose to provide the sons of needy parishioners of Evangelical parishes in the city of Moscow with elementary intellectual and religious-moral education.

2. The school, being subject to the authority of the Trustee of the Moscow educational district, shall be under the immediate administration of the Director of Popular Schools of Moscow governorate.

3. The school shall be maintained from: a) interest on a capital sum of twenty-five thousand rubles donated by the parishioners of the Evangelical churches in the city of Moscow; b) an annual contribution made by Baron L. Knoop in the amount of one thousand rubles; c) tuition fees; and d) donations made in favor of the institution.

4. Direct administration of the school shall be entrusted to a School Council, composed of ecclesiastical and lay members. The former shall be, by virtue of their office, all the preachers of the Evangelical churches in the city of Moscow, and the latter shall be elected by the councils of these churches for a term of three years, in a number equal to that of the ecclesiastical members. The Chairman of the Council shall be elected by the Council, either from among its own members or from outside persons. The Chairman shall have the right to invite the person in charge of the school to the Council's meetings, such person being granted only a consultative voice.

5. The School Council shall:

a) review the reports on the academic and educational condition of the institution submitted to it by the person in charge of the school;

b) submit to the Trustee of the educational district, and communicate to the church councils, a report on the school, and conduct correspondence on the latter's affairs;

c) elect an inspector of the school — preferably from among the ecclesiastical members of the council — and a treasurer, from among its lay members;

d) elect candidates for filling teaching posts at the institution and submit them for confirmation by the Trustee of the educational district;

e) apply to the Trustee with submissions for the confirmation of the teacher of the senior class in the office of person in charge of the school (Art. 10), for the commendation of those employees of the school who shall deserve it by their useful activity, as well as for the dismissal of the person in charge and the teachers from their posts;

f) request leave for employees;

g) administer the property and building of the school, as well as its treasury, sharing with the treasurer responsibility for the latter;

h) fix the salaries of the school's employees;

i) determine the tuition fee, bearing in mind that it must not exceed one third of the fee charged by the schools attached to the Evangelical parishes in the city of Moscow;

j) exempt, insofar as possible, orphans and children of entirely destitute parents from tuition fees, basing its decisions in this regard on certificates issued by the pastors of the parishes to which the minors belong.

Note. Submissions of the School Council shall reach the Trustee of the educational district through the Director of Popular Schools.

6. Matters shall be decided in the Council by a majority of votes, and in case of an equal division, according to the opinion adopted by the Chairman. With regard to the dismissal from service and the granting of leave to officials enjoying the advantages of state service, as well as in submissions for the commendation of employees, the existing enactments on these subjects shall be observed.

7. For the discussion of matters relating to the academic and educational aspects of the school, a Pedagogical Council shall be established at it, under the chairmanship of the person in charge of the school (Art. 5, item e, and Art. 10), consisting of all the teachers who teach academic subjects at it (Art. 9).

8. The teaching of the Russian language, as well as of the history and geography of Russia, in the school shall be conducted in Russian; the remaining subjects included in the school's curriculum may be taught in German as well.

9. The school shall have three teachers, of whom two (one in each class) shall be for teaching subjects in German, and the third for the subjects taught in both classes in Russian.

10. The duties of person in charge of the school shall be laid upon the teacher of the senior class.

11. Teachers of academic subjects shall be granted all the service advantages assigned by law to teachers of municipal schools, with the sole exception of pensions and lump-sum benefits from the State Treasury.

12. Pupils of the Alexander School who successfully complete its full course shall be granted all the rights assigned to pupils of two-class municipal schools of the Ministry of National Enlightenment. Those who leave the school upon completing the course of the junior class shall be admitted, without examination, to the first class of Gymnasiums and Realschulen; and those who have spent two years in the junior class shall enjoy the exemption of the fourth category with respect to the performance of military conscription.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was pleased to confirm, Highest, the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the establishment of the Alexander Evangelical School in the city of Moscow, and commanded that it be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 3. Vol. III. Pp. 469-470.*

## No. 145. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE GIRLS' GYMNASIUM AT THE LUTHERAN CHURCH OF ST. ASCENSION IN KHARKOV, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER III (1884)

2600. — December 18. Highest-confirmed opinion of the State Council (Coll. of Statutes 1885, January 18, art. 77). — On the transformation of the girls' school existing at the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of St. Ascension, in the city of Kharkov, into a seven-class Gymnasium.

The State Council, in the Department of Laws and in General Assembly, having examined the report of the Minister of Public Education on the transformation of the girls' school existing at the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of St. Ascension, in the city of Kharkov, into a seven-class Gymnasium, resolved as its opinion:

That the first-class girls' school existing at the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of St. Ascension, in the city of Kharkov, be transformed into a seven-class girls' Gymnasium, on the basis of the Highest-confirmed Statute of 24 May 1870 on Girls' Gymnasiums and Progymnasiums of the Ministry of Public Education (Complete Collection of Laws, Vol. XLV, No. 48406) and the following special rules:

1. The Gymnasium is maintained: a) at the expense of funds disbursed by the church council of the Evangelical-Lutheran community in the city of Kharkov, and b) from donations by private persons.

2. Attached to the Gymnasium there shall be an elementary school, consisting of two divisions: junior and senior. The following subjects are compulsory in the school's course: a) the Law of God of the Orthodox and Lutheran confessions, b) the Russian language, c) the German language, d) arithmetic, e) penmanship, f) singing, and g) gymnastics.

3. The instructional course of the Gymnasium includes the German language as a compulsory subject for all classes. General history, geography, and pedagogy may, at the discretion of the Gymnasium's Board of Trustees, be taught in either Russian or German.

4. The children of pastors, the headmistress, teachers (male and female), and the Gymnasium's class matrons are exempted from tuition fees.

5. Persons serving in the Gymnasium and in the elementary school attached to it are not entitled to receive from the treasury quarterly salary not counted toward pension, nor lump-sum allowances and pensions from the said source. Likewise, the other rights granted to persons serving in girls' Gymnasiums do not extend to teachers of the elementary school.

6. Pensions and allowances to persons serving in the Gymnasium are assigned by its Board of Trustees from the pension fund attached to it, with a principal capital of ten thousand one hundred forty-four rubles. The charter of this fund is confirmed by the Minister of Internal Affairs.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was pleased to Highest-confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the transformation of the girls' school existing at the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of St. Ascension, in the city of Kharkov, into a seven-class Gymnasium, and ordered it to be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 3. Vol. IV. Pp. 563-564.*

## No. 146. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE MILITARY SERVICE OF MENNONITES IN FORESTRY DETACHMENTS, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER III (1885)

581. On the rights, duties, and liability of Mennonites performing compulsory service in forestry detachments.

HIS IMPERIAL MAJESTY was pleased to Highest-confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the rights, duties, and liability of Mennonites performing compulsory service in forestry detachments, and ordered it to be carried out.

Signed by: Chairman of the State Council MIKHAIL.

OPINION OF THE STATE COUNCIL. 7 May 1885.

Extracted from the journals of: the Joint Departments of Laws and of Civil and Ecclesiastical Affairs, 22 December 1884, and of the General Assembly, 22 April 1885.

The State Council, in the Joint Departments of Laws and of Civil and Ecclesiastical Affairs and in General Assembly, having examined the report of the Minister of State Domains on the rights, duties, and liability of Mennonites performing compulsory service in forestry detachments, resolved as its opinion*.

I. With regard to the rights and duties of Mennonites serving in forestry detachments under compulsory service, as well as the liability of such persons for those violations of service duties whose penalties exceed the bounds of disciplinary punishments, the following rules are hereby established:

1) The general management of each detachment of obligated workers, of the buildings erected for it, and of its economy, is entrusted to the forester. In the performance of state works, the obligated workers are subordinate both to the foresters and likewise to other persons appointed to direct the works and to overseers elected from among the members of the detachments.

2) Complaints against the actions of the forester are brought by the obligated workers to the local administration of state domains, and against the latter — to the Minister of State Domains.

3) Obligated workers may, at their own wish, be transferred from one detachment to another. Such transfers are authorized by the local administrator of state domains during the period from October to March, and the expenses connected with the relocation of the transferred worker are charged to the account of the relevant Mennonite community.

4) Obligated workers are permitted to request discharge, whether due to illness, on leave, or entirely from service. In such cases the workers are examined by the physician attending them, in the presence of officials of the department of state domains appointed by the local administration thereof, and a separate report is drawn up for each examination. Those found by this procedure to require temporary release from service are granted leave, depending on the nature of the illness, for a term not exceeding one year, at the expiration of which they are obliged to return to their detachments. Those found to be entirely incapable of either state works or economic occupations in the detachments are discharged from service altogether, without being enrolled in the reserve.

5) Obligated workers who, while serving in the forestry detachments, become incapable of compulsory service, in the event of their incapacity for personal labor and, moreover, having neither their own means of subsistence nor relatives willing to support them, are maintained at the expense of the Mennonite communities from which they entered service.

6) The Minister of State Domains is granted: a) the right to discharge obligated workers into the reserve, where this proves possible, upon completion of four years of active service, counting from 1 January of the year following their call-up, and b) the right to call up such workers from the reserve into service whenever he finds it necessary, and in such numbers and for such terms as he deems necessary.

7) The registration of obligated workers while in the reserve, as well as the execution of orders for calling up such workers from the reserve into service, is entrusted to police officials.

8) The procedure for transferring obligated workers from one detachment to another, for discharging such persons on leave or altogether from service, for registering them while in the reserve, and for calling them up from the reserve into service, is determined by rules confirmed by the Minister of State Domains in agreement with the Minister of Internal Affairs.

9) Obligated workers, for crimes and offenses involving violation of service duties, are brought to trial by the local administrators of state domains.

10) Obligated workers, for crimes and offenses involving violation of service duties, where the penalties for them exceed the bounds of disciplinary punishments, are subject to liability under the Code of Punishments and the Statute on Punishments Imposed by Justices of the Peace. Excepted from this are the following criminal acts: a) insulting, whether verbally, in writing, in print, or by indecent action, a person to whom the obligated worker is subordinate; b) striking such a person, or raising a hand or weapon against him with intent to strike, as well as any kind of violent or highly insolent action against him; c) disobedience to a superior or willful non-performance of his orders; d) giving or presenting testimony of a feigned illness, or willfully inflicting injury upon oneself, or committing any other deception in order to be released from the obligation to serve; e) desertion or unauthorized absence from the detachment or place of service lasting longer than six days; f) failure to report for service at the appointed time without lawful cause; and g) squandering or willful damage of tools used in the performance of works, or of other state property. For the commission of the above-listed violations, obligated workers are subject to the penalties prescribed for them in the Military Statute on Punishments (arts. 97, 98, 101-103, 105, 126, 127, 131-135, 140, 162-164, and 168), with these penalties reduced, depending on the circumstances of the case, by two or three degrees and replaced by the punishments prescribed in the Code of Punishments, on the basis of Appendix I to article 8 of the Military Statute on Punishments (1869, second edition). In this connection, forest rangers, foresters, and overseers are equated to sergeant-majors, non-commissioned officers, and corporals, respectively.

II. Chapter three of section one of book two of the Statute on Criminal Procedure (Judicial Statutes of Emperor Alexander II, 1883 edition) is to be supplemented with the following provision:

"Mennonites performing compulsory service in forestry detachments, for all crimes and offenses, whether or not connected with violation of service duties, are tried by the criminal court of the civil department."

III. The Rules on the Performance by Mennonites of Compulsory Service in Forestry Detachments of the Department of the Ministry of State Domains (Code of Laws, Vol. VIII, Part I, Forestry Statute, art. 26, note, appendix, per the 1883 continuation) are to be supplemented with the following provision:

"For the rendering of initial medical aid to obligated workers from among the Mennonites, one hired paramedic (feldsher) is to be maintained at each forestry detachment. In cases where the placement of sick workers for treatment in military medical institutions is found to be inconvenient or disadvantageous for the treasury, zemstvo or other physicians are to be engaged to treat the sick, by prior agreement with them. The expense required for the maintenance of paramedics, the engagement of physicians, and the procurement of medicines, is charged to the sums appropriated under the estimate of the Ministry of State Domains for forestry works."

The original opinion is signed in the journals by the Chairmen and Members.

*SURP. 1885. 1st half-year. No. 70. Pp. 1355-1359.*

## No. 147. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE SETTLEMENT OF FOREIGN SETTLERS IN THE SOUTHWESTERN GOVERNORATES, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER III (1888)

5357. — June 15. Highest-confirmed opinion of the State Council (Coll. of Statutes 1888, September 6, art. 804). — On the arrangement of the condition of foreign settlers established in the governorates of Kiev, Podolia, and Volhynia.

The State Council, in the Joint Departments of Laws and of State Economy and in General Assembly, having examined the report of the Minister of Internal Affairs on the arrangement of the condition of foreign settlers established in the governorates of Kiev, Podolia, and Volhynia, resolved as its opinion:

1. With regard to the arrangement of the condition of foreign settlers established in the governorates of Kiev, Podolia, and Volhynia, the following rules are hereby established:

A. Regarding settlers who have accepted Russian subjecthood.

1) Foreign settlers who have accepted Russian subjecthood and who have not, prior to the promulgation of the present rules, acquired the rights of a higher estate, are to be entered into the ranks of rural or urban inhabitants on the bases set forth in the following articles (arts. 2-11).

Note. Among those recognized as having accepted Russian subjecthood are, incidentally, also those settlers who, by virtue of their former place of residence in the governorates of the Kingdom of Poland, acquired subjecthood there by being entered in the registers of the permanent population.

2) The settlers referred to in article 1 are assigned: a) those residing in towns, posads, and boroughs — to the estate of urban inhabitants, and b) those settled outside towns, posads, and boroughs — to the estate of rural inhabitants, with the exceptions specified in articles 3 and 4 of the present rules.

3) Those among the settlers established outside towns, posads, and boroughs who, possessing a considerable quantity of land, do not personally engage in agriculture but cultivate the land with hired labor, are permitted, within six months from the day of the promulgation of the present rules, to choose their mode of life according to the generally established procedure. Those who fail to do so are, upon expiration of the said term, assigned to the estate of rural inhabitants by order of the Government.

4) Those among the settlers established outside towns, posads, and boroughs who, prior to the promulgation of the present rules, acquire the rights of urban status, are assigned, retaining these rights, to the volosts nearest their place of settlement, on the bases indicated in article 7, and are subject to the volost authorities strictly in respect of police and obligation matters.

5) Settlers assigned to the estate of urban inhabitants are registered with the meshchanin (townsman) societies of the towns and boroughs where they permanently reside.

6) Settlers assigned to the rural estate who are proprietors and have common economic interests are united into rural societies, which are included within the existing volosts. The officials of rural administration elected by such societies are confirmed by the Peace Mediators.

7) All settlers assigned to the rural estate who have not entered into the composition of rural societies may register with such societies, with the latter's consent. Those who do not avail themselves of this right within one year from the day of assignment are compulsorily registered with the volosts nearest their place of settlement, applying the rules attached to note 2 to article 147 of the General Statute (Code of Laws, Vol. IX, special appendix, 1876 edition, I), but without requiring admission resolutions from the relevant volost assemblies.

8) At volost assemblies in which elected representatives of foreign settlers participate, only persons belonging to the indigenous Russian population may be elected to the positions of volost elders and clerks.

9) Settlers of the rural estate (item b, art. 2) who, prior to the promulgation of the present rules, registered with societies and volosts other than those in which they permanently reside, are subject to transfer to their actual place of settlement.

10) Persons assigned to the rural estate may transfer to urban societies only in the event of their actual settlement in the localities in which they wish to be registered.

11) Those foreign settlers who, under various designations, were formerly included in the census rolls but have hitherto not been entered into the general composition of rural or urban inhabitants, are subject to assignment to rural or meshchanin societies, on the same bases as the settlers referred to in the preceding articles.

B. Regarding settlers who have not accepted Russian subjecthood.

12) Settlers who have not accepted Russian subjecthood, established outside towns, posads, and boroughs on lands owned or leased by them, are assigned, for the performance of obligations, to the volosts nearest their place of settlement, without requiring admission resolutions from the relevant volost assemblies. Settlers of this category are subject to volost administration, moreover, also in respect of police matters.

Note. The rule set forth in article 12 does not apply to foreign nobles, nor to foreigners who have entered state service, who have been assigned the rank of honorary citizens, or who are enrolled in the merchant guilds.

13) The settlers referred to in article 12 perform all state, zemstvo, and communal obligations on the same bases as peasants registered with volosts (arts. 4-6 of the appendix to note 2 to art. 147 of the General Statute), but without the right to participate in volost assemblies.

14) The punctual performance of obligations (art. 13) is secured by all movable and immovable property of the settlers.

15) Foreigners who, having no permanent settlement outside towns, posads, and boroughs, reside on the lands of persons subject to volost administration, are, together with their families, subject to the jurisdiction of this administration, on the same basis as the settlers mentioned in article 12 of the present rules, but only in respect of police matters.

16) In the event of difficulties in the administration, in respect of police matters, of settlers assigned on the aforesaid bases to the volosts, the volost assembly is permitted to elect the necessary number of special assessors to assist the volost elder in the police and administrative matters entrusted to him, in accordance with note 2 to article 87 of the General Statute on Peasants (Code of Laws, Vol. IX, special appendix, 1876 edition).

Note. The assessors referred to in article 16 may also be elected from among persons assigned to the volosts on the basis of articles 4 and 7 of the present rules.

II. The Governor-General of the Southwestern Territory is authorized to determine, by a special instruction, the procedure for putting the present rules into effect by the relevant institutions, and also to resolve misunderstandings and complaints arising from the application of these rules, with the exception of those which, by their nature, require Highest resolution or are subject to review by judicial institutions.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was pleased to Highest-confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the arrangement of the condition of foreign settlers established in the governorates of Kiev, Podolia, and Volhynia, and ordered it to be carried out.

*PSZRI. Coll. 3. Vol. VIII. Pp. 409-411.*

## No. 148. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON PRIVILEGES FOR THE CAUCASIAN COLONY OF GNADENBURG, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER III (1888)

5382. — July 2. Highest-confirmed decision of the Committee of Ministers (Coll. of Statutes 1888, September 9, art. 818). — On granting various privileges to the settlers of the colony of Gnadenburg, Terek Region.

The Committee of Ministers, having heard the memorandum of the Minister of Internal Affairs on granting various privileges to the settlers of the colony of Gnadenburg, Terek Region, resolved: to seek His Imperial Majesty's Highest consent to grant the following privileges to the German settlers, established in 1882-83 in the Caucasus on land purchased by them, of the colony of Gnadenburg, Vladikavkaz district, Terek Region:

1. Members of the said colony are granted the free exercise of their faith, as well as the administration of the colony's ecclesiastical affairs according to the charter, teaching, and rites existing in the community of these colonists.

2. Pending the general transformation of the condition of foreign colonists in the Caucasus, the settlers of the colony of Gnadenburg are permitted to establish, for the administration of communal affairs, a board elected from among themselves consisting of one elder and two members, with elections of these persons renewed every three years.

3. All settlers of this colony, numbering forty families, are to be exempted for five years, beginning in 1888, from payment of state and monetary zemstvo assessed dues.

4. In addition, there is to be returned to them: a) the entire state land tax already paid by them into the treasury for the years 1883-1888, and b) four hundred forty-six rubles and ninety-three kopecks in duties and incidental fees collected from them by the Verzhbolovo Customs House.

5. All members of the same colony from among the aforementioned families, established there in 1882-1883, who may by their age be liable to call-up for military service, are to be exempted from such service up to and including 1892; and

6. If, upon announcing the granted privileges to the colonists, it is discovered that they are not yet Russian subjects, then, prior to the granting of these privileges, all colonists are to be sworn to allegiance to Russia; and in the event of their refusal to take the oath of allegiance, these colonists are subject to immediate expulsion abroad, after everything given to them for their settlement has been taken back from them.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 2nd day of July 1888, was Highest pleased to consent to this.

*PSZRI. Coll. 3. Vol. VIII. Pp. 421-422.*

## No. 149. DECISION OF THE SENATE ON THE PROCEDURE FOR COLLECTING PRIVATE DEBTS FROM FORMER COLONISTS (1890)

329. On the application of note 3 to article 24 of the General Statute on Peasants Emerging from Serfdom to peasant-proprietor settlers (former colonists).

The Governing Senate, in the general assembly of the 1st and cassation departments, on 22 January 1890, having heard the proposal of the Chief Procurator, based on the order of the Minister of Justice No. 601, on the printing in the Collection of Statutes and Orders of the Government of the decision of the Governing Senate rendered by the general assembly of the 1st and cassation departments on 28 May 1879 concerning the procedure for collecting private debts from peasant-proprietors, resolved: that the decision of the said general assembly of the Governing Senate, of 28 May 1879, concerning the procedure for collecting private debts from peasant-proprietors, be printed in the Collection of Statutes and Orders of the Government, and that notice thereof, together with a copy of the said decision, be sent to the office of the Senate Printing House.

28 May 1879. By decree of His Imperial Majesty, the Governing Senate heard: the report of the Governor of Kherson, forwarded with the notice of the chancellery of the 1st department of the Governing Senate, concerning a dispute that had arisen between the peasant institutions and the Odessa district justice-of-the-peace assembly regarding the application to peasant-proprietor settlers (former colonists) of the statutory provisions and of the Senate's decree of 11 January 1878, No. 1,106, concerning peasants in the collection of private debts from them.

The Governor of Kherson, in his report of 12 December 1878, No. 3,477, submitted for the resolution of the 1st department of the Governing Senate a copy of the journal of the Kherson Provincial Presence for Peasant Affairs of 23 November 1878, from which it appears that, on the question that had arisen concerning the satisfaction of private debts of temporarily obligated peasants, the general assembly of the cassation departments of the Governing Senate, at its session of 15 December 1869, recognized that, according to the 1869 continuation of the Code of Laws, issued already after the Judicial Statutes of 1864, the rules set forth in Vol. XII, Part 2, of the Statute on Order in State Villages, articles 384-407, to which reference is made, and in the General Statute on Peasants, are not shown as repealed or supplemented, and that, therefore, the said rules concerning the procedure for the execution of court decisions relating to monetary claims against peasants must be considered to have retained their force even after the issuance of the Judicial Statutes of 1864, in which the repeal of those rules is not expressly stated. Since, according to information received in the Ministries of Internal Affairs and of Justice, it appeared that, in the course of collecting private debts from peasants, the most essential property in their households was often sold, there having been repeated instances of the sale, to cover such claims, of literally all of a peasant's property, the Minister of Justice, in agreement with the Ministers of Internal Affairs and of Finance, communicated by circular proposals the above-stated clarification of the general assembly of the cassation departments of the Governing Senate to the chairmen of the assemblies of justices of the peace and the chairmen of the district courts, and requested them to instruct the court bailiffs attached to the assemblies and courts entrusted to them to be guided, in the aforesaid case, by note 3 to article 24 of the General Statute on Peasants and articles 384-407 of Vol. XII, Part 2, of the Statute on Order in State Villages. Notwithstanding this clarification, difficulties were constantly encountered in practice in the precise understanding and application of the cited articles, owing to the fact that the execution of court decisions on the collection of debts from peasants, under the Judicial Statutes of 20 November 1864, is entrusted to court bailiffs, who in these cases are guided exclusively by the relevant articles of the Judicial Statutes. The Governing Senate, as appears from its decree of the 1st department of 11 January 1878, No. 1,106, in order to remove such difficulties and misunderstandings in those cases where the execution of a court decision on the collection of a debt from individual peasants, bypassing the village authorities, is entrusted to a court bailiff, found it necessary to clarify: a) that the court bailiff, in the event of non-payment by a peasant-debtor of the sum awarded against him by a court decision, must first, in accordance with articles 384 and 385 of the Statute on Order in State Villages, set a term within which the defendant is obliged to pay the debt; b) that, upon expiration of the term set, in the event of non-payment of the debt by the defendant, the bailiff may proceed to inventory his property, but only in the presence of the village elder and the volost elder, in order to determine what part of the debtor peasant's property may be sold to satisfy the plaintiff without disrupting the peasant household; and c) that, out of the sum obtained through the sale of the property, the court bailiff, according to information communicated to him by the relevant volost administration, is obliged to satisfy in full the arrears recorded against the peasant-debtor in respect of taxes, communal dues, and redemption payments or landlord quit-rents, and to apply only the remaining sum to the satisfaction of the creditor and the recovery of court costs. Meanwhile, the court bailiff of the Odessa district assembly of justices of the peace, Leiman, on 16 March 1878 inventoried the movable property of the Freudental peasant-proprietor settlers Peter and Heinrich Rener in satisfaction of private debts, without observing the conditions specified in the aforementioned decree of the Governing Senate, explaining that that decree applies only to peasants, but not to settlers; and another court bailiff of the same justice-of-the-peace assembly, Braikevich, in 1877 inventoried the property of certain peasant-proprietor settlers of the village of Kuban and scheduled it for sale on 20 April 1878, and although the volost elder informed the court bailiff that the inventoried property constituted the last necessity in the household, the court bailiff nevertheless sold this property; for example, he sold at auction the last and only horse of the settler Afanasy Meikhov for 15 rubles, and out of the proceeds paid 4 rubles 66 kopecks toward Meikhov's arrears of state and zemstvo obligations, retaining the remaining money for travel expenses (progony). Recognizing that the Governing Senate's decree of 11 January 1878, No. 1,106, and the statutory provisions cited therein, apply to all peasants, including settlers (former colonists), the chairman of the Odessa district Presence for Peasant Affairs, pursuant to reports from the Freudental volost administration and the Kuban volost elder, communicated the above-described actions of the court bailiffs to the Odessa district assembly of justices of the peace. In response, the assembly of justices of the peace communicated that the settlers Reiner could themselves petition on their own behalf, and that the assembly did not consider itself entitled to extend the effect of the cited decree of the Governing Senate to peasant-proprietor settlers, since it applies exclusively to peasants.
