On 27 September 1878 the court bailiff of the same assembly of justices of the peace, Leiman, inventoried the property of the settler of the village of Kandel, Georg Rieger, and scheduled it for public sale on 4 October in payment of a debt to the meshchanin Leiba Itskovich, and in doing so the bailiff invited neither the village elder nor the volost elder, whereas, as the Odessa Presence for Peasant Affairs reported, on the basis of information furnished by the Seltz volost administration, the sale of the inventoried property would bring about the complete ruin of the settler Rieger. In view of the foregoing circumstances, the Kherson Provincial Presence for Peasant Affairs and the chairman of that Presence, the Governor of Kherson, applied to the Odessa district assembly of justices of the peace, requesting it to direct that the court bailiffs subordinate to it, in enforcing claims against peasant-proprietor settlers (former colonists), be guided by the Governing Senate's decree of 11 January 1878, No. 1,106, which applies to them as well, inasmuch as, according to the precise meaning of the statutory provisions of articles 1 and 2 of the Rules on the Arrangement of Peasant-Proprietor Settlers (Former Colonists), Code of Laws on Rural Estates, 1876 edition, and of article 700, with the note thereto, of Vol. IX of the Code of Laws on Estates, 1876 edition, peasant-proprietor settlers are the same as peasants. In response, the Odessa district assembly of justices of the peace informed that it adhered to its previous opinion that the Governing Senate's decree of 11 January 1878, No. 1,106, does not extend to peasant-proprietor settlers, since the procedure set forth therein, concerning claims by private persons, applies only to peasants. Taking into consideration: first, that under the law of 4 June 1871 (Rules on the Arrangement of Peasant-Proprietor Settlers [Former Colonists], 1876 edition), the provisions of 19 February 1861 concerning peasants have been extended to former colonists; second, that, under the same law (art. 2), former colonists have entered into the composition of rural inhabitants and have been assigned "to the category of peasant-proprietors"; third, that, on the basis of the same law, former colonists have the same rural and volost administration as peasants (art. 3), and also perform the same communal obligations and zemstvo dues as peasants of all designations, and likewise pay quit-rent tax for the land allotments received under title deeds, on the same bases as state peasants (art. 5); and, finally, fourth, that in the laws on estates (Vol. IX, art. 700 and the note thereto, 1876 edition), former colonists are shown as assigned to the number of rural inhabitants — the Provincial Presence found that former colonists, transferred to the jurisdiction of the general provincial and district, as well as local, institutions for peasant affairs, are peasants as of 4 June 1871, and that, therefore, it is beyond doubt that the statutory provisions cited in the Governing Senate's decree of 11 January 1878, No. 1,106, and the decree of the Senate itself, extend to them as they do to peasants, even though the designation "peasant-proprietor settlers" is not used therein. But since the Odessa district assembly of justices of the peace holds an entirely contrary opinion, the result of which is the sale of the last property necessary in the households of peasant-proprietor settlers (former colonists), thereby ruining the peasants and rendering them potentially insolvent payers of state and zemstvo dues, the Provincial Presence for Peasant Affairs resolved: to submit the foregoing for the resolution of the Governing Senate through the 1st department. The present case was transmitted, together with the notice of the chancellery of the 1st department, to the like general assembly of the cassation departments.

Having heard the opinion of the acting deputy chief procurator, the Governing Senate, in a joint session of the 1st and cassation departments, turning to consider the question raised by the Kherson Provincial Board for Peasant Affairs as to whether the decree of the 1st Department of the Governing Senate of 11 January 1878, No. 1,106, extends to settler-proprietors (former colonists), finds that settler-proprietors (former colonists), by the exact force of articles 700, 731, and 748 of Vol. IX with the notes thereto, and article 2 of the rules on their organization, set forth in No. XV of the statute on the rural estate (special appendix to Vol. IX, 1876 edition), have entered into the composition of rural inhabitants and been assigned to the category of peasants, whereby, as stated in this latter article, they retained, on the grounds indicated in the subsequent articles, also the personal privileges which they had hitherto enjoyed. From the literal sense of the said provisions it is evident that settler-proprietors (former colonists) have been granted not merely the name of peasant-proprietors, but that, besides the personal rights and privileges established in the special rules concerning settler-proprietors and those which they had hitherto enjoyed, they must also enjoy those rights, personal and pertaining to status, which are common to all rural inhabitants assigned to the category of peasant-proprietors, and which do not contradict the special provisions concerning settler-proprietors. Such a right is unquestionably the right granted to peasants in note 3 to article 24 of the General Statute on Peasants Emerging from Serfdom, establishing the rights of peasants with respect to claims, complaints, petitions, and litigation, and consisting in the following: "monetary exactions from peasants are carried out in accordance with the rules established in articles 384–407 of the Statute on the Good Order of State Villages, and that, in the sale of peasants' property to satisfy an exaction, out of the proceeds, arrears on state and seigneurial dues, as well as on communal levies, are satisfied first and in full, and only thereafter other exactions in proportion to the claims." Basing itself precisely on this note and on other provisions of the General Statute, as well as of the Statute on Redemption and the Local Statute of the Great Russian governorates relating to the procedure for collecting arrears on state taxes, communal levies, redemption payments, and seigneurial quitrents, the Governing Senate, through the 1st Department, by decree of 11 January 1878, No. 1,106, printed in article 62

## No. 16. of the Collection of Statutes and Orders of the Government, resolved the question raised, among others, of the procedure by which the inventory and sale of the property of individual peasants should be carried out to satisfy private debts adjudged by court decisions, and then, in furtherance of the aforementioned laws, issued the rule set forth above in the journal of the Kherson Provincial Board for Peasant Affairs, for the guidance of court bailiffs, in the case where the execution of court decisions on the recovery of debts from individual peasants is entrusted to them apart from the village authorities. In consequence of this, and taking into account: 1) that, on the basis of the aforementioned rules on the organization of settler-proprietors, 1876 edition, former colonists have the same village and volost administration as peasants (art. 4), and likewise perform the same communal duties and zemstvo levies as peasants, and pay for the land allotments received under title deeds, on the same grounds as state peasants, the quitrent tax (arts. 5 and 18); 2) that the proper fulfillment by settlers of the taxes and levies, zemstvo and communal duties due from them, is likewise secured by the procedure indicated in articles 187–191 of the General Statute on Peasants and the supplementary provisions thereto (art. 5); 3) that the principal motivating cause for the issuance of the rules mentioned in the Senate decree of 11 January 1878 was the necessity of extreme caution in the sale of peasants' property to satisfy private debts, in order to safeguard the economic life of the peasant estate and its financial and economic interests, and 4) that the same necessity exists with respect to settler-proprietors (former colonists), who, as stated above, form part of that same peasant estate — the Governing Senate resolves: to recognize that the decree of the Governing Senate of 11 January 1878 applies also to settler-proprietors; and to send decrees to this effect to the Kherson Governor and to the Odessa District Justice of the Peace Congress.

*SURP. 1890. 1st half. No. 38. Pp. 778–783.*

## No. 150. DECREE OF ALEXANDER III ON THE SUBORDINATION OF LUTHERAN SCHOOLS TO THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION (1890)

7211. — November 22. Imperial command, announced by the Minister of Internal Affairs (Collection of Statutes 1890, December 23, art. 1184). — On the subordination of Protestant schools in the districts of the St. Petersburg and Moscow Lutheran Consistories to the Ministry of Public Education.

The Sovereign Emperor, upon the most loyal report of the Minister of Internal Affairs, on the 22nd day of November 1890, was Highest pleased to command: that all Lutheran church schools without exception in the districts of the Moscow and St. Petersburg Evangelical Lutheran Consistories, located in the governorates indicated in points 1 and 5 of article 434 of the Digest of Laws, Vol. XI, Part I, per the 1886 Supplement, together with all property belonging to these schools, be subordinated to the department of the Ministry of Public Education, on the same general basis as other primary schools under the administration of that Ministry, and with the proviso that, under the new order of administration, the right of the Protestant clergy to oversee the religious education of youth in the said establishments be preserved.

*PSZRI. Coll. 3. Vol. X. Sect. 1. Pp. 742–743.*

## No. 151. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE APPOINTMENT OF PRESIDENTS OF THE EVANGELICAL LUTHERAN CONSISTORIES, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER III (1891)

389. On the procedure for filling the offices of presidents of the evangelical Lutheran consistories.

His Imperial Majesty was Highest pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the procedure for filling the offices of presidents of the evangelical Lutheran consistories, and commanded that it be carried into effect.

Signed: Chairman of the State Council, MIKHAIL.

OPINION OF THE STATE COUNCIL. 4 March 1891.

Extracted from the journals of the Department of Laws of 9 February and of the General Assembly of 18 February 1891.

The State Council, in the Department of Laws and in the General Assembly, having considered the submission of the Minister of Internal Affairs concerning the amendment of article 436 of the Digest of Laws, Vol. XI, Part I, per the 1886 Supplement, resolved in its opinion:

In amendment of article 436 of the Statute on the Spiritual Affairs of Foreign Confessions (Digest of Laws, Vol. XI, Part I, per Supplement) and other pertinent statutes, to enact:

"The presidents of the St. Petersburg, Moscow, Livonia, Courland, and Estonia evangelical Lutheran consistories shall be appointed by His Imperial Majesty, upon the submission of the Minister of Internal Affairs, who shall first request the opinion of the general consistory concerning the candidates proposed."

The authentic opinion is signed in the journals by the Chairmen and Members.

*SURP. 1891. 1st half. No. 36. P. 808.*

## No. 152. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE KEEPING OF LUTHERAN VITAL RECORDS IN THE RUSSIAN LANGUAGE, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER III (1891)

1057. On the keeping of vital records of the Lutheran confession in the Russian language.

His Imperial Majesty was Highest pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the keeping of vital records of the Lutheran confession in the Russian language, and commanded that it be carried into effect.

Signed: for the Chairman of the State Council, State Secretary

D. Selsky.

OPINION OF THE STATE COUNCIL. 3 June 1891.

Extracted from the journals of the Department of Laws of 23 March and of the General Assembly of 20 May 1891.

The State Council, in the Department of Laws and in the General Assembly, having considered the ruling of the First General Assembly of the Governing Senate on the clarification of the language in which Lutheran preachers must keep vital records, as well as issue extracts therefrom, resolved in its opinion:

I. In amendment and supplement of the pertinent articles of the Digest of Laws on Estates (Digest of Laws, Vol. IX), the Statutes on the Spiritual Affairs of Foreign Confessions (Digest of Laws, Vol. XI, Part I), and the Digest of Local Statutes of the Baltic Governorates, to enact the following rules:

1) Vital records of the Lutheran confession are to be kept in the Russian language.

2) With respect to extracts issued, at the request of the authorities or upon petitions of private persons, from those vital records which prior to the issuance of the present law were not kept in the Russian language, evangelical Lutheran preachers are obliged to attach a translation of such extracts into Russian, certified by the preacher's signature and the affixing of the church seal.

II. The provisions set forth in the preceding (I) section shall take effect from 1 January 1892.

The authentic opinion is signed in the journals by the Chairmen and Members.

*SURP. 1891. 2nd half. No. 104. Pp. 2740–2741.*

## No. 153. DECREE OF ALEXANDER III ON THE RULES FOR THE SETTLEMENT IN VOLHYNIA OF PERSONS OF NON-RUSSIAN ORIGIN (1892)

363. On the establishment of temporary rules concerning the settlement in Volhynia Governorate of persons of non-Russian origin.

**DECREE TO THE GOVERNING SENATE.**

In 1884 and 1887 special statutes were issued directed at strengthening Russian landownership in the western governorates of Russia.

Now, in view of the special situation of Volhynia Governorate, We have deemed it proper, in furtherance and supplement of the aforementioned statutes, to establish, pending the issuance of a new law on Russian subjecthood, temporary rules concerning the settlement in Volhynia Governorate of persons of non-Russian origin.

In consequence of this, in accordance with the decision of the Committee of Ministers, We command:

1) To prohibit all foreign immigrants, including those who have accepted Russian subjecthood: a) henceforth from settling within the confines of Volhynia Governorate outside urban settlements, and b) in future, from acquiring in the said governorate, by whatever means, other than inheritance by law, the right of ownership of immovable properties located outside urban settlements, as well as the right of possession or use of such properties.

2) To preserve, for those of the aforementioned persons who, by the day of the promulgation of the present Decree, have already settled in the said governorate outside urban settlements, the right to the possession and use of land plots acquired by them in ownership or leased by them on a lawful basis; and for those among them who profess the Orthodox faith — also the right to acquire in ownership and in use immovable properties outside urban settlements.

3) To recognize as invalid all manner of transactions concluded in violation or circumvention of the prohibition set forth in point 1 of the present Decree.

4) If a transaction mentioned in the preceding point 3 of this Decree is discovered by the local provincial authorities, then, upon obtaining the necessary information, which the said authorities are obliged to furnish immediately — whether judicial or all other government bodies and persons — the Governor shall authorize an official subordinate to him to bring, in the local district court, a suit for the annulment of the transaction concluded or the act performed. These matters are to be conducted according to the procedure established for matters of state administration, and

5) To grant to the Governor of Volhynia the authority to expel by administrative procedure, to their place of permanent residence, persons who have settled, after the promulgation of the present Decree, outside urban settlements of Volhynia Governorate, contrary to the prohibition set forth in point 1.

The Governing Senate will not fail to make the appropriate arrangement for the execution hereof.

Signed in the original by His Imperial Majesty's own hand: "ALEXANDER."

At Gatchina.

14 March 1892.

*SURP. 1892. 1st half. No. 33. Pp. 661–663.*

## No. 154. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON SPECIAL RULES FOR THE SETTLEMENT IN VOLHYNIA OF PERSONS OF NON-RUSSIAN ORIGIN, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER III (1892)

568. On the establishment of special rules for the settlement in Volhynia Governorate of persons of non-Russian origin.

The Committee of Ministers, having considered the submission of the Minister of Internal Affairs on the establishment of special rules for the settlement in Volhynia Governorate of persons of non-Russian origin, held:

I. That the draft of the Imperial Highest Decree to the Governing Senate concerning the procedure for settlement in Volhynia Governorate of persons of non-Russian origin, composed by the Minister of Internal Affairs and revised in accordance with the Committee's remarks, be submitted for the Highest consideration of His Imperial Majesty, presenting it for the Highest signature of His Majesty, and

II. To grant to the Governor-General of Kiev, Podolia, and Volhynia the authority to issue free emigration certificates to foreign settlers established in the governorates under his jurisdiction, without seeking special Highest permission on each occasion.

The Sovereign Emperor was Highest pleased to approve the decision of the Committee, and the draft of the Imperial Highest Decree to the Governing Senate was honored with His Majesty's signature, at Gatchina, on the 14th day of March 1892.

*SURP. 1892. 1st half. No. 57. Pp. 1164–1165.*

## No. 155. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE TRANSFER OF PROTESTANT SCHOOLS TO THE JURISDICTION OF THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER III (1892)

497. On the transfer of Protestant church schools in the Transcaucasian territory and in the settlement of Sarepta, Saratov Governorate, to the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Public Education.

His Imperial Majesty was Highest pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the transfer of Protestant church schools in the Transcaucasian territory and in the settlement of Sarepta, Saratov Governorate, to the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Public Education, and commanded that it be carried into effect.

Signed: Chairman of the State Council, MIKHAIL.

OPINION OF THE STATE COUNCIL. 30 March 1892.

Extracted from the journals of the Joint Departments of State Economy and Laws of 23 January and of the General Assembly of 16 March 1892.

The State Council, in the Joint Departments of State Economy and Laws and in the General Assembly, having considered the submission of the Minister of Internal Affairs on the transfer of Protestant church schools in the Transcaucasian territory and in the settlement of Sarepta, Saratov Governorate, to the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Public Education, resolved in its opinion:

The Protestant church schools in the Transcaucasian territory and in the settlement of Sarepta, Saratov Governorate, which are under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, together with all property belonging to them, are to be transferred to the administration of the Ministry of Public Education.

The authentic opinion is signed in the journals by the Chairmen and Members.

*SURP. 1892. 1st half. No. 52. P. 1022.*

## No. 156. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE KEEPING OF PROTESTANT VITAL RECORDS IN THE RUSSIAN LANGUAGE, CONFIRMED BY ALEXANDER III (1892)

602. On the keeping of vital records of the Protestant confessions in the Russian language.

His Imperial Majesty was Highest pleased to confirm the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the keeping of vital records of the Protestant confessions in the Russian language, and commanded that it be carried into effect.

Signed: For the Chairman of the State Council, Alexander Abaza.

OPINION OF THE STATE COUNCIL. 28 April 1892.

Extracted from the journals of the Department of Laws of 29 February and of the General Assembly of 13 April 1892.

The State Council, in the Department of Laws and in the General Assembly, having considered the submission of the Minister of Internal Affairs on the introduction of the Russian language into the registration of vital records of Protestants, resolved in its opinion:

The effect of the rules of the opinion of the State Council of 3 June 1891, Highest confirmed, on the keeping of vital records of the Lutheran confession in the Russian language (Collection of Statutes and Orders of the Government, 1891, art. 1057), is to be extended, from 1 July 1892, to all other Protestant confessions whose vital records are kept by their preachers and spiritual mentors.

The authentic opinion is signed in the journals by the Chairmen and Members.

*SURP. 1892. 1st half. No. 59. P. 1214.*

## No. 157. DECREE OF ALEXANDER III ON THE SUBORDINATION OF CATHOLIC SCHOOLS TO THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION (1892)

164. On the subordination of schools attached to Roman Catholic churches in the Empire to the department of the Ministry of Public Education.

The Sovereign Emperor, upon the most loyal report of the Minister of Internal Affairs, on the 10th day of December 1892, was Highest pleased to command that all schools attached to Roman Catholic churches in the Empire be transferred to the department of the Ministry of Public Education, on the same general basis, and with the proviso that, under the new order of administration, the right of the Catholic clergy to oversee the religious education of youth in the said establishments be preserved.

*SURP. 1893. 1st half. No. 16. Pp. 294–295.*

## No. 158. DECISION OF THE COMMITTEE OF MINISTERS ON THE AMENDMENT OF THE RULES FOR THE SETTLEMENT OF PERSONS OF NON-RUSSIAN ORIGIN IN VOLHYNIA, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS II (1895)

11477. — March 19. Highest confirmed decision of the Committee of Ministers (Collection of Statutes 1895, April 28, art. 472). — On the amendment of the Temporary Rules, Highest confirmed on 14 March 1892, concerning the settlement in Volhynia Governorate of persons of non-Russian origin.

The Sovereign Emperor, upon the decision of the Committee of Ministers, on the 19th day of March 1895, was Highest pleased to command: that in place of the Temporary Rules, Highest confirmed on 14 March 1892 (8419, 8420), concerning the settlement in Volhynia Governorate of persons of non-Russian origin, the following be enacted:

1. The acquisition of the right of ownership of immovable properties outside urban settlements of Volhynia Governorate, as well as the right of possession and use of such immovable properties arising from a contract of hire or lease, is henceforth prohibited to: a) foreign settlers who are Russian subjects (Digest of Laws, Vol. IX, art. 1003, note 5, appendix, per the 1890 Supplement) and b) persons resettling from the Vistula governorates.

2. The effect of the rule set forth in article 1 does not extend to those of the persons named therein who settled outside urban settlements prior to the issuance of the present decision of the Committee of Ministers, nor to their successors in title by inheritance by law.

3. If a transaction concluded in violation or circumvention of article 1 of this decision is discovered by the local provincial authorities, then, upon obtaining the necessary information, which the said authorities are obliged to furnish immediately — whether judicial or all other government bodies and persons — the Governor shall authorize an official subordinate to him to bring, in the local District Court, a suit for the annulment of the transaction concluded or the act performed. These matters are to be conducted according to the procedure established for matters of state administration.

4. The Governor of Volhynia is empowered to expel, by administrative procedure, from the confines of Volhynia Governorate, persons mentioned in article 1 of the present decision, as well as foreign subjects who, in violation — the former of the said article of this decision, and the latter of the law of 14 March 1887 — are found actually to possess immovable properties outside urban settlements of Volhynia Governorate under verbal agreements and generally informal arrangements, or after court decisions have been rendered annulling transactions concluded by them for the possession and use of these properties; — and

5. The Governor-General of Kiev, Podolia, and Volhynia is empowered to determine, by special instruction, the procedure for the execution of the present rules by the competent administrative institutions, and also to resolve any misunderstandings that may arise in these institutions in the application of the said rules.

*PSZRI. Coll. 3. Vol. XV. Pp. 142–143.*

## No. 160. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON TEACHING IN THE RUSSIAN LANGUAGE IN COLONIST SCHOOLS, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS II (1897)

463. On the introduction, in the schools of settler-proprietors (former foreign colonists), of instruction in the Russian language.

Signed: Chairman of the State Council, MIKHAIL.

OPINION OF THE STATE COUNCIL. 24 February 1897.

The State Council, in the Joint Departments of Laws, State Economy, and Civil and Ecclesiastical Affairs and in the General Assembly, having considered the submission of the Minister of Public Education on granting to the Ministry entrusted to him the right to introduce Russian as the language of instruction in schools established for settler-proprietors (former foreign colonists), resolved in its opinion:

## No. 161. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE TRANSFER OF THE TRANSCAUCASIAN COLONIES TO THE JURISDICTION OF THE GENERAL ADMINISTRATIVE INSTITUTIONS, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1903)

1014. On the transfer of the Transcaucasian colonists to the jurisdiction of the general provincial and district institutions, as well as the local institutions for peasant affairs.

His Imperial Majesty was graciously pleased to confirm and ordered to be carried out the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the transfer of the Transcaucasian colonists to the jurisdiction of the general provincial and district institutions, as well as the local institutions for peasant affairs.

Signed: Chairman of the State Council, MIKHAIL.

OPINION OF THE STATE COUNCIL. June 10, 1903.

Extracted from the journals of the United Departments of Laws, Civil and Ecclesiastical Affairs, State Economy and Industry, Sciences and Trade, of April 26, and of the General Assembly of May 31, 1903.

The State Council, in the United Departments of Laws, Civil and Ecclesiastical Affairs, State Economy and Industry, Sciences and Trade, and in the General Assembly, having examined the report of the Minister of Internal Affairs on the transfer of the Transcaucasian colonists to the jurisdiction of the general provincial and district institutions, as well as the local institutions for peasant affairs, resolved as follows:

To transfer the German colonists settled on the crown lands of the Tiflis and Elisavetpol governorates (Caucasian Institution, art. 120) to the jurisdiction of the general provincial and district institutions, as well as the local institutions for peasant or settler affairs, while retaining in force, with respect to the said persons, articles 1—14, 16—60, points 1—4 of article 61, and article 62 of the Rules on the Colonists of the Caucasian Region [Laws on the Estates, Appendix I to art. 680 (note 2), 1899 edition], with the following additions and amendments thereto:

1) Decisions of the rural administration may be appealed within a 30-day period to the justice of the peace, whose rulings may, within the same period, be appealed to the local provincial presence for peasant or settler affairs. Both the justice of the peace and the provincial presence shall examine cases of this kind on their merits.

2) The distribution of the colonies among the districts of the justices of the peace (justice sections), as well as subsequent changes in such distribution, shall be carried out, upon the submissions of the governors concerned, by the Chief Administrator of Civil Affairs in the Caucasus.

The original opinion was signed in the journals by the Chairmen and Members.

*SURP. 1903. Section One. 2nd half-year. No. 87. P. 1985.*

## No. 162. DECISION OF THE STATE COUNCIL ON THE ORGANIZATION OF THE LIVONIAN COLONIES, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1904)

24667. — May 31. Opinion of the State Council, Highest Confirmed (Collection of Statutes, 1904, August 24, sect. I, art. 1381). — On the administrative and judicial organization of the Livonian colony within the boundaries of the crown manors of Hirschenhof and Helfreichshof, Wenden district, Livonia governorate.

The State Council, in the United Departments of Laws, Civil and Ecclesiastical Affairs, State Economy and Industry, Sciences and Trade, and in the General Assembly, having examined the report of the Minister of Internal Affairs on the administrative and judicial organization of the Livonian colony within the boundaries of the crown manors of Hirschenhof and Helfreichshof, Wenden district, Livonia governorate, resolved as follows:

I. To extend to the Livonian colony within the boundaries of the crown manors of Hirschenhof and Helfreichshof, Wenden district, Livonia governorate, the effect of the Highest Confirmed Statutes of February 19, 1866 (43034), and July 9, 1889 (6188), on Volost Public Administration and on the Transformation of Peasant Judicial Institutions in the Baltic Governorates, as well as of the Highest Confirmed Rules of June 11, 1866 (43383), on Public Welfare in the Volosts of the said governorates, with the following changes and additions:

1) The general assembly of the colony shall consist of all owners of immovable property within the colony's boundaries and one deputy from every ten adult non-resident laborers.

2) The colony shall constitute an independent volost judicial district.

3) In the presence chamber of the colony's volost court there must be, during sessions, a mirror-board [zertsalo] bearing the text of the decrees, set forth in the state language with translation into German.

4) In the correspondence of the colony's volost court with volost officials, as well as in the record-keeping of the said court and in the drafting of judicial written instruments, the use of German, in addition to the state language, shall be permitted temporarily, pending the issuance of special rules on this subject.

5) Only a person able to read and write, in addition to Russian, in German and Latvian, may serve as chairman of the colony's volost court.

6) The colony's volost court, as well as the upper peasant court, in adjudicating the civil cases of the colonists, shall be guided by the general provincial law in force in the Livonia governorate (Code of Civil Laws of the Baltic Governorates, part III).

II. The note to article 573 of the Institution of Judicial Establishments (Code of Laws, Vol. XVI, part I, 1892 edition) is hereby abolished.

III. The educational branch in the colony (sect. I) shall be reorganized on the basis of the statutes in force in the Livonia governorate concerning public schools, provided that: 1) this reorganization be carried out gradually, without burdening the colony's public treasury, during the first three years after the issuance of the present statute, with special expenses for schooling beyond those already incurred, and 2) that in the colony's schools reorganized on the above basis, instruction be conducted in strict accordance with the statutes in force concerning the volost schools of the governorate (Code of Laws, Vol. XI, part I, Statutes of Educational Institutions, 1893 edition, art. 3640), with German being recognized as the native language of the pupils.

IV. The introduction in the colony of the organization of public administration and of the educational branch envisaged by sections I and III of the present statute shall be entrusted to the relevant district institutions, under the immediate supervision and direction of the Livonia Governor and the Trustee of the Riga Educational District, as appropriate. The introduction of the new judicial organization in the colony shall be entrusted to the Congress of Justices of the Peace of the Wenden-Walk district.

V. The Minister of Internal Affairs is authorized to determine the procedure for putting into effect in the colony (sect. I) the Highest Confirmed Statutes of February 19, 1866, and July 9, 1889, on Volost Public Administration and on the Transformation of Peasant Judicial Institutions in the Baltic Governorates, on the basis of the Highest Confirmed Rules of July 9, 1889, on Putting into Effect the Legislative Provisions on the Reorganization of the Judicial Branch and of the Peasant Judicial Institutions in the Baltic Governorates, and of the instruction issued by the Baltic Governor-General on July 29, 1866.

Resolution. His Imperial Majesty was graciously pleased to confirm and ordered to be carried out the opinion rendered in the General Assembly of the State Council on the administrative and judicial organization of the Livonian colony within the boundaries of the crown manors of Hirschenhof and Helfreichshof, Wenden district, Livonia governorate.

*PSZRI. Coll. 3. Vol. XXIV. Sect. 1. Pp. 573-574.*

## No. 165. ORDER OF GENERAL M.I. EBELOV ON THE PROHIBITION OF GATHERINGS OF GERMANS AND THE USE OF THE GERMAN LANGUAGE (1914)

**MANDATORY ORDER**

**OF THE CHIEF COMMANDER OF THE ODESSA MILITARY DISTRICT**

**AND GOVERNOR-GENERAL**

Issued on the basis of paragraphs 1, 2, and 3 of article 19 of the Appendix to article 23 of the General Institution of the Governorate, Vol. II of the Code of Laws of the Russian Empire (Rules on Localities Declared to Be under Martial Law).

**I HEREBY PROHIBIT:**

1) Gatherings of more than two adult German men, even among those of Russian citizenship, whether in their own dwellings or outside them.

2) Conversations in German outside one's own dwelling.

3) Signs in German, as well as door-plates on the entrance doors of apartments, visiting cards, and letters.

4) The printing by print shops of newspapers, pamphlets, books, announcements, posters, and visiting cards in German, as well as the cutting or casting of metal plates in the same language by workshops engaged in such work.

Persons found guilty of violating the present mandatory order, which takes effect on the day of its publication, shall be subject to imprisonment in a jail or fortress for a term of up to three months, or to a monetary fine of up to three thousand rubles, and, in especially serious cases, to exile to remote localities of the Empire, not excluding Germans who are Russian subjects.

I authorize the governors and city governors concerned to impose fines or imprisonment on the guilty, but reserve to myself the right of exile, upon the submissions of these officials. October 25, 1914. City of Odessa.

Signed: Chief Commander of the Odessa Military District and Governor-General, General of the Infantry Ebelov.

*RGVIA. F. 2005. Inv. 1. File 28. Fol. 3. Printed copy.*

## No. 166. CHAIRMAN OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS I.L. GOREMYKIN TO GENERAL N.N. YANUSHKEVICH ON THE ORDER OF GENERAL M.I. EBELOV (NOVEMBER 14, 1914)

## No. 8504.

Dear Sir Nikolai Nikolaevich,

The Minister of Internal Affairs, at the session of the 11th of this November, brought to the attention of the Council of Ministers the mandatory order issued on October 25, 1914, by the Chief Commander of the Odessa Military District and Governor-General, General of the Infantry Ebelov <...>.

Having examined the said mandatory order, the Council of Ministers took into account that, on the basis of the Rules on Localities Declared to Be under Martial Law (Code of Laws, vol. II, General Institution of the Governorate, 1892 edition, art. 23, appendix), commanders-in-chief and army commanders, as well as governors-general and chief administrators, are granted the right to adopt extraordinary measures necessary for the success of the conduct of the war, or directed at preventing violations of public order and state security. Examining from this standpoint the mandatory order issued by General of the Infantry Ebelov, the Council of Ministers could not but dwell on the question of the extent to which the rules contained in the said order are indeed justified by the pressing requirements of safeguarding state interests in wartime.

First of all, attention is drawn to the prohibition of the simultaneous presence of more than two adult German men, even among those of Russian citizenship, especially in their own dwellings. Under such conditions, families of Russian subjects of German nationality consisting of more than two adult men are apparently deprived of the right to gather in a single dwelling. Further, in the opinion of the Council of Ministers, military circumstances hardly require the prohibition of correspondence in German, nor likewise the publication of newspapers in that language, all the more so since the censorship rules in force in this regard would appear sufficiently to guard against the appearance in the periodical press of articles inappropriate to the conditions of the present time; while the mere fact of everyday correspondence among Germans who are Russian subjects being conducted in German, given the presence in the Empire of a considerable number of subjects of German nationality, can hardly in itself be regarded as evidence of criminal intent. In view of the serious doubts thus arising as to the expediency of the mandatory order issued by General of the Infantry Ebelov, and considering it desirable that the said order be repealed or revised, the Council of Ministers deemed it necessary to bring these views of its own to Your Excellency's attention.

In communicating the foregoing, with a copy of the explained order of General of the Infantry Ebelov attached, I ask you, dear sir, to accept the assurance of my complete respect and sincere devotion.

I. Goremykin

*RGVIA. F. 2005. Inv. 1. File 28. Fol. 1—2. Original.*

## No. 167. CHIEF OF STAFF OF THE SUPREME COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF N.N. YANUSHKEVICH TO GENERAL M.I. EBELOV ON THE ORDER CONCERNING PERSONS OF GERMAN NATIONALITY (NOVEMBER 19, 1914)

## No. 519.

Dear Sir Mikhail Isaevich,

The Chairman of the Council of Ministers has forwarded to me the mandatory order issued by Your Excellency on the 25th of last October concerning the use of the German language, as well as gatherings of persons of German origin. Please accept the assurance of my complete respect and devotion.

Signed: N. Yanushkevich

Certified true: Acting Secretary A. Danilov

*RGVIA. F. 2005. Inv. 1. File 28. Fol. 4. Certified copy.*

## No. 168. GENERAL M.I. EBELOV TO GENERAL N.N. YANUSHKEVICH ON PROHIBITIVE MEASURES AGAINST GERMANS (1914)

## No. 1402. Odessa

Dear Sir Nikolai Nikolaevich,

The considerable number of Germans inhabiting the towns and colonies of our southern governorates, lying within the region of the Odessa Military District entrusted to me in the theater of military operations, compelled me to give this circumstance serious attention, especially following the special order of His Imperial Highness the Supreme Commander-in-Chief concerning Germans of German, Austrian, and dual citizenship.

The treacherous attack of the German-Turkish fleet, without a declaration of war, on the ports of the Black Sea further underscored this state necessity.

I had least of all in mind the native Germans who are Russian subjects, some of whom have become related by marriage to, and some of whom have simply grown accustomed to living among, the Russian population — but only outside the German colonies, which are scattered in considerable numbers across the entire expanse of the Bessarabia, Kherson, Ekaterinoslav, and Tauride governorates.

These colonies, notwithstanding their having existed for more than a century, live in such isolation from the native Russian population that, taken together across the whole expanse of our southern governorates, they constitute a ready-made base for a German invasion.

To this day these colonies have retained German names taken from the towns of Germany or from the places from which our German colonists came. To this day these colonists have retained German customs, way of life, and language, and scarcely speak Russian. Before the present war, the dwellings of some colonists were adorned with portraits of Emperor Wilhelm II, members of the German imperial-royal house, allied German sovereigns, and high dignitaries of the German Empire.

All this points to the sympathies of our colonists for Germany, which cannot but instill distrust of them on the part of the local organs of our government.

The consequence of the above-described circumstances was the mandatory order issued by me on October 25 of this year, prohibiting gatherings of Germans and their use of the German language.

Turning to the lawfulness of the issuance of this mandatory order, I consider it necessary to explain that gatherings — that is, unauthorized assemblies of more than two adult German men, whether in their own dwellings or outside them — are impermissible for the sake of preserving state order, public security, and the interests of the army. In doing so I did not intend to violate the integrity of the family union provided for by the Code of Civil Laws (vol. X, part 1, of the Code of Laws of the Russian Empire), since, in accordance with articles 236 and 421 of vol. II of the same Code, mandatory orders must not contradict the laws in force. Therefore, in a family where more than two Germans have gathered, the members of the family are excluded from the count.

In speaking above of safeguarding state order, public security, and the interests of the army, I had in mind the exceptional patriotic upsurge — having an enormous influence on the spirit of our army — among all strata of our society since the very beginning of the present war, and the marked exasperation of the population against the Germans that has arisen as a consequence thereof, the Germans having astonished and continuing to astonish the world with their atrocities against the peaceful population in districts occupied by right of war. This exasperation is directed also against the German language, both spoken and printed.

Therefore the patriotic upsurge among our population and the exasperation against the Germans could lead to open hostile demonstrations, especially on the part of the lower strata of the population, against free gatherings of Germans, both within their dwellings and outside them, conversing openly in German and making use of German literature. Such demonstrations could not fail to disturb state order and public security. Consequently, I considered myself obliged to forestall such demonstrations by issuing the aforementioned order; otherwise I should have had to reckon only with the regrettable consequences of these demonstrations, and moreover to the extreme disadvantage of the Germans themselves, whose safety in that case would not have been safeguarded.

There remained open only the question of which Germans should be prohibited from gathering and conversing in German — all of them, or only Germans who are German and Austrian subjects. I decided to prohibit this for all of them, on the assumption that Germans who are native Russian subjects, obliged to speak and who do speak Russian, have no reason to form gatherings. If, nevertheless, they should take part in such gatherings — that is, unauthorized assemblies — together with Germans who are subjects of states at war with us, then in any case it would not be with benevolent but with hostile intentions toward our army and state, and such Germans I would have the undoubted right to regard as dual subjects.

There then remains the mass of German colonists who, although Russian subjects, display in individual cases ill-will and even hostility toward our army. I have already had occasion to exile more than a dozen such colonists, chiefly from Ekaterinoslav governorate, to Tomsk governorate, upon the governor's submission, in accordance with the mandatory order I issued for such cases.

Free gatherings of German colonists are likewise impermissible in safeguarding the above-mentioned state principles.

Nevertheless, the measures set out in my mandatory order under consideration cannot but be recognized as harsh with respect to Germans in general. But war itself is a harsh phenomenon, and since it is the Germans who display the greatest harshness in this regard, the question arises: are the measures taken by the local civil and military authorities in the theater-of-war region, in safeguarding state order, public security, and the interests of an army exhausted by daily continuous battles with the Germans, with enormous losses in killed and wounded in the glorious ranks of our valiant armies, sufficiently strict?

Leaving this question open, since its resolution depends on one's views regarding the loyalty and reliability of the Germans inhabiting our Empire in vast numbers, but considering myself obliged to take into account the views of the Council of Ministers, I would propose to soften my mandatory order of October 25 of this year, without substantial harm to the matter, in the following respects:

1) To exclude Germans living outside the colonies who are Russian subjects, but on the definite condition that if these Germans take part in gatherings of Germans who are German and Austrian subjects left in the region for various valid reasons on the basis of special rules, then the said Germans who are Russian subjects shall be classed as dual subjects, liable to exile to remote localities.

2) To deem punishable gatherings of German colonists numbering not more than two but more than five adult persons, equating this number to the average size of a family of 5 persons.

3) To permit private correspondence in German, door-plates on the doors of apartments, and visiting cards.

4) To permit the printing by print shops of pamphlets, books, and visiting cards in German, as well as the cutting or casting of metal plates by workshops engaged in such work, but on condition that these plates be displayed inside houses and not on their exterior.

At the same time, conversations in German outside dwellings, signs in German, as well as newspapers, announcements, posters, and the placement of plates on the exterior of houses cannot be permitted, since this would continue to provoke exasperation among the public, the consequence of which would be the unauthorized tearing down of these items from their places, the destruction of newspapers, and, perhaps thereafter, hostile action by the public against the Germans.

In accordance with the foregoing considerations, I attach herewith a draft of the mandatory order as amended by me, requesting, should it be approved, that I be notified thereof by telegraph so that it may be announced to the population of the region entrusted to me.

Please accept the assurances of the complete respect and devotion of your most humble servant.

M. Ebelov

Draft

**MANDATORY ORDER**

In view of changed circumstances, in revocation of my mandatory order of October 25 of this year, in safeguarding state order, public security, and the interests of the army, I hereby prohibit:

1) Gatherings (unauthorized assemblies) of more than two adult German men who are German and Austrian subjects, whether in enclosed premises or outside them. The family of the persons in whose apartment such a gathering occurs shall not be taken into account. Settlement certificates are of no significance in determining the said citizenships.

The same applies to gatherings of German colonists numbering more than five persons, under the conditions set forth above.

2) Conversations in German outside one's own dwelling — for everyone without exception.

3) Signs, announcements, posters, and metal plates in German on the exterior of enclosed premises.

4) The printing by print shops of newspapers, announcements, and posters in German.

The present order shall not repeal the existing laws concerning the laws on estates, family rights, and ecclesiastical affairs (vols. IX, X, and XI of the Code of Laws of the Russian Empire).

Persons found guilty of violating the present mandatory order, which takes effect on the day of its publication, shall be subject to imprisonment in a jail or fortress for a term of up to three months, or to a monetary fine of up to three thousand rubles, and, in especially serious cases, to exile to remote localities of the Empire, not excluding Germans who are Russian subjects, should they take part in gatherings of Germans who are German or Austrian subjects.

I authorize the governors and city governors concerned to impose fines or imprisonment on the guilty, but reserve to myself the right of exile, upon the submissions of these officials.

Chief Commander of the Odessa Military District and Governor-General, General of the Infantry

Ebelov November 26, 1914, Odessa

*RGVIA. F. 2005. Inv. 1. File 28. Fol. 5—8 verso. Original and copy.*

## No. 169. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON THE CONSCRIPTION OF MENNONITES INTO THE ARMY, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1914)

61. On the conscription of first-category militia warriors from among the Mennonites.

The Council of Ministers resolved: on the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Code of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, ed. 1906), in amendment and supplement of the relevant enactments, to decree:

I. The Chief Administrator of Land Settlement and Agriculture is authorized to call up, for the performance of military-sanitary service, first-category militia warriors from among the Mennonites, in accordance with the Imperial Personal Decrees given to the Governing Senate of 18 and 21 July, 1 and 17 September, and 7 November 1914.

II. The number of Mennonites of the ages indicated in the preceding (I) section to be called up, and the districts in which the call-up is to be carried out, as well as the timing and procedure of the call-up itself, are to be determined by the Chief Administrator of Land Settlement and Agriculture, in agreement with the Ministers of Internal Affairs and of War.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 24th day of December 1914, most graciously deigned to approve this measure.

*SURP. 1915. Section One. 1st half-year. No. 7. P. 105.*

## No. 170. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON THE LANGUAGE OF INSTRUCTION IN GERMAN PRIMARY SCHOOLS, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1914)

63. On amending the enactments currently in force regarding the language of instruction in primary schools for children of German nationality.

The Council of Ministers resolved:

I. In primary schools, both existing and newly opened, for children of German nationality in the Warsaw educational district and in the settlements of former German colonists throughout the Empire, instruction in all subjects is to be conducted in the state language, with the exception of the Law of God and the students' native language, which are to be taught in the latter language. In one-class schools and in the first grades of other primary schools, the use of the students' native language as an auxiliary aid is to be permitted at the outset, but for no longer than the first year of instruction.

II. Note 5 to Article 3423 and the note to Article 3686 of the Code of Statutes of Learned Institutions and Educational Establishments of the department of the Ministry of Public Education (Code of Laws, Vol. XI, Part 1, per the 1912 Continuation) are hereby repealed.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 24th day of December 1914, most graciously deigned to approve this measure.

*SURP. 1915. Section One. 1st half-year. No. 7. P. 107.*

## No. 171. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON RESTRICTING THE LAND OWNERSHIP AND LAND USE OF SUBJECTS OF ENEMY POWERS, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1915)

349. On land ownership and land use in the Russian State by Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects.

The Minister of Justice submitted to the Governing Senate, for publication, the Statute of the Council of Ministers, most graciously approved on 2 February 1915, on land ownership and land use in the Russian State by Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects.

On the original, in His Imperial Majesty's own hand, is written: "SO BE IT."

At Tsarskoye Selo.

2 February 1915.

Countersigned by: Chairman of the Council of Ministers, Secretary of State Goremykin.

In repeal, amendment, and supplement of the relevant enactments, pursuant to Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Code of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, ed. 1906), it is decreed:

I. With respect to the acquisition by Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects of rights to immovable property, as well as its use and management, the following rules shall be observed:

1. The said subjects are henceforth forbidden, throughout the entire Russian State, by any means whatsoever and on any grounds permitted by general or local laws,

DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 563

to acquire the right of ownership and other proprietary rights to immovable property, as well as the right of possession and use of immovable property separate from the right of ownership.

This rule does not extend to the rental of apartments, houses, and other premises.

2. In cases where immovable property is acquired through inheritance by the persons indicated in Article 1, such persons are obligated to sell, or voluntarily, through the established procedure, transfer such property within two years from the time they acquired rights to it. If this rule is not observed, the property is to be sold at public auction by the relevant provincial administration or the institution corresponding to it. The sum realized at auction, after covering claims presented by third parties and the costs of inventory and sale, is to be turned over for the benefit of the former owner of the property.

3. The public auctions indicated in the preceding (2) article are to be conducted in accordance with the rules in force in the given locality governing the conduct of uncontested collections. In the Grand Duchy of Finland, with respect to the conduct of public auctions, the rules on the enforcement of collections without a court determination shall apply, the procedure for applying these rules to the sale of the property indicated in Article 2 being determined by administrative legislation.

4. If the property subject to sale at public auction forms part of property held in joint ownership by persons falling and not falling under the provisions of Article 1, then the shares subject to alienation are to be separated out, at the request of the provincial administration or the institution corresponding to it, in the general procedure established for the division of common property.

5. The provisions of Articles 2–4 also extend to immovable property passing by inheritance to the persons indicated in Article 1 of the same section not by right of ownership, but under other proprietary rights of use and possession, such as, for example, quit-rent tenure, the right of building lease, or hereditary lease, with the sole exception of various forms of lifetime rights of use and possession, which rights are deemed invalid.

6. Mortgage rights to immovable property, and, in general, the collection of debt claims, may not result either in the acquisition of ownership of such property, or in entry into actual possession or use thereof, for the persons indicated in Article 1.

7. The persons indicated in Article I are forbidden to manage immovable property in the capacity of attorneys or managers (administrators).

8. The provisions of the preceding articles extend, in their respective parts, to all manner of societies and partnerships formed on the basis of Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish laws, even if they have received permission to operate in Russia, as well as to general partnerships and limited partnerships formed under the laws in force in the Russian State, if among the general partners or contributors of these partnerships there are Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects.

9. Any transactions concluded in violation or circumvention of the rules set forth in Articles 1–8 are deemed invalid.

10. Each of the parties who took part in concluding the transaction indicated in Article 9 is granted the right to bring, in the district court (and in the Grand Duchy of Finland — in the herad or rådhus court, as applicable), at the location of the immovable property to which the given transaction pertains, a suit for the transaction to be declared invalid, or to report the matter to the local provincial authorities.

11. If information about the transactions mentioned in Article 9 is received by the chief or provincial authorities, then, upon requisition of the necessary data — which all judicial bodies and all other government offices and officials are obligated to furnish immediately to the said authorities — the chief administrator or governor, through officials specially authorized for this purpose (in the provinces of the Warsaw Governor-Generalship and Chełm — through the procuracy), shall bring, in the district court (and in the Grand Duchy of Finland — in the herad or rådhus court, as applicable), at the location of the immovable property to which the given transaction pertains, a suit for the annulment of the latter. These cases are to be conducted in the procedure established for cases of государственное [state] administration.

12. The expiration of the statute-of-limitations periods established in general or local laws, reckoned from the time of concluding the transactions indicated in Article 9, does not preclude the possibility of bringing the suits indicated in Articles 10 and 11. Likewise, the statute of limitations does not serve as grounds for the consolidation of ownership rights to immovable property, whether acquired under such transactions or held in possession by persons covered by these rules under oral agreements, informal transactions, or without any transaction whatsoever.

13. In the event that the suits indicated in Article 11 are upheld, immovable property belonging to persons falling under the provisions of Article 1 is to be sold at public auction by the relevant provincial administration or the institution corresponding to it. In doing so, the provisions of Articles 3–5 are to be observed, with the proviso that of the sum realized at auction, only the portion equal to the sum indicated in the deed of acquisition of the estate is to be turned over for the benefit of the owner of the property and applied to cover claims presented by third parties, court costs, and the costs of inventory and sale. Any surplus that may arise is to be turned over to the revenue of the State Treasury or the Finnish Treasury, as applicable.

The provincial or corresponding authority may declare to the court that the price indicated in the deed of acquisition of the estate does not correspond to the amount actually paid by the acquirer. Should the court find such a declaration to be correct, the court is obligated to determine in its decision the sum actually paid by the acquirer.

14. The provisions of Articles 9–13 also apply in cases where persons indicated in Article 1 acquire immovable property at public auctions.

15. Persons who, in violation of the rules set forth in the preceding (1–14) articles, are found to be in actual possession or management of immovable property on the basis of oral agreements, informal transactions, without any transaction whatsoever, or after court decisions have been rendered annulling transactions they concluded for the possession and use of such property, are to be deported abroad in the established procedure.

II. In share-based partnerships and joint-stock companies established on the basis of general or local laws in force in the Russian State and having the right to acquire immovable property, persons belonging to Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjecthood are not permitted to hold the positions of chairmen and members of the council, board, executive committee, or any other committees, candidates for membership on the council, board, and committees, managing directors, authorized representatives, chief agents, agents, attorneys in general and attorneys for mining-industry affairs in particular, persons in charge of and managing the immovable property of the society or partnership, wherever such property may be located, as well as individual enterprises, wherever such may be found, technicians, clerks, and employees of societies or partnerships in general.

III. Upon the expiration of one year from the day of promulgation of the present enactment, all rights to immovable property arising from a contract of hire or lease, belonging to Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects, as well as to the societies and partnerships indicated in Article 8 of Section I of the present enactment, shall lapse. This rule does not extend to contracts for the rental of apartments, houses, and other premises.

The management and administration of immovable property indicated in Article 7 of Section I of the present enactment, whether based on formal instruments or on oral agreements, informal transactions, or without any transaction whatsoever, shall cease upon the expiration of two months from the period indicated in this section (III).

IV. Immovable property located outside urban settlements, currently in the possession and use of Austrian, Hungarian, or German subjects, or of the societies or partnerships indicated in Article 8 of Section I of the present enactment — located in the provinces of: Petrograd, Estland, Livland, Courland, Kovno, Grodno, Vilna, Minsk, Suwałki, Łomża, Płock, Warsaw, Kalisz, Piotrków, Kielce, Radom, Lublin, Chełm, Volhynia, Podolia, Bessarabia, Kherson, Taurida, Yekaterinoslav, the Don Cossack Host oblast, and in all localities of the Caucasus Krai, the Grand Duchy of Finland, and the Amur Governor-Generalship — shall be subject to the following rules:

1. The said persons, societies, and partnerships are granted, within the period established by these rules, the right to alienate, by voluntary agreements, their immovable property in the above-named localities, failing which such property shall be sold at public auction.

2. The provisions of Article 1 of this section also extend to immovable property belonging to persons, societies, and partnerships falling under this same article not by right of ownership, but under other proprietary rights of use and possession, such as, for example, quit-rent tenure, the right of building lease, or hereditary lease, with the sole exception of various forms of lifetime rights of use and possession that arose prior to 1 November 1914.

3. Persons subject to Article 1 are to be entered by the provincial administrations or the institutions corresponding to them into special personal registers indicating the immovable property belonging to each of these persons that is subject to this section (IV), on the basis of data furnished, at the request of the governors, by all relevant offices and persons. The said registers are to be published in the local provincial gazettes, and, in the Grand Duchy of Finland, in the official gazettes, and, moreover, are to be posted for general inspection in the provincial administrations or the institutions corresponding to them no later than two months from the day of promulgation of the present enactment. In addition, these registers are to be sent to the district police administrations, volost and gmina boards, and the institutions and officials replacing them, and, in the Grand Duchy of Finland, to the municipal police administrations, crown bailiffs (fogdes), crown lensmen, and rural communal boards. The property of the societies and partnerships mentioned in Article 8 of Section I is also to be entered in the above-mentioned registers.

Should omissions subsequently be discovered in the registers compiled on the basis of this (3) article, supplementary registers are to be compiled in the same procedure by the relevant provincial administrations or the institutions corresponding to them.

4. Complaints regarding the incorrect compilation of the registers or their supplementation (Article 3) may be brought, within one month from the day of publication of the registers, to the Governing Senate, First Department, where they are to be scheduled for hearing out of turn and are to be finally resolved, upon hearing the opinion of the Chief Procurator, by a majority vote of the Senators present and the Minister of Internal Affairs, and, in the event of a tie, according to the opinion adopted by the Senator acting as First Presiding Officer. In the Grand Duchy of Finland, the said complaints are to be brought, within the same period indicated above, to the Economic Department of the Imperial Finnish Senate, where they are to be scheduled for hearing out of turn and are to be finally resolved. The filing of a complaint does not halt the further progress of the case, unless a special order to that effect is issued by the Governing Senate or the Economic Department of the Imperial Finnish Senate, as applicable.

5. Extra-urban immovable property subject to these rules that has not been alienated within six months from the day of publication of the registers mentioned in Article 3, by voluntary agreements with persons entitled to acquire such property, is to be sold at public auction by the relevant provincial administration or the institution corresponding to it, in the procedure indicated in Articles 3 and 4 of Section I, and on condition of timely notification of the date of such auctions to the Peasant Land Bank.

6. Personal creditors of the owner of immovable property subject to this section, whose rights arose prior to 1 November 1914, and who have not secured their claims against any property of the debtor, are granted the right to petition the relevant judicial institution, under the general rules of jurisdiction and prior to the maturity of payment under their obligations, for the securing of these claims against the immovable property being alienated by voluntary agreement or to be sold at public auction, or against the sum of money due to the owner of this property, with the corresponding application, as appropriate, of the provisions of Articles 1825–1827, 1829, and 1831–1833 of the Statute of Civil Procedure, edition of 1914.

7. Injunctions (prohibitions) placed on immovable property to secure various claims do not constitute an obstacle to its alienation by voluntary agreement, if the sum paid by the acquirer covers the said claims. In this case, the purchase sum, in its corresponding portion, is to be applied to the discharge of the claims secured against the estate, even if the payment period for them has not yet arrived, with the exception of claims disputed by the owner of the said property. In this latter case, the corresponding portion of the purchase sum is to be sent to the local district court for safekeeping pending resolution of the dispute.

8. Mortgage and other proprietary encumbrances and rights, arising from contracts of hire or lease, established on immovable property subject to this section after 1 November 1914, are deemed non-binding upon the acquirer of such property at public auction.

9. Landholdings that fall only partly within the localities enumerated in this section are subject to its provisions in respect of the entire area which, together with this part, is enclosed by a single boundary line.

10. In localities where the immediate implementation of these rules proves impossible owing to wartime conditions, the running of the periods established in Articles 3–5 of this section shall be reckoned from a time to be determined by the Minister of Internal Affairs (and, in the Grand Duchy of Finland, by the Governor-General), in agreement with the senior local military authorities. A register of the localities indicated in this article is to be compiled in the same procedure. These orders are to be published for general information through the Governing Senate.

11. The localities enumerated in this (IV) section are not covered by the exemption provided for in Article 1 of Section I of the present enactment for German, Austrian, or Hungarian subjects with respect to the rental of houses, apartments, and other premises. Rights arising from contracts of hire and lease shall lapse upon the expiration of one year from the day of promulgation of the present enactment.

V. For reasons of national defense, the operation of the rules established in Articles 1–7, 9, and 11 of Section IV of the present enactment may be extended, independently of the localities indicated in the said Section IV, to individual localities of the Russian State, subject to the following provisions.

1. The said localities are to be determined by a Standing Interdepartmental Commission established under the Ministry of War, under the chairmanship of the Chief of the General Staff, consisting of the Chief of the Naval General Staff and, as designated by the heads of the relevant departments, the Deputy Ministers of: Internal Affairs, Foreign Affairs, Justice, Finance, Communications, and Trade and Industry, as well as the Deputies of the Chief Administrator of Land Settlement and Agriculture and of the State Controller.

2. The resolutions of the said Commission (Article 1) are to be submitted by the Minister of War to the Council of Ministers, whose decisions on these matters are to be submitted for the Most Gracious approval of His Imperial Majesty and thereafter published, in the established procedure, for general information.

3. The periods indicated in Articles 3 and 11 of Section IV are to be reckoned from the day of promulgation of the decision of the Council of Ministers mentioned in the preceding (2) article.

4. Mortgage and other proprietary encumbrances and rights, arising from contracts of hire or lease, established on immovable property subject to this section after the promulgation of the decision of the Council of Ministers mentioned in Article 2 of this section, are deemed non-binding upon the acquirer of such property at public auction.

VI. By German, Austrian, and Hungarian subjects, the present enactment means subjects of both Germany and Austria-Hungary and of all the individual states and parts thereof incorporated into the said powers.

VII. The Minister of Internal Affairs is authorized to request, through the budgetary process, the allocation of the credits necessary for carrying out the measures indicated in Articles 3–5 and 10–14 of Section I and Article 5 of Section IV of the present enactment, while in the Grand Duchy of Finland such allocations are to be authorized upon submissions of the Imperial Finnish Senate.

VIII. The establishment of detailed rules on the procedure for applying the present enactment is entrusted to the Council of Ministers.

*SURP. 1915. Section One. 1st half-year. No. 39. Pp. 559–564.*

## No. 172. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON RESTRICTING THE LAND OWNERSHIP AND LAND USE OF RUSSIAN GERMANS, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1915)

350. On the land ownership and land use of certain categories of Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés holding Russian subjecthood.

The Minister of Justice submitted to the Governing Senate, for publication, the Statute of the Council of Ministers, most graciously approved on 2 February 1915, on the land ownership and land use of certain categories of Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés holding Russian subjecthood.

On the original, in His Imperial Majesty's own hand, is written: "SO BE IT."

At Tsarskoye Selo.

2 February 1915.

Countersigned by: Chairman of the Council of Ministers, Secretary of State I. Goremykin.

In amendment and supplement of the relevant enactments, pursuant to Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Code of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, ed. 1906), it is decreed:

1. Volost, rural, village, and communal societies formed from settler-proprietors, colonists, settlers, and foreign farmers and other foreign émigrés of German origin who were formerly Austrian, Hungarian, or German subjects, or from the descendants of the aforementioned persons, are henceforth forbidden to conclude any kind of instrument for the acquisition of the right of ownership, the right of mortgage, or the right of possession and use of immovable property separate from the right of ownership, and are likewise forbidden to participate in public auctions of the said property.

2. The prohibition established in Article 1, with respect to the acquisition of rights to immovable property outside urban settlements, also extends to individual persons among Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés, as well as their descendants in the male line, who belong to one of the following categories: a) who are members of the societies indicated in Article 1; b) who are registered as members of colonies and villages in the provinces of the Warsaw Governor-Generalship and Chełm; c) who own land within the limits provided for in Article 63 of the Statute of the Peasant Land Bank, edition of 1912, and who, in their way of life, are not distinguishable from peasants; d) who transferred to Russian subjecthood after 1 January 1880, or after that date transferred to the subjecthood of other powers and thereafter to Russian subjecthood, as well as partnerships that include any of the aforementioned persons among their members; and e) who have lost immovable property as a result of alienation, whether voluntary or at public auction, on the basis of the decision of the Council of Ministers approved on this same date "on the termination of land ownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border localities." The said prohibition does not apply to the acquisition of rights to immovable property by way of inheritance.

3. The provisions of these rules do not extend to: 1) persons who have certified one of the following conditions: a) their affiliation with the Orthodox faith from birth, or their conversion to Orthodoxy before 1 January 1914; b) their affiliation with a Slavic nationality; c) their own participation, or the participation of one of their ascendants or descendants in the male line, in combat operations of the Russian army or Russian navy against the enemy in the rank of officers or as volunteers, or their own inclusion, or that of one of the said persons, among those who have received awards for distinction in combat in the operations of the said army or navy, or the death of one of their ascendants or descendants on the field of battle; 2) widows of the persons enumerated in point 1; and 3) the temporary use of immovable property under contracts of hire or lease concluded by individual persons as tenants or lessees for a term not exceeding six years, and, moreover, outside the localities indicated in Article 1 of the rules approved on this same date "on the termination of land ownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border localities." Contracts of hire or lease concluded by the said persons prior to the present time shall remain in force until the expiration of the term indicated therein, but not longer than six years from the day of promulgation of the present enactment. Contracts of hire or lease concluded by the societies or partnerships mentioned in Articles 1 and 2 shall lapse upon the expiration of one year from the day of promulgation of the present enactment.

4. In the execution of the instruments indicated in Article 1, the institutions and officials executing such instruments are entitled to require, of persons who have not presented certification of the conditions enumerated in the preceding (3) article, in the event doubts arise, the presentation of certificates from the local governors attesting that the acquirers do not belong to persons falling under these rules.

5. Any transactions concluded in violation or circumvention of the foregoing rules are deemed invalid, in the procedure established in Articles 10–14 of Section I of the decision of the Council of Ministers approved on this same date "on land ownership and land use in the Russian State by Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects."

6. The allotment lands of the societies indicated in Article 1, as well as of persons who are members of these societies, are not subject to the provisions set forth in Articles 18, 19, 19-1, 20, 22, Notes 1 and 2 thereto, and Article 10 with the notes thereto, of the appendix to Article 16 (note) of the General Statute on Peasants (Code of Laws, Vol. IX, Special Appendix, Book I, ed. 1902, and per the 1912 Continuation).

7. By persons who were subjects of Germany or Austria-Hungary, as well as by émigrés from these countries, the present rules mean former subjects of both the said powers and of all the individual states and parts thereof incorporated into the said powers.

8. The establishment of detailed rules on the application of the present enactment is entrusted to the Council of Ministers.

*SURP. 1915. Section One. 1st half-year. No. 39. Pp. 564–566.*

Published in part: *The History of Russian Germans in Documents (1763–1992). Compiled by V.A. Auman, V.G. Chebotareva. Moscow, 1993. Pp. 36–38.*

## No. 173. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON THE TERMINATION OF LANDOWNERSHIP AND LAND USE BY RUSSIAN GERMANS IN BORDER LOCALITIES, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1915)

351. On the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border localities.

The Minister of Justice submitted to the Governing Senate, for publication, the regulation of the Council of Ministers, Highest approved on 2 February 1915, on the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border localities.

On the original, written in His Imperial Majesty's own hand: "SO BE IT."

At Tsarskoye Selo.

2 February 1915.

Countersigned by: Chairman of the Council of Ministers, Secretary of State Goremykin.

In amendment and supplementation of the pertinent statutes, pursuant to Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Digest of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, 1906 ed.), it is enacted:

1. In the western and southern border zones, Russian subjects of German, Austrian, or Hungarian extraction are afforded, within the time limits established by these rules, the opportunity to alienate, by voluntary agreements, their immovable properties located outside urban settlements, in the following localities:
