a) within the one-hundred-fifty-verst strip along the existing state border with Germany and Austria-Hungary and the region adjoining that strip, bounded by the line of the said border, the coast of the Baltic Sea and the Gulf of Riga, the Western Dvina River from its mouth to Dvinsk, the line of the railways Dvinsk—Vilna—Lida—Baranovichi—Luninets—Sarny—Korosten and further to the border of Kiev Governorate, the line of this latter border southward to its intersection with the Kazatin—Zhmerinka railway line and further along the railway line to Zhmerinka, Mogilev-Podolsky, Ochnita, and Novoselitsy;

b) within the one-hundred-verst strip: 1) to the north of that indicated in the preceding point — beginning from the mouth of the Western Dvina along the coast of the Baltic Sea with its bays as far as the Tornio River, together with all islands situated opposite this strip, and 2) to the south of that indicated in point a — along the state border in Bessarabia Governorate, along the coast of the Black and Azov Seas with their bays, including the entire territory of the Crimean Peninsula, and along the entire state border in Transcaucasia from the Black Sea to the Caspian Sea.

Extra-urban immovable properties subject to these rules, not alienated within the time limits allowed for this by voluntary agreements with persons entitled to acquire such properties, shall be sold at public auction.

2. The effect of Article 1 extends to immovable properties belonging to the societies, partnerships, and individual persons named in these rules, whether held by right of ownership or by other patrimonial rights of use and possession, such as, for example, chinsh right, right of building (superficies), or hereditary lease, with the sole exception of various kinds of lifetime rights of use and possession that arose before 1 November 1914.

3. The effect of these rules extends both to properties acquired by volost, rural, settlement, and communal societies formed of former settler-proprietors, colonists, settlers, and foreign farmers who were subjects of Austria, Hungary, or Germany, and their descendants, and to the properties of individual persons of Austrian, Hungarian, or German extraction, as well as their descendants in the male line, belonging to one of the following categories: a) members of the societies named in this article, b) persons registered as part of colonies and villages in the governorates of the Warsaw General-Governorship and in Chełm Governorate, c) persons owning land within the limits provided for in Article 63 of the Statute of the Peasant Land Bank (1912 edition), and not distinguishable in their way of life from peasants, d) persons who entered Russian subjecthood after 1 January 1880, or — after that date — the subjecthood of other powers and thereafter Russian subjecthood, as well as partnerships that include any of the aforementioned persons.

4. The effect of these rules does not extend to allotment lands assigned to the societies and persons named in Article 3 under acts of land settlement, nor to any lands whatsoever belonging to: 1) persons who have certified one of the following conditions: a) their affiliation with the Orthodox faith from birth, or conversion to Orthodoxy before 1 January 1914, b) their affiliation with a Slavic nationality, c) their own participation, or the participation of one of their ascendants or descendants in the male line, in the military operations of the Russian army or Russian navy against the enemy in the rank of officer or as volunteers, or their own inclusion, or that of any of the aforementioned persons, among those who received awards for distinction in combat in the operations of the said army or navy, or the death of one of their ascendants or descendants on the field of battle, and 2) widows of the persons enumerated in point 1.

5. With regard to the conditions for alienation by voluntary agreements of the immovable properties indicated in this statute, and, failing that, the procedure for conducting public auctions thereof, Articles 2–6 of Section I and 3–10 of Section IV of the rules established in the regulation of the Council of Ministers approved on this date "On the Landownership and Land Use in the Russian State of Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish Subjects" shall apply, save that the six-month period established by the said rules for the alienation of immovable property by voluntary agreements is extended — for the one-hundred-fifty-verst strip (point a of Article 1) to ten months, and for the one-hundred-verst strip (point b of Article 1) to one year and four months.

6. Upon the expiration of one year from the day of the promulgation of these rules, all rights to immovable properties in the localities named in Article 1, arising from lease or rental agreements and belonging to the societies, partnerships, and individual persons named in Article 3, shall lapse. Henceforth the said societies, partnerships, and persons are forbidden any renting or leasing of such properties in these localities. These provisions do not extend to agreements for the rental of apartments, houses, or other dwellings.

7. The effect of these rules extends, independently of the localities indicated in Article 1, to separate districts established pursuant to Section V of the regulation of the Council of Ministers approved on this date, "On the Landownership and Land Use in the Russian State of Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish Subjects." In such cases, the period indicated in Article 6 is reckoned from the day of promulgation of the corresponding regulation of the Council of Ministers.

8. By persons who were subjects of Germany or Austria-Hungary, as well as émigrés from these countries, these rules mean former subjects both of the said powers and of all separate states and parts thereof that entered into the composition of the aforementioned powers.

9. The establishment of detailed rules on the application of this statute is entrusted to the Council of Ministers.

*PSZRI. Coll. of Statutes and Orders of the Government (SURP). 1915. First Section. First Half-Year. No. 39. Pp. 566—568.*

Published in: The History of Russian Germans in Documents (1763–1992). / Compiled by: V.A. Auman, V.G. Chebotareva. Moscow, 1993. Pp. 38–40.

## No. 174. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON THE USE OF MENNONITES CALLED UP TO THE ARMY, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1915)

790. On the assignment of Mennonite militiamen to forestry work.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 17th day of March 1915, upon the regulation of the Council of Ministers, Highest deigned, on the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Digest of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, 1906 ed.), in amendment and supplementation of the pertinent statutes, to enact:

To grant the Chief Administrator of Land Settlement and Agriculture the authority to assign, to forestry work in state forestries, those first-category Mennonite militiamen called up for military-sanitary service who shall be found by the military department to be surplus to its requirements.

*SURP. 1915. First Section. First Half-Year. No. 98. P. 1174.*

## No. 175. FROM THE RESOLUTION OF THE SPECIAL CONFERENCE AT THE STAFF OF THE SUPREME COMMANDER ON THE CLEARING OF FRONT-LINE AREAS BY THE TROOPS (23 JUNE 1915)

Special conference on measures to be taken when the troops evacuate certain localities of the Northwestern and Southwestern fronts.

At the session, presided over by the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Commander, General of Infantry Yanushkevich, the following were present: Generals of Infantry Mavrin and Danilov, Adjutant General Prince Engalychev, Lieutenant General Kondzerovsky, Major General Ronzhin, State Councillor Prince Obolensky, and the clerk of the Chancellery for Civil Administration, Collegiate Assessor Lodyzhensky.

Having discussed the measures to be applied when the troops evacuate certain localities, the Conference deemed it desirable to establish the following procedure in this regard:

**I. EXPULSION OF THE POPULATION**

1) German colonists owning land or other immovable property in rural localities, as well as those without land but registered with colonist societies, even if they reside in towns, are subject to mandatory expulsion at their own expense to localities outside the theater of war. The districts from which German colonists are to be expelled are to be determined by the commander-in-chief of the armies of the front, who, in agreement with the Minister of Internal Affairs, shall also designate the governorates for their resettlement. The time limits for expulsion and other details of the matter are likewise established by the commander-in-chief, who may delegate his authority in this matter to the chief of supply of the armies of the front. Exempted from mandatory expulsion are loyal wives and mothers of colonists serving in the active army, as well as their children. The immovable property of the colonists is subject to sequestration and is transferred to the jurisdiction of the Main Administration of Land Settlement and Agriculture, whereby, depending on local conditions, refugees from localities evacuated by the troops may be engaged in its exploitation.

Signed by: Chief of Staff, General of Infantry            Yanushkevich

Countersigned by: Clerk of the Civil Chancellery         Lodyzhensky

Certified true: Secretary                                            A. Denisov

Note: Approved by the Supreme Commander. Chief of Staff, General of Infantry Yanushkevich. 24 June 1915. Certified true: Secretary A. Denisov.

*RGVIA. Fond 2005. Inv. 1. File 28. Fols. 227–228 rev. Certified copy.*

## No. 176. DECREE OF NICHOLAS II ON THE CALL-UP OF MENNONITES TO THE ARMY (1915)

1852. On the call-up of second-category militiamen of the call-up years from 1916 to 1912 inclusive, and of first-category Mennonite militiamen who did not serve in the ranks of the troops of the call-up years from 1916 to 1898 inclusive.

**TO THE GOVERNING SENATE.**

Having found it necessary to bring the reserve battalions up to strength and to reinforce the personnel of sanitary institutions with Mennonites, We command, in accordance with the law approved by the State Duma and the State Council and confirmed by Us on the 22nd day of August of this year, that there be called up:

<...>

2. First-category Mennonite militiamen who did not serve in the ranks of the troops of the call-up years from 1916 to 1898 inclusive, in all governorates, oblasts, and city-governorships of the Empire, with the exception of the governorates, oblasts, and city-governorships of the Warsaw General-Governorship, the Caucasus Territory, the Amur General-Governorship, and Chełm Governorate.

The date of call-up for second-category militiamen and first-category Mennonite militiamen is 5 September of this year.

The Governing Senate shall not fail to make the appropriate arrangements for the execution hereof.

On the original, signed in His Imperial Majesty's own hand: "NICHOLAS."

At the Imperial Headquarters (Stavka).

3 September 1915.

Countersigned by: Administrator of the Ministry of War, General of Infantry Polivanov.

*SURP. 1915. First Section. Second Half-Year. No. 247. P. 2435.*

## No. 177. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON THE CALL-UP OF MENNONITES TO THE ARMY, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1915)

1985. On the call-up for compulsory service of second-category militiamen from among the Mennonites.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 14th day of September 1915, upon the regulation of the Council of Ministers, Highest deigned to command, on the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Digest of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, 1906 ed.), in amendment and supplementation of the pertinent statutes, temporarily, pending further orders on the matter, to enact:

To grant the Chief Administrator of Land Settlement and Agriculture the authority, in cases of call-up throughout the Empire of second-category militiamen into the troops, to call up such militiamen also from among the Mennonites for the performance of military-sanitary service and forestry work in state forestries, on the same bases, and including the same ages and in the same governorates, as shall be designated for the aforementioned militiamen entering the troops.

*SURP. 1915. First Section. Second Half-Year. No. 267. P. 2600.*

## No. 178. CHANCELLERY FOR CIVIL ADMINISTRATION AT THE STAFF OF THE SUPREME COMMANDER — TO THE DUTY GENERAL UNDER THE SUPREME COMMANDER P.K. KONDZEROVSKY, ON THE EXPULSION OF THE GERMAN POPULATION (30 OCTOBER 1915)

## No. 6311.

Returning herewith the telegram of General Bonch-Bruevich concerning the request that he be informed of all orders issued by the Staff of the Supreme Commander for the area of the Northern Front regarding the expulsion of German colonists, the Chancellery for Civil Administration has the honor to report the following:

The Conference at the Stavka on 23 June of this year established that German colonists owning land or other immovable property in rural localities, as well as those without land but registered with colonist societies, even if residing in towns, are subject to mandatory expulsion at their own expense to localities outside the theater of war. <...> No subsequent general orders from the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Commander concerning the fronts have been received by the Chancellery for Civil Administration; there have been only individual instructions, which in substance amount to the following:

1) In response to the inquiry of Adjutant General Ruzsky of 7 September, No. 169 kr, concerning the possibility of expelling the 300,000 Russian-subject Germans aged 17 to 45 residing in Livonia Governorate and Riga, General Alekseev reported that on the basis of establishing national origin there could be inaccuracies and abuses, wherefore it would be more expedient to apply the proposed measure in a general form, and that the decision of the matter in any case is left to the discretion of the commander-in-chief, but that advance notification of the population and gradual implementation are necessary in order to prepare the routes of movement, having first come to an agreement with the Minister of Internal Affairs regarding the places of resettlement and the routing of those to be expelled (telegram of 9 September, No. 5964).

2) In response to the inquiry of General Bonch-Bruevich of 21 September, No. 30522, asking for clarification as to whether the order (which had not passed through the Chancellery) on the non-compulsory expulsion of the population extended to German colonists, or whether the latter, by virtue of the aforementioned paragraph of the journal of the Special Conference, were subject to mandatory expulsion, the Chief of Staff (by telegram of 28 September, No. 6094) informed General Bonch-Bruevich that the compulsory expulsion of colonists extends only to those fit for work of call-up age, and moreover only in localities threatened, at the discretion of the commander-in-chief, with invasion by the enemy.

Apart from the orders set forth above regarding the expulsion of German colonists from the localities of the former Northwestern and now Northern fronts, no other matters have been processed by the Chancellery to date.

Independently of this, the Chancellery for Civil Administration deems it necessary to bring to the attention of the Administration of the Duty General that the exemptions granted by the Conference of 23 June to the loyal wives, mothers, and children of colonists serving in the active army have now, upon the representation of Adjutant General Ivanov, been rescinded for persons residing in the area to the west of the line Sarny—Rovno—Ostrog—Izyaslavl, in view of the report by General Brusilov concerning cases of espionage by colonists who had originally been exempted from expulsion.

Acting Chief of the Chancellery                        Lodyzhensky

For the clerk, Ensign                            Raevsky

Certified true: Secretary                                         A. Denisov

*RGVIA. Fond 2005. Inv. 1. File 28. Fols. 236–237. Certified copy.*

## No. 179. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON AMENDMENTS AND ADDITIONS TO THE LIQUIDATION STATUTES OF 2 FEBRUARY 1915, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1915)

2749. On certain amendments and additions to the statutes of 2 February 1915 concerning the landownership and land use of subjects of powers at war with Russia, as well as of Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 13th day of December 1915, upon the regulation of the Council of Ministers, Highest deigned to command, on the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Digest of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, 1906 ed.):

<...>

B. Concerning the statute on the landownership and land use of certain categories of Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés who are Russian subjects (Collection of Statutes, 1915, Art. 350):

1. Article 2 shall be set forth as follows:

2. The prohibition established in Article 1, with respect to the acquisition of rights to immovable property outside urban settlements, extends also to individual persons of Austrian, Hungarian, or German extraction, as well as their descendants in the male line, belonging to one of the following categories: a) members of volost, rural, settlement, and communal societies; b) persons registered as part of colonies and villages in the governorates of the Warsaw General-Governorship and in Chełm Governorate; c) persons owning land within the limits provided for in Article 63 of the Statute of the Peasant Land Bank, 1912 edition, and not distinguishable in their way of life from peasants; d) persons who entered Russian subjecthood after 1 January 1880, or after that date the subjecthood of other powers and thereafter Russian subjecthood, and e) persons who have lost immovable property on the basis of the statutes in force concerning the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border localities. This prohibition does not apply to the acquisition of rights to immovable property by way of inheritance.

II. The said statute shall be supplemented with the following provisions:

1) The effect of Article 2 of the aforementioned statute extends, in the corresponding parts, also to general partnerships and partnerships of faith (associations based on trust), formed under the laws in force in the Russian State, if among the general partners or contributors to these partnerships there is any of the persons enumerated in the same Article 2.

2) The effect of point 3 of Article 3 does not extend to localities newly included, pursuant to the regulation of the Council of Ministers approved on this date, in the list indicated in Article 1.

3) In share partnerships and joint-stock companies established on the basis of the general or local laws in force in the Russian State and having the right to acquire immovable property outside urban settlements, the persons indicated in Article 2 of the aforementioned statute are not permitted to hold the offices of chairmen and members of the council, board, executive and all other committees, candidates for membership of the council, board, and committees, managing directors, authorized representatives, chief agents, agents, attorneys in general and attorneys for matters of the mining industry in particular, superintendents and managers of the immovable property of the company or partnership, wherever such may be located, as well as of individual enterprises, wherever such may be found, technicians, clerks, and employees of the companies or partnerships generally.

V. Concerning the statute on the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border localities (Collection of Statutes, 1915, Art. 351):

I. The said statute shall be supplemented with the following provisions:

1) Persons indicated in Article 3 of the aforementioned statute are forbidden to superintend, as attorneys or managers (administrators), immovable properties located outside urban settlements in the localities enumerated in Article 1 of the same statute. Such superintendence and management of immovable property, whether based on formal instruments or on verbal agreements, informal transactions, or no transactions at all, shall cease upon the expiration of two months from the day of promulgation of this resolution.

2) Persons who, in violation of the rules of the aforementioned statute, are found actually to possess or superintend immovable property on the basis of verbal agreements, informal transactions, without any transactions, or after judicial decisions annulling transactions concluded by them regarding the possession and use of such property, shall be expelled, in the established manner, from the bounds of the governorate, with a prohibition on the right of residence therein.

3) Rights belonging to persons indicated in Article 3 of the aforementioned statute to estates constituting the subject of a hereditary (family) or ancestral fideicommissum are declared void, and the fideicommissum estate passes to the heirs called, in the founding instrument, next after the said persons.

4) Immovable properties subject to the effect of the aforementioned statute, for as long as they remain in the possession and use of the persons, societies, and partnerships named in the same statute, may henceforth be neither pledged nor encumbered with other patrimonial rights, nor with rights arising from contracts of hire, lease, or timber felling.

Furthermore, the said properties may not, in the event of unsuccessful public auctions, be retained by mortgagees under mortgage deeds executed after 1 November 1914.

5) Upon the expiration of one year from the day of promulgation of this resolution, all rights belonging to the societies, partnerships, and individual persons named in Article 6, under contracts concluded by them for timber felling on immovable estates situated in the localities named in Article 1, shall lapse, provided that, during the aforesaid one-year period, felling shall be permitted only on that forest area either designated in the contract itself for felling within the specified period, or, in the absence of such a stipulation, not exceeding the ordinary annual proportion or share attributable to this period in relation to the whole agreed felling period, provided in all cases that such felling does not conflict with the rules of the Statute on the Conservation of Forests (Digest of Laws, Vol. VIII, Part 1, Forest Statute, 1905 ed.).

6) In localities newly included, pursuant to the regulation of the Council of Ministers approved on this date, in the list indicated in Article 1, the two-month period for the publication of the nominal lists of owners of properties to be alienated in these localities (Art. 5), as well as the period indicated in Article 6, shall be reckoned from the day of promulgation of this resolution.

II. Articles 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 shall be set forth as follows:

1. Russian subjects of German, Austrian, or Hungarian extraction are afforded, within the period established by these rules, the opportunity to alienate, by voluntary agreements, their immovable properties located outside urban settlements, in the localities named in Section IV of the rules "On the Landownership and Land Use in the Russian State of Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish Subjects."

Extra-urban immovable properties subject to these rules, not alienated within the period allowed for this by voluntary agreements with persons entitled to acquire such properties, shall be sold at public auction.

2. The effect of Article 1 extends to immovable properties belonging to the societies, partnerships, and individual persons named in these rules, whether held by right of ownership or by other patrimonial rights of use and possession, such as, for example, chinsh right, right of building (superficies), or hereditary lease, with the sole exception of various kinds of lifetime rights of use and possession of immovable property, which rights are deemed to have terminated.

3. The effect of these rules extends: 1) to the immovable properties of volost, rural, settlement, and communal societies formed of former settler-proprietors, colonists, settlers, and foreign farmers who were subjects of Austria, Hungary, or Germany, and their descendants; 2) to the immovable properties of individual persons of Austrian, Hungarian, or German extraction, as well as their descendants in the male line, belonging to one of the following categories: a) members of volost, rural, settlement, and communal societies, b) persons registered as part of colonies and villages in the governorates of the Warsaw General-Governorship and in Chełm Governorate, c) persons owning land within the limits provided for in Article 63 of the Statute of the Peasant Land Bank (1912 ed.), and not distinguishable in their way of life from peasants, d) persons who entered Russian subjecthood after 1 January 1880, or after that date the subjecthood of other powers and thereafter Russian subjecthood, as well as partnerships that include any of the aforementioned persons; and 3) to allotment lands held by the societies mentioned in point 1 of this article, as well as by individual persons of Austrian, Hungarian, or German extraction and their descendants in the male line, or partnerships including any of these persons and their said descendants.

4. The effect of these rules does not extend to any lands whatsoever belonging to: 1) persons who have certified one of the following conditions: a) their affiliation with the Orthodox faith from birth, or conversion to Orthodoxy before 1 January 1914, b) their affiliation with a Slavic nationality, c) their own participation, or the participation of one of their ascendants or descendants in the male line, in the military operations of the Russian army or Russian navy against the enemy in the rank of officer or as volunteers, or their own inclusion, or that of any of the aforementioned persons, among those who received awards for distinction in combat in the operations of the said army or navy, or the death of one of their ascendants or descendants on the field of battle; 2) widows of the persons enumerated in point 1.

5. With regard to the conditions for alienation by voluntary agreements of the immovable properties indicated in this statute, and, failing that, the procedure for conducting public auctions thereof, Articles 2–6 of Section I and 3–10 of Section IV of the rules "On the Landownership and Land Use in the Russian State of Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish Subjects" shall apply, save that the six-month period established by the said rules for the alienation of immovable property by voluntary agreements is extended to ten months.

G. In amendment and supplementation of the statutes on the landownership and land use in the Russian State of Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects (Collection of Statutes, 1915, Art. 349) and on the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border localities (Collection of Statutes, 1915, Art. 351), it is enacted:

1. 1. The Peasant Land Bank is authorized, until 1 January 1921, to purchase immovable properties at its own expense and to sell these properties on the basis of the rules laid down in the Bank's charter and in this statute.

2. Lists of all immovable properties subject to alienation in the localities under their jurisdiction, pursuant to Section IV of the statute "On the Landownership and Land Use in the Russian State of Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish Subjects," as well as pursuant to the statute "On the Termination of Landownership and Land Use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German Émigrés in Border Localities," shall be forwarded to the senior notaries.

3. The senior notaries are obliged to inform the local branch of the Peasant Land Bank of every notarial act subject to their confirmation concerning the alienation of the properties indicated in Article 2, forwarding an extract from the register of deeds relating to the property being alienated. The same duty of notification is imposed on the provincial boards or the corresponding institutions, on the judicial bodies, and on credit institutions with regard to properties of the said kind sold by them at public auction, if the Bank did not participate in the auction through its representative. The said notification, together with a copy of the auction sheet, must be sent after the conduct of the auction but before its confirmation.

4. The period of time between the sending by the senior notary of notification concerning the property to be alienated and his receipt of a reply as to the Peasant Land Bank's wish or unwillingness to acquire the property is not counted toward the time limits established by law for voluntary alienation of the property.

5. The Peasant Land Bank is authorized to acquire, at its own expense, the property being alienated at the price stated in the proposed instrument of alienation, or at the price at which property sold at public auction is to be confirmed to the purchaser or retained by the mortgagee under the mortgage deed.

6. If the price of the property stated in the instrument of alienation, or offered at auction by the purchaser (Art. 5), or the sum at which the property is to be retained by the mortgagee under a mortgage deed belonging, prior to the promulgation of these rules, to persons, societies, and partnerships falling under the statutes of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Statutes, Arts. 349–351), as well as under this statute, manifestly exceeds the actual value of the property, the Peasant Land Bank is entitled to acquire this property at a valuation corresponding to its actual value. In this case the valuation is carried out by the local branch of the Bank, subject to the following rules: 1) the owners and purchasers of properties, if their place of residence is known to the branch, are notified by registered letter with return receipt of the day set for the session of the Bank's branch for the valuation proceedings; if the owners' place of residence is unknown, the corresponding written notices are handed to the police of the uyezd or district in which the estate is located, for forwarding to the estate and for taking such other measures as may be needed to deliver them to their addressees; 2) the owners of the property, as well as the purchasers of such properties, are entitled to submit to the Bank's branch written or verbal explanations, either in person or through attorneys; 3) the failure of the said persons to appear on the day of the branch's session, as well as the failure to deliver to them the notices indicated above in point 1, shall not halt the valuation proceedings, and 4) of all its actions the Bank's branch shall draw up a protocol setting forth the data on which the determination of the actual value of the property is based, and shall submit this protocol, together with the file and all documents pertaining thereto, to the administration of the Bank.

7. In proceeding to the valuation of an estate, the Peasant Land Bank has the right, pending completion of the sale, to entrust the oversight of the integrity and preservation of the property to a person authorized by the Bank, on the basis of an inventory drawn up in the presence of the owner of the property, or, in the event of his absence or refusal to take part in the inventory, in the presence of a local police official or of outside persons.

In the event of a decrease in the value of the property, the purchase price may be correspondingly reduced by the Bank in its accounting.

8. For the notification of the competent institution (Art. 3) concerning the acquisition of the property by the Peasant Land Bank, as well as, if necessary, for carrying out the valuation of this property (Art. 6), a period of three months is set, until the expiration of which the confirmation of the notarial act or of the auction concerning the said property, as well as the decision to retain the property for the mortgagee, is suspended. The aforesaid period is reckoned from the day of receipt of the notification provided for in Article 3, or from the day of the auction in which the Bank's representative took part. If the Bank's receipt of the said notification, or, in the appropriate cases, the public auction, occurred at such a time of year when carrying out the valuation of the property would be inconvenient or impossible, then the period indicated in this (8th) article is, upon application by the Bank, extended by a further three months.

9. Insufficiency of the price at which the Peasant Land Bank, in accordance with the rules of Articles 3–8, retains the property for itself, to cover the debts secured on this property under mortgages, shall not constitute an obstacle to the confirmation of the estate to the Bank, if the said mortgages were executed after November 1, 1914, or belonged, prior to the promulgation of the present rules, to Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects or emigrants subject to the statutes of February 2, 1915 (Collection of Statutes, Arts. 349–351), as well as to the present statute. In any case, priority of satisfaction over these mortgages and any other claims secured on the property under obligations arising after November 1, 1914, shall be enjoyed by the purchaser's claim, charged against the purchase sum, for the return of the purchase price paid by him upon execution of the proposed notarial act (Art. 3), or a part thereof, as well as of the deposit.

10. Regarding the acquisition of property under the procedure established by Articles 3–8, the Peasant Land Bank shall issue a resolution, which it shall forward to one of the local notaries for the execution of the deed, from the time of issuance of which the property passes into the disposition of the Bank. It is at the Bank's discretion to suspend the execution of the deed until the expiration of the period for appealing its resolution as to the amount of compensation due for the property (Art. 13), and, if a complaint is filed, until the resolution thereof; otherwise, the filing of a complaint shall not stop the execution and issuance of the deed, nor the payment and distribution of the purchase price.

11. In the deed the acquired property shall be described in accordance with the notarial act submitted for confirmation to the senior notary (Art. 3), and with the information requested by the senior notary under Article 1681 of the Statute on the Notarial Service, 1914 edition. The act submitted for confirmation, together with the appendices thereto and the information under Article 1681 of the Statute on the Notarial Service, shall be forwarded by the senior notary immediately to the Peasant Land Bank upon receipt from it of the communication specified in Article 8 of the present rules.

12. If the Peasant Land Bank resolves to acquire property sold at public auction (Art. 3), then, upon notification thereof by the Bank to the institution that conducted the auction (Art. 8) and to the senior notary, the former shall forward to the Bank the entire record of the auction proceedings, and the latter shall forward an extract from the register of deeds of title relating to the property sold, on the basis of which the property shall be described in the deed.

13. Against the resolution of the Peasant Land Bank as to the amount of compensation due for the property, complaints may be lodged, within one month from the day of dispatch, through the local police, to the property being acquired, of notice of the said resolution, to the Governing Senate, First Department, where they are examined out of turn and resolved finally, after hearing the opinion of the Chief Procurator, by a majority of votes of the Senators present and of the Ministers of Internal Affairs, Finance, and Agriculture, and, in the event of an equality of votes, in accordance with whichever opinion is adopted by the Senator acting as First Presiding Officer.

14. If the Peasant Land Bank disagrees with an increase in the price of the property determined by the Governing Senate upon its examination of complaints, the Bank has the right to decline the acquisition thereof, provided that execution of the deed for this property was suspended in the manner provided for in Article 10 of the present rules. In other cases the Bank shall make the additional payment fixed by the Governing Senate, with distribution thereof on the general basis.

15. In the acquisition by the Peasant Land Bank of properties under voluntary agreements with the owners of such properties, the periods established by law for such agreements shall, upon application by the Bank to the competent provincial board or the institution corresponding thereto, be extended for the entire time necessary for the completion of the Bank's purchase of the property.

16. In the sale to the Peasant Land Bank of properties belonging to minors and, in general, persons under guardianship, the restrictions established in the Civil Laws (Digest of Laws, Vol. X, Part 1), in the Code of Civil Statutes of the Baltic Governorates, and in the Civil Laws of the Governorates of the Kingdom of Poland shall not apply, whether as to the cases in which voluntary sale of the said properties is permitted, or as to the requirement of authorization from the Governing Senate or, generally, from a guardianship institution.

17. In the sale of immovable properties at public auction, the Peasant Land Bank may, through its representative, take part in the auction without depositing security, if such is required under the rules governing the conduct of the auction.

18. In the event that the Peasant Land Bank acquires a right in jointly-owned property and an amicable agreement on partition is not reached, the Bank has the right, pursuant to Article 1409 of the Statute of Civil Procedure (1914 edition), to petition the competent court for the separation of the share belonging to it in the joint ownership of the property, and, in submitting such petition, the Bank is obliged to present an inventory and valuation of the estate drawn up by it, together with its proposed plan of partition, setting forth the grounds adopted by it in this regard. Upon such petition the court shall proceed with the partition without awaiting the expiration of the period established in Article 1317 of the Digest of Civil Laws (1914 edition). Petitions and suits for re-partition (Art. 1332 et seq. of the Civil Laws (1914 edition) and Art. 1420 of the Statute of Civil Procedure, 1914 edition) shall not be admitted.

II. 1. In all cases of acquisition by the Peasant Land Bank of properties subject to the statutes of February 2, 1915 (Collection of Statutes: Art. 349, Section IV, and Art. 351), as well as of the present statute, compensation for the properties acquired shall be paid by the Bank in registered obligations, entered in the Bank's books in the amount of the said compensation (Arts. 6–12 of this section), with the exception, from the said sum, of: (a) the debts to land banks assumed by the Bank on the basis of Articles 160–174 of its Statute, and (b) that portion of the aforementioned compensation which, pursuant to Article 47 of the Bank's Statute, is covered by the Bank's four-and-one-half percent state certificates and which is subject to application toward the payment of treasury, zemstvo, and other public dues of every kind by means of the realization of the said certificates at the expense of the property owners (Art. 7 of the Bank's Statute). That portion of the compensation which must go toward covering encumbrances resting on the property in security of claims of various kinds, and, in the case of sale at public auction, also levies charged against the property, shall be paid, if creditors and claimants file a notarially certified statement to this effect, likewise in registered obligations made out in the name of such creditors and claimants, and, in the absence of such a statement, by means of realization of the Bank's certificates at the expense of the property owners. The said statements shall be filed, as appropriate, with the senior notary or, prior to the auction, with the institution conducting the auction.

2. The sum due to be paid to the former owner of the property, as well as the debts secured on the property (Art. 1) under mortgages executed after November 1, 1914, or which belonged, prior to the issuance of the present rules, to persons, societies, or partnerships falling under the statutes of February 2, 1915 (Collection of Statutes, Arts. 349–351), as well as under the present statute, shall be discharged by the issuance of the registered obligations of the Peasant Land Bank specified in the preceding (1) article. In the same manner shall be discharged all other claims secured on the property under obligations arising after November 1, 1914.

The Peasant Land Bank is granted the right, in discharging the sum due to be paid to the former owner of the property: (a) to pay in cash a sum corresponding to the whole or a part of the value of the inventory, and (b) to discharge the remaining portion, after deduction of the said sum, within a limit not exceeding twenty percent of the remainder, in four-and-one-half percent state certificates of the Bank, this latter measure being applied only in the case where the amount of land being acquired by the Bank from the given person does not exceed fifty desiatinas.

To cover — over and above the compensation paid under the procedure established in Article 1 — the expenses of purchase, improvement, and sale of the estates acquired, state certificates of the Bank may be realized at the Bank's expense.

3. In order to comply with the requirements of Article 7, Section IV, of the statute of February 2, 1915, "On Landownership and Land Use in the Russian State by Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish Subjects" (Collection of Statutes, Art. 349), the senior notary, prior to the confirmation of the deed of sale, shall communicate to the Peasant Land Bank a computation of all encumbrances resting on the estate, with a precise indication, based on the data available to him, of the means of their discharge in accordance with Articles 1 and 2 of this section, and shall thereafter confirm the deed of sale only if the Peasant Land Bank notifies him that the realization of the Bank's certificates, in the relevant portion of the purchase price, will amount to a sum covering the claims corresponding to the said encumbrances.

4. The provisions of the preceding (1–3) articles shall likewise apply to the issuance by the Peasant Land Bank, in respect of properties specified in Article 1 of this section, of loans provided for by its Statute.

5. The making of the settlement for the property acquired, on the bases indicated in Articles 1 and 3 of this section, may be made by the Peasant Land Bank a condition of transactions concluded under voluntary agreements with owners, the subject matter of which is land and estates belonging to Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects and to Austrian, Hungarian, or German emigrants who are Russian subjects, and which are not subject to the statutes of February 2, 1915 (Collection of Statutes, Arts. 349 and 351), as well as to the present statute.

6. The registered obligations of the Peasant Land Bank issued on the basis of these rules shall be assigned an annual yield of four rubles fifty kopecks per hundred.

7. The difference between the sums of interest paid by the Peasant Land Bank on its registered obligations (Art. 6) and the payments due to it on loans shall be reimbursed to the Bank from the State Treasury, with the entry of the credit required for this purpose in the state schedule of revenues and expenditures.

8. Registered obligations (Art. 6) shall be entered in the books of the Peasant Land Bank and issued in round hundreds of rubles. Sums not covered by the said obligations as a result of this shall be discharged by 4½% certificates of the Bank, realized (Art. 7 of the Bank's Statute) at the expense of the owners of the properties sold.

9. The principal on the registered obligations of the Peasant Land Bank (Art. 6) shall be paid upon the expiration of twenty-five years from the day of their entry in the Bank's books, provided, however, that the Bank is permitted to pay the said principal even before this term, in whole or in part, in a manner established by the Minister of Finance.

10. Three months before the date fixed in accordance with the preceding (9) article, a publication to this effect shall be made in the "Government Herald," the "Herald of Finance, Industry, and Trade," as well as in three of the more widely circulated Petrograd newspapers designated by the Minister of Finance. In addition, the publications shall be printed, by order of the Minister of Finance, in widely circulated newspapers published in Moscow, Kiev, Odessa, Kharkov, and several other cities.

11. Payment of the principal on the registered obligations of the Peasant Land Bank, in the manner provided for in Articles 9 and 10 of this section, shall be made by the State Bank, by order of the Minister of Finance, from the sinking fund available for this purpose of the Peasant Land Bank and from the funds obtained from the realization of certificates issued on the basis of its Statute, to a nominal amount not exceeding the amount of principal on the registered obligations discharged at the expense of the said realization. The sum required to cover losses on the exchange-rate difference in this operation shall be allocated to the State Bank under the state schedule for the year following the conduct of the operation. Profits that may result from the realization of the said certificates shall be applied to cover the expenses of the State Treasury on the operation of paying the principal on the four-and-one-half percent registered obligations, as well as any additional payments thereon, on the basis of Article 7 of this section.

12. Payment of interest and principal on the registered obligations issued by the Peasant Land Bank is secured both by the lands accepted by the Bank as collateral and acquired by it at its own expense, and by all funds at the disposal of the Government.

13. Transfer of a registered obligation from the person named therein to another is permitted only by way of inheritance or the allotment of a share to descendants, as recorded. If there are several heirs, the obligation of the Peasant Land Bank shall, at their wish, be replaced by registered obligations for each of the heirs in sums corresponding to their hereditary shares. Upon the allotment to a descendant of a portion of the principal under a registered obligation, the latter shall be replaced by registered obligations in sums corresponding to the division that has occurred.

14. Recovery on payments made by the Peasant Land Bank on its registered obligations may be enforced under the general procedure provided for in Articles 1079–1082 of the Statute of Civil Procedure (1914 edition), the rule of Article 1083 of that Statute not being applicable.

III. The duties of senior notaries specified in Sections I and II of Part [G] of the present statute are assigned, in the governorates of the Kingdom of Poland and the Baltic governorates, to the competent mortgage or deed-registry departments.

*SURP. 1915. Section One. 2nd half-year. No. 366. Pp. 3545–3556.*

Published in part: The History of Russian Germans in Documents (1763–1992). / Comp.: V.A. Auman, V.G. Chebotareva. Moscow, 1993. Pp. 41–44.

## No. 180. REGULATIONS ON THE SPECIAL COMMITTEE FOR COMBATING GERMAN DOMINATION, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS II (1916)

1278. On the confirmation of the Regulations on the Special Committee for Combating German Domination.

The Minister of Justice, on June 10, 1916, submitted to the Governing Senate, for publication, the Regulations on the Special Committee for Combating German Domination, forwarded by the Administrator of Affairs of the Council of Ministers, which had received the confirmation of His Imperial Majesty's own hand on June 1, 1916.

On the original, in His Imperial Majesty's own hand, is written: "SO BE IT."

At Imperial Headquarters.

June 1, 1916.

Countersigned: Chairman of the Council of Ministers B. Stürmer.

**REGULATIONS**

**ON THE SPECIAL COMMITTEE FOR COMBATING GERMAN DOMINATION.**

1. For the purpose of unifying, coordinating, and providing overall direction to the activity of government and public institutions and officials in implementing both the statutes and orders of the Government currently in force, and those that may follow, restricting the rights of enemy subjects and emigrants, and also for the purpose of considering and discussing proposals concerning measures for freeing the country from German influence in all spheres of the national life of the Russian State, a Special Committee is hereby established.

2. Such of the measures indicated in the preceding article as require, for their implementation, the issuance of new laws or Imperial commands in the manner of Supreme administration, shall be submitted for consideration to the Council of Ministers.

3. The Special Committee shall consist of: a Chairman, appointed by the Supreme authority upon the report of the Chairman of the Council of Ministers; senior officials, chiefly holding the rights of Assistant Minister, of the following departments: military, naval, internal affairs, foreign affairs, agriculture, trade and industry, justice, finance, ways of communication, public education, the Orthodox Confession, and state control, appointed by the Chief Heads of these departments; the official replacing His Imperial Majesty's Viceroy in the Caucasus in the higher state institutions; the Assistant Governor-General of Finland; and the Administrator of Affairs of the Council of Ministers.

Should the said officials be unable to attend particular sessions of the Special Committee, they shall be replaced by other officials of the respective departments, appointed by their Chief Heads.

4. Persons from whose official or public activity, occupation, and experience useful explanations may be expected may be invited by the Chairman to take part in the sessions of the Special Committee with a consultative voice.

5. Should the Chairman, for whatever reason, be unable to attend the Committee, the performance of the Chairman's duties shall devolve upon his deputy.

6. The Deputy Chairman shall be selected by the Chairman from among the members of the Committee and confirmed in this office by the Supreme authority.

7. Matters in the Special Committee shall be decided by a majority of votes, and, in the event of an equality of votes, the opinion shared by the Chairman shall be deemed adopted.

A matter on which the representative of some department has recorded a dissenting opinion shall be referred for resolution to the Council of Ministers, should a statement to this effect be received from the Chief Head of the department within seven days from the date of the Committee's resolution.

8. The Chairman, in exceptional cases, may suspend the implementation of a general measure adopted by resolution of the majority of the members of the Special Committee, if he does not share the opinion of that majority. A measure whose implementation has been suspended shall be submitted immediately for consideration by the Council of Ministers.

9. The Special Committee, for the purpose of accomplishing the tasks assigned to it, has the right:

1) to enter, through its Chairman, into direct relations with Ministers and Chief Administrators of separate departments;

2) to require from the organs of central and local administration of all departments, as well as from local judicial institutions and authorities, notarial institutions, and government inspectors of commercial and industrial enterprises, the furnishing of necessary information;

3) to review, through its members, and, by agreement with the competent Chief Heads of departments, also through persons specially authorized for this purpose by the Committee, the affairs of local administrative institutions of all departments relating to matters within the Committee's jurisdiction, and to require the submission of such matters for review by the Committee;

4) to issue to local administrative institutions of all departments, through their Chief Heads, instructions and explanations for guidance in resolving matters entrusted to the Committee's jurisdiction.

10. All general questions and proposals concerning the matters specified in Articles 1 and 2 of these Regulations, as well as all doubts or misunderstandings arising in the practical application of the restrictive laws and Government orders specified in Article 1, shall be referred for consideration to the Special Committee by the Chief Heads of departments and by Governors-General.

Resolutions adopted by the Committee shall be subject to obligatory execution, through administrative channels, by government institutions and officials.

11. The Chairman, in matters before the Special Committee that admit of no delay, has the right to adopt an appropriate measure on his own authority, but in such cases it shall be submitted for discussion at the next session of the Committee.

12. The Chairman of the Special Committee, or his deputy acting as Chairman, shall be invited to the sessions of the Council of Ministers on all matters relating to the sphere of jurisdiction of the Special Committee.

13. For the resolution of matters of certain defined categories, on bases worked out by the Special Committee, special sections may be formed within its composition.

14. For the conduct of business in the Special Committee, a chancery shall be attached to it, headed by an Administrator of the Committee's Affairs appointed by the Chairman. For clerical work and for the performance of legal-counsel duties, officials of government institutions (not excluding judicial ones) and public institutions shall be seconded to the Chairman's disposal, by agreement with their respective superiors, while retaining their offices. The internal order of business shall be determined by instructions confirmed by the Chairman.

15. The Special Committee shall have its own seal bearing an image of the State Emblem and, beneath it, the inscription: "Special Committee for Combating German Domination."

16. The Chairman of the Special Committee shall submit to the Sovereign Emperor, through the Council of Ministers, a report on the Committee's activity not less than once a year.

Signed: Chairman of the Council of Ministers Stürmer.

*SURP. 1916. Section One. No. 156. Pp. 1511–1513.*

Published in part: The History of Russian Germans in Documents (1763–1992). / Comp.: V.A. Auman, V.G. Chebotareva. Moscow, 1993. Pp. 45–46.

## No. 181. CHIEF OF STAFF OF THE SUPREME COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF M.A. ALEKSEEV TO THE CHAIRMAN OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS B.V. STÜRMER ON THE DEPORTATION OF GERMAN COLONISTS (JUNE 16, 1916)

## No. 7592.

Dear Sir Boris Vladimirovich,

The Commander-in-Chief of the armies of the Southwestern Front approached me on the 11th of this June with a communication in which he indicated the desirability, in the course of the gradual clearing of our territory of the enemy, of applying to the German colonists who remained there after the withdrawal of our troops in the autumn of last year the measure of their deportation into the interior of the country.

Adjutant-General Brusilov bases his opinion on considerations of the necessity of safeguarding the army from espionage in favor of the enemy, and in general from the active manifestation, by various persons, of a hostile attitude toward our military interests.

Finding on my part no obstacles to the implementation of the said measure, in view of cases that occurred in the area of the 8th Army of German colonists damaging our telegraph and telephone lines, and having given my consent thereto to the Commander-in-Chief of the armies of the Southwestern Front, I am obliged to bring this to Your Excellency's attention.

In connection with this, another question has arisen at the Staff of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief — concerning the procedure for the settlement and movement, outside the localities of the theater of war, of persons deported on the basis of point 17 of Article 19 of the "Rules Concerning Localities Declared to Be under Martial Law," into the interior governorates of the Empire.

The matter is that, from individual petitions addressed to the Staff, it appears that the higher administration of certain localities, where various persons removed by order of the military authorities from the area of the theater of war are held in exile, in examining petitions submitted by deportees for permission to move from one locality to another, give petitioners answers to the effect that the resolution of these questions lies entirely within the jurisdiction of the military authorities, to whom the corresponding petitions should accordingly be addressed.

In this connection I consider it my duty to explain that such explanations given to petitioners place in a very difficult position those military commanders to whom administratively deported persons apply for permission to move from one locality to another, in cases, of course, where that locality does not fall within the area of the theater of war or has not been declared under martial law. In such cases the military authorities are obliged to forward the said petitions to the Ministry of Internal Affairs together with their own opinion, since, for their part, they naturally encounter no obstacles to such a transfer, if the Ministry of Internal Affairs deems it possible.

The military authorities, given the removal of unreliable elements from the localities of the theater of war, are, in most cases, entirely unconcerned as to precisely where the said persons will be held within the interior governorates, all the more so since police supervision over them, as well as responsibility for its vigilance, rests with the local provincial administration at the places of settlement.

By its very nature, moreover, the measure of deportation is a measure of prevention and suppression of crimes, and not a punitive one, since, should the guilt of a given person be established, that person is brought to trial.

In view of all the foregoing, I am of the opinion that the consideration of questions concerning the transfer of persons deported by order of the military authorities, within localities not declared under martial law and not included in the areas of the theater of war, ought properly to be assigned to the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, since it is extremely difficult for the military authorities to render competent opinions, still less orders, in these matters.

Please accept the assurance of my complete respect and sincere devotion.

Signed: Mikh[ail] Alekseev

Certified true: Secretary A. Denisov

*RGVIA. F. 2005. Inv. 1. File 28. Fols. 259–261.*

## No. 182. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON MEASURES TO SUPPORT FARMING ON COLONIST LANDS SUBJECT TO EXPROPRIATION, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1916)

1685. On certain measures for supporting farming on colonist lands subject to liquidation.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 10th day of July 1916, upon the report of the Council of Ministers, was Most Highly pleased to command, on the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Code of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, ed. 1906), in amendment and supplement of Section D of the enactment of 13 December 1915 concerning certain amendments and supplements to the enactments of 2 February 1915 on landownership and land use by subjects of powers at war with Russia, as well as by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), to decree as follows:

1) In the event of the acquisition by the Peasant Land Bank of lands at public auction or in the exercise of the right of preferential purchase (Section 1, Articles 5 and 6), the Bank is permitted, in making settlement, to withhold: a) from five to ten percent of the purchase price, if by the time the land passes into the Bank's disposal (Section I, Article 10) the regular sowing or other work necessary for the proper conduct of farming has not been performed, and b) five percent of the said price, if by the same time the necessary agricultural livestock and dead stock are not present or not in good order, such as: work and domestic animals, agricultural implements, containers and other items, fertilizer and fuel procured for the current farming year, as well as stocks of grain, hay, and straw necessary for the coming sowing and for feeding livestock until the new harvest.

In the cases cited above (points "a" and "b"), the former owner of the land may not be granted the relief provided for in point "b" of the second part of Article 2 of Section II.

2) Upon acquisition of lands by the Peasant Land Bank, the Bank is permitted, on conditions established by it, but for a term not exceeding one year from the date of the said acquisition, to leave the former owners on the said lands for the purpose of carrying out sowing and other work required by the proper conduct of farming, but only in cases where the lands came into the Bank's disposal at such a time that the adoption of other measures for continuing the farming operations and carrying out the regular work would be inconvenient or impossible.

*SURP. 1916. Section One. 2nd half-year. No. 200. Pp. 2021–2022.*

## No. 183. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS SUPPLEMENTING THE LIQUIDATION ENACTMENT OF 2 FEBRUARY 1915, No. 351, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1916)

1713. On supplementing Article 4 of the law of 2 February 1915 on the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border localities.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 15th day of July 1916, upon the report of the Council of Ministers, was Most Highly pleased to command, on the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Code of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, ed. 1906), in confirmation and clarification of the meaning of the enactment of 2 February 1915 on the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border localities (Collection of Enactments, Art. 351), to decree as follows:

The conditions provided for in letter "c" of point 1 of Article 4 of the said enactment give the right to the exemption established by that article if they were fulfilled no later than the publication of the relevant name lists or their supplements, drawn up in accordance with the same enactment (Article 5), in the manner set out in Article 3 [Section IV] of the Rules of 2 February 1915 "on the landownership and land use in the Russian State by Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects" (Collection of Enactments, Art. 349).

*SURP. 1916. Section One. 2nd half-year. No. 207. P. 2064.*

## No. 184. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON THE PROHIBITION OF TEACHING IN THE GERMAN LANGUAGE, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1916)

1882. On the prohibition of teaching in the German language.

The Council of Ministers, by a special journal of 12 July 1916, resolved:

I. On the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Code of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, ed. 1906), in amendment and supplement of the relevant enactments, to decree:

In all educational institutions, not excluding private ones and those maintained by Evangelical-Lutheran parishes, teaching in the German language is prohibited throughout the Empire, beginning with the 1916–1917 academic year, with the exception from this rule of the teaching of the Law of God to those persons of the Evangelical-Lutheran confession for whom German is their native language, and of the teaching of the German language itself.

II. To authorize the Minister of Public Education to arrange for the introduction of teaching in Russian at the Faculty of Theology of the Imperial University of Yuriev, with an exemption from this rule permitted with respect to the teaching of practical theology.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 18th day of August 1916, was Most Highly pleased to approve the aforesaid report of the Council of Ministers.

*SURP. 1916. Section One. 2nd half-year. No. 237. P. 2342.*

Published in: History of Russian Germans in Documents (1763–1992). Compiled by V.A. Auman, V.G. Chebotareva. Moscow, 1993. P. 47.

## No. 185. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON AMENDING AND SUPPLEMENTING THE LIQUIDATION ENACTMENT OF 13 DECEMBER 1915, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1916)

1867. On amending, supplementing, and clarifying the Most Highly approved report of the Council of Ministers of 13 December 1915 concerning certain amendments and supplements to the enactments of 2 February 1915 on landownership and land use by subjects of powers at war with Russia, as well as by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 19th day of August 1916, upon the report of the Council of Ministers, was Most Highly pleased to command, on the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Code of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, ed. 1906):

<...>

II. In amendment and supplement of the report of the Council of Ministers indicated in the preceding (I) section, to decree:

1) Immovable properties constituting the subject of a hereditary (family) or ancestral fideicommissum, in the event that the rights of their owners are found invalid on the basis of the said enactment, pass into the administration of the local institutions of the Ministry of Agriculture pending clarification of the rights of the summoned heirs to the said properties.

2) If the allotment referred to in Article 18 of Section I, Part D of the said report of the Council of Ministers concerns property encumbered with a general debt to a credit institution or a private person, the distribution of the general debt between the plot allotted at the request of the Peasant Land Bank and the remaining part of the property is carried out by the court, irrespective of the consent of the mortgagee, after which each newly formed holding is liable only for the share of the former general debt transferred to it.

The Peasant Land Bank shall include in the allotment plan it submits (Article 18, Section I, Part D) its proposals regarding the distribution of the general debt among the new holdings.

3) The Peasant Land Bank assumes the portion of the general debt to the credit institution transferred to the plot allotted to it, and the allotted plot is thereby released from the mortgage held by that institution, subject to the rules set forth in Articles 164–174 of the Bank's Charter, 1912 edition; the authorizing article regarding the release from mortgage of the allotted plot, however, is sent to the senior notary directly by the court.

A debt to a private person transferred to a plot allotted to the Peasant Land Bank may be repaid ahead of schedule, with interest payable on it only up to the day of repayment of the debt.

4) In the cases indicated in Article 2 of this section, in the manner provided by Article 1410 of the Statute of Civil Procedure, 1914 edition, in addition to the co-owners of the common estate, the mortgagees of the latter are also summoned.

*SURP. 1916. Section One. 2nd half-year. No. 233. Pp. 2316–2317.*

## No. 186. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON AMENDMENTS AND SUPPLEMENTS TO THE LIQUIDATION ENACTMENTS OF 1915, APPROVED BY NICHOLAS II (1916)

1869. On certain amendments and supplements to the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 on measures to reduce foreign landownership and land use in the Russian State.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 19th day of August 1916, upon the report of the Council of Ministers, was Most Highly pleased to command, in amendment and supplement of the Most Highly approved reports of the Council of Ministers of 2 February and 13 December 1915 on the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border localities and on certain amendments and supplements to the enactments of 2 February 1915 on landownership and land use by subjects of powers at war with Russia, as well as by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 351 and 2749), in the manner of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Code of Laws, Vol. I, Part 1, ed. 1906), to decree as follows:

1. I. Allotments and immovable properties, falling under the effect of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 351) and the supplementary rules thereto of 13 December of the same year (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), belonging to volost, rural, village, and communal societies, regardless of the form of land use established among them (communal, household, or mixed), are subject to expropriation by voluntary agreement or sale at public auction only in their entirety, with the exception of plots allotted in the course of land settlement to individual locations, which are expropriated on the basis of the aforementioned enactments separately, depending on whether their owners fall under the effect of these enactments.

2. Structures and buildings erected on the lands of the societies indicated in the preceding (1) article and intended for the needs of public administration, public amenities, welfare, public health, and education, such as: buildings of volost and rural administrations, grain-reserve storehouses, schools, hospitals, almshouses, and the like, as well as the inventory established for them, are not subject to expropriation.

3. Immediately upon the promulgation of these rules, the zemstvo chief or the corresponding official shall, in the presence of officials of the rural or volost administration and three impartial outside persons invited by him, draw up an inventory of the structures and buildings indicated in the preceding (2) article and the property belonging to them, and shall entrust the village elder or volost elder, as appropriate, with oversight of the integrity and safekeeping of the inventoried property.

4. In the event of embezzlement or damage to the inventoried property, the person entrusted with oversight of it (Article 3), if found guilty of permitting or failing to prevent such abuse, shall be subject to:

imprisonment for a term of eight months to one year and four months.

5. Losses arising from the embezzlement or damage indicated in the preceding (4) article are to be compensated from the remuneration due to the society for the expropriated lands and shall be withheld from each householder in proportion to the amount of land holdings in his possession.

6. From the time of the promulgation of these rules, the available sums of assessed dues (state, zemstvo, and communal), as well as all communal funds under the jurisdiction or disposal of the volost, rural, village, and communal societies referred to in Article 1 (quitrent, charitable, penalty, sheep-breeding, insurance, provisioning, guardianship, and other funds), shall be transferred, by order of the zemstvo chief or the corresponding official, to the deposits of the relevant district congress or the institution replacing it, together with all records and accounting relating to such dues and funds.

7. The district congress or the institution replacing it, upon completing the accounting of the sums and funds indicated in the preceding (6) article, shall transfer the sums due for payment of state and zemstvo dues, as appropriate, to the treasury and the cash offices of the zemstvo institutions, and from the sums of communal funds intended to meet the current needs of public administration, public amenities, welfare, public health, and education, shall make the necessary expenditures upon the representations of the relevant zemstvo chiefs or corresponding officials.

8. Allotments and immovable properties of volost, rural, village, and communal societies (Article 1) are subject to acquisition by the Peasant Land Bank in compliance with the following provisions (Articles 9–22).

9. Upon the transfer to the Peasant Land Bank of the lands of volost, rural, village, and communal societies, these societies shall be deemed abolished from the time of the final resolution, adopted in the manner established below in Article 21, regarding the apportionment among all householders of the remuneration due for the expropriated lands.

10. Individual members of societies exempted from the effect of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 351 and 2749) shall, in the course of the sale carried out in the manner established in Article 1, retain their right to the portion belonging to them within the allotment and the communal immovable property. This right shall be compensated to such householders, upon the sale of the society's lands to the Peasant Land Bank, either by remuneration in the amount of the share, calculated for the said right, of the general purchase price, or by the allotment to them, at the Bank's discretion, of an equivalent plot from the sold lands, with the issuance for such plot of a deed in the amount of the said remuneration.

11. Upon the transfer to the Peasant Land Bank of communal lands expropriated under these rules, the structures and buildings indicated in Article 2, together with the inventory belonging to them, shall pass into the ownership of the Bank free of charge, and on the same basis shall be transferred by the Bank, by deeds of gift, together with the land plots occupied by the said structures and buildings, either to peasant societies newly formed on the said lands, or to the local zemstvo and other governmental or public institutions, in accordance with local conveniences and needs, as well as other circumstances that may come to light.

12. Upon the acquisition by the Peasant Land Bank of the lands of the societies indicated in Article 1, the district congress or the institution replacing it shall determine the disposition of the funds belonging to these societies on the basis of the following rules: 1) communal funds intended, in accordance with existing society resolutions or the established practice of the society, to meet the needs of public administration or public amenities, as well as all funds established for purposes of public health and education, charity and welfare, shall be transferred to the jurisdiction of the Peasant Land Bank for covering current expenditures for their assigned purpose therefrom, and subsequently for transfer to the disposal of newly formed societies or the local zemstvo and other governmental and public institutions that have assumed responsibility for carrying out the aforementioned purposes; 2) communal provisioning funds and provisioning grain reserves, as well as collected payments and arrears on provisioning loans made from the said funds and reserves, shall pass to the disposal of the local provincial board or the corresponding institution to augment the provincial (regional) provisioning fund; 3) sheep-breeding funds shall be transferred to the Peasant Land Bank to replenish the Bank's own capital (Credit Statute, Section VII, Article 3, point 3, per the 1912 Continuation); 4) insurance funds shall be transferred to the deposits of the provincial board or the corresponding institution for application to their assigned purpose; 5) funds belonging to minors and persons under guardianship or trusteeship shall remain on deposit with the district congress or the corresponding institution pending their transfer to the jurisdiction of the relevant guardianship institutions; and 6) communal funds having no defined purpose, and funds established under Article 10 of the appendix to Article 16 (note) of the General Statute on Peasants (ed. 1902 and per the 1912 Continuation) and under Article 22 of the same Statute, shall be distributed among all householders in accordance with the procedure adopted by the society for this purpose, and in the absence of such a procedure, in proportion to the amount of land holdings held separately by each of them.

13. The amount of debts recorded against individual departing members of societies: a) on provisioning loans issued from the treasury, communal, provincial, and general Empire-wide provisioning funds, as well as debts to grain-reserve storehouses, with the conversion of the latter debts into monetary terms, and b) on the sheep-breeding fund, shall be determined by the district congress or the institution replacing it, concerning which a special protocol shall be drawn up and forwarded to the local branch of the Peasant Land Bank for withholding, in priority over any other debts, from the remuneration due to the debtors for the expropriated land.

14. Upon retaining for itself the immovable property of the societies indicated in Article 1, the Peasant Land Bank shall notify the relevant zemstvo chief or corresponding official of the amount of the total remuneration for the acquired lands, for announcement to the society and for the apportionment by the latter of the said remuneration among all householders.

The above-mentioned apportionment shall be carried out with respect to householders who have received, for their plots, deeds of confirmation, certification, or other instruments establishing ownership, in proportion to the amount of land holdings shown in such instruments, and with respect to the remaining householders, in accordance with the extent of the actual possession by each householder of holdings held in his permanent separate possession.

Simultaneously with the apportionment, lists of householders shall be drawn up indicating how much is due to each from the total sum of remuneration, which of them is obliged to resettle and which is free of such obligation and wishes to retain the right belonging to him in the expropriated lands, whereby a householder who has not declared a wish to retain the said right shall be listed as departing.

15. The zemstvo chief or the corresponding official, no later than three days from the time of receiving the communication indicated in the preceding (14) article, shall instruct the volost elder or village elder, as appropriate, to convene the relevant assembly for the purpose of apportioning the remuneration due to the society among the individual householders and drawing up lists of the latter, in accordance with the provisions of the same article.

16. The volost elder or village elder, no later than seven days after receiving the instruction of the zemstvo chief or corresponding official, shall convene the relevant assembly and propose that it carry out the actions indicated in Article 14. The assembly shall take place in the presence of the zemstvo chief or corresponding official.

17. For the lawful constitution of an assembly convened on the basis of the preceding (16) article, the participation of not less than two-thirds of all householders entitled to vote in the assembly is required; the resolution itself shall be adopted by decision of a simple majority of the participants present at the assembly; if the assembly is divided into two halves equal in number of votes, the majority shall be deemed to lie on the side with which the volost elder or village elder, as appropriate, agrees.

18.
