If the assembly does not convene in lawful composition within the appointed time (Article 16), or fails, for whatever reason, to carry out the actions entrusted to it, the zemstvo chief or the corresponding official, having drawn up a record thereof, shall himself immediately carry out these actions in the presence of officials of the rural or volost administration, the number of householders present, and three impartial outside persons. In this case, the apportionment of the remuneration due to the society shall be carried out on the bases indicated in the second part of Article 14.

19. Concerning the actions carried out (Article 18), the zemstvo chief or the corresponding official shall draw up, under his own signature and that of the persons present, a resolution setting forth the grounds adopted in this matter and indicating the procedure for appealing the decision reached. This resolution shall be immediately announced to the relevant public administration.

20. The resolution of the assembly (Article 17) or, where applicable, the resolution indicated in Article 19, may be appealed to the district congress or the institution replacing it, both as to the substance of the apportionment carried out and in the event that irregularities or omissions are discovered in the lists of householders relating to the said resolution or decision (Article 14). Complaints shall be lodged through the zemstvo chief or the corresponding official within a seven-day period, calculated from the time of the assembly's adoption of the resolution or the announcement of the above-mentioned decision to the relevant public administration.

21. The resolutions of assemblies or, in the relevant cases, the decisions indicated in Article 19, together with the lists of householders relating thereto (Article 14), as well as any complaints filed, shall be submitted, not later than three days after the expiration of the period for appeal, by the zemstvo chief or the corresponding official, together with an opinion on the substance of the resolution and an explanation regarding the substance of the complaint, for consideration by the district congress or the institution replacing it, which is obliged, within a seven-day period from the receipt of the matter, to consider it on the merits, without returning it to the lower instance for renewed proceedings and decision. The decision thereupon reached may not be appealed in any manner and, being deemed final, is subject to execution, for which purpose the district congress or the institution replacing it shall, not later than three days from the date of the decision, forward a copy of the said decision together with the entire case file to the local branch of the Peasant Land Bank.

22. The Peasant Land Bank, guided by the decision of the district congress or the institution replacing it (Article 21), shall pay remuneration to each of the departing householders separately. Remuneration shall be paid to householders not falling under the effect of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 351 and 2749) in state certificates of the Bank, and to householders falling under the effect of these enactments, on the bases set forth in the enactment of 13 December 1915 concerning certain amendments and supplements to the enactments of 2 February 1915 on landownership and land use by subjects of powers at war with Russia, as well as by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés.

II. 1. With respect to plots of land situated outside urban settlements in the localities named in Section IV of the Rules on landownership and land use in the Russian State by Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects (Collection of Enactments, 1915, Arts. 349 and 2749), belonging to Russian subjects of Austrian, Hungarian, or German origin, as well as to partnerships, full or limited, in the membership of which any of the said persons is included, the effect of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 351 and 2749) may be suspended for a term not exceeding two years from the time of the promulgation of this enactment, in cases where the said plots contain operating industrial enterprises fulfilling primarily orders for the needs of state defense, or serving needs connected with wartime circumstances.

2. The deferrals mentioned in the preceding (1) article shall be granted for a precisely defined term by decisions of the provincial boards or the corresponding institutions, in the composition of which, when resolving matters of this kind, representatives of the Ministries of War, the Navy, Agriculture, Communications, Trade and Industry, and Finance shall participate with the right to vote, invited primarily from among the local officials of these departments by the Provincial Governors, with the consent of the Chief Heads of these departments.

3. It is prohibited to sell otherwise than in their entirety the industrial enterprises indicated in Article 1 of Section II of this enactment, or to suspend their operations.

The Minister of Trade and Industry is authorized, for the purpose of preventing this, to establish special oversight over the said enterprises, in accordance with the rules of the Most Highly approved report of the Council of Ministers of 16 January 1916 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 138).

4. By decisions of the provincial boards or the corresponding institutions, the deferral provided for in Article 1 of this section shall be revoked, and the immovable property shall immediately, regardless of the time remaining for its voluntary alienation, be subjected to public sale, if, on the basis of reports from the oversight mentioned in Article 3 or from other reliable sources, the provincial board or corresponding institution becomes convinced that the industrial enterprise, for the preservation of which the deferral was granted, has ceased operations or has reduced them to such an extent that it has lost the significance indicated in Article 1 of this section.

5. The Council of Ministers is authorized to extend the term mentioned in Article 1 of this section.

*SURP. 1916. Section One. 2nd half-year. No. 233. Pp. 2318–2322.*

## No. 187. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON AMENDING THE REGULATION ON THE SPECIAL COMMITTEE FOR COMBATING GERMAN DOMINATION, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS II (1916)

1861. On amending Article 8 of the Regulation on the Special Committee for Combating German Domination.

The Sovereign Emperor, on the 27th day of August 1916, upon the resolution of the Council of Ministers, was Most Highly pleased to command that Article 8 of the Regulation on the Special Committee for Combating German Domination, Most Highly confirmed on 1 June 1916, be set forth as follows:

"In exceptional cases the Chairman may suspend execution of a resolution adopted by a majority of the members of the Special Committee, if he does not share the opinion of that majority. A resolution whose execution has been suspended shall be submitted immediately for consideration by the Council of Ministers."

*SURP. 1916. Part One. 2nd half-year. No. 231. P. 2310.*

## No. 188. INSTRUCTION ON THE APPLICATION OF THE LIQUIDATION ENACTMENTS OF 1915, CONFIRMED BY THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS (1916)

1933. On the confirmation of the instruction on the application of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 349–351 and 2749).

The Minister of Justice, on 6 September 1916, submitted to the Governing Senate, for publication, an instruction on the application of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 349–351), confirmed by the Council of Ministers on the basis of Section VIII of the enactment of 2 February 1915 on landownership and land use in the Russian State by Austrian, Hungarian, German, and Turkish subjects, Article 8 of the enactment of 2 February 1915 on landownership and land use by certain categories of persons of Austrian, Hungarian, or German origin who are Russian subjects, and Article 9 of the enactment of 2 February 1915 on the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés in border areas.

**INSTRUCTION**

**ON THE APPLICATION OF THE ENACTMENTS OF 2 FEBRUARY AND 13 DECEMBER 1915**

**(COLLECTION OF ENACTMENTS, ARTS. 349–351 AND 2749).**

I. On the enactment concerning landownership and land use in the Russian State by Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 349 and 2749).

1) The prohibition on Austrian, Hungarian, German, or Turkish subjects from henceforth acquiring proprietary rights to immovable property also extends to the right of pledge (mortgage).

2) Permits issued to the societies, partnerships, and individuals specified in the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 349 and 2749) granting the right to prospect for mineral resources on state-owned lands are, from the promulgation of the said enactments, deemed invalid, and henceforth the issuance of such permits to the above-mentioned societies, partnerships, and persons may not take place.

3) Societies and unions established under the temporary rules of 4 March 1906 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 308) are not subject to the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 349) and the supplementary rules of 13 December 1915 thereto (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), even if enemy subjects are among the members of such societies and unions.

4) Mutual credit societies, operating by means of pooled capital formed from contributions (shares) of individual members who bear liability for the obligations of the society on the basis of joint and several suretyship — even beyond the contributions made, but within the limits precisely defined by the charter — belong to the category of share partnerships, and therefore, in the application of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, are subject to those provisions of these enactments which relate to share partnerships.

5) By virtue of Article 12, Section I, the statute of limitations does not serve as a basis for the confirmation of rights to immovable property in favor of subjects of powers at war with Russia, regardless of whether the term expired before or after the promulgation of the enactment of 2 February 1915.

6) Article 13, Section I, applies only to cases of satisfaction of claims for the annulment of transactions aimed at the acquisition of immovable property by subjects of powers at war with Russia.

7) The prohibition on Austrian, Hungarian, German, and Turkish subjects from managing immovable property in the capacity of attorneys, managers, or administrators also extends to the management of such property in the capacity of stewards, clerks, caretakers, and the like.

8) The claims of third parties provided for in Article 13, Section 1, are understood to mean claims both secured by a pledge on the property sold and based on personal obligations.

9) The rule established in Article 2, Section 1, on the application of the sum obtained at auction to cover the claims and costs asserted by third parties in respect of the inventory and sale, is also applied in the conduct of auctions of property provided for in Section IV.

10) Officials of administrative departments receive no special remuneration for their actions relating to the inventory, valuation, and public sale of properties alienated on the basis of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 349 and 2749), and may be compensated only with travel allowances at the generally established rate, if the action entrusted to them is to be performed in a place other than their place of residence, such sums being charged to the costs of the inventory and sale.

11) In the event of the acquisition by enemy subjects, through inheritance occurring after the promulgation of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 349) or, in applicable cases, the rules of 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), of extra-urban immovable property located within the prohibited areas provided for in Section IV of the said enactment as amended by the aforementioned rules, such property shall be subject to alienation within a two-year term on the basis of Article 2, Section I, and the provisions of the aforementioned Section IV shall not apply.

12) Immovable property located within land holdings belonging to towns but registered as being within a district [uezd], in particular within the urban patrimonial districts in the Baltic governorates, is deemed extra-urban property; consequently such property, if located in prohibited areas, is subject to Section IV of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 349) and the supplementary rules of 13 December of the same year thereto (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749).

13) The recognition of a given settlement as a "mestechko" [small town], in the sense of an urban settlement, may be considered established either when there is a resolution of the legislative authority to that effect, or when the government has introduced in the given settlement, as a mestechko, the municipal administrative structure and fiscal taxation characteristic of urban settlements. Therefore, in prohibited areas, immovable property of Austrian, Hungarian, or German subjects located in mestechki must be deemed extra-urban and subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, if the said mestechki do not meet one of the conditions set forth above.

14) The rules of 13 December 1915, in classifying all areas of the Caucasus Territory as prohibited, also include the Stavropol Governorate among such areas.

15) Immovable property located within prohibited areas belonging to female persons who are enemy subjects and who entered into marriage with Russian subjects after the promulgation of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 349) and, in applicable cases, the supplementary rules of 13 December 1915 thereto (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), is not exempted from the operation of Section IV of the said enactment and its supplements, and is subject to compulsory alienation in accordance with the rules of that Section.

16) The expiration of the established six-month period for the alienation of property by voluntary agreements does not prevent the confirmation of the deed of alienation, if such deed was submitted to the senior notary within the said period, but the confirmation of the deed itself could not follow within that period for reasons beyond the control of the parties, e.g., due to a significant backlog of cases in the notarial archive.

17) The re-registration by voluntary agreement of immovable property subject to alienation is not permitted after the expiration of the term established for such agreements.

18) The enactment of 13 December 1915 places upon the senior notary the obligation to notify the local branch of the Peasant Land Bank only of those deeds of alienation of property subject to the rules of 2 February and 13 December 1915 on the termination of landownership by enemy subjects and émigrés which are submitted to him for confirmation, satisfy all legal requirements, and to whose confirmation the senior notary sees no obstacle.

19) In the Baltic governorates, in the event that compulsory alienation is required under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 349 and 2749) of immovable properties not recorded in the deed registers [krepostnye knigi] as belonging to their owners, it is first necessary to secure the entry of such properties into the deed registers by means of a judicial suit, the filing of which in the competent court is the duty of the local governor.

20) Contracts of hire or lease of immovable property, as well as contracts for timber felling, subject to termination within the one-year term established by the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, may not be transferred to third parties who would have the right to conclude such contracts for a period exceeding the aforementioned term. However, in cases of such a transfer, the administration is under no obligation to bring suits for the annulment of the transaction that took place.

21) Contracts of hire or lease of immovable property falling under Section III and Article 11 of Section IV, even if they include the right to erect buildings, but which do not correspond to contracts on the right of building lease (Arts. 5421–54227 of the Civil Laws, 1914 edition) and are not otherwise linked to a right in rem over the property, are subject only to termination within the established one-year term, and the question of the fate of buildings erected by the lessee must be resolved on the basis of the civil laws in force and, as a general rule, does not fall at all within the competence of the administrative authority. However, if the former lessee retains actual possession and use of the said property, and in particular of the buildings, such unlawful possession and use must be terminated by the local administrative authority by means of the expulsion, in the established manner, of the former lessee — being among enemy subjects — abroad, on the basis of Article 15, Section 1. Such expulsion, permitted in this manner, is not tied to any exceptional or martial-law regime and has the character of a standing and normal power of the local administrative authority.

22) The enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 349), together with the supplementary rules of 13 December of the same year thereto (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), as well as the charter of the Peasant Land Bank, do not prohibit that Bank, whether by voluntary agreement or through the appraisal procedure established by the said rules, from acquiring, without prior partition, shares belonging to enemy subjects in immovable properties held in common ownership with persons not falling under the aforementioned restrictive enactments.

23) The price stated in the proposed deed of alienation, at which the Peasant Land Bank is entitled to acquire the property being alienated, is deemed, in cases involving a deed of gift, to be the value of the gifted property as stated on the basis of Article 988 of the Civil Laws, 1914 edition.

24) The Peasant Land Bank, in exercising its right of pre-emptive purchase, may retain the property for itself at the price realized at auction even where that price is lower than the amount of the mortgage, provided that price was offered by the mortgagee himself.

25) The declaration of insolvency of a debtor who is the owner of immovable property subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 does not exclude the operation of these enactments.

26) Simultaneously with the public posting of the lists of properties subject to alienation, the said lists shall be forwarded by the provincial boards or corresponding institutions, in no fewer than two copies, to the Department of General Affairs of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

27) The relief established by the enactment of 1 July 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 1608) for Austrian, Hungarian, or German subjects of Slavic origin confers only the right to a deferral, for the duration of the war, of enforcement actions relating to the compulsory sale of immovable properties of the said subjects alienated on the basis of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, but by no means implies the non-inclusion of persons enjoying such relief in the nominal lists of owners whose property is subject to alienation, or the subsequent removal of such persons from lists already published.

28) The raising of the question of applying the relief established by the enactment of 1 July 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 1608) for Austrian, Hungarian, and German subjects who have proven their Slavic ethnicity depends, in each individual case, not only on the person concerned but also on the provincial board or corresponding institution, if it has received appropriate information attesting to the existence of that person's right to the relief.

29) Sums due to the owners of alienated properties, realized from the sale of such properties at public auction, are subject to unimpeded payment to the rightful recipients, whether to the said owners themselves or to their attorneys, provided that such owners are within the borders of Russia. Otherwise, the provisions of the Imperial Personal Decree of 15 November 1914 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2923) apply.

30) The acts of the consular institutions of neutral states, which have been entrusted for the duration of the war with replacing Russian consular agents in enemy countries, are accorded the same significance and force as the acts of such agents, and the authenticity of the certifications of the said institutions may, in case of doubt, be confirmed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

31) The consular institutions of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs are entitled to certify only those powers of attorney issued abroad by subjects of powers at war with Russia whose issuance does not contravene the laws of the Russian Empire. Therefore, for example, powers of attorney for the conduct of cases in judicial institutions may not be certified, since, by law, in accordance with the decision of the General Assembly of the First and Cassation Departments of the Governing Senate of 1915, No. 1, enemy subjects, except in cases provided for by the enactment of 5 November 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2446), are deprived of the right to defense in the ordinary judicial procedure for the entire duration of the war. On the contrary, in view of the special provisions of Articles 72 and 88 of the Regulation on Maritime Prizes (annex to Article 353 of the Naval Statute), the issuance by the said subjects of powers of attorney for the conduct of cases in prize courts, and consequently the certification of such powers of attorney by consular institutions, are entirely lawful. Furthermore, in the sphere of private-law relations, to the extent of actions permitted to enemy subjects (cf. the enactments of 11 January, 2 February, 8 and 29 March 1915; Collection of Enactments, Arts. 157, 349, 757, and 795), these subjects are entitled to be represented by attorneys and to issue powers of attorney to the latter in the established manner.

32) Under the procedure of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, the share of each co-owner in common property subject to the said enactments is to be sold at public auction separately from the shares of the other co-owners, unless all co-owners petition for the sale of their common property in its entirety.

33) In the alienation, under the rules of 13 December 1915, of the shares of one or several of the participants in common property, the right of pre-emptive purchase granted to the Peasant Land Bank by these rules displaces the same right of the other co-owners in the said property, which belongs to them by virtue of Articles 548 and 555 of the Civil Laws, 1914 edition.

34) The Peasant Land Bank, under the rules of 13 December 1915, is entitled to secure immovable property for itself even if the proposed deed of alienation or public auction took place before the promulgation of the said rules, or if before that time the mortgagee had filed a petition to retain the property for himself owing to the failure of the auction, provided that the confirmation of the deed or of the auction, or the securing of the property to the mortgagee, had not yet followed prior to the said promulgation.

35) Debts under solo-bill [solo-veksel] credit extended on the basis of a pledge certificate presented in respect of the debtor's immovable property, with an injunction placed on that property, have entirely equal standing with debts under mortgage deeds.

36) Debts under mortgages executed before 1 November 1914, though having belonged to enemy subjects or émigrés specified in the rules of 13 December 1915, but transferred, before the promulgation of the said rules, to persons not falling under either these rules or the enactments of 2 February 1915, are recognized as binding upon the Peasant Land Bank and are to be covered in full out of the purchase price, if the transfer prior to the said promulgation is attested by notarial or registration procedure, or by an appropriate notation in the register of deeds.

37) By the various other claims referred to in Article 9, Section I, Paragraph G, of the rules of 13 December 1915, secured on property being confirmed to the Peasant Land Bank in respect of obligations arising after 1 November 1914, are meant not personal debt claims secured by judicial injunction on the property that carries no preferential right of satisfaction out of the purchase price, but claims of an in rem character, whether under various contracts registered against the property or under loan obligations and other transactions secured not by mortgage deeds but by injunctions based on pledge certificates.

38) The right of preferential satisfaction ahead of the mortgages referred to in the rules of 13 December 1915, executed after 1 November 1914 or having belonged, prior to the promulgation of the said rules, to the enemy subjects or émigrés specified therein, as well as ahead of other claims of an in rem character arising after 1 November 1914, is enjoyed only by such claims of a purchaser displaced by the Peasant Land Bank under a proposed notarial deed for the return of the purchase price paid by him, or part thereof, as well as of a deposit, provided such claims arose before the promulgation of the rules of 13 December 1915 and are attested in a deed of alienation executed before that time, or in another notarial document.

39) Out of the purchase sum due from the Peasant Land Bank, claims under mortgages executed before 1 November 1914 and which, as of the date of promulgation of the rules of 13 December 1915, did not belong to the enemy subjects or émigrés specified in these rules, are to be paid in full. If a balance then remains, it is applied first to satisfy the claim of the purchaser displaced by the Bank for the return of monies paid in advance, provided such claim is attested in a deed of alienation executed, or in another notarial document drawn up, before the promulgation of the rules of 13 December 1915. Thereafter, claims under mortgages executed after 1 November 1914, or belonging as of the date of promulgation of the rules of 13 December 1915 to enemy subjects or émigrés, as well as claims of an in rem character secured on the property arising after 1 November 1914, are paid in order of priority of pledge rights. Finally, the remaining balance is applied to secure or satisfy proportionally all personal claims, including the claims of the purchaser under the proposed deed of alienation arising after the promulgation of the rules of 13 December 1915.

40) The claim referred to in the rules of 13 December 1915 (G, I, Art. 9) of a purchaser displaced by the Peasant Land Bank, under a proposed notarial deed, for the return of the purchase price paid by him, or part thereof, as well as of a deposit, is satisfied, if it arose before the promulgation of the said rules, at the wish of the displaced purchaser as expressed in an appropriate statement, by means of registered obligations of the Peasant Land Bank issued in his name, and in the absence of such a statement, by means of the realization of Bank certificates at the expense of the owner of the property. A claim of a displaced purchaser for the return of the said sums arising after the promulgation of the rules of 13 December 1915 is discharged exclusively by the issuance of registered obligations.

41) Instead of remitting to the local district court the portion of the purchase sum corresponding to disputed claims encumbering property acquired by the Peasant Land Bank, the Bank is obligated only to notify the competent district court of the sums held at the Bank's disposal, withheld in respect of the said claims, indicating the basis of calculation for each of them.

42) Pending the issuance of registered obligations of the Peasant Land Bank for sums due to the former owners of immovable properties confirmed to the Bank, enforcement actions directed against the said sums are discharged by registered obligations of the Bank issued in the names of the claimants.

43) When inventoried immovable property is left in the management of its owner or the owner's attorney, the owner or his attorney is obligated to accept the property in accordance with the inventory.

44) The rule on the separate sale of each of several estates belonging to one owner does not apply to a case in which several estates located in one place constitute the subject of a single undivided pledge.

45) Property may be sold below its appraised value not only at a second auction but also at a first auction.

46) Under the procedure of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, every auction, whether first or second, must begin at the appraised sum, and, in the absence of persons wishing to bid above that sum, the auction is to continue at the price offered by any of the persons participating in the auction, and is by no means to be terminated on account of the absence of bids above the appraisal.

47) The filing of a complaint concerning the improper compilation of the lists, or their supplementation, does not suspend the confirmation, in favor of the purchaser, of an estate sold at public auction, unless a special order to that effect follows from the Governing Senate or the Economic Department of the Imperial Finland Senate, as applicable.

48) The non-receipt of returned copies of announcements of the day of the auction, sent to the police — and indeed not only to the district [uezd] police but also to the municipal police (Art. 241 of the Regulation on the Collection of Undisputed Treasury Claims, 1910 edition) — may not serve as an obstacle to the conduct of a public sale of properties subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915.

49) Immovable properties subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 may be sold at public auction under the procedure of the said enactments, notwithstanding the unknown whereabouts of the owners and the absence of an established guardianship. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 605

50) The purchaser of property sold at public auction under the procedure of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 is obligated to pay the entire purchase sum due from him within the fifteen-day term specified in Article 282 of the Regulation on the Collection of Undisputed Treasury Claims, 1910 edition, such term to be reckoned from the day of the auction and not from the day of confirmation of the auction, which confirmation may follow only after the Peasant Land Bank has communicated its refusal to acquire the property.

51) In the event of the failure of the auctions, mortgagees may petition to have the unsold property retained for themselves, no later than the deadline specified to them in the notice of the outcome of the auction, and in any event — after the failure of the first auction — no later than the appointment of the second, and after the failure of the latter, no later than the issuance of a resolution placing the property that was offered for sale under sequestration.

52) In determining, under the appraisal procedure, the sum at which property placed under sequestration pursuant to the enactment of 13 December 1915 may be confirmed to the Peasant Land Bank, the appraisal is conducted in accordance with the rules provided in the charter of the Bank (Art. 2, annex to Art. 46 of the Charter of the Peasant Land Bank, 1912 edition).

53) In the acquisition by the Peasant Land Bank of immovable properties sequestered on the basis of the enactment of 13 December 1915, the appraised value of the said properties may be set by the Bank even below the amount of a mortgage held by a private person, but not below one held by a credit institution.

54) Immovable properties subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, in the event that a sequestration has been imposed upon them on the basis of Article 19, annex to Article 23, of the General Provincial Institution, 1892 edition, and Article 26, Annex 1 to Article 1 (note 2) of the Statute on the Prevention and Suppression of Crimes, 1890 edition, may be alienated under the procedure of the said enactments either upon the lifting of the sequestration, or in cases where the departments in charge of them declare that the said enactments are to be applied to these properties.

55) The imposition of a sequestration on immovable properties subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 does not suspend or interrupt the running of the term established for the alienation of the said properties by voluntary agreement.

56) In the event of the imposition of a sequestration on immovable properties subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, contracts of hire, lease, or timber felling concluded by the owners of such properties for the needs thereof are not subject, during the period of sequestration, to the rules of the said enactments, and such contracts are instead governed by Article 9 of the enactment of 12 January 1916 on the procedure for the administration and management of sequestered enterprises and properties (Collection of Enactments, Art. 118).

In this case, the rule of the enactments of [—] December 1915 prohibiting the future encumbrance of the said properties with rights arising from the above-mentioned contracts likewise does not apply during the period of sequestration.

II. On the enactment concerning landownership and land use by certain categories of persons of Austrian, Hungarian, or German origin who are Russian subjects (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 350 and 2749).

1) The acquisition of rights to immovable property by volost, rural, settlement, and communal societies specified in Article 1 is prohibited everywhere throughout the entire expanse of the Russian State, while for the individuals and partnerships specified in Article 2 and the supplementary enactment of 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), it is prohibited only outside urban settlements.

2) Volost, rural, settlement, and communal societies, as well as individuals and partnerships formed with their participation, falling under the enactment on landownership and land use by certain categories of persons of Austrian, Hungarian, or German origin who are Russian subjects, and who had already, in the established manner, prior to the promulgation of the said enactment, obtained the right to redeem into ownership a state quit-rent parcel [obrochnaya statya] — the first everywhere, and the second and third outside urban settlements — do not, after such promulgation, retain the right to acquire the said property into ownership or to receive title thereto.

3) Societies and unions established under the temporary rules of 4 March 1906 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 308) are not subject to the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 350) and the supplementary rules of 13 December 1915 thereto (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), even if enemy émigrés are among the members of such societies and unions.

4) Mutual credit societies, operating by means of pooled capital formed from contributions (shares) of individual members who bear liability for the obligations of the society on the basis of joint and several suretyship — even beyond the contributions made, but within the limits precisely defined by the charter — belong to the category of share partnerships, and therefore, in the application of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, are subject to those provisions of these enactments which relate to share partnerships.

5) Permits issued to the societies, partnerships, and individuals specified in the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Arts. 350 and 2749) granting the right to prospect for mineral resources on state-owned lands are, from the promulgation of the said enactments, deemed invalid, and henceforth the issuance of such permits to the above-mentioned societies, partnerships, and persons may not take place.

6) A subsequent registration with other societies or estates has no bearing upon, and does not exempt from subordination to, the restrictive rules those enemy émigrés and their descendants in the male line who, on the day of promulgation of the said rules, were members of societies or were listed among the colonies and villages specified in Article 2, subparagraphs "a" and "b." Therefore, relatives of the above-mentioned émigrés who had already, by the day of promulgation of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 350) or, in applicable cases, the enactment of 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), left the categories provided for by these enactments are not subject to their operation and may acquire the property of the said émigrés notwithstanding their kinship with the latter, and, in particular, may demand the issuance of the certificates established in Article 4.

7) Membership of enemy émigrés in one of the first two categories specified in Article 2, subparagraphs "a" and "b," is determined as of the day of promulgation of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 350) or, in applicable cases, the supplementary rules of 13 December 1915 thereto (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), in the sense that a subsequent exit of the owners from these categories does not exempt the property belonging to them from subordination to this enactment and the supplementary rules thereto.

8) In applying the rule concerning the time limit for transfer into Russian subjecthood (Art. 2, subparagraph "d"), the possibility or impossibility for a given person to have observed this time limit may not be taken into account.

9) Female persons who are Russian subjects and who married Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés who were already Russian subjects at the time of the marriage, but who had acquired such subjecthood after 1 January 1880 (Art. 2, subparagraph "d"), do not, through marriage to such émigrés, become subject to the restrictive enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 350) and the supplementary rules of 13 December of the same year thereto (Collection of Enactments, Art. 2749), and the relation of these persons to the said enactment and rules is determined by their personal legal status as it existed prior to marriage.

10) Confirmation of the time of transfer into Russian subjecthood of Austrian, Hungarian, or German émigrés who hold such subjecthood (Art. 2, subparagraph "d") may be provided, preferably, by a certificate of the provincial board attesting to the taking of the oath, and, where it is difficult to produce such a certificate, by other official documents, e.g., service records, certificates of vital records, and the like (excluding, however, passports), which indisputably attest to the person's status as a Russian subject and the time of entry into such status.

11) The exemptions enumerated in Article 3, paragraph 1, may apply to persons of both the male and, in applicable cases, the female sex, but do not extend to the spouses of such persons.

12) The exemption established in Article 3, paragraph 1, subparagraph "b," in favor of persons who have proven their Slavic ethnicity, applies to Slavs among the enemy émigrés even if their transfer into Russian subjecthood occurred after the promulgation of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, Art. 350).

13) Participation in the rank of officers or as volunteers in the combat operations of the Russian army or the Russian fleet (Art. 3, paragraph 1, subparagraph "v") is recognized only as direct participation in the combat engagements of the active army and fleet, provided there is no evidence refuting the legal presumption of the valorous conduct of the said persons.

14) The exception established in Article 3, point 1, letter "v," extends only to military ranks forming part of the combat strength of the army or navy, and not to non-combatant persons, even if they are attached to the armed forces of the state, such as, for example, various field officials, physicians, and the like, and in any case not to persons unconnected with the army or navy.

15) The exception in favor of persons who have certified the death of one of their ascendants or descendants on the field of battle (Art. 3, point 1, letter "v") does not extend to persons whose corresponding relatives are missing in the war.

16) Point 3 of Article 3 refers only to fixed-term leases of immovable property. Rights of perpetual lease, including of state land, however, have the character of a hereditary acquisition and fall under the operation of Articles 1 and 2, and, within the prohibited zone, under the operation of the enactment on the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals in border areas.

17) Upon the termination of the rights to immovable property provided for in Article 3, point 3, arising from a contract of hire or lease, the question of buildings erected by the lessee must be resolved on the basis of the civil laws in force and does not fall within the jurisdiction of the administrative authority.

18) The rule contained in the second part of point 3 of Article 3 concerning the termination, within a one-year period, of contracts of hire or lease concluded by the societies or partnerships mentioned therein does not extend to contracts for the hire of apartments, houses, or other premises.

19) The obligation established in Article 4 for local governors to issue to acquirers of immovable property the certificates specified in that article does not depend in any way on the possible inclusion of the immovable property belonging to the acquirers in the as-yet-uncompleted lists of properties situated in prohibited areas that are subject to alienation.

20) Contracts of hire or lease of immovable property subject to termination within the period established by the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 may not be assigned to third parties having the right to conclude such contracts for a period exceeding the aforementioned term. However, in the event of such an assignment, the administration is under no obligation to bring suits for the annulment of the transaction that has taken place.

21) Prescription does not serve as grounds for the confirmation of rights to immovable property in favor of the individual persons, societies, and partnerships covered by the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 350) and the supplementary rules thereto of 13 December 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 2749), regardless of whether the prescriptive period expired before or after the promulgation of the said enactment.

III. On the enactment concerning the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals in border areas (Coll. of Laws, arts. 351 and 2749).

1) Re-registration by voluntary agreement of immovable property subject to alienation is not permitted after the expiration of the periods established for such agreements.

2) Permits issued to the societies, partnerships, and individual persons specified in the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Coll. of Laws, arts. 351 and 2749) for the right to prospect for mineral resources on state lands are deemed invalid as of the promulgation of the said enactments, and henceforth the issuance of such permits to the aforementioned societies, partnerships, and persons may not take place.

3) Societies and unions established under the temporary rules of 4 March 1906 (Coll. of Laws, art. 308) are not subject to the operation of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 351) and the supplementary rules thereto of 13 December 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 2749), even if enemy nationals are among the members of such societies and unions.

4) In the alienation of allotment-external communal lands of volost, rural, settlement, and communal societies (Art. 3, point 1), such lands must be alienated in their entirety, regardless of the personal rights of individual members of the societies that would exempt them from the operation of the restrictive rules.

5) The membership of enemy nationals in one of the first two categories specified in Art. 3, point 2, "a" and "b," is determined as of the day of promulgation of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 351) or, in applicable cases, of the supplementary rules thereto of 13 December 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 2749), in the sense that the subsequent departure of the owners from these categories does not release the property belonging to them from being subject to this enactment and the supplementary rules thereto.

6) Extra-urban immovable properties belonging in border areas to Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals, encumbered with a life-estate right of third parties not falling under the operation of the restrictive rules of 2 February and 13 December 1915, are subject to alienation within the period established by these rules, with preservation of the rights of the life-tenants.

7) Immovable properties situated within land estates belonging to towns but registered in the district (uezd), in particular within urban patrimonial districts in the Baltic governorates, are deemed to be extra-urban properties; consequently, such properties, when situated in prohibited areas, are subject to alienation under the procedure of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 351) and the supplementary rules thereto of 13 December of the same year (Coll. of Laws, art. 2749).

8) The recognition of a given settlement as a market town (mestechko), in the sense of an urban settlement, may be deemed to have taken place either upon the existence of a resolution to that effect by the legislative authority, or upon the introduction by the Government, in the given settlement, as a market town, of the communal organization and fiscal taxation characteristic of urban settlements. Therefore, in prohibited areas, immovable properties of Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals situated in market towns must be deemed extra-urban and are subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 if the said market towns do not satisfy one of the conditions set forth above.

9) In the Baltic governorates, in the event of the necessity of compulsory alienation, in accordance with the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Coll. of Laws, arts. 351 and 2749), of immovable properties not recorded in the land registers (fortification books) under the names of their owners, it is first necessary to achieve the entry of such properties into the land registers by means of a judicial suit, the filing of which in the competent court is the duty of the local governor.

10) The enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 351) together with the supplementary rules thereto of 13 December of the same year (Coll. of Laws, art. 2749), as well as the charter of the Peasant Land Bank, do not prohibit that Bank, by voluntary agreement or under the valuation procedure established by the said rules, from acquiring, without prior partition, shares belonging to enemy nationals in immovable properties held in joint ownership with persons not falling under the operation of the above-mentioned restrictive enactments.

11) The letting, in accordance with the charter on the administration of state estates in the Western and Baltic governorates (Digest of Laws, vol. VIII, part 1, 1893 ed.), of state quit-rent (obrok) items for a fixed, albeit lengthy (e.g., 99-year), term of holding cannot be equated with hereditary lease, but constitutes a contract of fixed-term lease subject to termination within one year in accordance with Art. 6 of the enactment on the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals in border areas, if the lessees are the societies, partnerships, and individual persons specified in this enactment.

12) In the compilation of lists of properties subject to alienation, the question of the time at which the owners of such properties entered Russian subjecthood may be of significance, and therefore is to be considered only with respect to those persons who do not fall within the categories specified under letters "a," "b," and "v" of point 2 and in point 3 of Art. 3 of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 351) as amended by the supplementary rules thereto of 13 December 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 2749).

13) Contracts of hire or lease of immovable property, as well as contracts for the felling of timber, subject to termination within the one-year period established by the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, may not be assigned to third parties having the right to conclude such contracts for a period exceeding the aforementioned term. However, in cases of such an assignment, the administration is under no obligation to bring suits for the annulment of the transaction that has taken place.

14) Contracts of hire or lease of immovable property falling under the operation of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, even with the right to erect buildings, but not corresponding to contracts on the right of building development (Arts. 5421–54227 of the Civil Laws, 1914 ed.) and not generally involving a real right to the property, are subject only to termination within the established one-year period, and the question of the fate of buildings erected by the lessee must be resolved on the basis of the civil laws in force and, as a general rule, does not fall within the jurisdiction of the administrative authority at all. However, in the event that the former lessee retains in his actual possession and use the said property, and in particular the buildings, such unlawful possession and use must be terminated by the local administrative authority by expelling, in the established procedure, the former lessee from the boundaries of the governorate, with prohibition of the right of residence therein, on the basis of the rules of 13 December 1915 (V, I, Art. 2). The expulsion permitted under this procedure is not tied to any exceptional or martial-law status and has the character of a permanent and normal power of the local administrative authority.

15) The enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 351) makes no distinction, among the volost, rural, settlement, and communal societies covered by it (Art. 3, point 1 and point 2, letter "a" as amended by the supplementary rules of 13 December 1915), based on their location within or outside the area of prohibited localities; consequently, the immovable properties of such societies or of their individual members, situated within the boundaries of the said area, are subject to alienation regardless of the location of the societies themselves.

16) The alienation of immovable properties belonging to the partnerships specified in Art. 3, points 2 and 3, does not of itself subject the individual members of these partnerships to the operation of the rule established in point "d" of Article 2 of the enactment on landownership and land use by certain categories of Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals in Russian DOCUMENTS 61 1

subjecthood, if these members were not personally the owners of the immovable properties alienated on the basis of the enactments in force with respect to the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals in border areas.

17) A later registration with other societies and estates of those enemy nationals and their descendants in the male line who, on the day of the promulgation of the said rules, were members of societies or were counted among the composition of the colonies and villages specified in Article 3, point 2, letters "a" and "b," has no significance and does not exempt them from being subject to the restrictive rules. Therefore, relatives of the aforementioned nationals who had already, by the day of promulgation of the restrictive enactments, left the categories covered by the latter are not subject to the operation of these enactments and may acquire the alienated properties of the said nationals, notwithstanding their kinship with the latter.

18) Persons of the female sex, Russian subjects, who married Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals who were already Russian subjects at the time of the marriage but had acquired such subjecthood after 1 January 1880 (Art. 3, point 2, "g"), do not, through marriage with such nationals, become subject to the operation of the restrictive enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 351) and the supplementary rules thereto of 13 December of the same year (Coll. of Laws, art. 2749); moreover, the relation of these persons to the said enactment and rules is determined by their personal legal status existing prior to marriage.

19) Certification of the time of entry into Russian subjecthood of Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals who are Russian subjects (Art. 3, point 2, "g") may serve, preferably, as a certificate of the provincial administration concerning the taking of the oath, and, where it is difficult to produce such a certificate, other official documents as well, e.g., service records, records of vital statistics, and the like (except, however, passports), which indisputably certify the person's status as a Russian subject and the time of entry into such subjecthood.

20) In applying the rule established in Art. 3, point 2, letter "g," concerning the period for entry into Russian subjecthood, the possibility or impossibility for the given person to observe this period may not be taken into account.

21) The exception established in Article 4, point 1, "b," in favor of persons who have certified their membership of a Slavic nationality, applies to Slavs among enemy nationals, even if their entry into Russian subjecthood followed after the promulgation of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 351).

22) The exceptions enumerated in Art. 4, point 1, may apply to persons of both the male and, in applicable cases, the female sex, but do not extend to the spouses of such persons.

23) Participation in the rank of officers or as volunteers in the combat operations of the Russian army or Russian navy (Art. 4, point 1, "v") is recognized only as direct participation in the combat engagements of the active army and navy, provided there are no facts on hand refuting the lawful presumption of the valorous conduct of the persons in question.

24) The exception established in Article 4, point 1, letter "v," extends only to military ranks forming part of the combat strength of the army or navy, and not to non-combatant persons, even if they are attached to the armed forces of the state, such as, for example, various field officials, physicians, and the like, and in any case not to persons unconnected with the army or navy.

25) The exception in favor of persons who have certified the death of one of their ascendants or descendants on the field of battle (Art. 4, point 1, letter "v") does not extend to persons whose corresponding relatives are missing in the war.

26) The ten-month period established in Article 5, as amended by the enactment of 13 December 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 2749), for the voluntary re-registration of properties subject to alienation applies also to those of such properties for which the said period, under the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 351), had been fixed at one year and four months.

27) The expiration of the established ten-month period for the alienation of properties by voluntary agreement does not prevent the confirmation of the act of alienation if that act was submitted to the senior notary within the said period, but the confirmation itself of the act could not follow within the period for reasons beyond the control of the parties, e.g., owing to a significant backlog of matters in the notarial archive.

28) The declaration of insolvency of the debtor-owner of immovable property subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 does not remove the operation of these enactments.

29) Immovable properties subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 may be sold at public auction under the procedure of the said enactments, notwithstanding the unknown whereabouts of the owners and the absence of an established guardianship.

30) Simultaneously with the posting for general public inspection of the lists of properties subject to alienation, the said lists are to be forwarded by the provincial administrations, or the institutions corresponding to them, in not fewer than two copies, to the Department of General Affairs of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

31) Officials of administrative departments receive no special remuneration for their actions in connection with the inventory, valuation, and public sale of properties alienated on the basis of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Coll. of Laws, arts. 351 and 2749), and may be compensated only with travel money (progonnye dengi) in the amount established on the general basis, if the action entrusted to them must be performed in a place other than that of their residence, such money to be charged to the expenses of the inventory and sale.

32) Sums due to enemy nationals residing abroad may be paid without hindrance to their attorneys, but the transfer of these sums abroad must be subject to the general rules existing on this subject for Russian subjects.

33) The prohibition on Austrian, Hungarian, and German nationals from managing immovable property in the capacity of attorneys, managers, or administrators also applies to the management of such property in the capacity of stewards, clerks, caretakers, and the like.

34) Immovable properties subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 that have had sequestration imposed on them on the basis of Article 19 of the appendix to Article 23 of the General Institution of the Governorates, 1892 ed., and Article 26 of Appendix I to Article 1 (note 2) of the Statute on the Prevention and Suppression of Crimes, 1890 ed., may be alienated under the procedure of the said enactments either upon the removal of the sequestration, or in cases where the departments administering them declare that the operation of the said enactments is to be applied to these properties.

35) The imposition of sequestration on immovable property subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 does not suspend or interrupt the running of the period established for the alienation of such property by voluntary agreement.

36) In the event of the imposition of sequestration on immovable property subject to alienation under the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, contracts of hire, lease, or timber-felling concluded by the owners of such property for its needs are not subject, during the period of sequestration, to the rules of the said enactments, and the operation of Article 9 of the enactment of 12 January 1916 concerning the procedure for the administration and management of sequestered enterprises and properties (Coll. of Laws, art. 118) extends to these contracts.

In this case, the rule of the enactment of 13 December 1915 prohibiting the encumbering, henceforth, of the said properties with rights arising from the above-mentioned contracts is likewise not applied for the duration of the sequestration.

*Collection of Statutes and Orders of the Government (SURP). 1916. Section One. Second half-year. No. 247. Pp. 2410–2422.*

Published in part: History of Russian Germans in Documents (1763–1992) / Comp.: V.A. Auman, V.G. Chebotareva. Moscow, 1993. Pp. 47–51.

## No. 189. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON EXTENDING THE OPERATION OF THE LIQUIDATION ENACTMENTS OF 1915 TO CERTAIN TERRITORIES, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS II (1916)

1955. On extending the operation of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915, restrictive with respect to enemy landownership and land use, to Kharkov governorate, as well as to Kainsk uezd of Tomsk governorate, and to Tyukalinsk and Ishim uezds of Tobolsk governorate.

The Council of Ministers, by special journal of 2 August 1916, resolved, on the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws:

<...>

III. In addition to the enactment on landownership and land use by certain categories of Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals in Russian subjecthood (Coll. of Laws, 1915, art. 350), to resolve:

The operation of point 3 of Article 3 does not extend to Kharkov governorate, to Ishim and Tyukalinsk uezds of Tobolsk governorate, and to Kainsk uezd of Tomsk governorate.

IV. In addition to the enactment on the termination of landownership and land use by Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals in border areas (Coll. of Laws, 1915, arts. 351 and 2749), to resolve:

In Kharkov governorate, as well as in Ishim and Tyukalinsk uezds of Tobolsk governorate, and in Kainsk uezd of Tomsk governorate, the two-month period for the publication of the nominal lists of owners of properties subject to alienation in these localities [enactment of 2 February 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 351), Art. 5], as well as the periods specified in Article 6 of the same enactment and in point 5 of Section I of Part V of the enactment of 13 December 1915 (Coll. of Laws, art. 2749), are to be calculated from the day of promulgation of the present resolution.

V. In addition to Sections I and II of Part IV of the enactment of 13 December 1915 concerning certain amendments and additions to the enactment of 2 February 1915 on landownership and land use by subjects of powers at war with Russia, as well as by Austrian, Hungarian, or German nationals (Coll. of Laws, art. 2749), to resolve:

1) The operation of Article 9 of Section I and Article 2 of Section II extends to the localities enumerated in Article 1 of Section II of the present resolution, if the mortgages specified in the said articles were executed after 1 November 1915 or belonged, prior to the promulgation of the present enactment, to the persons specified in the same articles, and if claims secured on property of another kind are based on obligations arising after 1 November 1915.

2) Immovable properties subject to the operation of the enactment specified in this (V) section, situated in the localities enumerated in Article 1 of Section II of the present resolution, so long as they remain in the possession and use of the persons, societies, and partnerships specified in the same enactment, may not henceforth be either pledged or encumbered with other real rights, nor with rights arising from contracts of hire, lease, or timber-felling.

Furthermore, the said properties may not be left, in the event of the failure of public auctions, to the mortgagees under mortgages executed after 1 November 1915.

His Majesty the Emperor, on the 8th day of September 1916, was Most Graciously pleased to approve the aforesaid resolution of the Council of Ministers.

*Collection of Statutes and Orders of the Government (SURP). 1916. Section One. Second half-year. No. 250. Pp. 2438–2440.*

## No. 190. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON A SPECIAL PROCEDURE FOR TERMINATING THE HOLDING OF ALLOTMENT LANDS IN SIBERIA BY RUSSIAN GERMANS, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS II (1916)

2361. On establishing a special procedure for terminating the holding of allotment lands by German, Austrian, and Hungarian immigrants in Kainsk uezd, Tomsk governorate, and in Tyukalinsk and Ishim uezds, Tobolsk governorate.

By a decision of the Council of Ministers confirmed by His Imperial Majesty on 20 October 1916, it was resolved, on the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Digest of Laws, vol. I, part 1, 1906 edition), in amendment and supplement of the decision of the Council of Ministers confirmed by His Imperial Majesty on 8 September 1916 on extending the effect of the restrictive enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 concerning enemy landholding and land use to Kharkov governorate, as well as to Kainsk uezd, Tomsk governorate, and Tyukalinsk and Ishim uezds, Tobolsk governorate (Collection of Enactments, art. 1955), to establish the following rules:

1. In Ishim and Tyukalinsk uezds, Tobolsk governorate, and in Kainsk uezd, Tomsk governorate, lands allotted, on the basis of the Rules on Resettlement (Digest of Laws, vol. IX, Special Appendix, Book VIII, per the 1912 Continuation), to rural societies formed of German, Austrian, or Hungarian immigrants and their descendants, as well as to individual householders from among such persons who have settled on unoccupied resettlement plots and who fall under the restrictive enactments on landholding and land use by enemy subjects and immigrants, pass into the disposal of the Resettlement Administration; while lands held, on the basis of Articles 1–111 of the Statute on Siberian Peasants (same source, Book VI) and the appendix to the note to Article 14 of the same Statute, per the 1912 Continuation, by such same householders who have joined other local rural or village societies, pass into the disposal of those societies, with the simultaneous exclusion of these owners from the societies, whereby the society is obligated to admit such a number of members as will correspond to the quantity of land passing into the society's disposal, calculated at 15 desyatinas per soul, and if this obligation is not fulfilled within 3 years from the time the land passes into the society's disposal, new members may be added to it by order of the appropriate local authority.

The buildings and farm equipment (livestock and implements) located on either category of land, except in cases where the owners avail themselves of the right granted to them by Article 3 of the present enactment, pass into the disposal of the Resettlement Administration.

2. Compensation to owners for the lands specified in the preceding (1st) article is calculated at the rate of: twenty rubles in Ishim, twenty-one rubles in Tyukalinsk, and seventy-three rubles in Kainsk uezd per desyatina, and for buildings and equipment — at their actual value.

Compensation for the lands of each individual householder who has joined local rural or village societies is calculated: for lands held in separate use — according to the extent of the owner's actual use of such lands at the time of issuance of the present enactment, and for lands held in undivided use — in proportion to that share of such lands which is due to the owner according to the ratio of the area of lands held in his separate use to the total area of lands held in separate use by all members of the society.

3. Owners are permitted to retain for themselves all their buildings or part thereof, as well as all or part of the equipment, by renouncing the corresponding portion of the compensation and assuming the obligation to demolish the buildings they retain in their possession and to remove the said equipment by the deadline specified below in Article 10.

4. The inventory and valuation of lands, buildings, and equipment passing into the disposal of the Resettlement Administration is carried out by a resettlement official or the local peasant chief (as appropriate) (Statute on Peasants, per the 1912 Continuation, Art. 438 and note 2 to this article), in observance of the rules established in Articles: 54, 55, 56, 59–66, 67 items 1 and 4, 70, 71, 75–78, 84, 87, 88, 89 items 1–3 and 7, 90, 92, 103 item 1, 106, 109, 111, 118–120, 121 (without the note), 122, 124–127, 129 and 144 of the Statute on Recovery in Undisputed Treasury Matters (Digest of Laws, vol. XVI, part 2, 1910 edition and per the 1912 Continuation). Upon completion of the inventory and valuation, the inventoried property remains in the management of its owner, or the owner's proxy, under the direct supervision of the volost elder and the village elder and the oversight of the uezd police.

5. The inventory and valuation are communicated in lists to the owner, who is given a period of two weeks from the time of their receipt to lodge a complaint with the General Presence of the Governorate Administration. The complaint is submitted to the resettlement official or peasant chief, as appropriate.

6. No later than one month from the expiration of the period specified in the preceding (5th) article, the resettlement official or, as appropriate, the peasant chief submits the inventory and valuation, together with any complaints lodged against them and his conclusions on the substance of these complaints, to the General Presence of the Governorate Administration.

7. The General Presence, upon reviewing the inventory and valuation, and in appropriate cases the complaints lodged against them, amends the valuation of the lands wherever it deems necessary. Independently of this, the Presence is permitted, in accordance with local conditions, to lower or raise the valuation of the lands within limits of up to 25 percent of the total sum of such valuation, and also, in the event a complaint against the inventory and valuation of buildings and equipment is found to merit consideration, to amend this valuation.

The valuation of buildings on a plot whose owner has availed himself of a free issue of timber materials from a state forest tract (Rules on Resettlement, Art. 60–62, per the 1912 Continuation) is reduced by 10–30 percent, depending on the nature of the buildings (stone or wooden).

From the compensation due to members of rural societies formed of German, Austrian, or Hungarian immigrants and their descendants, there are deducted any arrears owed by them in state, zemstvo, and communal volost dues, as well as unpaid portions of loans received by them for travel and for economic establishment (Rules on Resettlement, Art. 34–59, per the 1912 Continuation), as well as debts to the agricultural and timber warehouses of the Resettlement Administration and to public credit institutions, while from the compensation due to householders from among such same persons who have joined other local rural or village societies, there are deducted, in addition, arrears in communal rural dues as well.

Rulings of the Presence on complaints against inventories and valuations, as well as on the confirmation of valuations, are deemed final and are not subject to further appeal.

8. Sums due to owners in compensation for the lands, buildings, and equipment taken from them are issued to them in 4% state rent certificates at par value, whereby, in the event of a petition by the owner, the sum corresponding to all or part of the value of the equipment taken from him is, depending on the owner's wish, paid out in cash.

9. The actions and orders of the Peasant Land Bank specified in the decision of the Council of Ministers confirmed by His Imperial Majesty on 19 August 1916 concerning certain amendments and supplements to the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 on measures to reduce foreign landholding and land use in the Russian State (Collection of Enactments, art. 1869) are carried out in Ishim and Tyukalinsk uezds, Tobolsk governorate, and in Kainsk uezd, Tomsk governorate, by the Resettlement Administration, in accordance with the rules of the present enactment, whereby the structures and buildings specified in Article 2 of the aforementioned decision of the Council of Ministers and in Article 68 of the Rules on Resettlement, per the 1912 Continuation, together with their equipment, pass into the disposal of the Resettlement Administration free of charge and are transferred by it to the jurisdiction of the appropriate societies or institutions in accordance with the instructions given in Article 11 of the same decision of the Council of Ministers.

10. The Resettlement Administration assumes actual management of the lands of rural societies specified in Article 1, together with the buildings and equipment located on these lands and not retained by their owners (Art. 3), from the time each of these societies is abolished in accordance with Article 9 of the decision of the Council of Ministers confirmed by His Imperial Majesty on 19 August 1916 (Collection of Enactments, art. 1869), while the lands, buildings, and equipment of individual householders from among German, Austrian, or Hungarian immigrants and their descendants who have settled on unoccupied resettlement plots pass into its management from the time such householders are paid the compensation due to them under Articles 2 and 7 of the present enactment. Likewise, local rural or village societies assume ownership of the lands of individual householders from among the said immigrants and their descendants who have joined them, from the time such householders are paid compensation for such lands.

11. Allotment deeds and allotment instruments issued to rural societies abolished under the procedure of the present enactment are deemed void, and corresponding notations to that effect are made on those copies of the said documents which are held in the archives of the local governorate administrations (Statute on Siberian Peasants, Art. 107) and by the officials in charge of the relevant resettlement districts.

12. The appropriation of the credits necessary to cover the expenses arising from the implementation of the present enactment is to be requested by the Minister of Agriculture through the budgetary process.

*SURP. 1916. First Section. 2nd half-year. No. 298. Pp. 2974–2976.*

## No. 191. DECISION OF THE COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ON AMENDMENTS AND SUPPLEMENTS TO THE LIQUIDATION ENACTMENTS, CONFIRMED BY NICHOLAS II (1916)

2406. On certain amendments and supplements to the enactments in force restricting enemy landholding and land use.

By a decision of the Council of Ministers confirmed by His Imperial Majesty on 25 October 1916, it was resolved, on the basis of Article 87 of the Fundamental State Laws (Digest of Laws, vol. I, part 1, 1906 edition), in amendment and supplement of the decision of the Council of Ministers confirmed by His Imperial Majesty on 13 December 1915 concerning certain amendments and supplements to the enactments of 2 February 1915 on the landholding and land use of subjects of powers at war with Russia, as well as of Austrian, Hungarian, or German immigrants (Collection of Enactments, art. 2749), and of the decision of the Council of Ministers confirmed by His Imperial Majesty on 19 August 1916 concerning certain amendments and supplements to the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 on measures to reduce foreign landholding and land use in the Russian State (Collection of Enactments, art. 1869):

A. Regarding the enactment of 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, art. 2749).

I. To resolve:

1. The Peasant Land Bank, in acquiring real property sold at public auction in the appropriate governorate board or an equivalent institution under the procedure of the enactments of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, art. 349 and 351) and the supplementary rules thereto of 13 December of the same year (Collection of Enactments, art. 2749), shall pay, in addition to the purchase price, forty rubles for each property passing to it under a single instrument, which sums pass into the disposal of the relevant Governor or the official acting in his stead, for payment, at his discretion, out of the capital thus formed, of special compensation to persons who took part in the work of alienating the real properties covered by the enactments and rules mentioned above.

2. The Minister of Finance, in agreement with the Minister of Internal Affairs, may, in warranted cases, permit the Peasant Land Bank to settle accounts for an estate it is acquiring at the sum of the valuation established by the Bank, even if the price at which the said estate could be secured to the Bank, under the rules of the enactment of 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, art. 2749) concerning public auctions conducted by the governorate board or an equivalent institution, were lower than the said valuation.

II. Articles 4 and 8 of Section II of Part A of the said enactment are to be set forth as follows:

4. The inventory and valuation of property subject to alienation are carried out in observance of the rules established in Articles 54, 55, 59–63, 67 (items 1 and 4), 70, 74–77, 88, 89 (items 1–3), 92, 103 (item 1), 106, 109, 118–121 (without note), 122, 124–127, 129, 137, 144 and 146–148 of the Statute on Recovery in Undisputed Treasury Matters (1910 edition and per the 1912 Continuation), and the following (Art. 5–7) provisions:

8. Public auctions of real properties subject to alienation are conducted according to the rules established in Articles 190 (note), 199, 203 (item 1), 204, 205, 220, 229–233, 239, 242, 246, 249–251, 252 (items 1 and 2), 258, 262–268, 272, 273, 282–284 (items 2 and 3), 296¹–298, 300–303 and 305–307 of the Statute on Recovery in Undisputed Treasury Matters (1910 edition and per the 1912 and 1913 Continuations), in observance of the following (Art. 9–21) special provisions:

B. Regarding the enactment of 19 August 1916 (Collection of Enactments, art. 1869).

Articles 1, 10, 11, and 14 of Section I are to be set forth as follows:

1. Allotments and real properties of volost, rural, village, and communal societies (colonies) falling under the effect of the enactment of 2 February 1915 (Collection of Enactments, art. 351) and the supplementary rules thereto of 13 December of the same year (Collection of Enactments, art. 2749), regardless of the established form of land use among them (communal, household, or mixed), are subject to alienation by voluntary agreement or sale at public auction only in their entirety, not excluding plots allotted under land management procedures to separate locations.

The effect of this provision extends also to real properties belonging to individual persons either by right of personal or joint ownership or under other patrimonial rights of use and possession, if the present owners of such properties, in order to satisfy their public or economic needs within the bounds of the latter, constitute the aforementioned societies (colonies), even though the formation of these societies may not have been confirmed through the established procedure.

10. Individual members of societies exempted from the effect of the enactments of 2 February and 13 December 1915 (Collection of Enactments, art. 351 and 2749) retain, in the conducting of a sale under the procedure established in Article 1, their right to the portion belonging to them within the composition of the real property being alienated. This right is compensated to these householders, upon sale of the said property to the Peasant Land Bank, either by compensation in the amount of the share of the total purchase price due in respect of the said right by calculation, or by the allotment to them, at the Bank's discretion, of an equivalent plot from the lands belonging to the Bank, with the issuance for such plot of a deed in the amount of the said compensation.

11.
